title: A virtual physicist framework integrating dose prediction and large language models for automated treatment planning.
abstract: Background Automated radiotherapy treatment planning has benefited from data-driven approaches; however, achieving consistently high plan quality across patients remains challenging. Dose prediction models provide patient-specific priors but lack adaptive optimization, whereas large language models (LLMs) offer strong reasoning capabilities but raise concerns regarding stability and safety in clinical use. Purpose To develop and validate a fully automated VMAT treatment planning framework integrating dose prediction and LLM-driven dynamic optimization, termed the Virtual physicist (VP), and to evaluate its dosimetric performance, plan complexity, and consistency relative to manual and other automated planning strategies. Methods A total of 70 cervical cancer patients previously treated with VMAT were retrospectively collected. The dataset was divided into 50 cases for training, 10 for validation, and 10 for testing. The input data consisted of patients' planning CT images with contoured planning target volumes (PTVs) and organs at risk (OARs). The outputs included predicted three-dimensional dose distributions (upper-, middle-, and lower-dose bands) and automatically generated VMAT treatment plans with corresponding dosimetric and plan complexity metrics. The VP framework was implemented in the MOZI treatment planning system via a Python scripting interface. A dose-band prediction model was used to initialize patient-specific optimization constraints. During optimization, an LLM iteratively adjusted objectives and weights based on real-time dosimetric feedback, subject to a rule-based safety engine enforcing clinical and physical constraints. Plans generated using dose prediction only (DP-only), LLM only (LLM-only), and combined dose prediction with LLM (DP + LLM) were compared with clinically delivered manual plans. Results The DP + LLM strategy significantly improved sparing of the bladder and bilateral femoral heads compared with all three other strategies and significantly reduced rectal doses relative to the DP-only and manual plans (P < 0.05), while maintaining PTV Dmean, HI, CI, and GI comparable to those of the manual plans (P > 0.05). For dual-layer MLC plan complexity, DP + LLM produced a more balanced modulation pattern than manual planning, with lower distal-layer complexity-significant for d-C/A and d-MCS but not d-BA-and higher proximal-layer complexity across all three metrics. Compared with DP-only and LLM-only plans, DP + LLM showed a consistent trend toward greater complexity in most metrics, with significant differences in several metrics. In addition, the automated strategies generally showed smaller standard deviations in complexity metrics, indicating improved planning consistency. Conclusion Integrating dose prediction with LLM-driven dynamic optimization enables a robust and fully automated planning workflow, improving OAR sparing and planning consistency without compromising target dose quality, and demonstrates strong potential for clinically applicable intelligent radiotherapy planning.

title: Automatic Lesion Morphometrics Reliably Predict Sensorimotor Recovery After Spinal Cord Injury: A Longitudinal, Multicenter Neuroimaging Study.
abstract: Objective To evaluate automatic magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-derived lesion morphometrics against manual measurements and their prognostic value for characterizing distinct acute to chronic neurological recovery trajectories after spinal cord injury (SCI). Methods We studied a retrospective, multicenter cohort of cervical and thoracolumbar SCI patients who underwent routine clinical MRI at 3-4 weeks post-SCI and neurological examinations over 6 months. Lesion severity was quantified using both established manual measurements and a novel automatic approach. We assessed the between-method agreement of MRI-derived lesion morphometrics, including lesion length, lesion width, and tissue bridge width, and their ability to stratify patients according to 6-month motor and sensory outcomes. Data-driven prediction models were used to identify clinically meaningful lesion measures and their respective thresholds, differentiating subgroups of specific recovery profiles. Results Eighty-three patients from eight sites were included. Automatically derived lesion morphometrics showed moderate to strong agreement with established manual measures (Spearman's ρ: 0.540-0.821, p < 0.001), capturing inter-individual differences in lesion severity and demonstrating comparable prognostic value. Lesion width represented the strongest predictor of 6-month neurological outcomes, splitting patients into recovery-specific subgroups. Patients with a smaller lesion width (threshold: 5.88-6.41 mm) demonstrated higher 6-month sensorimotor scores and superior recovery trajectories, while tissue bridges (threshold: 0.17 mm) further refined motor prediction-based stratification of more severely affected patients. Interpretation Automatic MRI measures of lesion severity hold promise as scalable, time-efficient in vivo biomarkers of SCI prognosis, with potential for clinical adoption to guide treatment decisions and multicenter trial planning.

title: Microwave-Responsive AIE Nanocomposite Induces Immunogenic Senescence for Imaging-Guided Therapy and Bone Repair in Osteosarcoma.
abstract: Osteosarcoma remains challenging due to incomplete tumor resection, local recurrence, and limited immunostimulatory efficacy of current microwave (MW)-based therapies. Here, we develop a multifunctional theranostic nanoplatform, GPC3@TTBC, by conjugating an osteosarcoma-targeting anti-GPC3 peptide onto aggregation-induced emission (AIE) nanoparticles. GPC3@TTBC enables selective tumor accumulation and high-contrast near-infrared fluorescence imaging, allowing precise tumor margin delineation and superior tumor-to-background resolution compared with clinically used dyes, including effective visualization in patient-derived xenograft models. Upon MW irradiation, lysosome-localized GPC3@TTBC generates robust nonthermal reactive oxygen species (ROS) through enhanced charge separation and electron transfer, resulting in substantial tumor cell apoptosis while simultaneously inducing a prominent immunogenic senescence-associated phenotype and senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) response. Importantly, MW + GPC3@TTBC suppressed tumor cell migration and invasion in vitro and reduced pulmonary metastatic lesions in vivo. Meanwhile, the SASP promoted dendritic cell maturation and cytotoxic T lymphocyte activation, thereby enhancing antitumor immune responses and remodeling the tumor immune microenvironment. Beyond tumor eradication, GPC3@TTBC facilitates osteogenic microenvironment reconstruction and bone regeneration after tumor clearance, while exhibiting favorable biosafety. Collectively, GPC3@TTBC integrates targeted fluorescence-guided imaging, MW-enhanced ROS generation, immunogenic senescence induction, and bone regeneration, providing a comprehensive theranostic strategy for precise osteosarcoma treatment.

title: Molecular MRI Reveals Macrophage-Enriched Peritumoral Immune Remodeling After Incomplete Ablation in Liver Cancer.
abstract: Incomplete image-guided ablation can promote local tumor progression by reshaping the residual tumor microenvironment toward immunosuppression, yet noninvasive biomarkers of this process remain limited. Here, a translational multiparametric PET/MRI strategy was developed to monitor macrophage-associated microenvironmental remodeling after incomplete microwave ablation (iMWA) in orthotopic VX2 liver tumors. Twenty-four tumor-bearing rabbits were assigned to untreated control, early post-iMWA (short-term), or late post-iMWA (long-term) groups and underwent clinical 3 T PET/MRI, including diffusion-weighted imaging, dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI, [ 1 8 F]FDG PET, and T2-weighted MRI before and after administration of Eu-VSOP. Eu-VSOP-enhanced MRI revealed a hypointense peritumoral rim after iMWA, with the largest rim-to-liver signal decrease and rim thickness observed in the long-term group. Prussian blue staining and LA-ICP-ToF-MS demonstrated preferential iron and europium enrichment in macrophage-rich, CD206-associated peritumoral regions. Histology and proteomics further demonstrated increased CD206 and MMP-9 expression, extracellular matrix remodeling, immunosuppressive myeloid-associated changes, and metabolic reprogramming in viable residual tumors, accompanied by altered [ 1 8 F]FDG uptake. Together, these findings indicate that incomplete ablation induces a temporally evolving, macrophage-rich immunosuppressive peritumoral niche and support the potential of Eu-VSOP-enhanced multiparametric PET/MRI for noninvasive monitoring of post-ablation microenvironmental remodeling.

title: Deep Learning for AD Risk Screening and Progression Prediction.
abstract: The rise of Alzheimer's disease (AD) immunotherapies underscores the need for accessible, time-efficient biomarkers for early diagnosis. MRI-based deep learning shows promise in this regard, yet few models have undergone comprehensive clinical validation. Using the SILCODE cohort (722 Chinese participants, 1,105 scans), we test the transportability of our classifier (pretrained on Western samples) to an independent Chinese cohort without retraining. The associations between risk scores and disease progression, cognitive performance, and plasma biomarkers are examined. In addition, an interpretable framework is developed to generate individualized brain risk maps and identify subtypes. The model classifies AD with an AUC of 0.913 and 95.2% sensitivity, identifying 90.5% of high-risk individuals 2-3 years before clinical diagnosis. Risk scores correlate significantly with cognitive and plasma indices, particularly p-tau 217. Brain risk maps reveal AD subtypes, including a subgroup with rapid cognitive decline. These findings establish a population-robust, clinically relevant MRI-based model for early AD detection and risk stratification.

title: A CT Lesion Foundation Model for Non-Invasive Assessment of Hepatocellular Carcinoma Aggressiveness and Prediction of Recurrence Risk.
abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, with high recurrence rates following curative resection. Accurate non-invasive assessment of tumor aggressiveness and recurrence risk is critical for surgical decision-making and postoperative surveillance, yet remains challenging with conventional imaging modalities. Here, we developed a CT lesion foundation model (LFM), trained via self-supervised learning on 32,120 generic lesion and 6,387 HCC-specific CT patches to capture transferable intra-lesional imaging phenotypes. Across one internal and two external validation cohorts, the sequentially pretrained LFM (LFM-Seq) achieved area under the curve values of 0.916, 0.846, and 0.920 for microvascular invasion (MVI) assessment, and 0.833, 0.885 and 0.795 for pathological grade assessment. The model remained robust under scenarios of limited training data and tumor localization perturbations. Furthermore, LFM-Seq-derived risk scores stratified recurrence-free survival (RFS), yielding an externally validated C-index of 0.701, and remained independently associated with RFS after adjusting for clinicopathological factors. Exploratory biological interpretability analyses showed that LFM-Seq-derived risk phenotypes were associated with suppressed lymphocyte-related immune programs. These results suggest that CT lesion foundation models can support non-invasive and robust characterization of HCC aggressiveness, recurrence risk stratification and discovery of interpretable prognostic imaging biomarkers.

title: <sup>18</sup>F-FGln PET/CT Imaging of Glutamine Uptake Has Potential for Predicting Immunotherapy Response in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
abstract: We investigated whether glutamine (Gln) uptake, imaged by 18 F-(2S,4R)-4-fluoroglutamine ( 18 F-FGln) PET/CT, could predict and modulate immunotherapy response in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Analysis of the Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA)-Liver Hepatocellular Carcinoma (LIHC) dataset revealed that SLC1A5 expression-which encodes a primary Gln uptake channel in HCC cells-was significantly associated with poor prognosis, higher tumor grade, and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. In murine HCC models, tumors with high 18 F-FGln uptake exhibited elevated Slc1a5 expression and poor response to anti-PD-1 therapy, whereas low-uptake tumors were more sensitive to immunotherapy. Genetic knockdown of Slc1a5 reduced 18 F-FGln uptake, enhanced anti-PD-1 efficacy, increased cytotoxic T lymphocyte infiltration, and decreased regulatory T cell abundance. Transcriptomic and single-cell analyses revealed activation of antitumor immune pathways and reprogramming toward an immune-inflamed phenotype after Slc1a5 suppression. V-9302 decreased tumor Gln uptake, as measured by 18 F-FGln PET/CT, and sensitized HCC to PD-1 blockade. In patient-derived organoid-T cell co-culture systems, low-SLC1A5 organoids were susceptible to PD-1 blockade, whereas high-SLC1A5 organoids were resistant, consistent with 18 F-FGln PET/CT findings. These results identify Gln uptake as a checkpoint of immune evasion in HCC and support that 18 F-FGln PET/CT has the potential to predict and monitor immunotherapy response.

title: Prenatal Detection of Arthrogryposis Multiplex Congenita, Present State and Future Perspectives.
abstract: Arthrogryposis multiplex congenita (AMC) is a heterogeneous group of conditions characterized by congenital contractures in at least two different body regions. Despite increasingly widespread prenatal ultrasound screening, prenatal detection rates for AMC remain disappointingly low, with fewer than half of affected fetuses diagnosed before birth. Missed or late diagnosis limits opportunities for informed counseling, optimal delivery planning, and early postnatal intervention. In this overview, we summarize current knowledge on prenatal detection of AMC, drawing on international cohort studies, registry data, literature on fetal motor assessment, and patient-reported experiences. We highlight the added value of systematic evaluation of fetal movements in addition to repeated structural anomaly scans, the role of multidisciplinary care pathways, and the importance of phenotypic classification (AMC Groups 1-3) for prognosis and counseling. We also review current and emerging genetic testing strategies, including exome- and genome-based approaches, and their diagnostic yield in fetuses with contractures. Finally, we outline future perspectives for international collaboration, standardized data collection from fetus to adulthood, and research priorities with patient support organizations. Together, these efforts aim to improve awareness, earlier recognition, and more tailored counseling for parents confronted with contractures and the possibility of diagnosing AMC during their pregnancies.

title: The Prenatal Phenotype: Illustrating the Complexities of Genetic Testing and Interpretation With the Goal of Understanding the Fetal Presentation of Genetic Disease.
abstract: Advanced prenatal imaging and chromosomal microarray have improved detection of fetal anomalies, yet many structurally abnormal fetuses remain without a unifying diagnosis. This manuscript describes representative prenatal cases evaluated with genome sequencing (GS) or exome sequencing (ES), demonstrating how genomic data refine etiologic understanding, reshape counseling, and reveal the complexities of variant interpretation within the prenatal context. Three illustrative fetal cases were selected based on characteristic imaging findings, including short long bones, echogenic kidneys, multisystem anomalies, and severe limb reduction defects. All underwent detailed ultrasound, standard genetic evaluation, and ultimately GS or ES. Variants were classified using ACMG/AMP criteria with prenatal-specific interpretive considerations. Diagnoses included a 17q12 deletion with concomitant ARID1B-related Coffin-Siris syndrome, a de novo FRYL variant in the setting of multisystem anomalies, and a de novo KMT2E truncating variant identified alongside placental pathology supportive of treated leptospirosis. Findings alter recurrence risks, reveal dual diagnoses, and highlight prognostic complexities. Prenatal sequencing clarifies fetal diagnoses, informs reproductive planning, and refines risk counseling, yet interpretation is constrained by limited prenatal phenotyping and reliance on postnatal genotype-phenotype literature. Integration of GS/ES with imaging and multidisciplinary counseling is essential as sequencing becomes routine in perinatal care.

title: Optimized amyloid-β PET centiloid and cognitive cutoffs predict progression from mild cognitive impairment to Alzheimer's dementia.
abstract: Introduction This study aimed to develop optimized prognostic cutoffs for amyloid-β-positron emission tomography (Aβ-PET) and Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) that predict 3-year progression from Clinical Dementia Rating Global (CDR-Global) score 0.5 to 1.0 in mild cognitive impairment (MCI) participants and validate against cognitive decline/functional trajectories. Methods We analyzed 454 CDR-global = 0.5 Aβ-positive (> 25 Centiloid [CL]) MCI participants from Australian Imaging Biomarkers and Lifestyle (AIBL) (N = 99) and Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) (N = 355), followed up to seven years. Youden index derived optimal Aβ-PET and MMSE thresholds for 3-year progression. Participants were stratified into four groups by combined Aβ-PET/MMSE status. Adjusted Cox models (age, sex, education, apolipoprotein E [APOE] ε4) assessed progression to CDR-Global score of 1.0 Alzheimer's disease (AD) dementia (confirmed with Aβ-PET); adjusted linear mixed models assessed CDR Sum of Boxes (CDR-SoB) and Preclinical Alzheimer's Cognitive Composite (PACC) trajectories. Results Optimal cutoffs were Aβ-PET > 71 CL (hazard ratio [HR] = 2.67; 3-year risk = 36.7%) and MMSE score of < 27 (HR = 2.27; 36.8%). The combined high Aβ/low MMSE group showed a 6.39-fold risk and 47.8% 3-year progression, with the steepest decline. Discussion Prognostically optimized Aβ-PET and MMSE cutoffs improve 3-year risk stratification beyond common diagnostic thresholds, supporting dual-cutoff prognostic enrichment.

Introduction

This study aimed to develop optimized prognostic cutoffs for amyloid-β-positron emission tomography (Aβ-PET) and Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) that predict 3-year progression from Clinical Dementia Rating Global (CDR-Global) score 0.5 to 1.0 in mild cognitive impairment (MCI) participants and validate against cognitive decline/functional trajectories.

Methods

We analyzed 454 CDR-global = 0.5 Aβ-positive (> 25 Centiloid [CL]) MCI participants from Australian Imaging Biomarkers and Lifestyle (AIBL) (N = 99) and Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) (N = 355), followed up to seven years. Youden index derived optimal Aβ-PET and MMSE thresholds for 3-year progression. Participants were stratified into four groups by combined Aβ-PET/MMSE status. Adjusted Cox models (age, sex, education, apolipoprotein E [APOE] ε4) assessed progression to CDR-Global score of 1.0 Alzheimer's disease (AD) dementia (confirmed with Aβ-PET); adjusted linear mixed models assessed CDR Sum of Boxes (CDR-SoB) and Preclinical Alzheimer's Cognitive Composite (PACC) trajectories.

Results

Optimal cutoffs were Aβ-PET > 71 CL (hazard ratio [HR] = 2.67; 3-year risk = 36.7%) and MMSE score of < 27 (HR = 2.27; 36.8%). The combined high Aβ/low MMSE group showed a 6.39-fold risk and 47.8% 3-year progression, with the steepest decline.

Discussion

Prognostically optimized Aβ-PET and MMSE cutoffs improve 3-year risk stratification beyond common diagnostic thresholds, supporting dual-cutoff prognostic enrichment.

title: Accelerated clinical evaluations for Alzheimer's disease: feasibility across specialty and rural care settings.
abstract: Introduction Timely diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease (AD) is increasingly important given the availability of disease-modifying therapies, yet current diagnostic pathways remain fragmented, resource-intensive, and difficult to access. We developed the accelerated clinical evaluation for Alzheimer's disease (ACE-AD), a nursing-led workflow integrating a clinical interview, cognitive testing, blood biomarkers, and portable magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to streamline dementia evaluation. Methods ACE-AD was evaluated in two phases. Phase 1 validated the workflow in 20 participants with standard-of-care (SOC) memory clinic diagnoses compared against ACE-AD-derived etiologic diagnosis, cognitive staging, and neuroimaging findings. Phase 2 adapted the workflow for a rural neurology practice, assessing feasibility, utility, and acceptability. Results In Phase 1 (n = 20), primary etiologic diagnoses were universally concordant between SOC and ACE-AD evaluations, with 90% agreement on AD as a primary or contributing etiology. Cognitive stage agreed in 13 participants (65%); ACE-AD rated all discordant cases as less impaired. Portable MRI identified clinically relevant abnormalities consistent with SOC MRI, and patients, care partners, and clinicians rated the workflow highly acceptable. In Phase 2 (n = 7), the rural neurologist reported improved diagnostic confidence, efficiency, treatment planning, and patient communication without workflow disruption. Discussion A structured, nursing-led evaluation integrating blood biomarkers and portable MRI can capture sufficient clinical information to support specialist dementia diagnosis while shifting much of the diagnostic workup earlier in the care pathway. These findings support further evaluation of ACE-AD as a scalable approach for expanding access to timely dementia diagnosis in both specialty and resource-limited settings.

Introduction

Timely diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease (AD) is increasingly important given the availability of disease-modifying therapies, yet current diagnostic pathways remain fragmented, resource-intensive, and difficult to access. We developed the accelerated clinical evaluation for Alzheimer's disease (ACE-AD), a nursing-led workflow integrating a clinical interview, cognitive testing, blood biomarkers, and portable magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to streamline dementia evaluation.

Methods

ACE-AD was evaluated in two phases. Phase 1 validated the workflow in 20 participants with standard-of-care (SOC) memory clinic diagnoses compared against ACE-AD-derived etiologic diagnosis, cognitive staging, and neuroimaging findings. Phase 2 adapted the workflow for a rural neurology practice, assessing feasibility, utility, and acceptability.

Results

In Phase 1 (n = 20), primary etiologic diagnoses were universally concordant between SOC and ACE-AD evaluations, with 90% agreement on AD as a primary or contributing etiology. Cognitive stage agreed in 13 participants (65%); ACE-AD rated all discordant cases as less impaired. Portable MRI identified clinically relevant abnormalities consistent with SOC MRI, and patients, care partners, and clinicians rated the workflow highly acceptable. In Phase 2 (n = 7), the rural neurologist reported improved diagnostic confidence, efficiency, treatment planning, and patient communication without workflow disruption.

Discussion

A structured, nursing-led evaluation integrating blood biomarkers and portable MRI can capture sufficient clinical information to support specialist dementia diagnosis while shifting much of the diagnostic workup earlier in the care pathway. These findings support further evaluation of ACE-AD as a scalable approach for expanding access to timely dementia diagnosis in both specialty and resource-limited settings.

title: Anatomical and histological characterization of the heart of the scarlet ibis (Eudocimus ruber).
abstract: Detailed information on the cardiac morphology of the scarlet ibis (Eudocimus ruber) remains limited. This study aimed to characterize the gross and microscopic anatomy of this species' heart and provide morphometric data. We examined six specimens (three males and three females) using gross anatomical analysis, morphometry, conventional radiography, three-dimensional scanning, light microscopy, and scanning electron microscopy. The mean heart mass was 5.93 ± 1.49 g (n = 6), corresponding to 1.10 ± 0.23% of body mass, and the mean radiographic cardiothoracic ratio was 66.90 ± 5.78% (n = 3). Macroscopic examination identified three venae cavae: the right and left cranial venae cavae and the caudal vena cava. The left atrioventricular valve had two cusps with chordae tendineae and papillary muscles, whereas the right atrioventricular valve had a single muscular fold. Histological examination identified uninucleated and binucleated Purkinje fibers in the subendocardial region, extending into myocardial muscle bundles. The base of the aorta showed hyaline cartilage containing chondrocytes and chondroblasts, with no bone tissue identified in the examined sections. These findings provide anatomical, morphometric, and histological data on the heart of E. ruber and a basis for future comparative studies of avian cardiac morphology.

title: Inferior Patient-Reported Outcomes After Primary Hip Arthroscopy in the Congenitally Narrow Joint Despite Similar Cartilage Quality When Compared With a Propensity-Matched Control Group.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate the outcomes after hip arthroscopy in patients with a symmetric congenitally narrowed hip joint space without radiographic evidence of degenerative changes. Methods Consecutive patients with Tönnis grade 0 undergoing hip arthroscopy between 2009 and 2022 for femoroacetabular impingement syndrome with labral repair and minimum 2-year postoperative outcomes were eligible for inclusion in the study. Subjects were considered congenitally narrowed if they had an average bilateral joint space width less than 3 mm without other radiographic evidence of osteoarthritis. This cohort was propensity-matched to patients with an average joint space greater than 4 mm. Preoperative demographic and radiographic variables, intraoperative findings and procedures, and postoperative outcomes were compared between the 2 groups. Results Thirty-one patients in the congenitally narrow group were propensity-matched to 57 patients in the control cohort. The groups were comparable in age, gender, body mass index, and radiographic variables other than joint space width between cohorts. The congenitally narrow group had no differences in femoral head or acetabular chondral damage compared with the control cohort (P > .05 for both). There were significantly lower postoperative patient-reported outcomes in the congenitally narrow group across multiple patient reported outcome measures. At 5-year time point, the control group had a significantly higher percentage, meeting patient acceptable symptomatic state for modified Harris Hip Score (80% vs 52%, P = .01) and International Hip Outcome Tool-12 (80% vs 56%, P = .03) and minimal clinically important difference for modified Harris Hip Score (89.5% vs 63%). There was no difference in revision arthroscopy (9.7% vs 10.5%, P = .9) or arthroplasty-free survivorship (100% vs 96.5%; P = .29) between the congenitally narrow and control groups, respectively. Conclusions There were no differences in intraoperative cartilage quality or reoperation rate in patients with a congenitally narrow joint compared with a propensity-matched control cohort. However, despite the lack of radiographic osteoarthritis, patients with a congenitally narrow joint had inferior patient-reported outcomes scores compared with the study control group. Level of evidence Level III, retrospective cohort study.

title: Open-Source and Commercial 3-Dimensional Computed Tomography Methods Show Limited Agreement for Classifying Acetabular Morphology in Patients Undergoing Hip Arthroscopy.
abstract: Purpose To compare acetabular morphology classifications derived from a validated open-source (freely available) method with those derived from commercially available software in patients undergoing hip arthroscopy for femoroacetabular impingement syndrome. Methods We analyzed preoperative 3-dimensional computed tomography imaging in patients with femoroacetabular impingement syndrome using open-source and commercial software. The open-source method calculated acetabular coverage across 5 regions and generated z -scores relative to an internal normative database. Hips with z -scores ≥2 or ≤-2 were classified as abnormal. The commercial method categorized hips as normal, undercovered, or overcovered based on published thresholds (lateral center-edge angle, Tönnis angle, coverage percentage, and crossover sign) and focal depth mapping. The primary outcome was categorical agreement between methods. Results Seventy-six hips (55 women, 21 men; mean age 35.5 ± 12.3 years) were included. The open-source method classified 58/76 hips as normal, 10/76 as dysplastic, and 8/76 as overcovered. The commercial method classified 14/76 hips as normal, 29/76 as undercovered, and 33/76 as overcovered. A total of 23/76 hips were classified the same in both systems and called agreed. Disagreements (53/76 hips) fell into 3 categories: (1) essentially similar despite different labels because of borderline z -scores or small focal areas (n = 24), (2) disagreements driven by Tönnis angle alone (n = 8), and (3) true disagreements (n = 21). Notably, 5 hips (6.6%) showed opposite classifications (e.g., dysplastic vs overcovered). Subanalysis of z -scores showed that 69.8% of disagreements reflected borderline morphology ( z -scores of ±1-2). Conclusions Although both open-source and commercial methods provide 3-dimensional classification of acetabular morphology, categorical agreement was limited. Most disagreements reflected borderline morphology or small focal areas of uncertain clinical relevance. A minority showed true classification opposites. Clinical relevance Awareness of the methodological differences between open-source and commercial 3-dimensional computed tomography platforms may help surgeons appropriately interpret acetabular morphology classifications during preoperative planning for patients undergoing hip arthroscopy for femoroacetabular impingement syndrome.

title: Pelvic sleeve pyeloplasty in adults: A technical refinement of Anderson-Hynes dismembered pyeloplasty.
abstract: Objectives To describe pelvic sleeve pyeloplasty, a technical refinement of Anderson-Hynes dismembered pyeloplasty for adult ureteropelvic junction obstruction, and to report perioperative and functional outcomes in an initial adult series. Methods Between 2009 and 2018, 12 adult patients with symptomatic ureteropelvic junction obstruction underwent pelvic sleeve pyeloplasty using a transperitoneal laparoscopic or robot-assisted approach. Preoperative evaluation included computed tomography intravenous pyelography and diuretic Tc-99m MAG3 renography. Patients with previous failed ureteropelvic junction surgery were excluded. The technique preserves and incorporates a sleeve of renal pelvic tissue into the reconstruction to create a broad, continuous, tension-free ureteropelvic anastomosis while minimizing manipulation of healthy ureteric tissue. Results All procedures were completed successfully without conversion to open surgery. Eight patients underwent laparoscopic and four underwent robot-assisted pyeloplasty. Mean operative time was 185 min (range 160-255 min), and estimated blood loss ranged from 90 to 350 mL. One patient had intraoperative bleeding from a gonadal vein injury, controlled without transfusion. One patient developed a transient postoperative febrile episode (Clavien-Dindo grade II). No patient developed urinary leakage or required secondary intervention. At a mean follow-up of 38 months (range 24-50 months), all patients were asymptomatic and diuretic Tc-99m MAG3 renography demonstrated unobstructed drainage. Conclusions Pelvic sleeve pyeloplasty is a feasible modification of dismembered pyeloplasty that preserves ureteric length, minimizes ureteric manipulation and facilitates a wide, continuous, tension-free ureteropelvic anastomosis. Larger comparative studies are required to validate reproducibility and long-term efficacy.

title: Targeting Ninjurin-1-Mediated Microglial Pyroptosis Attenuates Neuroinflammation and Neuronal Injury Following Intracerebral Hemorrhage.
abstract: Objective This study aims to delineate the pathophysiological contribution of Ninjurin-1 (Ninj1) to secondary neural injury following intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH), specifically elucidating its function in microglial pyroptosis and its upstream transcriptional governance by nuclear factor-kappa B (NF-κB). Methods Candidate targets were initially identified via in silico transcriptomic profiling. We subsequently employed a collagenase-induced murine ICH paradigm alongside hemin-challenged microglia. Mechanistic pathways were interrogated utilizing targeted genetic silencing (in vivo siRNA and in vitro shRNA) and pharmacological blockade. Disease phenotypes-encompassing pyroptotic execution, neuroinflammation, and collateral neuronal death-were quantified via immunoblotting, molecular assays, and histopathology. The upstream regulatory architecture was validated through ChIP-qPCR, EMSA, and dual-luciferase reporter assays. title: Association of High-Grade Components < 20% on DFS in Stage I Lung Adenocarcinoma: A Real-World Study of Risk Analysis and Predictive Nomogram Development.
abstract: Objective To assess whether high-grade components occupying < 20% of the tumor have prognostic value and whether an Adjusted Grade nomogram improves risk stratification in Stage I invasive lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). Methods We retrospectively analyzed 1539 patients with pathologically confirmed Stage I invasive LUAD undergoing R0 resection; 1321 with follow-up, including 967 with preoperative CT. Tumors were classified by IASLC Grade and reclassified according to predominant pattern and high-grade components; Adjusted Grade 3 was subdivided into MHGC ≤ 5%, DHGC > 5% to < 20%, and SHGC ≥ 20%. Cox models identified DFS predictors. Nomograms were internally validated with 1000 bootstrap resamples and assessed for discrimination, calibration, and net benefit. Results During a median 38-month follow-up, 124 DFS events occurred. Adjusted Grade 3 independently predicted recurrence (HR 3.07, 95% CI 1.54-6.12), while MHGC and DHGC were associated with poorer DFS (HR 3.95, 95% CI 1.53-10.15; HR 2.55, 95% CI 1.12-5.80). In the CT subgroup, consolidation-to-tumor ratio (CTR) independently predicted DFS (HR 3.08, 95% CI 1.46-6.51). Optimism-corrected C-index was 0.740 for the Adjusted Grade-based nomogram, compared with 0.727 for the IASLC-based nomogram and 0.612 for TNM staging. After adding CTR, they were 0.763 and 0.745 for the Adjusted Grade- and IASLC-based nomogram. Decision-curve analysis showed similar net benefit profiles for the two nomograms. Conclusion High-grade components below 20% were associated with poorer DFS. The Adjusted Grade-based nomogram improved internal discrimination versus IASLC Grade and TNM staging but showed no clear clinical-benefit advantage over IASLC Grade. External validation is needed to establish optimal thresholds and clinical utility.

title: CT-Derived Body Composition Enhances Risk Prediction for Early Progression and Platinum Resistance in High-Grade Serous Ovarian Cancer.
abstract: Background Patients with high-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC) who develop resistance to platinum-based chemotherapy experience significantly poorer outcomes and shorter progression-free survival (PFS). This study evaluates whether pretreatment CT-based abdominal body composition is associated with platinum resistance and PFS, and whether its incorporation alongside clinical variables improves prognostic model performance. Methods This retrospective study included 321 patients with HGSOC (mean age 65 ± 10 years; 28.0% platinum-resistant) treated with platinum-based chemotherapy between 2011 and 2023. Deep learning algorithms quantified abdominal body composition features from pretreatment CT scans, including skeletal muscle, bone, subcutaneous (SAT), visceral (VAT), and intramuscular (IMAT) adipose tissues. Platinum resistance, defined as disease progression during therapy or within 6 months of the final infusion, was the primary outcome. PFS was analyzed as a secondary outcome using Cox proportional hazards modeling. Analyses were stratified by chemotherapy sequence (neoadjuvant vs. adjuvant). Survival models incorporating clinical and CT-derived features were evaluated using 10-fold cross-validated time-dependent AUC over a 5-year follow-up window to predict PFS. External validation was partially performed in an independent cohort of 58 patients with HGSOC. Results Increased SAT and IMAT and decreased skeletal muscle density were independently associated with platinum resistance, with high SAT remaining significant in both the internal and external cohorts (p < 0.05). High adiposity and low muscle density were similarly associated with shorter PFS. Survival models combining clinical and CT-derived features consistently outperformed clinical-only models across all evaluated model classes. The Elastic Net Cox regression model incorporating both feature sets achieved the highest AUC of 0.704 (95% CI: 0.660-0.748). Conclusions Pretreatment CT-derived abdominal body composition is independently associated with platinum resistance and PFS in HGSOC, and its incorporation into predictive clinical models improves discrimination. Body composition assessment may help identify patients at increased risk of platinum resistance and early disease progression.

title: Guided bone regeneration using CAD-CAM zirconia barriers: A case series with digital evaluation of bone changes.
abstract: Background CAD/CAM zirconia barriers represent an advanced option for guided bone regeneration (GBR) in three-dimensional defects, integrating mechanical stability, biocompatibility, and digital precision. The objectives of this case series were to evaluate, clinically, histologically, and three-dimensionally, the use of customized zirconia barriers designed using CAD/CAM technology in GBR procedures. Methods and results Three patients with severe maxillary bone atrophy were included and treated with GBR using customized zirconia barriers. Digital planning was performed based on cone beam computed tomography and intraoral scanning, followed by CAD/CAM design and fabrication of the barriers. The defects were regenerated using a mixture of autogenous bone and xenograft. After the healing period, implants were placed using guided surgery, and bone biopsies were obtained for histological analysis. Bone gains were evaluated through linear and volumetric digital analysis based on three-dimensional model superimposition. All surgeries were completed without complications, allowing implant placement in all cases without the need for additional augmentation procedures. Mean horizontal bone gains of 6.17 mm at the crestal level and mean vertical gains of 2.62 mm were recorded, with maximum values of up to 5.11 mm. Volumetric analysis revealed bone gains of 797.158 mm 3 (case 1), 459.718 mm 3 (case 2), and 1416.870 mm 3 (case 3). Histological analysis demonstrated vital, well-vascularized newly formed bone undergoing active remodeling, with no evidence of inflammation. Conclusions Customized zirconia barriers demonstrated favorable clinical and histological outcomes in GBR. The digital workflow, combined with three-dimensional analysis, allowed a precise and reproducible evaluation of bone changes. Key points This case series presents a comprehensive clinical protocol for guided bone regeneration using customized zirconia barriers, based on prosthetically driven planning, individualized barrier design, graft stability, and meticulous peri-implant soft tissue management, including histological analysis of the regenerated tissue. The incorporation of a standardized digital protocol for linear and volumetric analysis enabled an objective, reproducible, and precise evaluation of dimensional changes in the alveolar ridge. Plain language summary Significant bone loss in the upper jaw can prevent dental implants from being placed in the correct position. In these situations, rebuilding the lost bone is necessary to achieve a stable long-term outcome. This case series describes the use of customized zirconia barriers designed to fit each bone defect and support bone regeneration. After the healing period, all treated defects showed sufficient bone gain to allow implant placement according to the original prosthetic treatment plan. Histological analysis confirmed the formation of new bone, while a standardized digital measurement protocol provided an objective and reproducible assessment of the bone changes achieved after treatment. These findings suggest that customized zirconia barriers may represent a promising alternative for the management of complex bone defects, although studies involving larger numbers of patients are needed to confirm these results.

title: Sequential Coronary Obstruction After Native TAVI: Immediate Acute Occlusion and Very Late Stent Compression by Aortic Wall Hematoma.
abstract: Coronary obstruction is a rare but catastrophic complication of transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) associated with high mortality. While acute and delayed presentations have distinct pathophysiological mechanisms, their occurrence in the same patient is exceedingly rare. We present a unique case of a 91-year-old female who developed acute left main coronary artery (LMCA) obstruction immediately following native TAVI using a balloon-expandable valve, which was successfully treated with bail-out percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Three months later (> 60 days, classified as "Very Late" coronary obstruction), she presented with severe angina and heart failure. Intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) revealed extrinsic compression of the previously implanted coronary stent caused by a localized aortic wall hematoma. A repeat PCI with a stent-in-stent technique restored coronary flow, leading to complete clinical recovery. This case expands the known mechanical spectrum of very late coronary obstruction according to recent classification frameworks and highlights the vital role of intravascular imaging and multimodality assessment in diagnosis and management.

title: Pregnancy-Induced Hypertension Complicated by Posterior Reversible Encephalopathy Syndrome: A Case Series of Two Patients.
abstract: Posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES) is a rare but potentially life-threatening neurological complication associated with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy. This report presents two cases of pregnancy-induced hypertension complicated by PRES, both clinically characterized by headache and visual disturbances, with characteristic neuroimaging findings. The clinical manifestations, laboratory findings, and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) characteristics of two patients are described. Following prompt multidisciplinary consultation and immediate interventions, including strict blood pressure control, seizure prophylaxis, infection prevention, and appropriate obstetric management, both patients achieved favorable clinical outcomes. No significant neurological abnormalities were observed at the 42-day postpartum follow-up. In patients with severe pregnancy-induced hypertension, PRES warrants recognition as a potential complication; management should prioritize rigorous blood pressure control, seizure prophylaxis, alleviation of pregnancy-related physiological stress, and timely neuroimaging to guide treatment, with strategies balancing maternal and fetal safety-early recognition and intervention underpinned by standardized protocols and multidisciplinary collaboration being critical to improving prognosis and reducing complications.

title: Right Ventricular Dysfunction and Ventriculo-Arterial Uncoupling in Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction: A Phenotype-Specific Review of Mechanisms, Diagnosis, and Therapeutic Strategies.
abstract: Background Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) accounts for nearly half of all global heart failure cases. Historically viewed as a left-centric diastolic disorder, emerging evidence identifies right ventricular (RV) dysfunction and impaired ventriculo-arterial (RV-PA) coupling as central drivers of exercise intolerance, functional decline, and adverse clinical outcomes. Objectives This review synthesizes current evidence on the pathophysiological mechanisms, advanced diagnostic modalities, prognostic implications, and phenotype-specific therapies for RV dysfunction in HFpEF, advocating for a transition to systematic biventricular evaluation. Methods A structured, PRISMA-informed search of PubMed and Scopus (2015-2024) identified 74 eligible studies evaluating RV structure, function, and hemodynamics in HFpEF cohorts. Results RV dysfunction is prevalent in 19% to 33% of HFpEF patients and independently predicts all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalizations. Key pathophysiological drivers include post-capillary pulmonary hypertension, impaired RV lusitropy, systemic inflammation, and inter-ventricular dependence. Non-invasive markers notably speckle-tracking echocardiography, 4D-flow cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR), and the TAPSE/PASP ratio enable early identification of subclinical RV-PA uncoupling. While traditional heart failure therapies show limited efficacy, emerging options including SGLT2 inhibitors, interatrial shunt devices, GLP-1 receptor agonists, and targeted pulmonary vasodilators demonstrate potential to preserve RV strain and restore hemodynamics across distinct clinical phenotypes. Conclusions RV dysfunction is a major prognostic marker in HFpEF. Routine inclusion of RV-PA coupling indices in diagnostic and risk-stratification algorithms is essential to guide precision-based, phenotype-guided management and improve clinical trajectories.

abstract: Background In definitive radiotherapy for FIGO Stage I-III cervical cancer, external beam radiotherapy and/or brachytherapy are used-alone or in combination with concurrent chemotherapy depending on stage-with target delineation largely guided by clinically apparent disease. However, discontinuous carcinoma in situ (CIS) "skip lesions" within the uterine corpus are well described in cervical adenocarcinoma, whereas their presence in cervical squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) has not been systematically evaluated. Aims This study aimed to investigate the presence or absence of CIS skip lesions in the uterine corpus of patients with cervical SCC. Methods and results This retrospective study included all patients who underwent total or radical hysterectomy for cervical SCC at Yamagata University Hospital between January 2013 and April 2020. Patients who underwent prior radiotherapy or preoperative chemotherapy, or had non-squamous histological components, were excluded. Fifty patients were enrolled. Pathological examination of serially sectioned uterine specimens was conducted to identify skip lesions, defined as discontinuous CIS lesions in the uterine corpus, as confirmed by a pathologist and a radiation oncologist. Pathological evaluation showed that 29 patients (58%) had FIGO Stage I disease, 6 patients (12%) had FIGO Stage II disease, and 15 patients (30%) were classified as FIGO Stage IIIC1. Preoperative imaging studies did not identify any skip lesions in the uterine corpus. However, one patient (2%; Clopper-Pearson 95% confidence intervals: 0.05%-10.5%) presented with a histologically confirmed CIS skip lesion located in the uterine corpus, approximately 2 cm cranial to the primary tumor margin, that was undetectable on imaging. The primary tumor after biopsy measured 3 mm and was diagnosed as non-keratinizing SCC without > 1/3 stromal invasion. Lymphovascular space invasion, parametrial invasion, and corpus invasion were not observed. Conclusion Although rare, CIS skip lesions in the uterine corpus can occur in patients with cervical SCC.

title: Automated Detection of Positioning Errors in Bitewing Radiographs Using Deep Learning.
abstract: Objectives Bitewing radiographs (BWs) are essential diagnostic tools in dentistry, but are often affected by positioning errors, compromising their diagnostic value and increasing retake rates. This study aimed to develop and evaluate a deep learning-based automated system for detecting and classifying BW type (premolar/molar), side (right/left), and common positioning errors in a controlled mannequin-based setting. Methods A total of 403 BWs were collected from dental student assessments acquired from dental radiology mannequins. BWs were consensus-labeled by dentomaxillofacial radiology experts for type, side, and the most common positioning errors. A balanced data set supported training and validation. Convolutional neural network architectures, including ResNet and DenseNet variants, were trained from scratch and evaluated as independent classification tasks using stratified fivefold cross-validation. Performance was assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, and area under the curve, reported as mean ± standard deviation across folds. A confusion matrix was generated for multi-class cone-cutting error (CCE) severity classification. Results The system achieved accuracies of 95.8% for BW type classification, 99.0% for side classification, 96.3% for CCE detection, and 93.4% for interproximal overlap detection. Multi-class CCE classification achieved an accuracy of 79.3%, with reliable identification of "critical" and "minimal" errors. Detection of incorrect receptor placement achieved an accuracy of 73.2%. Conclusions The CNN-based system showed strong performance for bitewing type, side, binary cone-cutting error, and interproximal overlap classification in mannequin-acquired radiographs. Performance was more limited for multi-class cone-cutting severity and incorrect receptor placement. These findings support the potential use of deep learning for radiographic quality assessment in education and quality-control workflows. A validation study using patient-acquired bitewing radiographs from clinical settings is required before clinical deployment.

title: Triphasic waves in leptomeningeal metastases and cycling alternating pattern of encephalopathy during sleep.
abstract: Background Triphasic waves (TWs), now termed generalized periodic discharges with triphasic morphology, may be mistaken for nonconvulsive status epilepticus (NCSE), particularly in critically ill patients. Changes in vigilance over time can help distinguish encephalopathic patterns from ictal activity. Case presentation A 69-year-old woman with breast cancer and leptomeningeal metastases developed progressive mutism and impaired consciousness. Cerebrospinal fluid analysis showed atypical cells and markedly elevated protein, while brain MRI demonstrated bilateral sulcal hyperintensities, most prominent in the posterior regions. An EEG performed 1 week after bevacizumab and paclitaxel were discontinued showed only mild background slowing without epileptiform discharges. A repeat EEG 1 week later showed nearly continuous TWs. The discharges disappeared during spontaneous sleep and recurred periodically, consistent with a cyclic alternating pattern of encephalopathy during sleep (CAPE). In the absence of significant metabolic and toxic derangements, these features favored an encephalopathic rather than ictal pattern. Given the advanced disease and poor prognosis, care remained supportive and palliative. Conclusion This case highlights the importance of interpreting TWs within their clinical context and in relation to the state of vigilance. Their disappearance at sleep onset, with periodic recurrence during sleep producing a CAPE, supports an encephalopathic rather than ictal interpretation, helping to avoid misdiagnosis of NCSE and unnecessary administration of antiseizure medications.

title: Repetitive clustered low-voltage fast activity on intracranial electroencephalogram in mild malformation of cortical development with oligodendroglial hyperplasia and epilepsy: A candidate electroencephalographic biomarker study.
abstract: Objective Mild malformation of cortical development with oligodendroglial hyperplasia and epilepsy (MOGHE) is a recently recognized cause of drug-resistant focal epilepsy. It is often magnetic resonance imaging-negative or radiologically resembles focal cortical dysplasias, which makes recognition difficult and limits presurgical counseling. We aimed to identify an intracranial electroencephalographic (iEEG) biomarker that distinguishes MOGHE from other developmental brain lesions encountered in epilepsy surgery. Methods We analyzed long-term stereo-EEG and subdural recordings in a retrospective multicenter test cohort (18 MOGHE, 20 non-MOGHE) to identify an iEEG pattern distinguishing MOGHE from other developmental brain lesions. We then evaluated its diagnostic performance by blinded visual assessment in an independent single-center validation cohort (11 MOGHE, 11 non-MOGHE). Firth-penalized multivariable logistic regression tested whether MOGHE histology independently predicted the presence of this pattern after adjustment for spasms, frontal localization, age at seizure onset, and age at implantation. Finally, within MOGHE, we assessed whether resection of the territory exhibiting this pattern was associated with postsurgical seizure freedom. Results We identified highly stereotyped clusters of very brief low-voltage fast activity (LVFA), recurring in statuslike episodes lasting several minutes and sometimes lacking clear clinical symptoms. LVFA clusters occurred in 16 of 18 MOGHE and in no non-MOGHE patients in the test cohort. In the validation cohort, visual identification of LVFA clusters correctly classified 10 of 11 MOGHE and 10 of 11 non-MOGHE cases (overall agreement = 90.9%, 95% Wilson confidence interval = 72.2%-97.5%). MOGHE histology was the dominant independent predictor of LVFA clusters. Within MOGHE, resection of LVFA cluster territory was associated with postsurgical seizure freedom (Mann-Whitney U-test, p = .0021). Significance Because LVFA clusters can be recognized visually on routine iEEG without specialized software, they may provide a clinically applicable candidate biomarker for presurgical identification of MOGHE and support surgical planning and outcome prediction. Prospective studies should validate their diagnostic and prognostic utility.

title: Integrating uncertainty and practice variability for epilepsy prognostication after intracranial EEG: A meta-analysis.
abstract: Objective Intracranial electroencephalography (iEEG) practices and diagnostic testing vary among institutions, limiting standardization and optimization of surgical outcomes. This study estimates resection rates and surgical outcome effect sizes after iEEG and develops individual patient-level data (IPD) models using the missing-indicator method to approximate real-world clinical uncertainties and practice variability in iEEG and surgical decision-making. Methods Databases were queried for studies reporting ≥12-month outcomes after epilepsy surgery in patients with drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE) who underwent iEEG. Random-effects meta-analysis estimated pooled outcome proportions. IPD analysis was performed using multivariable generalized linear regression and logistic regression models with cross-validation and calibration assessment. Missing values for key predictors were retained as a "not specified" category to evaluate the impact of incorporating uncertainty in common clinical data on outcome prediction. Results Primary outcomes were seizure freedom (Engel class IA or International League Against Epilepsy [ILAE] 1) and favorable seizure outcomes (Engel I or ILAE 1-2). Of 4975 studies identified, 115 met the inclusion criteria. The pooled frequency of patients undergoing resection after iEEG was 67% (95% confidence interval [CI] 60%-74%), 52% achieved seizure freedom (95% CI 48%-56%), and 58% achieved a favorable outcome (95% CI 54%-62%). IPD analysis included 1305 patients from 29 studies and identified a lesional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI; odds ratio [OR] 1.94, CI 1.48-2.55, p < .0001) and a cortical malformation (OR 1.47, CI 1.08-2.00, p = .01) as independent predictors of a favorable outcome, whereas iEEG implantation strategy (bilateral implantation OR .61, 95% CI .42-.89, p = .01) was an independent predictor of a less favorable outcome. Significance About two-thirds of patients undergoing iEEG proceeded to resection, and about half achieved seizure freedom. Multivariable models incorporating clinical uncertainty and practice variability were well calibrated. However, modest discrimination suggests that routinely available clinical variables alone have limited ability to predict individual surgical outcomes. More standardized and granular clinical and practice-related data may improve individualized prognostication after iEEG.

title: Intraoperative Management of Fibular Free Flap With Chronic DVT: Case and Technique.
abstract: Background Chronic post-thrombotic syndrome (PTS) involving the peroneal venae comitantes is an uncommon but potentially flap-threatening finding during fibular free flap reconstruction that may not be detected on routine preoperative computed tomography angiography. We describe the successful management of extensive chronic PTS encountered unexpectedly during fibular free flap reconstruction for advanced oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma. Methods Following unsuccessful mechanical thrombectomy, arterial inflow was established before venous reconstruction to identify the dominant functional venous outflow pathway, followed by selective venous anastomosis. Results Early postoperative venous congestion was successfully managed with revision and a second venous anastomosis. The flap remained viable with excellent functional and oncologic outcomes at 1 year. Conclusion This case demonstrates that chronic PTS should not necessarily preclude fibular free flap reconstruction and presents a practical intraoperative and postoperative strategy for managing this challenging and previously underreported scenario.

title: Outcomes Following Extreme Elective Nodal De-Escalation in HNSCC Treated With Curative Intent: A Community Program Experience.
abstract: Purpose/objective(s) To evaluate elective nodal recurrence rates in HNSCC patients treated with extreme dose de-escalation to 30 or 40 Gy followed by a sequential boost to gross disease or high-risk sites. Elective nodal volumes (ENV) defined as any uninvolved adjacent, distant ipsilateral or contralateral anatomic nodal level were treated to either 30 or 40 Gy, followed by a sequential boost to the PTVp/PTVn+ or high-risk surgical bed (PTVp+ PTVn+). A subset of 6 patients received 24-36 Gy (1.5-1.8 Gy BID) based on the Mayo-DART regimen. Assignment to 40 Gy versus 30 Gy reflected the radiation oncologist preference based on emerging trial evidence. All cases were reviewed prospectively in a head and neck multidisciplinary conference, and treatment planning required diagnostic FDG PET-CT fused to the planning CT. Concurrent systemic therapy was administered in 99% of patients. The primary endpoint was regional failure rate within the de-escalated ENV. Secondary endpoints included 1- and 2-year locoregional control (LRC), progression-free survival (PFS), distant metastasis-free survival (DMFS), and failure patterns. Results The analysis included 102 patients of whom the majority 81.4% received definitive chemoradiotherapy, 17.6% underwent surgery with adjuvant chemoradiotherapy, and 1% received surgery with adjuvant radiation alone. The elective nodal volume was treated to 40 Gy at 2 Gy per fraction in 81 patients and to 30 Gy at 2 Gy per fraction in 15 patients; the remaining 6 adjuvant patients received 24-36 Gy at 1.5-1.8 Gy twice daily per the Mayo-DART regimen. The 1- and 2-year progression-free survival (PFS) rates were 88.6% and 87.3%, respectively, while distant metastasis-free survival (DMFS) rates were 95.0% and 95.0%, respectively. In total, 13 recurrences were recorded comprising 7 locoregional and 6 distant failures. Reduced doses to the ENV ranging from 40 Gy to as low as 30 Gy were associated with exceptionally low failure rates regardless of treatment approach, stage, or HPV, and validate similar findings previously reported from larger academic centers. Importantly, 99% of patients received concurrent systemic therapy, and these results should not be extrapolated to radiotherapy alone.

title: Value of Intratumoral and Peritumoral Ultrasound Radiomics Nomogram for Differential Diagnosis of C-TIRADS 4 Thyroid Nodules.
abstract: Objective The Chinese Thyroid Imaging Reporting and Data System (C-TIRADS) 4 thyroid nodules (TNs) have intricate sonographic features that potentially lead to overdiagnosis or misdiagnosis. This study aimed to improve the precision of differentiating C-TIRADS 4 TNs using radiomic nomograms that include both intratumoral and peritumoral features. Methods A total of 337 patients with C-TIRADS 4 thyroid nodules confirmed by pathology or FNAB were retrospectively enrolled and randomly divided into a training cohort (n = 269) and a validation cohort (n = 68) at a ratio of 8:2. Radiomics features were extracted from intratumoral and peritumoral (1-3 mm) regions on B-mode ultrasound images. Feature stability was assessed using intraclass and intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC). Key features were selected through a sequential process involving the Mann-Whitney U test, recursive feature elimination (RFE), and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, followed by calculation of the radiomics score (Rad-score). Independent predictors were identified by univariate and multivariate logistic regression. Three models were constructed: a clinical and ultrasound model (Model 1), a radiomics model (Model 2), and a combined nomogram integrating both (Model 3). Model performance and clinical utility were evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curves, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Results Multivariate analysis showed that age, margin, echogenic foci, and the intratumoral and peritumoral 1 mm Rad-score were independent predictors for the benign or malignant nature of C-TIRADS 4 nodules (p < 0.05). The combined nomogram (Model 3) achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.852 (95% CI: 0.804-0.892) in the training cohort, significantly higher than that of Model 1 (AUC = 0.737) and Model 2 (AUC = 0.784) (p < 0.05). In the validation cohort, Model 3 yielded an AUC of 0.916 (95% CI: 0.851-0.980), outperforming Model 1 (AUC = 0.766) and Model 2 (AUC = 0.807) (both p < 0.05). The calibration curve of the nomogram showed good agreement with the ideal curve (Hosmer-Lemeshow test p > 0.05), and DCA indicated that it provided the greatest clinical net benefit. Conclusion The nomogram integrating clinical characteristics, ultrasound characteristics, and intratumoral and peritumoral 1 mm Rad-score can distinguish benign from malignant C-TIRADS 4 TNs, with superior diagnostic performance compared to single-modality models. It may serve as a non-invasive and reliable tool to reduce unnecessary FNAB rates.

title: Epicardial Fat Thickness in Fetal Growth Restriction: Impact on Neonatal Outcomes and Predictive Value.
abstract: Purpose Fetal growth restriction (FGR) is a condition associated with heightened risks of perinatal morbidity and mortality. Epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) has been identified as a potential marker for metabolic changes in fetuses, but its role in FGR remains underexplored. This study aimed to assess fetal epicardial fat thickness (EFT) in the third trimester and its correlation with FGR diagnosis and fetal measurements. Method A cross-sectional analytical study was conducted at a Perinatology Clinic involving 82 pregnant women, including 43 with FGR and 39 controls. FGR diagnosis was based on Delphi criteria. EFT measurements were performed using echocardiography techniques, and statistical analyses were conducted to assess correlations and predictive values. Fetal EFT was measured using ultrasound, and interobserver reliability was assessed using the Intraclass Correlation Coefficient (ICC). Results In the FGR group, EFT was significantly lower than in controls (p < 0.001). A significant moderate positive correlation was observed between EFT and fetal abdominal circumference (r = 0.363, p = 0.017). ROC analysis identified an EFT cutoff value of ≤ 1.41 mm for discriminating FGR, with 60.5% sensitivity and 92.3% specificity (AUC = 0.802, p < 0.001). In addition, EFT showed significant discriminatory ability for composite adverse neonatal outcomes (AUC = 0.727, p = 0.001). Conclusion This study highlights the potential clinical significance of fetal EFT thickness in FGR diagnosis and neonatal outcome prediction. EFT measurements offer valuable insights into fetal metabolic status and may aid in early identification of high-risk pregnancies. Further research is warranted to validate these findings and integrate EFT assessments into routine prenatal care for improved perinatal management strategies.

title: Thymidine Kinase 2 Deficiency in the Era of Approved Therapy: From Diagnosis to Evidence Across the Disease Spectrum.
abstract: Thymidine kinase 2 deficiency (TK2d) is an ultra-rare autosomal recessive mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) maintenance disorder caused by pathogenic variants in the nuclear TK2 gene. Loss of TK2 activity disrupts intramitochondrial deoxynucleotide pools, impairing mtDNA replication and resulting in a spectrum of quantitative (mtDNA depletion) and qualitative (multiple deletions) alterations whose severity is a key determinant of prognosis. Clinically, TK2d presents as a continuous phenotypic spectrum, from rapidly progressive infantile disease to adult-onset forms, predominantly manifesting as progressive myopathy with early bulbar and respiratory involvement, the principal drivers of morbidity and mortality, with overall severity inversely correlated with age at onset. Central nervous system involvement may occur in severe early-onset cases, whilst extramuscular manifestations are otherwise limited, with sensorineural hearing loss and subclinical axonal sensory neuropathy described across the spectrum. Circulating biomarkers, particularly GDF-15, support diagnosis, correlate with disease severity and show dynamic changes with treatment; serum creatinine, muscle MRI fat fraction and forced vital capacity further contribute to prognostic stratification. Oral supplementation with doxecitine and doxribtimine, recently approved by the FDA (2025) and EMA (2026) for patients with symptom onset ≤ 12 years, represents the first disease-modifying therapy for TK2d, demonstrating marked survival benefit, stabilisation of disease progression and partial recovery of motor function. Evidence in adult patients remains limited and largely retrospective, underscoring the need for dedicated prospective studies with outcome measures sensitive to slowly progressive phenotypes.

title: Fetal Liver Volume and Morphology in Growth-Restricted Fetuses and Their Association With Neonatal Morbidity: An MRI Study.
abstract: Background Fetal growth restriction (FGR) may induce redistribution of the fetal circulation to preserve perfusion of vital organs. Reduced hepatic delivery of oxygen- and nutrient-rich blood may cause volumetric and morphological remodeling. Purpose To quantify fetal liver volume and morphology in FGR and assess associations with adverse neonatal outcomes. Study type Single-center, prospective and retrospective. Population Ninety-two singleton pregnancies: 36 FGR cases (prospective) and 56 appropriate-for-gestational-age (AGA) controls (retrospective). Field strength/sequence 3-T, True Fast Imaging with Steady-State Free Precession (TrueFISP) for fetal liver and body imaging, and TrueFISP or Half-Fourier Acquisition Single-shot Turbo Spin-Echo for brain imaging. Assessment The fetal liver, body, and brain were segmented using deep learning tools. Liver volume, liver-to-body and brain-to-liver volume ratios, and 12 liver PyRadiomics shape features were assessed. Neonates were followed for composite adverse neonatal outcomes (CANO) until discharge. Statistical tests Linear regression assessed associations with gestational age in AGA fetuses. Linear mixed-effects models compared groups, adjusting for gestational age and fetal sex. Univariable logistic regression assessed associations with CANO. Benjamini-Hochberg correction controlled the false discovery rate at 0.05. Results FGR fetuses had significantly lower liver volume than AGA fetuses (74.95 ± 1.76 vs. 114.89 ± 2.18 cm 3 ), lower liver-to-body ratio (0.053 ± 0.001 vs. 0.057 ± 0.001), and higher brain-to-liver ratio (2.637 ± 0.085 vs. 1.978 ± 0.047). FGR fetuses demonstrated significantly less elongated liver geometry, (10.7% higher PyRadiomics elongation values) and had a significantly higher surface-to-volume ratio (11.9%). CANO occurred in 30/92 neonates (27 FGR, 3 AGA). Higher brain-to-liver ratio (OR = 4.12, 95% CI: 1.93-8.77), PyRadiomics elongation values (less elongated geometry; OR = 2.04, 95% CI: 1.26-3.30), PyRadiomics flatness values (less flattened geometry; OR = 1.69, 95% CI: 1.07-2.65), and surface-to-volume ratio (OR = 3.26, 95% CI: 1.80-5.90) were significantly associated with CANO. Data conclusion FGR was associated with reduced fetal liver size and altered geometry, which were associated with neonatal morbidity. Evidence level 2. Technical efficacy 2.

title: Daytime Idle Energy Reduction in Radiotherapy Simulation Computed Tomography: A Prospective Workflow-Based Evaluation.
abstract: Introduction Previous computed tomography (CT) energy-saving studies have primarily focused on after-hours shutdown or idle energy use in diagnostic CT. Radiotherapy simulation, however, includes preparation and immobilisation steps that may prolong daytime non-acquisition periods. This study quantified daytime energy use in radiotherapy simulation CT and evaluated the contribution of power-saving operation. Methods In this prospective single-centre study, electrical power consumption was directly measured using a three-phase power logger during five baseline and five power-saving weekdays (08:00-18:00). Power measurements were integrated with patient in-room intervals and simulation procedure categories. Staff perceptions of workflow impact were assessed using an anonymous questionnaire, and carbon implications were estimated from the measured energy reduction. Results Mean directly measured clinical-hour energy consumption decreased from 38.7 to 36.5 kWh/day with power-saving operation, a 5.8% reduction. Non-acquisition time during patient presence varied markedly by procedure, from 56.5% for respiratory-gated four-dimensional CT to 97.1% for head-and-neck simulation. Power-saving operation shifted daytime power use towards a lower-power state, corresponding to an estimated reduction of 0.84-1.01 kg-CO 2 per clinical day across the emission-factor sensitivity range. Twenty of 21 staff (95.2%) reported no impact on patient throughput. Conclusion Power-saving operation reduced daytime energy consumption without meaningful workflow disruption. Radiotherapy simulation CT has prolonged, procedure-dependent idle periods arising from radiotherapy-specific preparation workflows, highlighting a practical and previously undercharacterised opportunity for energy reduction.

title: Pulmonary Vein Anatomy, Cooling Kinetics, and Recurrence After Cryoballoon Ablation for Atrial Fibrillation.
abstract: Background Cryoballoon pulmonary vein isolation depends on balloon-to-ostium contact. We assessed whether computed tomography-derived pulmonary vein ostial area (OA) and ovality index (OI) were associated with cooling after accounting for pulmonary vein (PV) branch and within-patient clustering, and whether PV anatomy was associated with recurrence. Methods We retrospectively studied 120 patients with symptomatic atrial fibrillation undergoing second-generation cryoballoon ablation. Vein-level associations with nadir temperature, 1 min temperature, and time to isolation were assessed using linear mixed-effects models with a patient random intercept and PV branch as a fixed effect; generalized estimating equations served as sensitivity analyses. Given 23 post-blanking recurrences, logistic models were limited to left atrial volume index (LAVI) and one clinically selected covariate, with Firth-penalized regression as a sensitivity analysis. Results All patients achieved acute PV isolation. Larger OA was associated with lower nadir temperature ( β = -0.583°C per 50 mm 2 ; 95% CI, -0.910 to -0.257; p < 0.001) and 1 min temperature ( β = -0.441°C per 50 mm 2 ; 95% CI, -0.764 to -0.118; p = 0.008) after branch and clustering adjustment. OI was not associated with either temperature outcome. Twenty-three patients (19.2%) developed recurrent atrial arrhythmia. LAVI was associated with recurrence (adjusted OR, 1.659 per 10 mL/m 2 ; 95% CI, 1.250-2.201; p < 0.001), whereas persistent AF was not. Conclusions OA showed a modest association with cryoballoon temperatures but should not be used as a stand-alone prognostic marker. LAVI remained associated with recurrence in parsimonious patient-level analyses.

title: Super-Resolution Ultrasound for Lymph Node Evaluation: Diagnostic Value of Static Time-Point Parameters Versus Dynamic Temporal Changes.
abstract: Objectives To evaluate quantitative super-resolution ultrasound (SRUS) parameters (static central-to-peripheral ratios and dynamic temporal changes) for differentiating benign and metastatic lymph nodes, and to compare the performance of corresponding predictive models. Methods A prospective study included 172 pathologically confirmed lymph nodes (100 benign, 72 metastatic). SRUS was performed to derive density and velocity parameters, with central-to-peripheral ratios and temporal changes calculated. Static and dynamic models were constructed using univariate analysis, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO), and logistic regression. Model performance was assessed by cross-validation, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration, decision curve analysis, and clinical impact curve. Results Metastatic lymph nodes showed significantly lower central-to-peripheral ratios of density and velocity parameters but higher relative temporal changes in density SD and velocity SD compared with benign nodes (all P < .05). The static time-point model retained 2 SRUS variables (Mean.Density_C_P_T2, Max.Density_C_P_T3), yielding a full-sample AUC of 0.8607. The temporal change model included 2 dynamic parameters (Velocity SD change from T1 to T2, Mean density change from T2 to T3) and achieved a higher AUC of 0.8715, with better accuracy, specificity, and model fit. Both models showed favorable calibration and clinical net benefit. Conclusion Quantitative SRUS parameters effectively reflect pathological angiogenesis in metastatic lymph nodes. The temporal change model provides superior diagnostic performance over the static time-point model and may serve as a reliable noninvasive tool for distinguishing benign from metastatic lymph nodes.

title: Prenatal Ultrasound in Predicting the Need for Postnatal Surgery in Fetal Non-duodenal Small Bowel Dilation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: The accuracy of prenatal ultrasound in recognizing fetal non-duodenal small bowel dilation (ND-SBD) due to obstructive conditions requiring neonatal surgery is not well established. We assessed the positive predictive value (PPV) of prenatal 2-dimensional (2D) ultrasound measurement of the small bowel diameter for identifying fetuses with ND-SBD who will require postnatal surgical intervention. We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, and Cochrane with terms related to fetal bowel dilation and postnatal outcome. For each included study, we estimated the PPV of prenatal ultrasound in predicting the need for neonatal surgery among live-born, evaluable newborns classified as having a prenatal diagnosis of ND-SBD, and performed a Bayesian random-effects meta-analysis of proportions to estimate the pooled PPV across studies. We identified 10 manuscripts, comprising 390 fetuses with a prenatal diagnosis of ND-SBD, of which 341 from 9 studies had data available for analysis. The observed PPV for postnatal surgery ranged from 8 to 82%, with a pooled estimate of 56% (90% credible interval (CrI) [44%, 67%]). Heterogeneity between studies was elevated, with an I 2 of 84.8% (90% CrI [68.3%, 92.4%]) and a wide 90% posterior predictive interval of 19-89%, indicating substantial variability in the PPV across populations. Most studies presented high or unclear risk of bias and applicability concerns based on QUADAS-2 evaluation. 2D prenatal ultrasound evaluation of the fetal small intestine diameter has a moderate ability in predicting the need for postnatal surgery due to ND-SBD conditions. The substantial between-study heterogeneity and wide posterior predictive interval indicate considerable variation in the predictive value across populations and clinical settings, limiting the interpretation of the pooled PPV alone. Our findings highlight the need for prospective studies to better define the normal development of the fetal small intestine and identify prenatal ultrasound markers predicting non-duodenal small bowel abnormalities.
