title: Multiparametric quantitative MRI in knee osteoarthritis: evidence and requirements for interpretation and reporting.
abstract: Quantitative MRI can characterize cartilage and other joint tissues beyond visible structural damage, but its contribution to individual management of knee osteoarthritis remains uncertain. This narrative review examines the evidence needed to interpret quantitative measurements, combine parameters, and report their uncertainty. An initial PubMed search in June 2026 was supplemented on 14 September 2026 by an updated PubMed search and broader Embase and Web of Science searches. Targeted full-text assessment addressed incremental value, outcome timing, validation, and measurement error. Selected development studies found better discrimination with integrated diffusion and relaxation measurements than with individual parameters, whereas other combined imaging models did not improve on simpler comparators. Longitudinal associations were outcome-specific, and independent external validation was limited. Treatment studies showed inconsistent agreement between imaging changes and symptomatic benefit. We propose a five-step interpretation framework that establishes the clinical question, verifies technical adequacy, assesses morphology and comparable reference data, evaluates measurement uncertainty, and separates observations from clinical inferences. Two hypothetical scenarios illustrate its application. Quantitative MRI currently provides its strongest support as a controlled research measurement. Demonstrated reproducibility, an appropriate comparator, and evidence of added decision value are required before a quantitative finding can justify patient-level diagnostic, prognostic, or treatment-response claims.

title: Calcified foraminal metastasis from ovarian low-grade serous carcinoma mimicking a nerve sheath tumor.
abstract: Ovarian low-grade serous carcinoma (OLGSC) is an uncommon subtype of epithelial ovarian cancer, characterized by an indolent clinical course with potential for late local recurrence and metastatic disease. Musculoskeletal involvement is rare. We report a case of late OLGSC metastasis presenting as a slowly growing, thoracic foraminal mass in a 55-year-old woman, 33 years after initial cancer treatment. Rising CA-125 levels prompted 18 F-FDG PET/CT, which revealed an FDG-avid mass in the left T9-T10 neural foramen (SUVmax 6.6). CT demonstrated foraminal widening and intralesional calcifications, while MRI showed a dumbbell-shaped mass extending into the epidural space and left costovertebral region, with heterogeneous signal intensity and mild diffuse heterogeneous enhancement. Retrospective review of a CT examination performed 12 years earlier revealed a smaller foraminal mass without visible calcifications. Given its location and morphology, the lesion initially suggested a nerve sheath tumor, while the presence of calcifications also raised the possibility of a chondroid lesion. Although nonspecific, calcifications are recognized in primary and metastatic OLGSC. The combination of increased FDG uptake and the patient's oncologic history, raised suspicion of metastatic disease. Image-guided biopsy confirmed metastatic OLGSC with psammoma bodies. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first reported case of OLGSC metastasis presenting as a slowly progressive, calcified paravertebral and foraminal mas mimicking a nerve sheath tumor. This case emphasizes the need for careful evaluation of atypical masses in patients with a history of cancer, even decades after initial treatment, and the importance of biopsy for diagnostic confirmation.

title: Synovial plica syndromes: a comprehensive overview from embryology to pathology.
abstract: Synovial plicae are folds of synovial tissue in the knee, hip, elbow, and shoulder, representing embryonic remnants of synovial septa. They are usually asymptomatic, but trauma, repetitive microtrauma, or prior surgery can render them thickened and fibrotic, producing pain and mechanical symptoms collectively termed plica syndrome. It is easily overlooked or misdiagnosed because the symptoms are nonspecific and other intra-articular disorders often coexist. This review addresses the embryology, histology, anatomy, clinical presentation, imaging, and treatment of synovial plicae across these joints, with emphasis on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) features. MRI is the preferred imaging modality for evaluating suspected plica syndrome, characterizing the fold and associated abnormalities, and excluding alternative causes of joint pain. Pathologic plicae appear thickened and irregular, with increased signal intensity and frequently associated focal synovitis or adjacent chondral damage. Plica thickness alone has limited diagnostic value, as measurements overlap between symptomatic and asymptomatic individuals. Establishing a diagnosis of symptomatic plica syndrome requires correlation of the imaging findings with the clinical presentation. When joint effusion is absent, magnetic resonance (MR) or computed tomography (CT) arthrography improves delineation of the synovial folds and associated lesions. Plica syndrome occurs most often in young, physically active patients, and management is initially conservative. When symptoms are refractory, arthroscopic resection relieves symptoms, particularly when the plica is the only abnormality and the cartilage is preserved. Most outcome data derive from the knee and the elbow.

title: Synthetic CT from biplanar radiographs for patellofemoral anatomical assessment: development and validation of an adapted X2CT-GAN model.
abstract: Objectives Accurate assessment of osseous morphology is essential for the diagnosis and surgical management of patellofemoral instability. Methods capable of providing CT-like anatomical information while reducing radiation exposure are therefore of considerable clinical interest. This study aimed to validate the accuracy of radiography-derived synthetic computed tomography (sCT) generated by a deep learning model for anatomical assessment of patellofemoral instability. Methods A total of 210 paired radiographs and CT scans were retrospectively collected and randomly divided into a training set (n = 170) and a validation set (n = 40). A deep learning model based on the X2CT-GAN framework was used to reconstruct sCT volumes from anteroposterior and lateral radiographs. Two blinded readers independently measured tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance, trochlear sulcus angle, and Caton-Deschamps index on both sCT and real CT images. Reliability, inter-modality agreement, and threshold-based classification agreement were evaluated. Results All intra- and inter-observer reliability values were excellent. Inter-modality agreement was excellent for TT-TG distance and good for trochlear sulcus angle. Agreement for patellar height was good. The mean absolute error for TT-TG distance ranged from 1.24 to 1.38 mm. Agreement for threshold-based classifications ranged from substantial to almost perfect, with high specificity observed across all evaluated cutoff values. Conclusions Radiography-derived sCT demonstrated good agreement with real CT for both quantitative measurements and threshold-based classifications relevant to clinical decision-making in patellofemoral instability. These findings suggest that radiography-derived synthetic CT may represent a promising lower-radiation alternative for anatomical assessment of patellofemoral instability in selected clinical scenarios.

title: CT-fibrosis score: development and internal validation for identifying advanced fibrosis in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease.
abstract: Purpose Advanced fibrosis in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) involves metabolic and anatomic remodeling beyond the liver. We developed and internally validated an interpretable CT-based score integrating abdominal body-composition and organ measurements and compared it with the Fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) index. Methods We retrospectively studied 151 patients with biopsy-confirmed MASLD (86 advanced [F3-F4], 65 early-stage [F0-F2] fibrosis). Deep learning-based segmentation quantified abdominal adipose tissue, skeletal muscle, bone, liver, and spleen measurements. The CT-Fibrosis Score was developed using repeated (50×) stratified 5-fold cross-validation, with imputation, standardization, and feature selection confined to each training fold and inner 5-fold cross-validation for hyperparameter selection. Performance was based on out-of-fold predictions and compared with FIB-4 using the DeLong test. Sensitivity analyses addressed missing data, age dependence, and ascites. Results Four features were consistently selected: age, bone-to-abdominal-cavity volume ratio, visceral adipose tissue (VAT) density, and spleen index. The CT-Fibrosis Score achieved an out-of-fold AUC of 0.77 (95% CI 0.69-0.85). Among 141 patients with an available FIB-4 score, no significant difference was detected between the CT-Fibrosis Score (AUC 0.76) and FIB-4 (AUC 0.79; difference - 0.03, 95% CI - 0.11 to + 0.04; p = 0.37); this comparison was not powered for non-inferiority. Adding the CT-Fibrosis Score to FIB-4 did not improve discrimination (AUC 0.80 vs. 0.79; difference + 0.003, 95% CI - 0.04 to + 0.05; p = 0.90), with the confidence interval excluding an improvement greater than approximately 0.05. Conclusion The CT-Fibrosis Score achieved moderate discrimination for advanced fibrosis but did not improve discrimination when added to FIB-4. External validation in an unselected population undergoing CT for non-hepatic indications is required before any opportunistic application.

title: Multimodality imaging of hepatic cystic echinococcosis: diagnostic approach, differential diagnosis, complications, and post-treatment assessment.
abstract: Cystic echinococcosis (CE), caused by the metacestode of Echinococcus granulosus sensu lato, is a zoonosis that remains endemic across the Middle East, the Mediterranean basin, North Africa and South America, and the liver is the organ most frequently involved. Because serological assays are of limited sensitivity and specificity, imaging carries the diagnostic burden: ultrasonography (US) is the cornerstone for initial diagnosis, staging, treatment planning and longitudinal follow-up; computed tomography (CT) best defines anatomical location, vascular relationships, mural calcification and acute complications such as rupture and superinfection; and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) more faithfully reproduces US-defined staging morphology than CT and provides superior soft-tissue contrast for assessing biliary involvement and separating CE cysts from cystic neoplasms. The aim of this pictorial review is fourfold: to illustrate the US, CT and MRI appearance of each World Health Organization Informal Working Group on Echinococcosis (WHO-IWGE) stage of hepatic CE and to explain how stage assignment translates directly into a stage-specific treatment decision-anti-parasitic treatment, percutaneous treatment, surgery or watch-and-wait; to present, stage by stage, the hepatic lesions that mimic CE and the findings that discriminate them; to depict the wall signs of the CE cyst that become visible with high-frequency linear transducers, including the three-layered wall, adherent brood capsules and hydatid sand; and to review the imaging of complicated CE together with the expected post-treatment appearance, procedure-related complications and the imaging strategy for detecting recurrence.

title: T2-weighted MRI-based radiomics for preoperative prediction of homologous recombination deficiency status in high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma.
abstract: Rationale and objectives The aim of this study was to explore the feasibility of T2-weighted imaging (T2WI) - based radiomics in preoperative prediction of homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) status in patients with high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma (HGSOC), and to establish a non-invasive approach for guiding individualized treatment planning. Materials and methods A total of 133 patients with pathologically confirmed HGSOC who underwent MRI scan (T2WI, T1-contrast enhanced) were retrospectively enrolled in this study. All patients were stratified into HRD-positive and HRD-negative group. These 133 patients (41 in HRD-negative group and 92 in HRD-positive group) were randomly allocated to a training set (n = 93) and a validation set (n = 40) at a 7:3 ratio. Three different models were constructed and evaluated: clinical characteristics only (clinical model); T2WI-radiomics features only (radiomics model); and a combination of them all (combined model). The predictive performance was evaluated using the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, and area under the curves (AUCs) were compared using the DeLong test. Calibration curves and decision curve analysis (DCA) were applied to validate the clinical-radiomic combined model. Results In the training set, the combined model achieved the best performance (AUC = 0.889; all P > 0.05). The radiomics model achieved predictive performance comparable to the clinical model (AUC of 0.762 vs. 0.790; P = 0.676). In the validation set, the combined model performed significantly better than the clinical or radiomics model (AUCs of 0.853 vs. 0.805 vs. 0.706; all P > 0.05). DCA demonstrated that the combined model achieved superior net benefit across a wide range of threshold probabilities compared with the clinical and radiomics models alone. Conclusions Our research demonstrated that the combined model achieved the optimal predictive performance. It is feasible to apply radiomics to predict HRD status of HGSOC patients, which can further assist clinicians in formulating individualized treatment strategies.

title: Percutaneous and endovascular procedures in adrenal disease: indications, technique, and outcomes.
abstract: Adrenal masses are found on roughly 4-5% of abdominal imaging studies, and the proportion rises with age. Most are benign, non-functioning adenomas that need imaging characterization and hormonal screening but no intervention. The remainder, comprising metastases, adrenocortical carcinoma, pheochromocytoma and hormonally active adenomas, raise questions that computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging cannot always settle; in these cases image-guided procedures can help. Percutaneous biopsy is reserved for hormonally inactive lesions whose benignity imaging has not established and whose histology would change management. Adrenal venous sampling remains the reference method for lateralizing aldosterone excess in primary aldosteronism and therefore decides who is offered adrenalectomy, although success depends heavily on operator experience and local protocol. Thermal ablation has produced biochemical and blood-pressure responses in selected aldosterone-producing adenomas and local control of limited metastases, but the evidence is largely nonrandomized and does not establish equivalence with surgery. Transarterial embolization serves three purposes: hemostasis in adrenal hemorrhage, devascularization before resection of hypervascular tumors, and functional treatment of aldosteronism, now supported by one small randomized trial. Each procedure carries hazards peculiar to the gland (catecholamine crisis, adrenal insufficiency after bilateral treatment, non-target embolization) that shape patient selection and periprocedural monitoring. This review covers indications, technique, outcomes and complications for each. Surgery remains the treatment of choice for most operable patients. Interventional radiology is most useful when the indications for sampling, ablation or embolization are recognized early and discussed at the multidisciplinary meeting, not only after surgery has been declined.

title: Automatic generation of training data from dual-energy CT scans: a new approach to train renal vessel segmentation models.
abstract: Objective To investigate the feasibility of automatic training data generation using virtual non-contrast (VNC) images of dual-energy CT and to evaluate the performance of medical segmentation models trained on auto-generated data. Methods Training images were generated from contrast-enhanced CT (CECT) scans using VNC algorithm. Corresponding training labels were generated from iodine-density images via intensity thresholding. The paired VNC images and labels constituted the dataset (791 cases in total) for training non-enhanced CT (NECT) segmentation models. We attempted to train segmentation models with VNC images alone, as well as the combination of VNC and real NECT images. Results Models trained with auto-generated data effectively performed renal vein segmentation on NECT images, achieving Dice score of 69.60%. It identified 100% (70/70) vein main trunks and 54.5% (6/11) accessory veins in the test set. The models' performance on artery segmentation was not satisfactory, with Dice score of 44.56%. It only identified 41.4% (29/70) artery main trunks and 4.54% (1/22) accessory arteries. However, the combination of generated data and labeled data greatly improved model's artery Dice to 71.23%. Combined model identified 100% (70/70) vein main trunks, 98.6% (69/70) artery main trunks, 68.2% (15/22) accessory arteries and 63.6% (7/11) accessory veins. Its accessory artery detection is significantly higher than the model trained with labeled data (15/22 vs. 5/22, p < 0.01), closing the gap with human radiologist (15/22 vs. 18/22, p = 0.250). Conclusion VNC and Iodine-density images can be utilized to automatically generate training data for segmentation models. This pipeline shows promise for training segmentation models on NECT images.

title: Ultrasound-derived fat fraction and shear wave elastography for liver assessment in bariatric surgery candidates: diagnostic performance and longitudinal changes.
abstract: Objectives To evaluate the diagnostic performance of ultrasound-derived fat fraction (UDFF) and auto-point shear wave elastography (Auto-pSWE) in bariatric surgery candidates, identify biological variables independently associated with their values and monitor postoperative changes in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) patients. Methods This prospective study enrolled patients who underwent UDFF and Auto-pSWE examinations within 3 days before bariatric surgery (October 2023-February 2025), with intraoperative biopsy as reference. Diagnostic performance of UDFF and Auto-pSWE (which measured shear wave velocity, SWV) were analyzed by receiver operating characteristic analysis. Multivariable generalized linear models identified variables independently associated with UDFF and SWV. Postoperative follow-ups were conducted at 3 and 6 months in MASLD patients. Results A total of 237 patients (mean age, 29.42 ± 9.37; 98 men) were included. UDFF showed excellent diagnostic performance for steatosis grades (AUCs: 0.991 for ≥S1, 0.911 for ≥S2, and 0.831 for ≥S3), with steatosis percentage as the strongest independent correlate (partial R 2 =0.302). SWV exhibited moderate diagnostic performance for significant fibrosis (AUC = 0.752), with fibrosis stages and alanine aminotransferase showing similar independent explanatory power (partial R 2 =0.067 and 0.063, respectively). In 104 MASLD patients, median UDFF decreased substantially by approximately 80% at 6 months while SWV transiently rose at 3 months before returning to a level comparable to baseline at 6 months. Conclusion UDFF provides accurate assessment of steatosis and shows potential for postoperative monitoring, whereas Auto-pSWE demonstrates moderate performance for significant fibrosis and transient postoperative changes, supporting its complementary rather than standalone role.

title: Association of Capsular Involvement with Delayed Re-intervention After Splenic Artery Embolization for Blunt Splenic Injury.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate whether splenic capsule involvement is associated with delayed re-intervention after splenic artery embolization for blunt splenic injury. Materials and methods This retrospective single-center study included 329 consecutive patients undergoing splenic artery embolization for blunt splenic injury (2017-2025). Capsule involvement was defined as a laceration reaching the splenic surface with capsular disruption or communication with the perisplenic space on contrast-enhanced computed tomography. The primary outcome was delayed re-intervention. Cox and Firth regression were performed, with interobserver agreement assessed by Cohen's kappa. Results Delayed re-intervention occurred in 26 patients (7.9%) at a median of 6 days; all underwent repeat embolization; none required splenectomy. Twenty (76.9%) were detected on routine surveillance computed tomography without preceding deterioration. Capsule involvement was present in 25 of 26 events. Initial computed tomography showed vascular injury elsewhere in 25 of 26 patients, but neither computed tomography nor angiography showed pseudoaneurysm or active bleeding at the eventual lesion site. Re-intervention occurred in 25 of 245 patients with capsule involvement (10.2%) versus 1 of 84 without (1.2%). Capsule involvement was associated with re-intervention (hazard ratio, 6.82; 95% confidence interval, 1.62-28.74; p = 0.009), but significance was lost after reclassifying two events. Sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, and negative predictive value were 96.2%, 27.4%, 10.2%, and 98.8%; pre-consensus agreement was 97.6% (Cohen's kappa = 0.938). Conclusion Capsule involvement was associated with delayed re-intervention, but the estimate was statistically fragile because only one capsule-negative event occurred. Surveillance-driven, single-center findings are exploratory; external validation is required before changes in surveillance practice. Level of evidence Level 3, prognostic study.

title: The tibialis posterior tendon revisited: a classification-based anatomical and radiological framework.
abstract: The tibialis posterior tendon (TPT) demonstrates substantial anatomical variability in its branching and attachment morphology, extending beyond the simplified concept of a predominantly navicular attachment. This narrative review critically reappraises the classification of TPT attachment patterns proposed by Olewnik and places it in the context of subsequent anatomical, radiological, and functional evidence. Later anatomical studies have confirmed extensive variation in the number, distribution, and surface area of TPT attachments and have identified configurations not represented within the original classification. These findings support the use of classification systems as structured descriptive frameworks rather than exhaustive catalogues of TPT morphology. Cadaveric imaging studies demonstrate that complex TPT branching and attachment anatomy can be depicted on MRI; however, individual anatomical types and subtypes have not undergone systematic radiological validation. Representative MRI examples are therefore included for anatomical illustration rather than as diagnostic criteria. The functional significance of individual attachment patterns and their potential relationship to hindfoot and midfoot joint morphology remain incompletely understood. Further anatomical, imaging, and biomechanical studies are required to determine whether specific TPT patterns have reproducible radiological or functional correlates.

title: Milwaukee shoulder syndrome: a neglected and underrecognized basic calcium phosphate crystal arthropathy.
abstract: Milwaukee Shoulder Syndrome (MSS) is a rare but extremely aggressive form of destructive arthropathy, primarily affecting elderly women. Despite its distinct clinical profile, it remains an under-recognized and frequently misdiagnosed entity. This review synthesizes current knowledge on pathogenesis, clinical presentation, and diagnostic nuances of MSS to improve clinical recognition. The condition is defined by the intra-articular deposition of basic calcium phosphate (BCP) crystals, such as hydroxyapatite. These crystals trigger the release of proteolytic enzymes, leading to massive rotator cuff tears, superior migration of the humeral head, and rapid joint destruction. A hallmark of MSS is the "inflammatory paradox": a striking dissociation between severe structural damage and a non-inflammatory or minimally inflammatory synovial fluid profile (typically < 2,000 cells/mm3), which often is hemorrhagic. Diagnosis is challenged by the nanocrystalline nature of BCP crystals, which are non-birefringent and invisible under standard polarized light microscopy, requiring specialized staining (Alizarin Red) or advanced analytics for confirmation. Multimodal imaging is essential, with plain radiography showing advanced degeneration and MRI or CT delineating the extent of soft tissue and bony destruction. Treatment is currently limited to supportive measures, including recurrent joint aspiration, analgesia, and physical therapy. In advanced cases, reverse total shoulder arthroplasty remains the primary surgical intervention for functional restoration. As the aging population grows, increasing clinician awareness of MSS-particularly its unique synovial fluid characteristics-is vital for reducing diagnostic delay and optimizing patient care.

title: Deep learning-based segmentation of the ischemic core and severe hypodensity on noncontrast head CT compared with CT perfusion and diffusion-weighted imaging.
abstract: Objectives To compare the spatial overlap, imaging marker agreement, and outcome associations of acute ischemic regions of interest (ROIs) using deep-learning NCCT (DLNCCT) versus manual NCCT, CTP, and DWI-based segmentations. Materials and methods We trained a deep learning model to segment ischemic ROIs on admission NCCT (DLNCCT). DLNCCT was compared with manual NCCT, CTP (rCBF < 30%/38%), and DWI using the Dice similarity coefficient (mean ± SD), Bland-Altman analysis (mean difference [95% CI]), and concordance correlation coefficient (CCC). For each ROI, we compared NCCT imaging biomarkers: average lesion density (HU); modified net water uptake (mNWU in %); total volume (mL); and hypodense (≤ 26 HU) volume (mL). DLNCCT biomarkers were associated with reversed 90-day ordinal modified Rankin Scale (genOR [95% CI]). Results We used 218/762 train/test cases. Dice was 0.30 ± 0.30 between DLNCCT and manual segmentation, 0.22 ± 0.25 between DLNCCT-DWI, and 0.15 ± 0.22/0.21 ± 0.24 between CTP (rCBF < 30%/< 38%)-DWI. DLNCCT-DWI biomarker agreement was -1 HU (95% CI: -7; 6) for average density (CCC: 0.71), 4.9% (95% CI: -7.0; 16.8) for mNWU (CCC: 0.35), -16 mL (95% CI: -108; 76) for total volume (CCC: 0.57), and -4 mL (95% CI: -31; 23) for hypodense lesion volume (CCC: 0.75). Average lesion density (1.11 [95% CI: 1.06; 1.16]) and hypodense volume (0.85 [95% CI: 0.72; 0.99]) were associated with 90-day mRS. Conclusion Spatial and biomarker agreement between DLNCCT and DWI was suboptimal but comparable to CTP-DWI. Nevertheless, DLNCCT-derived average lesion density and hypodense volume were associated with functional outcomes. Key points Question Deep-learning models segment ischemic tissue on NCCT, but their spatial overlap and accuracy of imaging biomarker assessment relative to DWI and CTP core remain unclear. Findings Deep-learning NCCT segmentation showed good agreement with DWI in measuring hypodense (≤ 26 HU) volumes (- 4 mL [95% CI: -31; 23]; CCC 0.75). Clinical relevance Despite limited spatial overlap, NCCT-derived deep learning biomarkers showed agreement comparable to DWI, with improved performance in patients with poor ASPECTS and collateral scores. Hypodense volume and average lesion density were associated with functional outcome.

title: ESR Essentials: MRI of the scrotum-practice recommendations by the European Society of Urogenital Radiology.
abstract: While conventional ultrasonography (US) remains the first-line imaging modality for scrotal pathology, multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (mpMRI) has emerged as a valuable problem-solving tool for indeterminate US findings. Owing to its superior soft-tissue contrast, functional imaging capabilities, and operator independence, mpMRI allows for the precise localization and characterization of scrotal lesions. This paper from the European Society of Urogenital Radiology Scrotal and Penile Imaging Working Group provides a comprehensive, evidence-based overview of scrotal mpMRI for a general radiologist. It details optimized imaging protocols, recommending a standard sequence of T1-weighted, T2-weighted, diffusion-weighted, and subtracted dynamic contrast-enhanced imaging. The article highlights key clinical indications, including the characterization of intratesticular and paratesticular masses, local staging of testicular germ cell tumors, and differentiation between germ cell and sex cord-stromal neoplasms. This paper familiarizes radiologists with normal MRI appearances and MRI findings of common scrotal diseases. Evidence-based recommendations for reporting basic MRI examinations of the scrotum are also provided. The potential of advanced techniques, such as diffusion tensor imaging and proton MR spectroscopy, and the future integration of artificial intelligence and radiomics, are also discussed. We hope the implementation of these recommendations into radiological practice will enhance diagnostic confidence and promote standardized practice in scrotal MRI for radiologists. KEY POINTS: While conventional ultrasound is the first-line modality for scrotal pathology, it can yield inconclusive findings regarding complex mass characterization and local tumor staging. Multiparametric MRI combines anatomical and functional data to accurately characterize scrotal masses, localize impalpable, undescended testes, and provide precise local tumor staging. Scrotal multiparametric MRI serves as a valuable problem-solving tool that enhances diagnostic confidence in sonographically indeterminate cases, prevents unnecessary radical orchiectomies, supports testis-sparing surgery or active surveillance, and standardizes radiological reporting templates to optimize personalized patient management.

title: Reducing operator-dependent variability in liver shear wave elastography through an AI-guided region-of-interest placement pipeline.
abstract: Objectives To develop and evaluate an artificial intelligence (AI) pipeline that automates optimal circular region-of-interest (ROI) placement and the surrounding elastogram box, provides probe-angle/contact guidance, and measures skin-to-capsule distance (SCD) to standardize liver SWE acquisition, aiming to reduce operator-dependent variability. Materials and methods A two-stage pipeline combined SimCLR self-supervised pretraining on 17,441 unlabeled ultrasound images, followed by ENet fine-tuning using 495 annotated images for liver segmentation and 1564 images for poor probe contact detection. Segmentation outputs were combined with constraints on valid liver tissue pixels, axial depth, lateral boundaries, and regions of poor acoustic coupling to generate masks for optimal ROI placement. A distance transformation algorithm then identified optimal ROI coordinates within these masks. An inter-observer reader study assessed AI performance by comparing automated ROI placement, SCD measurements, and probe-angle correction guidance with annotations from expert attending radiologists. Results 18,182 US images from 654 liver elastography examinations in 609 patients (mean age, 52.6 ± 12.95 years; 55.4% male) were acquired from three ultrasound systems. The AI pipeline achieved liver segmentation performance with a Dice coefficient of 0.89, sensitivity of 0.95, specificity of 0.93, and an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.94. The reader study demonstrated significantly higher AI-to-attending radiologist agreement (93.8%) compared to inter-attending agreement for ROI placement (81%). Cohen's kappa agreement between two attending radiologists was 0.25. Conclusion The proposed AI-driven pipeline significantly improved ROI placement consistency and reproducibility, highlighting its potential to enhance clinical reliability in liver fibrosis assessment. Key points Question Operator-dependent variability in region-of-interest (ROI) placement compromises measurement reproducibility in B-mode shear wave elastography. We developed an AI pipeline to place an optimal ROI. Findings The AI pipeline achieved liver segmentation performance of Dice 0.89 (AUC 0.94) and demonstrated higher AI-to-attending agreement (93.8%) than inter-attending agreement (81%) for ROI placement. Clinical relevance By standardizing ROI placement, elastogram box selection, and probe angle/contact guidance, the AI pipeline reduces operator-dependent variability in liver SWE acquisition, supporting more reproducible liver stiffness measurements that could improve fibrosis staging reliability.

title: An integrated MRI-pathology model for predicting response to TACE combined with targeted therapy and immunotherapy in hepatocellular carcinoma.
abstract: Objectives The efficacy of transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) plus targeted therapy and immunotherapy in unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is limited by variable responses. We aimed to develop and validate an integrated magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-pathology model for response prediction and survival stratification (IMPRESS), which combines pretreatment MRI habitat radiomics and paired biopsy whole-slide images (WSIs) pathomics. Materials and methods This multicenter, retrospective study enrolled patients with unresectable HCC receiving TACE plus targeted therapy and immunotherapy from January 2019 to December 2024. Eligibility required pretreatment MRI and paired biopsy WSIs within 1 month before therapy, Child-Pugh class A/B, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status ≤ 1, and at least one measurable intrahepatic lesion ≥ 1 cm. Patients with missing or poor-quality MRI or WSIs, prior locoregional or systemic HCC therapy, second malignancy, ECOG ≥ 2, or incomplete data were excluded. Habitat MRI radiomics, WSI pathomics, and clinical features were integrated into IMPRESS. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the curve (AUC) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Single-cell analysis was performed to explore the biological basis of the IMPRESS predictions. Results Among 231 patients, 94 (40.7%) achieved a treatment response. IMPRESS achieved AUCs of 0.957 (95% CI: 0.931-1.0), 0.878 (95% CI: 0.789-0.966), and 0.875 (95% CI: 0.782-0.966) in the training, validation, and test cohorts, respectively. Predicted responders and non-responders showed significantly different overall survival in all cohorts (all p < 0.001). Single-cell RNA sequencing revealed distinct immune and proliferative patterns consistent with model predictions. Conclusion IMPRESS model may provide a promising tool for pretreatment response prediction and survival risk stratification in unresectable HCC undergoing TACE-based combination therapy. Key points Question Reliable pretreatment tools are needed to identify unresectable HCC patients likely to benefit from TACE plus targeted therapy and immunotherapy. Findings An integrated MRI-pathology model combining habitat radiomics and deep-learning pathomics predicted treatment response, with validation and testing areas under the curve of 0.878 and 0.875. Clinical relevance The integrated model may support pretreatment response stratification for TACE-based triple therapy and help inform surveillance intensity or alternative treatment considerations, pending prospective validation.

title: A fractal-integrated CT score predicts high-risk pathology and early recurrence in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.
abstract: Objective To develop and validate a noninvasive CT-based imaging score incorporating fractal analysis to predict high-risk pathological features in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) and to assess its prognostic value for early recurrence. Materials and methods This retrospective bicenter study included 514 patients with pathologically confirmed PDAC who underwent curative resection, divided into training (n = 219), internal validation (n = 94), external validation (n = 100) and outcome datasets (n = 101). The fractal dimension (FD) and lacunarity were extracted from portal venous-phase CT images via box-counting algorithms. Imaging predictors of high-risk pathological features, including high tumor grade, lymphovascular invasion (LVI) and perineural invasion (PNI), were identified by logistic regression and integrated into a comprehensive weighted imaging score. Cox regression analyses were performed to assess its prognostic value for early recurrence. Results Patients with high-risk pathological features exhibited greater FD and lacunarity. The final score included six imaging features: necrosis, peripancreatic fat infiltration, venous involvement, regional lymphadenopathy, FD and lacunarity. For any high-risk pathology, the fractal-integrated score achieved AUC of 0.94, 0.88 and 0.84 in the training, internal validation and external validation datasets, respectively. For high pathological burden, the AUCs were 0.92, 0.80, and 0.77. In the outcome dataset, the score was an independent predictor of early recurrence (HR = 2.71; p = 0.004) and improved prognostic discrimination when combined with pathologic predictors. Conclusion This CT-based score, integrating fractal biomarkers, enables accurate, noninvasive preoperative prediction of aggressive pathological features in PDAC and provides incremental value for early recurrence risk stratification. Key points Question Can the fractal-based imaging features be used to predict high-risk pathological features and guide risk stratification for early recurrence in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC)? Findings This CT-based score integrating fractal analysis predicted high-risk pathological features and was independent predictors of early recurrence and provided incremental prognostic value beyond pathologic factors. Clinical relevance This CT-based imaging score may help identify patients at high-risk of aggressive pathology before surgery and may further complement postoperative pathological risk stratification for early recurrence.

title: Virtual liver biopsy for detecting steatohepatitis in chemotherapy-treated patients: comparison with whole-liver radiomics and external validation.
abstract: Objectives Chemotherapy-associated steatohepatitis (CASH) increases the risk of postoperative liver failure and mortality in patients undergoing liver surgery. However, non-invasive diagnosis remains an unmet need. Radiomics has potential for characterizing liver parenchyma. This study evaluated the performance of a virtual liver biopsy for CASH prediction, comparing it with whole-liver radiomic analysis. Materials and methods Two retrospective series of patients undergoing hepatectomy for colorectal liver metastases were analyzed: the public "Colorectal-Liver-Metastases" dataset (training and internal validation) and a monocenter series from Humanitas Research Hospital (external validation). Inclusion criteria were preoperative chemotherapy (≥ 2 months) and post-chemotherapy CT (thickness ≤ 5 mm). IBSI-compliant radiomic features were extracted from whole-liver parenchyma and from a virtual biopsy (manually segmented 2-mL cylinder of non-tumoral liver parenchyma). Estimated liver volume (eLV) was computed using three orthogonal diameters. Four XGBoost models were developed (70/30 split, 5-fold cross-validation): clinical; clinical + VB-radiomics (ViB); clinical + VB-radiomics + eLV (ViBE+); clinical + whole-liver radiomics (WholeLiver). Results One hundred eighty patients were included: 105 internal (63 males, mean age 58.9 years, 38% CASH+) and 75 external (44 males, mean age 62.4 years, 19% CASH+). WholeLiver and ViBE+ models achieved excellent and comparable performance in internal validation (WholeLiver: AUC = 0.857 (95% BS-CI: 0.676-0.954), accuracy = 0.774 (95% BS-CI: 0.613-0.903); ViBE + : AUC = 0.831 (95% BS-CI: 0.549-0.956), accuracy = 0.839 (95% BS-CI: 0.710-0.935); p = 0.814), outperforming ViB model (AUC = 0.724 (95% BS-CI: 0.483-0.896), accuracy = 0.774 (95% BS-CI: 0.613-0.903)). SHAP analysis confirmed liver volume metrics as key predictors. In external validation, the ViBE+ model achieved AUC = 0.745 (95% BS-CI: 0.604-0.886) and accuracy = 0.680 (95% BS-CI: 0.562-0.783). Conclusion Virtual biopsy provides a reproducible, non-invasive radiomic sampling strategy for CASH prediction. Combined with liver volume metrics, it achieves performance comparable to whole-liver analysis, supporting its potential clinical application. Key points Question Despite its association with postoperative morbidity, the non-invasive preoperative assessment of CASH remains challenging in patients undergoing liver surgery. Findings Radiomic analysis based on a virtual liver biopsy, combined with volumetric measurements, showed excellent performance in predicting CASH, comparable to whole-liver analysis, with liver volume emerging as a key predictor. Critical Relevance Statement A standardized virtual biopsy-based radiomic analysis represents a promising non-invasive approach for evaluating liver parenchymal injury, as demonstrated in preoperative assessment of CASH and identification of high-risk surgical patients.

title: TotalSpineSeg: automated whole-spine vertebral segmentation with high robustness to labeling errors.
abstract: Objectives To develop TotalSpineSeg, a robust tool for vertebrae and intervertebral disc instance segmentation, along with spinal cord and spinal canal segmentation, capable of processing any 3D medical image regardless of contrast, resolution, or field of view, while overcoming fusion and fragmentation errors common in standard segmentation. Materials and methods A two-stage cascaded deep learning model was trained on 1404 MRIs. To explicitly prevent errors where adjacent vertebrae merge or a single vertebra splits, the architecture employs a novel "odd/even" representation. The second stage is conditioned on an odd-intervertebral disc mask from the first stage to assign distinct semantic classes to alternating vertebrae, enforcing accurate separation between neighboring vertebrae. Finally, a landmark-based logic uses key anatomical points (C2-C3, C7-T1, T12-L1, and L5-S) to anchor sequential labeling, while a localizer-based strategy ensures accurate identification even in truncated, short field-of-view scans. Results Evaluation across diverse contrasts and pathologies yielded a vertebral identification rate of 96.22% on localizer MRI and generalized to CT scans with a 92.87% identification rate. For intervertebral disc instance labeling, where vertebral separation is not mandatory, both model stages attained 99% labeling accuracy with a mean positional L2 error of 1.55 mm, surpassing existing state-of-the-art methods. Conclusion TotalSpineSeg successfully generalizes to diverse 3D medical images, overcoming variations in contrast, resolution, and field of view. The proposed topological constraints effectively eliminate vertebral fusion and fragmentation errors, delivering a state-of-the-art identification rate for both vertebrae and intervertebral discs across MRI and CT modalities. Key points Question Can a topology-constrained framework overcome heterogeneous contrasts and resolution limits, including localizers, to ensure robust, automated vertebral and disc labeling? Findings TotalSpineSeg achieved a high identification rate across diverse contrasts, localizers, and CT, surpassing state-of-the-art methods by eliminating fusion and fragmentation errors. Clinical relevance TotalSpineSeg enables fully automated biomarker extraction from clinical scans, allowing precise assessment of stenosis, lesions, and atrophy against normative ranges.

title: CT-derived fractional flow reserve for anatomically long-segment coronary disease: a multicentre diagnostic accuracy study.
abstract: Objectives To evaluate the diagnostic performance of CT-derived fractional flow reserve (CT-FFR) for detecting haemodynamically significant coronary disease in patients with anatomically long-segment lesions. Materials and methods This retrospective multicentre study included patients who underwent coronary CT angiography and invasive pressure-wire FFR within 30 days. Anatomically long-segment disease was defined as lesion length ≥ 20 mm. Invasive FFR ≤ 0.80 was the reference standard. CT-FFR was assessed at vessel and patient levels, with patient-level CT-FFR defined as the minimum value per patient and patient-level disease as any invasive FFR ≤ 0.80. Diagnostic discrimination, threshold-based classification, and Bland-Altman agreement were evaluated. Results The diagnostic cohort included 329 patients and 377 vessels; 137 patients and 144 vessels had anatomically long-segment disease. At the vessel level, CT-FFR achieved an AUC of 0.941 (95% CI: 0.917-0.966), sensitivity of 94.3%, specificity of 83.7%, and accuracy of 88.6%. In anatomically long-segment vessels, the AUC was 0.961 (95% CI: 0.922-1.000), with sensitivity of 95.7%, specificity of 92.2%, and accuracy of 94.4%. At the patient level, the overall AUC was 0.941 (95% CI: 0.915-0.967) and 0.971 (95% CI: 0.934-1.000) in anatomically long-segment disease. Mean bias was small, although limits of agreement were clinically relevant. Conclusion CT-FFR showed high diagnostic discrimination for invasive FFR-defined ischaemia, including in anatomically long-segment disease. However, agreement limits and threshold-zone uncertainty support its use as a non-invasive physiological adjunct rather than a direct substitute for invasive pressure-wire assessment. Key points Question Does machine learning-based CT-FFR maintain diagnostic performance for invasive FFR-defined ischaemia in anatomically long-segment coronary lesions? Findings CT-derived FFR showed high diagnostic discrimination overall and maintained performance in anatomically long-segment disease, although subgroup comparisons remained exploratory. Clinical relevance CT-derived FFR may provide non-invasive physiological information in anatomically long-segment coronary disease before invasive angiography, while values near the 0.80 threshold require cautious interpretation.

title: Evaluating strategies to optimize breast MRI screening: a modeling study of abbreviated protocols, dockable tables, and staffing scenarios.
abstract: Objective MRI is increasingly recommended for breast cancer screening, particularly in women with dense breast tissue. However, widespread adoption is constrained by limited capacity and high costs. This study evaluated how optimized MRI screening workflows could address these barriers through three targeted interventions: an abbreviated scan protocol, dockable MRI tables, and expanded technician staffing. Materials and methods A calculation model was developed to compare seven workflow strategies against the current standard care. Strategies included reducing MRI acquisition time from 13 to 6 min, introducing dockable tables with breast coils, adding a third technician, and combinations thereof. Workflow durations and cost inputs were derived from published literature, hospital data, and expert opinion. Primary outcomes were daily screening capacity, cost per screening, annual screening costs, and staffing requirements for a screening volume of 5500 screening examinations per year. Results After evaluating several optimized workflow strategies, we found that reducing MRI acquisition time increased daily screening capacity from 30 to 47 scans, with associated annual savings of €147,505 (8.4%) and a reduction of 1320 technician hours. Combined strategies integrating reduced scan time, additional technicians, and dockable tables increased the daily capacity from 30 to 67 scans and reduced annual costs by up to €160,557 (9.2%) compared with the current workflow. Conclusions Optimizing MRI breast cancer screening workflows with abbreviated scan protocols and dockable tables can substantially increase screening capacity, reduce costs, and technician workload. This would expand access to MRI screening, without requiring additional scanners, potentially providing a solution for (future) capacity problems. Key points Question Which workflow optimization strategies, including abbreviated scan protocols, dockable tables, and additional technicians, offer the greatest capacity and cost benefits for MRI breast cancer screening? Findings Abbreviated scan protocols provide the largest cost savings, while combined workflow changes can substantially increase capacity and still reduce costs. Clinical relevance Optimizing MRI breast cancer screening workflows with abbreviated scans and dockable tables can increase screening capacity and reduce costs and technician workload. This expands access to MRI screening, without requiring additional scanners, potentially providing a solution for capacity problems.

title: AI for reducing claims and compensation payments from missed fractures on radiographs.
abstract: Objectives To evaluate the potential of BoneView, an artificial intelligence (AI) tool for fracture detection on radiographs in claims cases related to missed fractures that resulted in financial compensation. Materials and methods This retrospective, multicenter study included all patients who submitted a claim and received financial compensation for missed fractures on radiographs between January 2013 and December 2019 across the 38 university hospitals of the Greater Paris area (AP-HP-France). For each claimant, 5 control patients were selected from a contemporary single-center cohort of patients who underwent radiographs of the same anatomical regions (with or without fracture) performed in the emergency department of a university hospital, irrespective of fracture status. Three radiologists (musculoskeletal fellow, 5-year fellowship-trained radiologist, and > 20-year expert) independently performed blinded, unassisted, and AI-assisted interpretations following a 3-month washout. Sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy were calculated with and without AI and for standalone AI. Compensation amounts were used to estimate potentially avoidable payouts. Results 156 patients (mean age, 42.2 years; 113 (72.4%) males), including 26 claimants with missed fractures on radiographs and 130 controls, were evaluated. 27/130 (20.8%) of the control cohort had fractures. Standalone AI sensitivity was 80.8% (21/26; 95% CI [60.7-93.5]) for claimants and 96.3% (26/27; 95% CI [81.0-99.9]) for the control cohort (p = 0.10). AI assistance did not significantly improve sensitivity, with expert reader sensitivity increasing from 81.1% to 92.5% (p = 0.10). Total compensation was €282,850 (€10,878 per case). AI-assisted detection could have potentially mitigated €265,314, representing a 93.8% theoretical reduction in institutional financial liability. Conclusion AI-assisted fracture detection identified most missed fractures on radiographs leading to compensation and may help reduce medicolegal risk and compensation-related financial burden. Key points Question Can AI-assisted fracture detection identify fractures missed by radiologists on radiographs that led to compensated medicolegal claims and institutional financial liability? Findings Standalone AI detected 21/26 (80.8%) of missed fractures in patients with compensated claims, corresponding to €265,314/€282,850 (93.8%) of total compensation in this cohort. Clinical relevance AI-assisted fracture detection can potentially increase radiologists' diagnostic accuracy and reduce medicolegal risk and compensation-related financial burden. Implementing AI tools in emergency settings may significantly mitigate patient harm and institutional costs associated with missed fractures.

title: Evolving role of cryoablation and cryoneurolysis for interventional pain management.
abstract: Despite advances in pain management, pain remains a major global health challenge in both oncological and non-oncological patients. Long-term pharmacological treatment is often restricted by insufficient therapeutic benefit and adverse events, highlighting the need for alternative approaches such as image-guided pain therapies. The idea of treating pain with cold has been recognized for centuries, and today cryotherapy has emerged as a valuable minimally invasive option for pain management. Cryoablation refers to the destruction of tissue with extreme cold and has an increasing role, especially in the treatment of benign (e.g., osteoid osteoma), malignant bone (i.e., metastases), and soft tissue tumors, either with a curative or palliative intent. Cryoneurolysis is a related but distinct application, focusing either on peripheral nerve modulation or nerve destruction. Cryoneurolysis may be highly effective for the treatment of acute or chronic pain, including sympathetic neurolysis in cancer and non-cancer-related pain syndromes. The general approach in patients with tumor-related pain depends on whether the lesion itself can be ablated or not. In non-oncologic patients, cryoneurolysis of the responsible nerve is typically performed following a positive response to a diagnostic nerve block. Potential indications for cryotherapy are constantly evolving; however, evidence, especially for cryoneurolysis, is still limited and based mostly on single-center case series and retrospective studies. Standardized ablation protocols are lacking, and for the duration of cycles, most experts rely on imaging visualization and validated protocols. Equally important, successful integration of cryoablation and cryoneurolysis into daily practice requires structured workflows across different patient pathways and interdisciplinary management. KEY POINTS: Question Pain management remains a major global health challenge and an unmet need in oncological and non-oncological patients. Findings Cryotherapy, in terms of cryoablation and cryoneurolysis, is increasingly incorporated in multimodal curative and palliative pain care concepts, for treatment of acute and chronic pain syndromes. Clinical relevance Advancement and validation of standardized treatment protocols are needed to strengthen evidence and further enhance clinical implementation in interventional radiology practice and interdisciplinary patient care.

title: Systolic pressure gradient across myocardial bridge mediates the effect of bridge depth on clinical symptoms.
abstract: Objective The relationship between myocardial bridging (MB) morphology and function and the pathways to clinical symptoms remained unclear. This study investigated the association between delta coronary computed tomographic angiography-derived fractional flow reserve (ΔCT-FFR) and angina-equivalent symptoms in left anterior descending MB without coronary atherosclerosis using photon-counting detector CT (PCD-CT). Materials and methods This retrospective cohort included 180 patients with deep MB (depth > 2 mm) and no plaques. All underwent PCD-CT angiography. CT-FFR was computed by machine learning; systolic (ΔCT-FFRsys) and diastolic (ΔCT-FFRdia) trans-bridge pressure gradients were derived. MB depth and length were measured. Associations with symptoms were assessed by logistic regression and mediation analysis. Results Symptomatic patients (n = 81) had greater depth (median 3.30 mm vs. 2.45 mm), longer length (mean 36.06 mm vs. 26.10 mm), higher ΔCT-FFRsys (3.81% vs. 1.62%) and ΔCT-FFRdia (3.45% vs. 2.15%) than asymptomatic patients (n = 99) (all p < 0.001). Multivariable analysis identified depth (OR = 1.77, 95% CI: 1.27-2.46, p = 0.001) and ΔCT-FFRsys (OR = 1.16, 95% CI: 1.05-1.27, p = 0.002) as independent predictors. Mediation analysis indicated that ΔCT-FFRsys significantly mediated the effect of depth on symptoms (indirect effect = 0.1881, 95% CI: 0.1023-0.2897). Conclusions MB depth and ΔCT-FFRsys were independent risk factors for symptoms, and ΔCT-FFRsys appeared to mediate the morphological-clinical symptoms link. These findings suggested that integrated assessment, particularly ΔCT-FFRsys, might be a new non-invasive imaging biomarker for clinically identify symptomatic MB and understand its potential pathogenic mechanisms. Key points Question The precise relationship between myocardial bridging morphological and functional features and clinical symptoms, and whether underlying key mediating factors exist, remains currently incompletely determined. Findings Depth, length, and systolic trans-bridge pressure gradient of myocardial bridging independently predicted symptoms, with the gradient significantly mediating the relationship between morphology and clinical presentation. Clinical relevance Noninvasive assessment of depth and systolic trans-bridge pressure gradient can assist in identifying patients with symptomatic myocardial bridging, serving as potential imaging biomarkers and providing insights into the underlying pathophysiology of symptom presentation.

title: Too good to be true? AI performance in CT-based urinary stone detection and classification: EAU endourology systematic review and diagnostic accuracy meta-analysis.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate pooled performance of artificial intelligence (AI) in computed tomography (CT)-based urinary stone detection and classification and identify methodological factors influencing results. Methods This review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261319940). A systematic search of PubMed, Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar was conducted up to March 15, 2026. Studies evaluating AI-based detection or classification of urolithiasis on CT with available validation/test cohort data (sensitivity/specificity or 2 × 2 tables) were included. A bivariate random-effects model generated pooled sensitivity, specificity, and hierarchical summary receiver operating characteristic (HSROC) curves. Meta-regression explored moderators related to dataset composition and AI pipelines. Risk of bias was assessed using QUADAS-AI. Results 14 studies (five detection-based, nine classification-based) were included. Overall pooled sensitivity and specificity were 0.967 and 0.979 (AUC 0.987). Classification studies demonstrated higher pooled sensitivity (0.977) and specificity (0.990) compared with detection studies (0.935 and 0.919; AUC 0.945). Significant heterogeneity was observed and influenced by training sample size, class imbalance, presence of bladder stones or other pathologies, and architectural choices. Most studies had high risk of bias, lacked external validation, and frequently used slice-level or pre-selected datasets, potentially overestimating performance. Conclusion Substantial methodological heterogeneity and high risk of bias limit clinical generalizability. Detection studies better reflect real-world workflows and show lower performance. Current evidence does not support routine clinical implementation without standardized reporting and robust external validation.

title: Feasibility of reducing Angiofil<sup>®</sup> concentration in multiphase postmortem CT angiography and implications for iodine consumption and environmental sustainability : an observational study.
abstract: Background Postmortem CT angiography (PMCTA) is widely used in forensic medicine to evaluate the vascular system before autopsy. The contrast mixture of 3,500 ml paraffin and 210 ml Angiofil ® , originally proposed by Grabherr et al. for multiphase postmortem CT angiography (MPMCTA) approach, provides reliable global vascular opacification. Recent advances in CT detector technology, image reconstruction techniques, and growing environmental concerns have encouraged the investigation of alternative contrast-agent dilutions aimed to reduce iodine consumption. The aim of this observational study was to explore whether lower Angiofil ® concentrations could be used while preserving adequate vascular visualization and diagnostic image quality. Methods Thirty cases were evaluated using four progressively diluted Angiofil ® -paraffin mixtures containing 200 ml, 180 ml, 150 ml, and 120 ml of Angiofil ® in 3,500 ml of paraffin. Contrast enhancement was quantified by measuring Hounsfield units (HU) within regions of interest (ROIs) placed in the ascending thoracic aorta and compared with a clinical case. Image quality was independently assessed by an experienced forensic radiologist based on opacification of the ascending thoracic aorta. In addition, a dedicated evaluation of coronary artery lumen and wall visualization was performed. Results The mixture containing 200 ml of Angiofil ® showed no relevant improvement in image quality compared with the original dilution. A mixture containing 180 ml of Angiofil ® allowed excellent vascular assessment in individuals with a BMI > 35 kg/m², whereas 150 ml of Angiofil ® provided optimal image quality in individuals with a BMI ≤ 35 kg/m². The 120 ml mixture remained diagnostically acceptable in most cases but produced photon-starvation artifacts in individuals with high muscle mass or a BMI > 33 kg/m², limiting vascular assessment. Conclusion Adjusting the Angiofil ® -paraffin mixture according to body morphology using 180 ml of Angiofil ® for individuals with a BMI > 35 kg/m² and 150 ml for those with a BMI ≤ 35 kg/m² maintains excellent vascular visualization while substantially reducing iodine consumption. This optimization supports more environmentally sustainable PMCTA practice without compromising diagnostic image quality.

Background

Postmortem CT angiography (PMCTA) is widely used in forensic medicine to evaluate the vascular system before autopsy. The contrast mixture of 3,500 ml paraffin and 210 ml Angiofil®, originally proposed by Grabherr et al. for multiphase postmortem CT angiography (MPMCTA) approach, provides reliable global vascular opacification. Recent advances in CT detector technology, image reconstruction techniques, and growing environmental concerns have encouraged the investigation of alternative contrast-agent dilutions aimed to reduce iodine consumption. The aim of this observational study was to explore whether lower Angiofil® concentrations could be used while preserving adequate vascular visualization and diagnostic image quality.

Methods

Thirty cases were evaluated using four progressively diluted Angiofil®-paraffin mixtures containing 200 ml, 180 ml, 150 ml, and 120 ml of Angiofil® in 3,500 ml of paraffin. Contrast enhancement was quantified by measuring Hounsfield units (HU) within regions of interest (ROIs) placed in the ascending thoracic aorta and compared with a clinical case. Image quality was independently assessed by an experienced forensic radiologist based on opacification of the ascending thoracic aorta. In addition, a dedicated evaluation of coronary artery lumen and wall visualization was performed.

Results

The mixture containing 200 ml of Angiofil® showed no relevant improvement in image quality compared with the original dilution. A mixture containing 180 ml of Angiofil® allowed excellent vascular assessment in individuals with a BMI > 35 kg/m², whereas 150 ml of Angiofil® provided optimal image quality in individuals with a BMI ≤ 35 kg/m². The 120 ml mixture remained diagnostically acceptable in most cases but produced photon-starvation artifacts in individuals with high muscle mass or a BMI > 33 kg/m², limiting vascular assessment.

Conclusion

Adjusting the Angiofil®-paraffin mixture according to body morphology using 180 ml of Angiofil® for individuals with a BMI > 35 kg/m² and 150 ml for those with a BMI ≤ 35 kg/m² maintains excellent vascular visualization while substantially reducing iodine consumption. This optimization supports more environmentally sustainable PMCTA practice without compromising diagnostic image quality.

title: In vivo assessment of brain microstructure in patients with Huntington's disease using quantitative MRI.
abstract: Objectives Using multiparametric mapping (MPM), we assessed the integrity of cortical and subcortical regions across different stages of Huntington's disease (HD), relating the derived findings to genetic modifiers and clinical measures. Methods Sixteen premanifest patients with HD (PwHD pre ), ten manifesting PwHD (PwHD man ), and forty-two healthy controls (HC) underwent clinical examinations and a 3 T imaging. We derived quantitative MPM maps to perform voxel-based quantification (VBQ) and voxel-based morphometry (VBM). We assessed group differences by combining PwHD pre and PwHD man (PwHD total ) and by comparing PwHD pre and PwHD man with age- and sex-matched HC. Using correlation analysis, we investigated the link between MPM-derived findings, CAG repeat length, and clinical scores. Results PwHD man presented with reductions in all four quantitative MPM maps across the bilateral caudate nucleus and the frontal, parietal, temporal, and occipital gyri. We observed spatial overlap between VBQ- and VBM-derived findings, demonstrating widespread volume loss in PwHD man . PwHD pre showed reductions in certain quantitative maps within the frontal and temporal regions. Reduced MPM values correlated with clinical scores of HD severity. Interpretation The observed reductions across four MPM modalities in PwHD man are consistent with demyelination and neuronal loss, as supported by widespread volume loss. The reductions observed in PwHD pre indicate early demyelination and inflammation. In this study, we demonstrated the utility and clinical relevance of MPM for detecting microstructural alterations across different stages of HD. MPM can serve as a non-invasive biomarker of neurodegeneration in HD, providing insight into the pathological events underlying the observed neuronal loss.

title: Coronary artery calcification is not associated with survival in advanced gastric and gastroesophageal junction cancer: a secondary analysis of the EXPAND trial.
abstract: Purpose Computed tomography (CT) is the clinical standard for staging of gastrointestinal cancer. Previous studies have highlighted the prognostic significance of coronary artery calcification (CAC) detected by CT in various types of cancer. However, the prognostic role of CAC scoring in gastrointestinal cancers is still unclear. The aim of this study was to investigate the impact of CT-defined CAC on overall survival (OS) in patients with advanced gastric or gastroesophageal junction cancer. Methods CAC was semiquantitatively measured using the visual Weston method on baseline CT scans in 785 patients with unresectable locally advanced or metastatic gastric or gastroesophageal junction cancer from the phase III EXPAND trial. This present study is a secondary analysis of the base line CT images. In the original analysis patients were randomly assigned to first-line treatment with cisplatin/capecitabin ± cetuximab. The primary endpoint of the current subanalysis is the OS. For statistical analysis group differences were calculated using the Mann-Whitney-U test and ANOVA test. Kaplan-Meier curves and multivariable Cox regression analysis were used to test the effect of CAC on mortality. Results The median CAC score was 1 (IQR 0; 3). A total of 337 patients (42.9%) had no visible CAC (CAC score 0). Male patients had statistically significant higher CAC score compared to female patients (median 1 versus 0, p < 0.0001). In univariable Cox regression CAC showed no significant association with survival when analysed as a continuous value (HR: 0.99, 95% CI: 0.96-1.02, p = 0.74), and when dichotomized for absence and presence of calcification (HR:1.08, 95% CI: 0.92-1.26, p = 0.34). Similar results were identified in further subgroup analyses. Conclusion CT-defined CAC scoring has no relevant prognostic impact in advanced gastric and gastroesophageal junction cancer undergoing first-line chemotherapy. The present study cannot confirm the promising results for CAC scoring in lung cancer patients.

title: Preoperative endoscopic ultrasound (EUS) strain elastography for the prediction of intraoperative pancreatic texture after pancreaticoduodenectomy: a prospective diagnostic accuracy study with exploratory analysis of clinically relevant postoperative pancreatic fistula.
abstract: Background Postoperative pancreatic fistula (POPF) is the most serious complication of pancreaticoduodenectomy (PD); established risk tools require intraoperative variables. We assessed the diagnostic accuracy of preoperative endoscopic ultrasound (EUS) strain elastography for intraoperative pancreatic texture and, exploratorily, predictors of clinically relevant POPF (CR-POPF). Methods Prospective single-centre study of 100 consecutive patients undergoing elective PD. The index test was preoperative EUS strain ratio (SR), threshold ≤ 2.5 prespecified before enrolment; the reference standard was intraoperative texture recorded independently by two blinded surgeons, with neck-margin fibrosis grade as secondary reference. CR-POPF (ISGPS 2016 Grade B/C) was adjudicated blind to EUS. Accuracy is reported with Wilson 95% confidence intervals (CIs). An exploratory index used Firth-penalised regression restricted to preoperative variables, with bootstrap validation. Reporting follows STARD, TRIPOD, and STROBE. Results Soft texture occurred in 58 (58%). SR ≤ 2.5 gave 51 true positives, 7 false positives, 7 false negatives, 35 true negatives: sensitivity 87.9% (95% CI 77.1-94.0), specificity 83.3% (69.4-91.7), predictive values 87.9 and 83.3%, accuracy 86.0% (77.9-91.5), and area under the curve (AUC) 0.91 (0.84-0.96). SR rose monotonically with fibrosis grade (2.0 ± 0.6 to 5.8 ± 1.9; Spearman ρ = +0.82, p < 0.001); mean histogram elasticity fell (ρ = - 0.79, p < 0.001). CR-POPF occurred in 16 (16%). Non-PDAC pathology was unassociated with CR-POPF (9/48 vs 7/52; odds ratio 1.48, 0.51-4.35; p = 0.59). Six preoperative variables were entered simultaneously (EUS-SR, duct diameter, albumin, haemoglobin, body mass index, serum amylase; amylase carried zero points in the rounded score). Apparent AUC was 0.87 (0.79-0.94), optimism-corrected 0.78, calibration slope 0.72, and Brier score 0.096. Conclusions Preoperative EUS strain elastography at a prespecified threshold identified intraoperative pancreatic texture accurately and tracked histological fibrosis, supporting it as an objective surrogate for parenchymal consistency. The index rests on 16 events, is hypothesis-generating, and requires external multicentre validation.

title: Opportunistic PSA testing is not the safe alternative : Why Austria's non-policy on prostate cancer screening maximizes harm and forfeits the benefits.
abstract: Austria has never implemented an organized prostate cancer screening program, yet opportunistic PSA testing has been widespread for more than three decades. This has produced the harms of screening without the safeguards of a program: testing outside appropriate age and life-expectancy windows, repeated testing of low-risk men, unnecessary biopsy, overdiagnosis and overtreatment, while generating little systematic information on quality or outcomes. Randomized evidence shows that organized, repeated screening can reduce prostate cancer mortality substantially, whereas opportunistic testing delivers less benefit with more overdiagnosis. Contemporary risk-adapted pathways further improve the balance of benefit and harm: defined start and stop ages, PSA-based risk stratification, MRI before biopsy, targeted biopsy, and active surveillance can reduce unnecessary biopsies and detection or treatment of indolent disease without compromising detection of clinically significant cancer. Europe has therefore moved toward organized, PSA-based screening with MRI as a follow-up test. Austria is now participating in PRAISE-U Plus and has initiated a national multidisciplinary consensus process involving 65 experts from 22 organizations. The policy question is no longer whether Austrian men are being screened-they are-but whether screening remains unstructured or becomes organized, quality-assured and equitable. The evidence supports the latter: invite the right men, stratify risk, biopsy selectively, treat only clinically relevant disease, and measure outcomes systematically.

title: Feasibility of a lumbar CT-to-MRI image translation framework using a conditional CycleGANs for fracture stage determination in osteoporotic compression fractures.
abstract: Purpose Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provides a reliable indicator of fracture stage. However, MRI scans can be expensive, time-consuming, and not readily accessible to all patients. With recent advances in artificial intelligence, translating lumbar CT images into MRI images has become feasible using cycle generative adversarial network (CycleGANs) based approaches. The aim of this study was to evaluate the feasibility of a model that translates lumbar CT images into MRI images (T1-weighted contrast-enhanced sequences) to predict the stage of osteoporotic compression fracture (OCFs) using conditional CycleGANs. Methods A total of 652 patients diagnosed with OCFs who underwent both CT and MRI within 2 weeks were retrospectively collected. Of these, 552 patients were used for training, and an independent set of 100 patients was reserved for testing. CT and MRI volumes were aligned using segmentation-based rigid registration. The proposed framework consisted of two stages: generation of vertebra-specific acute fracture maps from CT images using a 3D ResNet-based model, followed by CT-to-MRI image translation using a 3D conditional CycleGANs with acute stage conditioning. Performance was evaluated using vertebra-level classification metrics, image similarity metrics, and qualitative assessment by five experienced readers, including three spine neurosurgeons, one orthopedic spine specialist, and one radiologist. Results Fractures were most common at the thoracolumbar junction. A total of 800 vertebral bodies were analyzed. Of 678 non-acute OCFs, 667 were correctly classified and 11 were misclassified as acute; of 122 acute OCFs, 106 were correctly identified and 16 were misclassified as non-acute. Acute fracture classification achieved a precision of 0.906, recall of 0.869, and F1-score of 0.887. Synthetic MRI images showed modest quantitative agreement with real MRI (Normalized MAE 0.094 ± 0.024; PSNR 18.7 ± 1.7 dB; SSIM 0.38 ± 0.04). Qualitative evaluation demonstrated high similarity in vertebral body morphology at the fracture level, with mean similarity scores of 87.2% for the conditional CycleGAN and 85.3% for the conventional CycleGAN. Conclusions This study demonstrates the feasibility of a lumbar CT-to-MRI image translation framework using a conditional CycleGAN for determining fracture stage.

Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provides a reliable indicator of fracture stage. However, MRI scans can be expensive, time-consuming, and not readily accessible to all patients. With recent advances in artificial intelligence, translating lumbar CT images into MRI images has become feasible using cycle generative adversarial network (CycleGANs) based approaches. The aim of this study was to evaluate the feasibility of a model that translates lumbar CT images into MRI images (T1-weighted contrast-enhanced sequences) to predict the stage of osteoporotic compression fracture (OCFs) using conditional CycleGANs.

Methods

A total of 652 patients diagnosed with OCFs who underwent both CT and MRI within 2 weeks were retrospectively collected. Of these, 552 patients were used for training, and an independent set of 100 patients was reserved for testing. CT and MRI volumes were aligned using segmentation-based rigid registration. The proposed framework consisted of two stages: generation of vertebra-specific acute fracture maps from CT images using a 3D ResNet-based model, followed by CT-to-MRI image translation using a 3D conditional CycleGANs with acute stage conditioning. Performance was evaluated using vertebra-level classification metrics, image similarity metrics, and qualitative assessment by five experienced readers, including three spine neurosurgeons, one orthopedic spine specialist, and one radiologist.

Results

Fractures were most common at the thoracolumbar junction. A total of 800 vertebral bodies were analyzed. Of 678 non-acute OCFs, 667 were correctly classified and 11 were misclassified as acute; of 122 acute OCFs, 106 were correctly identified and 16 were misclassified as non-acute. Acute fracture classification achieved a precision of 0.906, recall of 0.869, and F1-score of 0.887. Synthetic MRI images showed modest quantitative agreement with real MRI (Normalized MAE 0.094 ± 0.024; PSNR 18.7 ± 1.7 dB; SSIM 0.38 ± 0.04). Qualitative evaluation demonstrated high similarity in vertebral body morphology at the fracture level, with mean similarity scores of 87.2% for the conditional CycleGAN and 85.3% for the conventional CycleGAN.

Conclusions

This study demonstrates the feasibility of a lumbar CT-to-MRI image translation framework using a conditional CycleGAN for determining fracture stage.
