title: RadStructAgent: agentic structuring of free-text chest X-ray reports with small language models.
abstract: Purpose Variability in chest X-ray (CXR) reporting hinders training and evaluation of vision-language models (VLMs) for radiology report generation. Our previous study showed that Structured Radiology Report Generation (SRRG)-style supervision improves VLM-based CXR reporting over free-text supervision. Here, we examine this finding in a larger multi-institutional setting and address a key preprocessing challenge: reliable free-text-to-structured-report conversion using open-source small language models (SLMs). Methods We evaluate Qwen2.5-VL-3B using free-text and SRRG-style structured supervision across 10 institutions covering 97K samples. We then propose RadStructAgent, an agentic framework that converts free-text CXR reports into structured reports using SLMs, combining LLM-based orchestration, judge feedback, and feedback-guided revision. RadStructAgent is evaluated on 1,000 free-text CXR reports using Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B. Results For the report generation task, structured supervision improves Qwen2.5-VL-3B over free-text supervision, increasing GREEN from 0.494 to 0.539, with similar gains across other clinical metrics. For the structuring task, RadStructAgent improves both clinical quality (GREEN) and anatomy-level assignment (RadFAA): for Qwen3-4B, from 0.844 to 0.867 and 0.883 to 0.891; for Qwen3-8B, from 0.863 to 0.881 and 0.889 to 0.902. Conclusion Structured supervision remains effective for VLM-based CXR report generation when evaluated in a larger multi-institutional setting. RadStructAgent shows that open-source SLMs can be strengthened through agentic verification and refinement, providing a resource-efficient approach for offline and privacy-preserving structured report preparation. Our code, prompt templates, and configuration files are publicly available at: https://github.com/badhon1512/RadStructAgent .

title: Integration of weight-bearing computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging for advanced musculoskeletal statistical shape modeling of the foot and ankle.
abstract: Purpose Statistical shape models (SSMs) from three-dimensional (3D) medical imaging describe morphology variation in normal and pathologic anatomy. Within the foot and ankle, weight-bearing computed tomography (WBCT) is used to characterize skeletal deformity but poorly visualizes soft tissue. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provides improved evaluation of soft tissue structures but less accurate bone visualization. This methodologic analysis describes and tests reliability of a novel process to generate SSMs from coregistered MRI and WBCT structures. This method is illustrated via two example models: a combined musculoskeletal model and a distal tibia growth plate model. Methods Bilateral WBCTs and T1-weighted DIXON MRIs of the lower legs were collected from 14 individuals aged 8 to 18 with no prior lower limb surgery in a control group and hereditary neuropathy group. Bones were segmented from WBCT and manually aligned in MRI space. Alignment reliability was evaluated with intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs). Six muscles were segmented semi-automatically and the distal tibia growth plate was manually segmented from MRI. Following cropping, size normalization, and alignment multi-domain SSMs were generated. SSMs were evaluated qualitatively through comparison with expected anatomy and quantitively by calculation of compactness, generalization, and specificity. Results The alignment method demonstrated excellent reliability with an intrarater ICC of 1 and interrater ICC of 0.999. The musculoskeletal model demonstrated expected atrophy in neuromuscular disease and the preliminary growth plate model showed variation in metaphyseal thickness. Both models demonstrated compactness, specificity, and generalization comparable to published SSMs, requiring 11 and 12 modes to account for 95% of population variance. Conclusion This method allows for application of shape modeling to novel questions in musculoskeletal morphology through simultaneous modeling of bone and soft tissue anatomy. Limitations include manual registration and MRI resolution. This analysis presented examples of muscle and growth plate models, but has broader applications in musculoskeletal analysis.

title: Projection restoration with dual-domain Swin refinement for sparse-view CT reconstruction.
abstract: Purpose We investigated whether projection restoration before reconstruction, followed by image-domain refinement, improves sparse-view computed tomography (CT) quality under aggressive undersampling. Methods A compact dual-domain Swin framework restores sparse sinograms before geometry-aware differentiable filtered back projection (FBP) and refines the resulting images. The projection branch uses gated Swin processing and angular upsampling with a bicubic bypass. Abdominal AAPM sinograms contained 2304 full views, retaining 576, 288, and 144 views at 4x, 8x, and 16x. Comparators were FBP, bilinear and bicubic interpolation, ProCT, and geometry-adapted DuDoTrans; ablations used ten epochs. Results DuDoSwin achieved PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS of 45.64 dB/0.981/0.011 at 4x, 44.11 dB/0.975/0.020 at 8x, and 42.02 dB/0.963/0.035 at 16x. Mean PSNR and SSIM exceeded ProCT and DuDoTrans; DuDoTrans had lower LPIPS at 4x and 8x. DuDoSwin used 1.36-1.80 million parameters but was slower than both learned comparators. Comparisons against interpolation and DuDoTrans were significant in Holm-corrected paired tests. Bypass removal improved ablation PSNR by 0.35 dB at 8x. Evaluation included the validation patient; exclusion changed mean PSNR by at most 0.1 dB and altered no ranking. Slice-wise tests ignore within-patient dependence. Conclusion Explicit projection restoration followed by image-domain refinement yielded favorable PSNR and SSIM, with perceptual metric and computational trade-offs. Neither residual shortcut improved the 8x ablation results. Independent patient evaluation remains necessary.

title: A Cohort Study of Lung Cancer Screening and Size at Diagnosis 2017-2023: Trends Among US Veterans.
abstract: Background Lung cancer, the leading cause of cancer death in the USA, is an important indicator to track effects of the COVID-19 pandemic on cancer diagnosis trends. Objective Evaluate pandemic impact on lung cancer screening, diagnosis, and cancer size at diagnosis. Design Cohort study (January 2017-June 2023). Participants Veterans who were users of Veterans Affairs (VA) healthcare system, and subgroup of Veterans eligible for lung cancer screening. Exposures Pandemic (March 2020-June 2023) versus pre-pandemic period (January 2017-February 2020). Main measures Among lung cancer screening eligible Veterans: expected screening rates compared to observed rates and cancer size at diagnosis. Among users of VA: cancer size at diagnosis, lung cancer diagnosis rates, CT scan utilization. Key results Among 1,867,387 screen eligible Veterans, annual screening fell from 7.3% in January 2020 to 5.7%, recovering to pre-pandemic rates by March 2022, ending at 11% (June 2023). Among screen eligible but non-participating Veterans, median cancer size decreased from 20 mm (95% CI 19, 20) to 18 mm (95% CI 16, 19) after pandemic onset. Among screening participants, cancer size was smaller (15 mm) and did not change with pandemic. Among VA users regardless of screening eligibility, lung cancer diagnosis rates were lower than expected based on pre-pandemic data. Conclusions The pandemic was associated with a prolonged disruption in lung cancer screening; recovery exceeded 2 years and screening remains low. The pandemic may have caused forward displacement of mortality: rates of lung cancer diagnosis decreased among older adults and median size at diagnosis got smaller among some groups. Clinical trial number Not applicable.

title: Coexistent tracheal bronchus and azygos lobe: surgical planning and operative technique for robotic-assisted right upper lobectomy.
abstract: Tracheal bronchus and azygos lobe are individually uncommon congenital anomalies arising from independent embryological mechanisms. Their simultaneous occurrence is exceptionally rare, with fewer than five cases identifiable in the published literature. We report an adult patient in whom a displaced apical segmental bronchus arising directly from the tracheal wall, a bifid right upper lobe bronchus comprising only the anterior and posterior segmental bronchi, and an associated azygos lobe. Elective robotic-assisted right upper lobectomy was undertaken for a biopsy proven primary lung cancer. Final histopathology confirmed grade 2 adenocarcinoma with clear surgical margins without lymph node involvement. Preoperative three-dimensional reconstruction was helpful for surgical planning and we describe the operative principles required to safely manage this unusual anatomical combination.

title: Advancements in Artificial Intelligence for Enhanced Diagnosis and Prognosis in Cardiac CT: a Comprehensive Review and Future Perspectives.
abstract: Purpose of review Cardiovascular disease, with coronary artery disease (CAD) as its main culprit, remains a leading cause of death worldwide. Traditional diagnostic methods that focus on the degree of arterial narrowing (percent diameter stenosis, or %DS) can miss early signs of disease or the specific plaque features that indicate high risk. The purpose of this review is to examine how artificial intelligence (AI) can enhance the diagnostic and prognostic capabilities of cardiac computed tomography (CCT), and to address where AI can most meaningfully improve diagnostic accuracy, workflow efficiency, and patient care. Recent findings AI is transforming cardiac CT across the entire imaging pathway. By applying AI algorithms, recent studies have refined the assessment of coronary artery calcium (CAC), improved plaque characterization, and detected subtle lesions that might evade traditional detection methods. AI further enables non-invasive assessment of ischemia (reduced blood flow), aids in the evaluation of myocardial infarction, analyzes adipose tissue surrounding the heart, improves image quality, and provides valuable prognostic insights for risk stratification. This comprehensive review explores the transformative potential of AI in cardiac CT, highlighting its role in accurate diagnosis, precise risk stratification, and personalized management of cardiovascular disease. Through collaboration between AI technology and clinical expertise, we envision a future where cardiac CT imaging is more powerful, efficient, and patient-centered, ultimately leading to improved outcomes in cardiovascular medicine. Continued standardization, external validation, and clinician education will be essential to realize this impact in routine practice.

title: From Radical Resection to Organ Preservation in Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer: A Narrative Review of Risk-Adapted Management.
abstract: Purpose To synthesise evidence informing risk-adapted treatment and organ preservation in locally advanced rectal cancer. Methods This narrative review used targeted English-language searches of PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library through 31 March 2026, supplemented by targeted source verification in September 2026. Results Magnetic resonance imaging, mismatch repair status, recurrence risk, and patient preferences inform treatment selection. Total neoadjuvant therapy is established for higher-risk mismatch repair-proficient/microsatellite-stable disease. Chemoradiation followed by consolidation chemotherapy can improve organ-preservation probability compared with induction sequencing, without a demonstrated disease-free survival advantage. Selected lower-risk surgical candidates may receive chemotherapy with selective chemoradiation. Both short-course radiotherapy and long-course chemoradiation remain evidence-based options; the long-term locoregional failure signal in RAPIDO cannot be attributed to fractionation alone. Watch-and-wait requires multimodal confirmation of clinical complete response, intensive surveillance, and access to salvage surgery; oncological equivalence to immediate resection is unproven. Prospective dostarlimab data support non-operative management in selected mismatch repair-deficient rectal cancers, while long-term durability requires further evaluation. Conclusion Management should integrate tumour anatomy, biology, treatment response, and patient priorities. Organ preservation requires careful selection and structured follow-up, with treatment intensity individualised rather than applied uniformly.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Gallbladder Carcinoma: A Review of Research Studies and Clinical Evidence.
abstract: Background Gallbladder carcinoma (GBC) is the most common biliary tract malignancy and is usually diagnosed at an advanced stage. Artificial intelligence (AI), including radiomics, machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL), is increasingly applied to its diagnosis, surgical management and prognostication, but how far the reported performance can be trusted is unclear. Methods PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library and Google Scholar were searched to 5 May 2026 using database-specific search strategies. Each primary prediction-model study was characterized separately by design, number of centers and validation type (internal, temporal or external). Results Of 31 primary AI studies in GBC, 29 were retrospective, 22 were single-center and 24 reported internal validation only. In independent test or external cohorts, DL and ML models discriminated benign from malignant gallbladder lesions with areas under the curve (AUCs) of approximately 0.80-0.89; a multicenter model distinguishing xanthogranulomatous cholecystitis from GBC achieved an external AUC of 0.88, and automated computed tomography (CT) segmentation an external Dice score of 0.76. The best recurrence model achieved an AUC of 0.76 on internal (random-split) validation; none of the reviewed prognostic models reported a quantified external-validation estimate. Intraoperative AI is technically feasible but has no outcome data, and federated learning has been tested only in simulation. Conclusion AI could plausibly assist several steps of GBC care, but the evidence is dominated by retrospective, single-center, internally validated studies from Asia, and metrics from different studies are not directly comparable. Prospective multicenter external validation, shared annotated datasets and standardized reporting are required before clinical adoption.

title: Postoperative ctDNA in Resectable Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma: From Molecular Residual Disease Detection Toward Risk-Adapted Adjuvant Therapy and Surveillance.
abstract: Background Postoperative circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) is emerging as a marker of molecular residual disease (MRD) after curative-intent treatment for esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). This review evaluates its ability to refine recurrence-risk assessment beyond pathological response and its potential role in guiding adjuvant therapy and surveillance. Methods A structured narrative review of studies evaluating perioperative and postoperative ctDNA in resectable ESCC was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE through August 17, 2026, supplemented by citation tracking and clinical trial registry searches. Evidence was synthesized across treatment pathways, assay platforms, and postoperative management settings. Results Across ESCC cohorts using digital PCR, fixed next-generation sequencing panels, and personalized tumor-informed assays, postoperative ctDNA positivity consistently identifies patients at increased risk of recurrence, although estimates remain imprecise in small cohorts. Serial testing can detect molecular relapse months before radiographic recurrence. Integrated pathology-MRD models demonstrate additional risk stratification within both pathological complete response and non-completeresponse groups. Observational findings suggest, but do not establish, that MRD-positive patients may derive greater benefit from adjuvant immunotherapy. Conversely, MRD negativity alone does not justify omission of indicated adjuvant treatment. Conclusions Postoperative ctDNA provides complementary molecular risk information beyond conventional pathology in resectable ESCC. However, prospective MRD-guided trials are required before postoperative treatment or surveillance strategies can be routinely modified on the basis of ctDNA results alone.

title: Deciphering intratumoral heterogeneity: An interpretable radiopathologic framework for lymph node staging in early-stage cervical cancer.
abstract: Preoperative assessment of lymph node metastasis (LNM) informs treatment planning in early-stage cervical cancer (CC). Traditional radiomics (TR) may obscure intratumoral heterogeneity. We developed multiparametric MRI habitat radiomics (HR) for LNM prediction and explored its histopathologic context. Patients underwent radical surgery and lymphadenectomy. Part I comprised 148 training and 63 test patients; Part II comprised 14 for spatially matched histopathology. Intratumoral voxels were clustered into habitats by K-means using T2-weighted imaging (T2WI), diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI), and contrast-enhanced T1-weighted imaging (CE-T1WI) signals. The number of habitats was selected using validation AUC. HR/TR scores and clinical-radiological predictors were integrated by logistic regression. AUC and accuracy were compared by DeLong's and χ² tests. Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) assessed contributions. Subregion-matched histopathology quantified Ki-67, CD3, CD31, and tumor-stroma ratio (TSR). LNM prevalence was 27.1% (61/225). The four-habitat HR model achieved a test AUC of 0.841 with 14 DWI/CE-T1WI-derived features. Test AUCs for clinical model (CL), TR, and HR + CL were 0.804, 0.784, and 0.890. HR + TR+CL achieved the highest AUC (0.902) and accuracy (87.30%), without a significant AUC difference from HR + CL (P = 0.277). SHAP ranked HR score above clinical lymph-node status, tumor diameter, and TR score. HR-3 exhibited highest Ki67 and lowest TSR, CD3, and CD31; HR-1 had highest TSR and lowest Ki67; HR-2 showed higher CD31 than HR-4. MRI-based HR may support preoperative LNM assessment in early-stage CC, with HR + CL representing a parsimonious candidate model for further evaluation. Spatially matched exploratory histopathology suggests possible regional tissue differences across MRI-defined habitats.

title: Proteomic and Metabolomic Profiling in Moyamoya Disease: A Systematic Review.
abstract: Moyamoya disease (MMD) is a progressive cerebrovascular disorder characterized by stenosis and occlusion of the internal carotid artery branches, leading to chronic ischemia and aberrant collateral vessel formation. Despite its clinical significance, the pathophysiology is not fully understood, and identification of MMD-related biomarkers may supplement invasive digital subtraction angiography, the current gold standard for diagnosis, as well as provide additional insights into prognosis and disease progression. High-throughput metabolomics and proteomics offer potential to elucidate disease mechanisms and identify diagnostic markers. Our goal is to systematically review the current literature on metabolomics and proteomics in MMD using high-throughput methods, identify candidate biomarkers, characterize implicated pathways, and assess the diagnostic and prognostic value of molecular signatures. We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus databases through April 13, 2026, for studies analyzing serum or CSF from MMD patients using mass spectrometry, nuclear magnetic resonance, or immunoassays. Studies were included if they employed case-control, cohort, cross-sectional, or RCT designs in human subjects. Two reviewers independently screened titles, abstracts, and full texts, with disputes resolved by a third reviewer. Quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. We extracted the top differentially expressed proteins or metabolites, results of any enrichment pathway analyses, and demographics information from each study. From 3071 studies identified, 31 were included after removing 1558 duplicates and excluding 1482 irrelevant studies. Recurrent differentially expressed proteins implicated inflammatory signaling (CRABP-I, PDGF-BB, IL-7, complement proteins), angiogenesis (VEGF, Ang-2, MMP-9), and cytoskeletal remodeling (FLNA, ZYX, keratins), while consistent metabolomic signatures highlighted BCAA elevation, urea cycle disruption, and lipid remodeling. Pathway analyses recurrently implicated immune activation, endothelial dysfunction, cytoskeletal reorganization, hypoxia signaling, and metabolic reprogramming. Demographically, cohorts were predominantly adult, East Asian, and bilateral MMD, with a sample-size-weighted mean age of 40.0 years. High-throughput proteomics and metabolomics identified recurring molecular alterations in Moyamoya disease, commonly identifying inflammatory signaling, pathological angiogenesis, and cytoskeletal remodeling as potential pathophysiological mechanisms. Despite predominantly good-quality studies (mean Newcastle-Ottawa Scale 6.77 ± 0.67), major limitations included small sample sizes, single-center designs, and regional specificity. Validation in larger, ethnically diverse, multicenter cohorts is essential before clinical translation of candidate biomarkers and therapeutic targets.

title: Prognostic value of integrated dynamic NLR and [<sup>18</sup>F]FDG-PET/CT parameters in resectable non-small cell lung cancer treated with neoadjuvant immunotherapy plus chemotherapy.
abstract: Objective This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic value of dynamic [ 18 F]FDG PET/CT metabolic parameters and the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), individually and in combination, in patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) receiving neoadjuvant immunotherapy plus chemotherapy. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 168 NSCLC patients treated with neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy followed by surgery. Pre- and post-treatment PET metabolic parameters assessed by iPERCIST and peripheral blood NLR were collected. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis and Kaplan-Meier survival analysis with Cox regression were performed to identify predictors of disease-free survival (DFS). Results During a median follow-up of 25.2 months (95% CI, 21.0-29.3 months), 59 patients experienced recurrence. Post-treatment PET metabolic parameters, their changes, and post-treatment NLR were significantly associated with DFS. Among these parameters, ΔSUVmax and post-treatment NLR were identified as independent prognostic factors. Patients were stratified into three risk groups according to the combination of ΔSUVmax and post-treatment NLR, with significantly different DFS outcomes among groups (p = 0.001). Patients achieving iCMR/iPMR according to iPERCIST criteria showed longer DFS than those without favorable metabolic response (p = 0.005) . Conclusions Dynamic PET metabolic parameters, and post-treatment NLR hold significant prognostic value following neoadjuvant immunotherapy plus chemotherapy in NSCLC. A combined model integrating PET metabolic parameters and post-treatment NLR stratified patients into distinct risk groups, suggesting potential utility in postoperative risk assessment.

title: Metabolomic Analysis of Patients with Coronary Artery Disease and Acute Myocardial Infarction by Using Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy.
abstract: This cross-sectional exploratory study investigates the potential of metabolomics to differentiate between stable coronary artery disease (CAD) and acute myocardial infarction (AMI) through Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) spectroscopic analysis. The study identifies distinct metabolic profiles for each condition, revealing significant variations in metabolite levels, particularly lactic acid, which is a key metabolic product of anaerobic glycolysis, emerges as a prominent marker in AMI patients, reflecting acute ischemic stress and providing insight into adverse outcomes associated with high lactate levels. Another metabolite found in the present study was hypoxanthine, which is key biomarker for myocardial ischemia. These findings underscore the potential of metabolomics in combination with pathway analysis in distinguishing between CAD and AMI and highlight the metabolic dysregulation that occurs in these diseases. Our results suggest that these metabolites could serve as potential biomarkers, paving the way for personalized prognostic and diagnostic strategies. Further large-scale studies are necessary to validate these findings and incorporate them into clinical practice.

title: Predicting neoadjuvant chemotherapy efficacy in triple-negative breast cancer using DCE-MRI and mammographic texture.
abstract: Objective This study aimed to develop and validate a predictive model integrating dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI) kinetic features and digital breast tomosynthesis (DBT) texture features for predicting pathological complete response (pCR) following neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) in patients with triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). Additionally, its predictive performance was compared with that of single-modality models. Materials and methods A total of 360 patients with pathologically confirmed TNBC who received NAC between January 2022 and December 2025 were retrospectively and consecutively collected. Patients were randomly allocated to a training set (n = 252) and a validation set (n = 108) at a 7:3 ratio. Pre-NAC DCE-MRI kinetic and DBT texture features were extracted. After feature selection using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, DCE-MRI and DBT radiomics scores (Rad-scores) were constructed. A nomogram prediction model was then developed using multivariable logistic regression incorporating clinicopathological and laboratory indicators. Model discrimination, calibration, and clinical net benefit were evaluated using the receiver operating characteristic curves, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis, respectively. These results were subsequently compared with those of a clinical-only model and single-modality combined models. Results The pCR rates in the training and validation sets were 41.67% and 40.74%, respectively. Multivariable logistic regression identified Ki-67 proliferation index, maximum tumor diameter, background parenchymal enhancement score, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, lactate dehydrogenase level, DCE-Rad score, and DBT-Rad score as independent predictors of pCR (P < 0.05). The dual-modality nomogram achieved area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.784 (95% CI: 0.718-0.851) in the training set and 0.759 (95% CI: 0.644-0.873) in the validation set, outperforming the clinical-only model (0.727), the clinical plus DCE-Rad score model (0.761), and the clinical plus DBT-Rad score model (0.766). Calibration curves showed good agreement between predicted probabilities and actual outcomes. Furthermore, decision curve analysis confirmed the clinical net benefit of the proposed model. Conclusions The multimodal radiomics fusion model based on DCE-MRI kinetic and DBT texture features effectively predicts pCR following NAC in TNBC patients. Its predictive performance is superior to that of single-modality models. Consequently, this model offers a non-invasive imaging tool for individualized pretreatment efficacy assessment. Nevertheless, further multicenter external validation is required to confirm its generalizability. For now, it should be viewed as a decision‑support aid that informs rather than dictates treatment choices, with specific actionable thresholds to be refined in future prospective studies.

title: Nonlinear association between age and volumetric breast density in Japanese women.
abstract: Background Volumetric breast density (VBD) is influenced by age, body mass index (BMI), and reproductive factors, yet the shape of the age-VBD association and age-specific VBD distributions in Japanese women remain incompletely characterized. We examined the associations of age, BMI, menopausal status, and parity with software-derived VBD and characterized age-specific VBD distributions, including the proportion of women with VBD ≥ 7.5%. Methods This cross-sectional study included 719 asymptomatic Japanese women undergoing screening mammography (mean age, 58.7 ± 12.6 years; range, 20-87 years) in whom no breast lesion was identified. VBD was quantified using Volpara Density. Age was modeled using restricted cubic splines, adjusted for BMI, menopausal status, and parity. Regression analyses used 672 complete cases. Mean VBD ≥ 7.5% defined volumetrically dense breasts. Results Overall, 72.7% (523/719) had VBD ≥ 7.5%. title: Towards Reliable Measurement of Cerebellar Morphology: A Comparative Assessment of Segmentation Pipelines.
abstract: Characterizing cerebellar morphology is fundamental for accurately mapping its structure and function across individuals, yet remains challenging due to its densely foliated architecture. Although multiple automated segmentation pipelines exist, the measurement reproducibility of these tools has not been comprehensively benchmarked. We conducted a systematic assessment of reliability for cerebellar morphology estimates using four commonly used pipelines: one classic parcellation method (CERES), two deep-learning methods (ACAPULCO, DeepCERES), and one voxel-based morphometry toolbox (SUIT). Leveraging the HNU dataset, which provides MRI scans for ten timepoints per individual over a month, we evaluated the test-retest reliability for each of the four pipelines using ReX, an integrative tool for quantifying and optimizing measurement reliability and individual differences. We quantified intra- and inter-individual variability, as well as the Intraclass Correlation Coefficient (ICC), for each pipeline at both global and region-of-interest levels. We used two pools of data: a common dataset of 12 subjects x 5 sessions to benchmark all the pipelines, and method-specific datasets including pools of subjects with 5 valid sessions for each pipeline to assess the generalizability of our findings. Overall, all pipelines yielded highly reliable segmentation volumes (ICC > 0.87). DeepCERES demonstrated the most consistent performance across all metrics and subject pools, while SUIT achieved the highest ICC on the common dataset but showed decreased reliability when evaluated on a larger subject pool. Importantly, our analysis highlighted substantial heterogeneity in reliability across lobules for each method. Lobule X consistently showed reduced reliability whereas lobules I-V, VI, Crus I, IX, and VIIIB were reliably estimated across all pipelines. While all pipelines demonstrated strong reliability, DeepCERES showed the most robust and consistent performance overall. Substantial lobule-specific variability and method-dependent failure rates underscore the need for reliability-aware pipeline selection to optimize cerebellar morphology estimation in research.

title: Type Vb double common bile duct complicated by gallbladder cancer.
abstract: Double common bile duct (DCBD) is an extremely rare biliary anomaly with subtype-dependent oncological risk. We report a case of DCBD (Choi classification type Vb) complicated by gallbladder cancer. A 75-year-old woman was incidentally found to have a gallbladder fundus tumor on screening ultrasonography. Preoperative imaging suggested gallbladder cancer within clinical T3 or less. Biliary evaluation by magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography (MRCP), drip infusion cholangiography-computed tomography (DIC-CT), and endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) confirmed Choi type Vb DCBD without pancreaticobiliary maljunction (PBM). The patient underwent open extended cholecystectomy with a stepwise intraoperative strategy guided by frozen section analysis. Frozen section confirmed adenocarcinoma; as the cystic duct margin was tumor-free, lymph node dissection was limited to the cystic duct nodes without hepatoduodenal ligament dissection. Final pathology: adenocarcinoma (well to moderately differentiated), pT1b, pN0 (0/3), pStage IB (Union for International Cancer Control [UICC] 9th edition), pR0. The patient was discharged on postoperative day 11 and remained recurrence-free at 6 months. To our knowledge, this is the fourth reported type Vb DCBD case in the English-language literature and the first associated with gallbladder cancer. Preoperative evaluation of biliary anatomy, including PBM status, and a stepwise intraoperative approach are essential for safe and oncologically appropriate management.

title: A prospective study of acoustic voice analysis and 24-h pH-metry for detecting gastroesophageal reflux disease in idiopathic hoarseness.
abstract: Background and aim Gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) is a known contributor to chronic hoarseness. This study aimed at determining the prevalence of GERD in patients with idiopathic hoarseness using endoscopy and 24-h impedance pH monitoring and to assessing associated acoustic voice parameters. Methods In this prospective study, 242 patients with hoarseness were screened, of which 40 (n = 40) with idiopathic hoarseness were selected for detailed evaluation. All underwent video laryngoscopy, acoustic voice analysis, esophagogastroduodenoscopy, esophageal manometry and 24-h impedance pH-metry. GERD diagnosis was based on findings such as LA grade B/C/D esophagitis, Barrett's esophagus, peptic strictures or abnormal acid exposure time and DeMeester scores. Acoustic parameters including jitter, shimmer and noise-to-harmonics ratio (NHR) were analyzed. Results Among 40 participants selected for evaluation, GERD was diagnosed in 25 (62.5%). Univariate binary logistic regression revealed significant associations between a confirmed GERD diagnosis and clinical severity markers, including the presence of erosive esophagitis (p = 0.02) and elevated reflux symptom index scores (p = 0.002). Crucially, objective acoustic voice analysis demonstrated robust correlations with reflux status. Patients with GERD exhibited distinct, quantifiable vocal fold instability, evidenced by significantly elevated absolute jitter (p = 0.03), jitter percentage (p = 0.04), shimmer percentage (p = 0.02) and noise-to-harmonics ratio (NHR) (p = 0.04) compared to non-GERD individuals. Conclusion GERD was identified in 62.5% of patients within this highly selected idiopathic hoarseness cohort. Both clinical indicators and objective acoustic perturbation measures-specifically jitter, shimmer and NHR-demonstrated significant, unadjusted univariate associations with GERD. These findings highlight that reflux causes measurable vocal disruption, suggesting acoustic voice analysis holds promising potential as a non-invasive adjunctive tool for evaluating laryngeal reflux. However, larger, controlled multi-center studies are necessary to perform multi-variable adjustment and firmly establish the clinical diagnostic role of these parameters.

title: A digital twin roadmap for adult spinal deformity.
abstract: Adult spinal deformity (ASD) surgery is a high-risk, high-cost domain in which preoperative planning plays a critical role in determining alignment goals, surgical strategy, and the balance between deformity correction and treatment-related complications, yet decisions still rely heavily on static radiographs, classification systems, and surgeon experience. In parallel, medical digital twins, continuously updated, patient-specific computational models that simulate alternative treatment paths, are emerging in other medical disciplines but have not been formally articulated for ASD. In this narrative review, we adapt the recently proposed five-component medical digital twin framework (patient, data connection, patient-in-silico, interface, and synchronization policy) to adult spinal deformity by mapping each component to ASD-specific data sources, computational models, clinical workflows, and validation pathways. We outline how existing tools in ASD, including classification systems, frailty and bone-health metrics, biomechanical modeling, motion analysis, mobile health data, and machine learning risk calculators, can serve as inputs to an ASD digital twin. We highlight priority use cases, such as choosing the magnitude of surgery, bone-health-aware planning, pelvic fixation and rod strategy, and selection among open, hybrid, and minimally invasive approaches, all reframed as comparative simulations with explicit uncertainty bands. Finally, we propose a staged roadmap, from minimal viable twins evaluated via retrospective replay, to shadow-mode deployment, to oversighted clinical pilots, while detailing challenges in data harmonization, model validity, governance, and equity. Rather than claiming that a mature ASD digital twin exists today, this work offers a practical blueprint for how digital twins could evolve into auditable, patient-specific decision-support tools that augment, rather than replace, surgeon judgment in spinal deformity surgery.

title: Determination of total free acids in UiO-66 via extraction-decoupled gas-evolvement headspace detection.
abstract: The accurate quantification of free acidic species occluded within metal-organic frameworks (i.e., UiO-66) is essential for evaluating synthesis completeness, material purity, and post-synthetic processing. In this work, a rapid and automated headspace gas chromatography (HS‑GC) method was developed for the determination of total free acids in MOFs. The strategy couples ultrasound‑assisted methanolic extraction with a selective phase‑conversion reaction: the extracted carboxylic acids react stoichiometrically with bicarbonate in a sealed headspace vial to liberate carbon dioxide, which is then detected by HS‑GC. Under systematically optimized conditions, the method exhibited excellent linearity, high sensitivity with a low limit of detection, and satisfactory precision. Accuracy was confirmed by near‑quantitative spike recoveries and by close agreement with a well‑established spectrophotometric reference method. Leveraging the automated headspace platform, the procedure substantially reduced sample cycle time and enabled high‑throughput operation while markedly decreasing organic solvent consumption relative to conventional wet‑chemical protocols. This approach provides a reliable, efficient, and environmentally favorable tool for routine monitoring of free acid content in MOFs (i.e., UiO-66), facilitating quality control in both laboratory‑scale research and scaled‑up synthesis.

title: AI-derived cardiothoracic structures and coronary artery calcification volumes on non-contrast CT as predictors of mortality in pulmonary hypertension.
abstract: Objective To assess the prognostic value of AI-derived cardiothoracic structures and coronary artery calcification volumetric measurements in pulmonary hypertension (PH) using non-gated, non-contrast CT. Materials and methods Patients with suspected PH who underwent non-gated, non-contrast chest CT and right heart catheterisation within one month were retrospectively identified from the Assessing the Spectrum of PH Identified at a Referral Centre (ASPIRE) registry. Two validated deep learning models were used to segment and measure the volumes of cardiothoracic structures and coronary artery calcifications. The prognostic value of AI-derived cardiothoracic structures and coronary artery calcification volumetric measurements was assessed using univariable and multivariable Cox regression adjusted for demographics and PH subgroups and REVEAL scores. Results Six hundred twenty patients were included (mean age 64 ± 13 years; 62% female; 388 patients died during follow-up), comprising 202 patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension, 84 with PH-LHD, 112 with PH associated with lung disease, 65 with chronic thromboembolic PH, 9 with unclear PH, and 148 patients without PH. Calcifications were present in the right coronary artery (RCA), mainstem and left anterior descending artery (LAD), and left circumflex artery (LCX) in 45%, 67%, and 35% of patients, respectively. In multivariable Cox regression analysis adjusted for age, sex, and PH subgroup, right atrial (RA) volume was independently associated with mortality (HR 1.024, 95% CI: 1.009-1.039, p = 0.001), as were coronary artery calcifications in the RCA (HR 1.378, 95% CI: 1.113-1.705, p = 0.003), mainstem and LAD (HR 1.868, 95% CI: 1.441-2.421, p < 0.001), and LCX (HR 1.342, 95% CI: 1.084-1.660, p = 0.007). After further adjustment for the REVEAL risk score, these associations remained significant (RA volume HR 1.026, RCA calcification HR 1.604, mainstem and LAD calcification HR 2.339, LCX calcification HR 1.576; all p < 0.001). Conclusion AI-derived RA volume and coronary artery calcifications are independently associated with increased mortality in PH patients. Key points Question The prognostic significance of AI-derived cardiothoracic volumes and coronary artery calcification measured on routine non-gated, non-contrast chest CT in patients with PH remains uncertain. Findings AI-derived RA volume and coronary artery calcification volumes independently predicted mortality in PH patients, even after adjustment for demographics, PH subgroups, and REVEAL score. Relevance statement Automated CT-based AI measurements can provide additional prognostic biomarkers to improve risk stratification in PH beyond established clinical scores. Graphical abstract

After further adjustment for the REVEAL risk score, these associations remained significant (RA volume HR 1.026, RCA calcification HR 1.604, mainstem and LAD calcification HR 2.339, LCX calcification HR 1.576; all p < 0.001).

Conclusion

AI-derived RA volume and coronary artery calcifications are independently associated with increased mortality in PH patients.

Key points

Question The prognostic significance of AI-derived cardiothoracic volumes and coronary artery calcification measured on routine non-gated, non-contrast chest CT in patients with PH remains uncertain. Findings AI-derived RA volume and coronary artery calcification volumes independently predicted mortality in PH patients, even after adjustment for demographics, PH subgroups, and REVEAL score. Relevance statement Automated CT-based AI measurements can provide additional prognostic biomarkers to improve risk stratification in PH beyond established clinical scores.

title: Deep Learning-Based Gadolinium-Free Virtual Contrast-Enhanced MRI for Predicting Immediate HIFU Ablation Outcomes in Uterine Fibroids.
abstract: Rationale and objectives Accurate assessment of microvascular perfusion is essential for predicting high-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) ablation outcomes in uterine fibroids. Contrast-enhanced T1-weighted imaging (CE-T1WI) is widely used for vascular evaluation; however, gadolinium-based agents pose safety concerns and may interfere with temperature monitoring. This study aimed to generate synthetic CE-T1WI (Syn-CE-T1WI) from T2-weighted imaging (T2WI) using deep learning for predicting immediate HIFU ablation outcomes. Materials and methods A mask-guided 3D conditional generative adversarial network (3D-cGAN) was developed using magnetic resonance imaging data from 300 patients (240 training, 60 testing). Syn-CE-T1WI was generated from T2WI. Image quality was assessed using peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR), structural similarity index (SSIM), and mean absolute error (MAE). Three radiologists performed blinded evaluations of image authenticity and quality. A binary classification task was used to compare Syn-CE-T1WI and Real-CE-T1WI for predicting HIFU outcomes. Results In the test set, PSNR was 27.05 ± 2.21 dB, SSIM was 0.825 ± 0.12, and MAE was 0.023. Radiologists achieved a mean accuracy of 52.8% in distinguishing real from synthetic images (all P > 0.05). Overall, 88.9% of Syn-CE-T1WI were rated clinically acceptable. For outcome prediction, Syn-CE-T1WI achieved areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) of 0.713-0.763, comparable to Real-CE-T1WI (0.725-0.775; all P > 0.05). Combining Syn-CE-T1WI with T2WI yielded AUCs of 0.775-0.800, numerically higher than T2WI alone (0.713-0.763), and similar to T2WI + Real-CE-T1WI (0.800-0.813; all P > 0.05). Conclusion The mask-guided 3D-cGAN enabled the generation of high-fidelity, gadolinium-free Syn-CE-T1WI that may support noninvasive prediction of immediate HIFU ablation outcomes in uterine fibroids.

title: Noninvasive Prediction of Tumor Malignancy Grade in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma with Dual-Energy CT: A Novel Index Integrating Histopathological Differentiation and Ki-67.
abstract: Rationale and objectives To preliminarily develop and validate an integrated model based on clinical features and rapid-kVp-switching dual-energy CT (DECT) 3D volumetric parameters for the noninvasive prediction of a novel Grade of Malignancy (GOM) in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC)-a composite index integrating histopathological differentiation and Ki-67 index. Materials and methods This retrospective study enrolled 183 patients with pathologically confirmed PDAC. Patients were randomly allocated into training (n=128) and validation (n=55) cohorts. From the portal venous phase scans, three quantitative 3D volumetric parameters were extracted from the tumor volume: iodine concentration (IC), the slope of the spectral attenuation curve, and effective atomic number. Independent predictors for the GOM were identified through univariate and multivariate logistic regression analysis. The discriminatory performance of the developed models was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curve analysis, and clinical utility was assessed with decision curve analysis. Results The integrated model, which combined the DECT parameter (3D VOI-IC) and CA125, demonstrated superior predictive performance compared to models using clinical or DECT features alone. In the training cohort, the integrated model achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.821 (95% CI: 0.743-0.899), which was robustly validated with an AUC of 0.806 (95% CI: 0.684-0.928) in the validation cohort. Decision curve analysis confirmed that this combined model provided the highest clinical net benefit across a wide range of threshold probabilities. Conclusion Our findings suggest that an integrated model incorporating the 3D volumetric parameter IC from DECT and CA125 could be a useful and noninvasive adjunct for preoperative prediction of the comprehensive GOM in PDAC, though further validation is needed.

title: Automatic Ultrasound Habitat Radiomics for Differentiating Henoch-Schonlein Purpura Nephritis from IgA Nephropathy in Children: A Multicenter Study.
abstract: Rationale and objectives To assess a noninvasive ultrasound habitat radiomics approach with automatic kidney segmentation for distinguishing pediatric Henoch-Schonlein purpura nephritis (HSPN) from immunoglobulin A nephropathy (IgAN). Materials and methods This retrospective multicenter study included 592 biopsy-confirmed pediatric patients from three centers (HSPN, n = 338; IgAN, n = 254). The development cohort (n = 453) was split into training (n = 362) and internal validation (n = 91) cohorts, and an independent external validation cohort (n = 139) was used for final testing. Kidney regions of interest were automatically segmented using nnU-Net. K-means clustering defined three echogenic habitat subregions, and 408 radiomics features were extracted from the whole-kidney region and habitat subregions. Feature selection was performed in the training cohort, and three machine-learning classifiers were evaluated. The selected radiomics model was compared with clinical and combined models. Results nnU-Net achieved high kidney segmentation performance, with a mean Dice similarity coefficient of 0.957 and a mean intersection over union of 0.918 in the independent healthy-child test set. Fifteen radiomics features were retained, including six whole-kidney features and nine habitat-derived features. Logistic regression showed stable performance, with areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) of 0.806 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.715-0.897) internally and 0.825 (95% CI, 0.758-0.892) externally. The combined model outperformed the clinical model in AUC in both cohorts (0.846 vs 0.717; 0.805 vs 0.733). Conclusion This deep-learning-assisted ultrasound habitat radiomics approach enabled automatic kidney delineation and showed encouraging performance as a reproducible imaging adjunct for differentiating pediatric HSPN from IgAN.

title: Atrophy-Robust Multiclass CNN Segmentation of Brainstem-Related Structures in Neurodegenerative Parkinson Syndromes.
abstract: Rationale and objectives Neurodegenerative Parkinson syndromes show regionally distinct tissue loss involving several brainstem and midbrain structures. Reliable volumetry is constrained by atlas-based segmentation in atrophy-affected brains. We developed a multiclass convolutional neural network (CNN) for the segmentation of 16 brainstem-related regions on routine magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Materials and methods In this retrospective single-center study, 200 manually annotated MRI datasets of patients with Parkinson's disease, atypical Parkinson syndromes, and healthy controls were used for model development and validation. A Deep Neural Patchwork model was trained on 150 datasets and evaluated in an independent test cohort of 50 participants against atlas-based segmentation using the Dice coefficient, 95% Hausdorff distance, and average symmetric surface distances (ASSD). In an extended validation cohort of 264 participants, CNN-derived regional volumes were analyzed across Parkinson's disease, progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP), and multiple system atrophy (MSA). Results CNN segmentation outperformed atlas-based segmentation across accuracy metrics. Overall medians were 0.75 vs 0.33 for Dice, 2.0 vs 5.0 mm for 95% Hausdorff distance, and 0.30 vs 1.02 mm for ASSD. CNN-derived volumetry recapitulated established disease-associated patterns, including predominant mesencephalic, superior cerebellar peduncle, and red nucleus atrophy in PSP and more marked pontine and middle cerebellar peduncle volume loss in MSA. Conclusion The principal contribution of this study is an atrophy-robust multiclass brainstem segmentation framework. This framework may enable anatomically more faithful extraction of quantitative MRI metrics than atlas-based approaches and may reduce contamination from adjacent CSF spaces, particularly in small atrophy-affected structures.

title: Preoperative Prediction of Lymph Node Metastasis in Rectal Cancer Using Multimodal Magnetic Resonance Imaging Radiomics Combined with Clinical Risk Factors.
abstract: Rationale and objectives This study aimed to investigate the preoperative predictive value of multimodal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) radiomics combined with clinical risk factors for lymph node metastasis in rectal cancer, and to construct and validate an efficient and reproducible preoperative prediction model. Materials and methods A retrospective analysis was conducted on 129 patients with pathologically confirmed rectal cancer who underwent surgery at our hospital between 2017 and 2023. Preoperative pelvic T2-weighted imaging (T2WI), contrast-enhanced T1-weighted imaging (T1CE), and complete clinical data were collected. Three-dimensional regions of interest were manually segmented on the tumors using ITK-SNAP software, and radiomic features were selected via variance filtering and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression. Patients were randomly divided into a training cohort (n = 90) and an internal validation cohort (n = 39) at a 7:3 ratio. Five Logistic regression prediction models were constructed: single-sequence radiomics, multimodal radiomics, multimodal radiomics combined with clinical risk factors, and clinical factors alone. Using postoperative pathology as the gold standard, the diagnostic performance of each model was evaluated by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy. Results The multimodal radiomics combined with clinical risk factors model demonstrated the best predictive performance, with an AUC of 0.885 (95% CI: 0.819-0.937), sensitivity of 85.3%, specificity of 82.1%, and accuracy of 83.6% in the internal validation cohort. Its performance was significantly superior to that of the single-sequence models, the multimodal radiomics model, and the clinical model alone (all P < 0.05). Entropy from T2WI, peak enhancement from T1CE, tumor volume, tumor size, carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA), and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) were identified as independent predictors of lymph node metastasis. Calibration curves and decision curve analysis confirmed that the model was well-calibrated and provided substantial net clinical benefit. Conclusion Integrating multimodal MRI radiomics from T2WI and T1CE with clinical indicators such as CEA and NLR significantly improves the preoperative prediction of lymph node metastasis in rectal cancer, demonstrating promising clinical applicability. However, as this was a single-center retrospective study, further multicenter, large-sample external validation is warranted to confirm the stability and generalizability of the model.

title: Imaging Subphenotypes of Thoracic Involvement in IgG4-Related Disease: A Latent Class Analysis.
abstract: Rationale and objectives Thoracic manifestations of IgG4-related disease (IgG4-RD) are heterogeneous. We aimed to identify distinct imaging subphenotypes using latent class analysis (LCA) of chest computed tomography (CT) features and assess their associations with clinical characteristics, radiologic outcomes, and relapse risk. Materials and methods We retrospectively included patients with IgG4-RD and CT-confirmed thoracic involvement. Baseline chest CT findings were independently assessed by two thoracic radiologists. LCA of binary CT features was performed to identify imaging subphenotypes. Clinical and serologic characteristics, extrathoracic involvement, radiologic outcomes, and relapse-free survival were compared across subphenotypes. Cox regression analyses were used to identify factors independently associated with relapse. Results Among 231 patients, bronchovascular bundle thickening was the most frequent CT finding (56.7%). LCA identified five imaging subphenotypes: bronchovascular bundle-lymph node (BVB-LN, 38.5%), nodular (13.9%), interstitial (13.0%), mediastinal-pleural (18.6%), and mixed (16.0%). These subphenotypes differed in age, respiratory symptoms, extrathoracic involvement, and immunologic profiles. The interstitial subphenotype had the lowest radiologic improvement rate (41.7%) and highest progression rate (37.5%). The mixed (hazard ratio [HR], 3.821; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.336-10.923; P = 0.012) and BVB-LN (HR, 2.804; 95% CI, 1.062-7.399; P = 0.037) subphenotypes were independently associated with higher relapse risk, whereas combined glucocorticoid and immunosuppressant therapy was associated with lower relapse risk (HR, 0.405; 95% CI, 0.223-0.735; P = 0.003). Conclusion In this single-center cohort, LCA identified five thoracic imaging subphenotypes of IgG4-RD with specific clinical profiles, radiologic outcomes, and relapse risk. External validation is required before broader generalization or adoption as a standard classification framework.

title: Bioelectrical and optogenetic modulation for neuroimmune therapeutics.
abstract: Neuroimmune interactions are emerging as key regulators of inflammation, immunity, immune homeostasis, and disease progression. Neural circuits do not merely sense tissue injury, but also actively shape immune-cell recruitment, cytokine production, vascular function, and organ-level inflammatory outcomes. Here, we overview bioelectrical and optogenetic systems for neuroimmune modulation in diseases via the defined neural and inflammatory pathway. First, we review systemic neuroimmune modulating pathway and local neuroimmune modulators, and identify established neuroimmune molecular interactions in diseases. After that, we explain bioelectrical and optogenetic systems employed to modulate neuroimmune interactions. We evaluate representative studies with advanced delivery systems in consideration of neural target, immune effector, disease-relevant outcome, and safety. Finally, this review highlights both positive and negative clinical evidence of electroceuticals, and ultrasound-mediated and optogenetic systems predominantly in preclinical development. In summary and perspective, we prioritize and discuss the requirements for their further clinical translation. The integration of neural targeting with advanced materials and adaptive gene and drug delivery would be successfully harnessed for programmable therapies to modulate disease-relevant immune circuits without broadly suppressing host defense systems.

title: Optic Disc Features in Nonarteritic Anterior Ischemic Optic Neuropathy: Spatial Organization and Structure-Function Associations.
abstract: Purpose To determine whether funduscopic features in non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION) are spatially organized and associated with structural and functional measures at presentation and outcome. Design Cross-sectional and longitudinal secondary analysis of the multicenter, QRK207 NAION treatment trial (NCT02341560). Participants Trial participants with symptomatic NAION and gradable color fundus photographs at enrollment (n=728) and Month 6 (M6; n=547). Methods We quantified hemorrhage, hyperemia, axoplasmic stasis (cotton wool spots/micro-opacities), pallid edema, and chronic changes via manual annotation. Each feature was analyzed both as presence versus absence (prespecified primary) and as burden standardized to disc area (secondary). Peripapillary swelling was graded 0-4 by degree of vessel obscuration. Spatial distribution was mapped using modified Garway-Heath sectors. We assessed associations with VF, OCT-derived swelling, and symptom duration. Main outcome measures Global and sectoral VF sensitivity (average total deviation; avgTD) and best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) at enrollment and M6; OCT-derived peripapillary retinal nerve fiber layer thickness, peripapillary optic nerve head volume, and rate of ganglion cell-inner plexiform layer (GCIPL) thinning. Results At enrollment, hyperemic swelling (88.9%) and hemorrhage (79.5%) predominated, and pallid edema was common (27.9%). Acute hyperemia clustered nasally. Hyperemic swelling area correlated with shorter symptom duration (r s = -0.12, p = 0.004). The presence of pallid edema was associated with faster GCIPL thinning (-1.12 vs -0.37 µm/day, p < 0.001), worse enrollment acuity in multivariable models (β = -6.69 letters; p = 0.002), and modestly longer symptom duration (median 11 vs 10 days; p = 0.03). Enrollment features weakly associated with VF but did not predict M6 avgTD. Inferior peripapillary swelling mildly correlated with worse enrollment superior field deviation (r s = -0.27, p < 0.001). At M6, pallor was most prevalent (86.7%), clustered temporally, and was independently associated with worse avgTD (Inferior ONH to superior VF: β=-2.07 dB; p= 0.007). Conclusions Funduscopic features in NAION exhibit distinct, topographically organized spatial and temporal patterns reflecting evolving tissue injury, but have limited standalone prognostic value for long-term visual outcomes. Notably, acute pallid edema is relatively common in NAION.

title: Baseline Macular OCT Thickness of Ocular Hypertensive Patients Improves Prediction of Glaucoma.
abstract: Purpose To determine whether baseline macular ganglion cell-inner plexiform layer (GCIPL) and circumpapillary retinal nerve fiber layer (cpRNFL) thickness add prognostic value for glaucomatous visual field (VF) damage in patients with ocular hypertension. Design Retrospective clinical cohort study. Participants 330 eyes of 235 patients with ocular hypertension, defined by intraocular pressure of 22 mmHg or higher or an International Classification of Diseases coded diagnosis, without repeatable glaucomatous VF damage at baseline. Eyes came from both the African Descent and Glaucoma Evaluation Study and a clinical cohort at the Shiley Eye Institute. Methods Baseline GCIPL and cpRNFL thickness were measured from the first good-quality Cirrus optical coherence tomography (OCT) macular and optic-disc cubes. Clinical predictors were assessed with the Ocular Hypertension Treatment Study (OHTS)-European Glaucoma Prevention Study (EGPS) Risk Calculator. Repeatable glaucomatous VF damage required a Glaucoma Hemifield Test outside normal limits or a pattern standard deviation at the 5% level or worse on three consecutive reliable Humphrey 24-2 examinations. Main outcome measures Hazard ratios per 1 standard deviation (SD) of thinner global and sectoral GCIPL or cpRNFL, and the change in the Harrell concordance (C) index (ΔC) after adding each measure to the Risk Calculator. Results Glaucomatous VF damage developed in 47 of 330 eyes (14%) over a median 4.4 years. Adjusted for the Risk Calculator, thinner macular GCIPL was associated with conversion (hazard ratio [HR] 1.89 per 1-SD thinner; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.50 to 2.37; P < .001), and every macular sector was significant (HR 1.71 to 2.02). The Risk Calculator alone showed modest discrimination (Harrell C-index, 0.57). Adding macular GCIPL improved discrimination (ΔC +0.101; 95% CI, +0.022 to +0.220). Global cpRNFL thickness did not improve discrimination (ΔC +0.004; 95% CI, -0.021 to +0.133); among cpRNFL quadrants, only the inferior quadrant was associated with conversion (HR 1.50; 95% CI, 1.02 to 2.22). Conclusions In patients with ocular hypertension, thinner baseline macular GCIPL was associated with glaucomatous VF damage and improved the discrimination of the OHTS-EGPS Risk Calculator, whereas global cpRNFL thickness did not.

Global cpRNFL thickness did not improve discrimination (ΔC +0.004; 95% CI, -0.021 to +0.133); among cpRNFL quadrants, only the inferior quadrant was associated with conversion (HR 1.50; 95% CI, 1.02 to 2.22).

Conclusions

In patients with ocular hypertension, thinner baseline macular GCIPL was associated with glaucomatous VF damage and improved the discrimination of the OHTS-EGPS Risk Calculator, whereas global cpRNFL thickness did not.

title: Assessment of sequential distalization with aligners using cone-beam computed tomography merged with intraoral scans.
abstract: Introduction Sequential distalization with clear aligners, supplemented by Class II elastics, is commonly used to treat mild-to-moderate Class II malocclusions. Although favorable clinical outcomes have been reported, the underlying mechanism of tooth movement remains incompletely understood because of the methodologic limitations of conventional analyses. Methods This retrospective study included 30 adults treated with Invisalign sequential distalization combined with Class II elastics. Pretreatment and posttreatment cone-beam computed tomography images and intraoral scans were merged using segmentation and registration software. The fused models were superimposed on stable maxillary structures with computer-aided design/computer-aided manufacturing software, and the movement of the maxillary first molars was quantified in 3 planes of space using a 3-dimensional coordinate system. Results The mesiobuccal cusp tip of the maxillary first molar moved distally by a mean of 1.75 mm, whereas the mesiobuccal root apex moved distally by only 0.35 mm, representing 69.7% and 27.6% of the planned movement, respectively. The achieved distal crown tipping (7.14°) significantly exceeded the planned value, whereas the mesial-out rotation (8.22°) was only slightly greater than planned. Conclusions In patients treated with sequential distalization and Class II elastics, maxillary first molar distalization occurred primarily through distal crown tipping and mesial-out rotation. Cone-beam computed tomography- intraoral scan fused models enabled precise 3-dimensional assessments of these tooth movements.

title: Offering prenatal CFTR modulators to prevent cystic fibrosis-related organ damage in utero.
abstract: Background CFTR modulator therapy has drastically improved the prognosis and quality of life for those with cystic fibrosis (CF). CF complications begin to manifest in utero, including meconium ileus, and current regulatory approvals for CFTR modulator therapy does not have a pregnancy indication. Despite this, there have been several documented cases of women taking CFTR modulator therapy during pregnancy with promising results of potential CFTR correction in utero. Objective To report one center's experience offering CFTR modulator therapy to pregnant women for prenatal CF treatment. Study design Eight pregnant women carrying a fetus at risk of having CF were presented with the option of CFTR modulator therapy during pregnancy with extensive counseling on the potential benefits and risks. Records from routine clinical care from prenatal, birth, and perinatal period were collected. Results Of the eight pregnant women, three intended to take the CFTR modulator, elexacaftor/ tezacaftor/ ivacaftor (ETI), however only two were able, as the third was unable to obtain insurance authorization. In one case, the infant was homozygous for F508del(p.Phe508del, c.1521_1523delCTT, 1653delCTT) variant with signs of worsening bowel obstruction on fetal imaging, however after ETI initiation at 27 weeks he was born without meconium ileus. In the other case of CFTR modulator therapy treatment, the infant carried a CFTR variant of varying clinical consequence, Y1032C (c.3095A>G, p.Tyr1032Cys), and one disease causing CFTR variant. After ETI initiation, ultrasound findings suggestive of bowel obstruction improved and there was no meconium ileus at birth. The family who desired prenatal ETI therapy but was unable to obtain insurance coverage, also had one disease causing variant and one of varying clinical consequence, G622D (c.1865G>A, p.Gly622Asp). Despite fetal imaging concerning for bowel obstruction this infant had no meconium ileus at birth and was classified as CFTR related metabolic syndrome/CF Screen Positive Inconclusive Diagnosis. Of the remaining pregnant women, 3 declined prenatal CFTR modulator therapy, one ultimately had negative prenatal diagnostics, and another terminated the pregnancy. Conclusion Decisions to treat with prenatal CFTR modulators are complex and influenced by multiple factors including phenotype variability, inconsistent insurance coverage, and uncertain potential risks and benefits. Outcomes of these cases ranged from pregnancy termination to successful reversal of ultrasound findings suggestive of developing meconium ileus.

title: Ophthalmic Artery versus Uterine Artery Doppler in the prediction of preterm pre-eclampsia at 11-13 weeks' gestation.
abstract: Background Preterm pre-eclampsia (PE) is a leading cause of maternal and perinatal morbidity and mortality. First-trimester screening using maternal factors (MF), mean arterial pressure (MAP), uterine artery pulsatility index (UtPI), and placental growth factor (PlGF) allows early risk stratification and effective prevention with aspirin. However, UtPI measurement is technically demanding and operator dependent. Maternal ophthalmic artery Doppler, expressed as the ophthalmic artery peak ratio (Oph-PR), reflects early maternal cardiovascular changes and may serve as an alternative or complementary marker for PE prediction. Objective To compare the predictive performance of adding maternal Oph-PR versus uterine UtPI to the first-trimester prediction model for preterm PE that uses MF, MAP, and, PlGF. Study design This was a prospective observational study involving women attending first-trimester screening at 11 +2 to 14 +2 weeks of gestation. Maternal factors, measurement of MAP, serum PlGF collection, ultrasound examination for UtPI and Oph-PR measurement, were performed during the visit. Receiver-operating characteristics (ROC) curve analysis was used to determine the area under the curve (AUC), detection rates (DR), and positive screening cut-off from the Bayesian Accelerated Failure Time (AFT) survival models in predicting the occurrence of preterm PE (<37 weeks of gestation). De Long's test was performed to compare the superiority of the AUCs among models. Results Of 946 eligible participants, 71 (7.49%) were affected by PE, and 21 (2.2%) had preterm PE. The predictive performance of the UtPI-based model (MF + MAP + UtPI and MF + MAP + UtPI + PlGF) was similar to that of the Oph-PR-based models (MF + MAP + Oph-PR and MF + MAP + Oph-PR + PlGF) in the prediction of preterm PE (AUC 0.805 and 0.837 vs 0.789 and 0.830; p=0.584 and 0.687, respectively). The combination of MF, MAP, UtPI, Oph-PR, and PlGF in predicting preterm PE demonstrated the highest AUC compared to the other prediction models (AUC 0.919, 95% CI 0.875-0.963). Conclusion UtPI and Oph-PR are comparable for first-trimester prediction of preterm PE. Combining both Doppler indices in a prediction algorithm may improve predictive performance for preterm PE.

title: Rising Prevalence of Metabolic Dysfunction - Associated Steatotic Liver Disease in an urban South Indian screening cohort: a Retrospective Cross-sectional Study.
abstract: Purpose Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), redefined in 2023 from non-alcoholic fatty liver disease, is highly prevalent globally, but population-level data using 2023 AASLD criteria and FibroScan-based assessment remain scarce in South Asia, particularly among asymptomatic adults undergoing routine health screening. Methods We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional study of 1,103 asymptomatic adults (mean age 43.1±12.7 years; 64.1% male) undergoing FibroScan-based Master Health Check-up at a tertiary centre in Chennai, India (2023-2025). MASLD was defined as controlled attenuation parameter (CAP) ≥249 dB/m plus ≥1 cardiometabolic risk factor; fibrosis was assessed by liver stiffness measurement (LSM). Results MASLD was identified in 716 participants (64.9%; 95% CI 62.1-67.7%). Affected individuals were older, had higher BMI, and more frequently had diabetes, hypertension, and dyslipidaemia (all p<0.01). In multivariable analysis, age, male sex, BMI, and diabetes were independently associated with MASLD. Notably, 53.4% of cases occurred in adults under 46 years, and 45.3% had normal liver function tests while 31.3% had normal ultrasound, indicating conventional screening substantially underestimates disease burden. Conclusions Nearly two-thirds of asymptomatic urban South Indian adults screened met MASLD criteria, predominantly working-age individuals under-detected by conventional tools. FibroScan-based screening should be considered in preventive health programmes to enable earlier detection.

title: Evolution and impact of sarcopenia and myosteatosis in the context of liver transplantation.
abstract: Introduction and objectives Sarcopenia and myosteatosis have a well-documented adverse impact on survival in liver cirrhosis patients. This study aimed to assess the prevalence and risk factors associated with muscle impairment before liver transplantation (LT), their evolution after LT, and to determine their prognostic value. Patients and methods All cirrhotic patients listed for LT at our center between 2006 and 2010 were included. Sarcopenia and myosteatosis were assessed on transverse L3 CT images at LT listing and at 12 (M12), 60, 120, and 180 months after LT. Results The study population consisted of 198 patients, 75.3% of whom were men, and 149 underwent LT. At LT listing, sarcopenia was diagnosed in 45.5% of patients and myosteatosis in 36.5% and 20.1% had both sarcopenia and myosteatosis. One year after LT, 56.1% of patients had persistent sarcopenia and 15.3% had de novo sarcopenia. Sarcopenia significantly improved at M12 post-LT (p=0.034). Post-LT patient survival was 89.2%, 76.3%, and 59.3% at 1, 5, and 10 years respectively. In multivariate analysis, at LT listing, MELD score ≥ 25 (HR: 2.549; p=0.001), sarcopenia (HR: 1.749; p=0.004) and myosteatosis (HR: 1.630; p=0.012) were found to be independent risk factors for overall mortality. The effects of sarcopenia and myosteatosis were additive: overall survival was significantly reduced in patients with both sarcopenia and myosteatosis compared to patients with isolated sarcopenia/myosteatosis (p=0.001). Conclusions Sarcopenia and myosteatosis are common in cirrhotic patients listed for LT, persist after LT, and have a major and independent impact on overall mortality.

In multivariate analysis, at LT listing, MELD score ≥ 25 (HR: 2.549; p=0.001), sarcopenia (HR: 1.749; p=0.004) and myosteatosis (HR: 1.630; p=0.012) were found to be independent risk factors for overall mortality. The effects of sarcopenia and myosteatosis were additive: overall survival was significantly reduced in patients with both sarcopenia and myosteatosis compared to patients with isolated sarcopenia/myosteatosis (p=0.001).

Conclusions

Sarcopenia and myosteatosis are common in cirrhotic patients listed for LT, persist after LT, and have a major and independent impact on overall mortality.

title: Smaller Lateral Gap Than the Medial Gap in Deep-Flexion was Associated with Lower Patient Satisfaction in Robotic-Assisted Restricted Kinematically Aligned Cruciate-Retaining Total Knee Arthroplasty.
abstract: Background Medio-lateral soft-tissue balance influences clinical outcomes after total knee arthroplasty (TKA). The purpose of this study was to investigate the intraoperative medial-lateral gap difference pattern in restricted kinematically aligned (rKA) TKA and its associations with radiographic parameters and clinical outcomes. Methods A total of 110 knees were retrospectively analyzed. Robotic-assisted rKA TKA using a cruciate-retaining implant was performed to restore the native joint surface. Preoperative and postoperative radiographic parameters were measured. Intraoperative component gaps were assessed during the implant trial stage. Medial-lateral gap balance was defined as the lateral gap minus the medial gap, with positive values indicating a larger lateral gap than the medial gap. Knees were classified into three groups; group 1 (n = 83; medial gap less than lateral gap consistently), group 2 (n = 11; medial gap greater than lateral gap from extension to mid-flexion), and group 3 (n = 16; medial gap greater than lateral gap from mid-range to deep flexion). Clinical outcomes were evaluated at one year postoperatively using the Knee Society Score (KSS) satisfaction, Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Arthritis Index (WOMAC), and Forgotten Joint Score-12. Results Compared with group 3, group 1 showed a significantly higher satisfaction score (30.9 versus 23.5, P < 0.001) and a significantly lower WOMAC pain score (3.4 versus 5.8, P = 0.032). Multiple regression analyses showed that significant risk factors for smaller medial-lateral gap balance were a smaller preoperative angle between the surgical epicondylar axis and the posterior condylar axis (SEA-PCA) (P = 0.003) and the change in SEA-PCA (P < 0.001). Conclusion A smaller lateral gap than the medial gap from mid-range to deep flexion was associated with lower patient satisfaction in robotic-assisted rKA TKA. Femoral component rotation based on gap simulation may help achieve the target medial-lateral gap pattern during flexion. Level of evidence III.

title: Posterior Transverse Plication of Tortuous Internal Carotid Arteries During Carotid Endarterectomy.
abstract: Objectives Excessive tortuosity of the internal carotid artery (ICA) can create a risk of kinking after carotid endarterectomy (CEA) with patch angioplasty. Posterior transverse plication (PTP) shortens and straightens the ICA without arterial transection or resection. This study reviewed our outcomes with PTP followed by patch angioplasty during CEA. Methods A retrospective cohort study identified patients who underwent CEA between 2006 and 2023. Patients treated with PTP and patch angioplasty (PTP+P) were compared with a contemporaneous cohort undergoing CEA with Dacron patch closure alone (DP) for the same atherosclerotic carotid disease. Early and long-term outcomes included neurologic events, restenosis, pseudoaneurysm formation, reintervention, and survival. Results Of 168 carotid interventions, 116 met inclusion criteria: 16 PTP+P and 100 DP. Patients in the PTP+P cohort were older and had higher rates of chronic renal insufficiency and coronary artery disease. There was no 30-day mortality or postoperative TIA/stroke in either cohort. During follow-up, no ipsilateral ischemic neurologic event occurred, and there was no significant difference in restenosis, pseudoaneurysm formation, reintervention, or overall survival. In adjusted analysis, increasing age was associated with worse survival, while PTP was not. Conclusions In this small series, adding PTP during CEA before patch angioplasty appeared safe for correcting ICA tortuosity. The complication profile was similar to that of patients with straighter ICAs who underwent DP closure alone. A wide patch and intraoperative duplex ultrasound are advisable to prevent and detect technical narrowing at the plication site. Meshwords Carotid endarterectomy; internal carotid artery tortuosity; posterior transverse plication; patch angioplasty; restenosis.
