title: Regional radiomics similarity networks reveal specific brain morphological connectivity patterns in migraine and tension-type headaches.
abstract: Objective This study investigated structural brain alterations in migraine and tension-type headache using regional radiomics similarity network to characterize disease-specific morphological connectivity patterns. Background Migraine and tension-type headache are the most prevalent primary headache disorders involving central nervous system dysfunction. While functional magnetic resonance imaging has revealed abnormalities, structural changes remain incompletely understood. Regional radiomics similarity network, a novel approach for modeling individualized morphological brain networks, has not been applied in primary headaches. Methods We enrolled 65 migraine patients, 49 tension-type headache patients, and 53 healthy controls. Regional radiomics similarity network was constructed using 88 radiomics features. Regional mean connectivity strength and voxel-based morphometry were compared across groups. Spearman correlation was performed between network measures and visual analogue scale scores. Generative adversarial networks were used for classification. Results Voxel-based morphometry revealed gray matter volume alterations in cortical, subcortical, and cerebellar regions across the three groups. Regional radiomics similarity network analysis identified distinct morphological connectivity patterns: patients with migraine showed altered connectivity involving frontal, limbic, and subcortical regions, whereas patients with tension-type headache exhibited prominent alterations involving the cerebellum and thalamic-temporal connections. Exploratory partial correlation analyses suggested associations between several altered connections and pain severity. The model achieved 84.31% classification accuracy. Conclusions Regional radiomics similarity network captures disease-specific morphological connectivity patterns beyond conventional structural measurements, providing insights into structural network substrates of primary headaches. This study establishes regional radiomics similarity network as a promising neuroimaging framework for investigating brain structural alterations in migraine and tension-type headache.

title: Cardiomyocyte-derived ACE2/Ang-(1-7) axis mediates DIZE-induced inhibition of TGF-β signaling to attenuate cardiac fibrosis following myocardial infarction.
abstract: Cardiac fibrosis represents a critical pathological determinant of poor prognosis in coronary artery disease (CAD). Pharmacological activation of the angiotensin-Converting enzyme 2/angiotensin-(1-7) (ACE2/Ang-(1-7)) axis is a promising anti-fibrotic approach for cardiac fibrosis, a condition that currently lacks effective therapies. Diminazene aceturate (DIZE) is recognized as an ACE2 agonist with anti‑fibrotic activity, the molecular mechanism of which has not been fully elucidated. This study demonstrates that the anti-fibrotic effects of DIZE are exerted via a cardiomyocyte-mediated paracrine mechanism, rather than through direct action on fibroblasts. Using a cardiomyocyte-fibroblast co-culture system and transcriptomic analysis, we found that ACE2 activated by DIZE on cardiomyocytes enhances the conversion of Ang II to Ang-(1-7), which subsequently suppresses the pro-fibrotic transforming growth factor beta (TGF-β) signaling in adjacent fibroblasts. This effect was partially abrogated by the Ang-(1-7) antagonist A779, confirming Ang-(1-7) as a key paracrine mediator. To exploit this mechanism in vivo, a collagen-binding, low-intensity focused ultrasound (LIFU)-responsive nanoplatform (CNA35-GDP) was developed for specific DIZE delivery. In a rat model of myocardial infarction, LIFU-triggered DIZE release from CNA35-GDP was found to significantly improve cardiac function and attenuate fibrosis. These therapeutic benefits were accompanied by restoration of the ACE2/Ang-(1-7) axis and suppression of TGF-β signaling, thereby validating the proposed mechanism. Collectively, activation of cardiomyocyte-derived ACE2 by DIZE inhibits collagen production in fibroblasts through paracrine Ang-(1-7) and downstream suppression of TGF‑β signaling.

title: Low Cross-Sectional Area of the Geniohyoid muscle Is Associated With Non-Home Discharge in Older Patients Admitted to the Emergency Department.
abstract: Background and aims Functional decline and non-home discharge are common among older patients hospitalized in acute care settings and are associated with poor prognosis. Swallowing dysfunction is a key factor affecting functional recovery; however, the association between swallowing-related muscle mass and discharge outcomes remains unclear. This study investigated the association between the cross-sectional area (CSA) of the geniohyoid muscle (GH) at admission and discharge destination in older patients admitted to an acute care hospital. Methods This single-center prospective observational study included patients aged ≥65 years who were admitted from home to the emergency department, hospitalized for ≥5 days, and received rehabilitation. GH-CSA was measured within 5 days of admission using ultrasonography. Participants were classified into low and high GH-CSA groups using sex-specific cutoff values (≤194.7 mm 2 for men and ≤172.5 mm 2 for women). The primary outcome was discharge destination (home vs non-home). Multivariable logistic regression analysis was performed to examine the independent association between low GH-CSA and non-home discharge, adjusting for clinically relevant covariates. Results A total of 242 patients were included in the analysis. Patients with low GH-CSA had a significantly higher proportion of non-home discharge compared with those with high GH-CSA (54.0% vs 30.0%, p <0.001). GH-CSA was significantly lower in patients discharged to non-home destinations than in those discharged home (median, 152.2 vs. 177.1 mm 2 ; p <0.001). In multivariable logistic regression analyses, low GH-CSA was independently associated with non-home discharge in both Model A (odds ratio [OR] 2.21, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.15-4.24; p = 0.017) and Model B (OR 2.63, 95% CI 1.40-4.95; p = 0.003). Conclusions Low GH-CSA at admission was independently associated with non-home discharge among older patients hospitalized in an acute care setting. Ultrasound assessment of GH-CSA may serve as a simple and objective marker for early identification of patients at high risk of adverse discharge outcomes.

title: Eu-doped gadolinium fluoride nanoparticles as MRI active theranostic agent with pronounced radiocatalytic activity.
abstract: Radiotherapy remains one of the most widely used and effective methods for tumor treatment. Nanoparticle-based sensitizers are regarded as promising tools in radiotherapy since they can enhance therapeutic efficacy while reducing adverse side effects. Due to their large X-ray absorption cross-section and high proton beam stopping power, lanthanide fluoride nanoparticles have attracted considerable attention as potential radiosensitizers. In this study, we synthesized europium-doped (5, 10 and 20 mass %) gadolinium fluoride nanoparticles (GdEuF 3 NPs) and evaluated their radiocatalytic activity under X-ray and proton beam irradiation. Additionally, we performed comprehensive analysis of their cytotoxicity (IC50) and bioactivity using 4 different cell lines (3 cancer and 1 normal cell lines). The synthesized GdEuF 3 NPs demonstrated not only high colloidal stability, but also pronounced MRI contrast properties exceeding commercial MRI contrast agents (Gadobutrol®). The GdEuF 3 NPs exhibited pH-dependent radiocatalytic activity, which was predominantly observed under acidic conditions (pH 6.5) under proton beam irradiation, while a weaker effect was detected at neutral pH under X-ray irradiation. The GdEuF 3 NPs were highly biocompatible with the 4T1, MNNG/Hos, EMT6/P, and NCTC L929 cell lines over a wide concentration range (10-100 μg/mL) and across different europium contents, with no detectable adverse effects. Taking into account the pH-dependent radiation-induced overgeneration of ROS when irradiated with various types of ionizing radiation (photons or protons), the pronounced MRI contrast properties, as well as low cytotoxicity, we can confidently talk about the prospects for their biomedical use as a radiosensitizer in the future.

title: Prognostic value of right ventricular ejection fraction measured by cardiac magnetic resonance in patients with transthyretin amyloidosis.
abstract: Introduction Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) plays an important role in both the diagnosis and follow-up of patients with transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (ATTR-CM), as it provides information on cardiac function, structure, and tissue characterization. Moreover, it is the gold standard for right ventricular (RV) assessment. However, evidence regarding the prognostic value of RV systolic dysfunction in this population remains limited. Objective To evaluate the prognostic value of right ventricular ejection fraction (RVEF) measured by CMR in patients with ATTR-CM. MéTODOS: This was a single-center, observational, retrospective cohort study. We included patients from an institutional ATTR-CM registry who underwent CMR within 6 months of diagnosis between 2011 and 2025. Patients with other types of amyloidosis were excluded. Clinical, biochemical, echocardiographic, and CMR variables were collected. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality. Kaplan-Meier curves were constructed according to the presence or absence of RV dysfunction on CMR, defined as RVEF <50%. Univariate and multivariable Cox regression models were performed to identify predictors of the primary endpoint. TAPSE was not included in the multivariable models to avoid collinearity. Resultados A total of 100 patients were included, with a median age of 79 years [IQR 73-84]; 84% were men. Median left ventricular ejection fraction was 50% [IQR 42-62], and median RVEF was 48% [IQR 38-57]. Patients with lower RVEF had higher all-cause mortality (log-rank p = 0.008, Figure). In the multivariable model including age, atrial fibrillation, and NT-proBNP, RVEF was independently associated with all-cause mortality (HR 0.95, 95% CI 0.92-0.98; p = 0.002, Table). Conclusiones In our cohort of patients with ATTR-CM, RVEF assessed by CMR was independently associated with all-cause mortality. These findings suggest that RV assessment may provide additional value for risk stratification in this population.

title: Fluorodeoxyglucose-PET in Theranostics and Therapeutic Decision-Making of Lung Cancer.
abstract: Fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) PET/computed tomography (CT) is central to lung cancer staging and can alter treatment intent by detecting occult nodal and distant disease. FDG PET/CT contributes to treatment planning, biopsy targeting, radiotherapy delineation and assessment of metabolic response. Quantitative PET parameters provide complementary information on tumor burden, biological aggressiveness, and prognosis. Programmed death-ligand 1, fibroblast activation protein, and somatostatin receptor PET extend molecular imaging toward noninvasive assessment of tumor phenotype and potential theranostic targets. Artificial intelligence and radiomics may characterize tumor heterogeneity and predict molecular phenotype and treatment response but require further standardization and validation.

title: Valuable Role of <sup>18</sup>F-Fluorodeoxyglucose-PET/computed Tomography in Therapeutic Decision-Making of Infectious and Inflammatory Disorders.
abstract: 18F-FDG (18F-Fluorodeoxyglucose)-PET/computed tomography (CT) has emerged as a pivotal molecular imaging modality that extends beyond diagnosis to influence therapeutic decision-making in infectious and inflammatory diseases. By detecting increased glucose metabolism in activated inflammatory cells, it enables whole-body visualization of active disease before structural abnormalities become apparent on conventional imaging. Quantitative parameters support reproducible longitudinal monitoring. Its incorporation into international guidelines highlights its growing role in precision-guided management. Emerging technologies, including digital and long axial field-of-view PET/CT, artificial intelligence, radiomics, PET/MR imaging, and pathogen-specific or immune cell-specific tracers, may further enhance diagnostic accuracy and personalized treatment.

title: Critical Role of Novel PET-Computed Tomography/MR Imaging-Based Quantitative Techniques in Assessing Efficacy of Theranostics.
abstract: Theranostics pairs a molecularly targeted diagnostic imaging agent with its therapeutic counterpart, enabling personalized, molecularly guided therapy. Although 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose PET/computed tomography is not itself a theranostic radiopharmaceutical, it complements the theranostic workflow from patient selection and treatment planning of primary and metastatic sites to quantitative response assessment. This article reviews novel PET-computed tomography/MR imaging-based quantitative techniques for assessing theranostic efficacy, including volumetric and global disease burden metrics, kinetic modeling, and multimodality integration, with applications in thoracic malignancies, metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, and neuroendocrine tumors.

title: Technical benchmark of a high-speed ring gantry kV-CBCT imager for CBCT-based dose calculation.
abstract: Purpose A CBCT platform (HyperSight (HS)) mounted on an O-ring linac (ETHOS v1.1), is compared with standard CBCT imagers installed on C-arm (TrueBeam v2.7) and O-ring (Halcyon v3.0) linacs, as well as planning CT (pCT). The study focuses on image quality, radiation dose, and dosimetric evaluation (Hounsfield unit (HU) accuracy and dose comparison). Methods Phantom-based comparisons were performed using default CBCT protocols and reconstruction algorithms available (FDK, iCBCT and iCBCT Acuros CTS). Quantitative image quality metrics (noise, CNR, TTF, low contrast resolution) were studied (IQMetrix software). Radiation dose measurements were compared between CBCT platforms and against manufacturer values.pCT-CBCT HU comparisons were performed on HU-density calibration and anthropomorphic phantoms (Mean Error (ME) and Mean Absolute Error (MAE)). Dosimetric evaluations included relative dose deviations (D50%), and 3D gamma analysis. Results The HS imager demonstrated improved image quality and detection efficiency associated with a reduction in radiation doses compared to standard CBCT imagers. HU accuracy improved markedly for HS images reconstructed with iCBCT Acuros CTS yielding MAE(Body) < 29HU except for Head, and |ME (Soft tissue)| <8HU except for Large Pelvis protocol. For density calibration phantom, HU deviations remained within ± 50 HU except for bone densities. Dosimetric comparisons showed dose deviations below 0.5% between pCT and CBCT-based calculations for all protocols using HyperSight with iCBCT Acuros CTS (except for Large Pelvis (0.9%)). Gamma passing rates were consistently above 97.7% for 0.5%/1 mm criteria. Conclusion These results confirm the value of 125 kVp HS images reconstructed with iCBCT Acuros CTS for CBCT-based dose calculation.

title: Multicentre study of activity quantification methods for 99m-Tc-pyrophosphate SPECT/CT in cardiac amyloidosis.
abstract: Objective 99mTc-PYP SPECT/CT imaging is used for diagnosis of transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (ATTR-CA). The calculation of quantitative metrics allows assessment of the myocardial amyloid burden and supports therapy response evaluations. This study explores the implementation of reliable metrics and the validation of activity quantification methods in a multicentre study. Methods As part of the IAEA Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy (iTAC) project, a multicentre phantom study was conducted at 10 institutions using 12 hybrid SPECT/CT systems. Standardized acquisitions consistent with clinical protocols were used to compute the activity calibration factors (ACF). Absolute activity verifications were based on cardiac insert measurements with known activity distributions. Multiple reconstruction/quantification approaches (RecMethod) were evaluated, including the institution method (SiteProc) and four alternative ones; results of the computed activity were compared with the true activity meter measurements. Accuracy was assessed using RecMethod-to-True activity ratios, summarized by median, interquartile range (IQR) and coefficient of variation (CV). Results Most institution ACF values (ACF SiteProc ) ranged 75-105 cps/MBq and were consistent with reference CoreLab estimates. Agreement between ACF SiteProc and reference CoreLab values showed a median ratio of 99.6 %, IQR 5.8 %, and CV 9.4 %, indicating no systematic bias. For activity quantification, median RecMethod-to-True ratios were 100.1 % for the SiteProc reconstructions and 97.8 %, 94.1 %, 95.6 % and 96.0 % for the alternatives. Conclusion The evaluated quantification methods demonstrated good median accuracy across institutions providing reliable activity estimates, essential for a robust implementation of quantitative metrics for ATTR-CA. The obtained inter-site variability indicates that precision remains a challenge at the multicentre quantitative imaging studies.

title: Single prior-based 3D volumetric tracking from a planar snapshot in spine SBRT: A proof-of-concept study.
abstract: Background Continuous 3D onboard monitoring is essential to ensure accurate dose delivery of stereotactic body radiation therapy. However, current approaches for 2D-to-3D volumetric estimation typically require extensive patient-specific data, or depend on auxiliary imaging hardware. This study introduces a proof-of-concept framework for data-efficient, patient-specific 3D volumetric tracking using only a single volumetric prior. Methods A retrospective dataset of 80 spine SBRT patients was utilized. Digitally Reconstructed Radiographs synthesized from cone-beam computed tomography volumes served as surrogates for onboard kV projections. The pipeline consists of patient-agnostic pre-training using an archival dataset, patient-specific adaptation using the single volumetric prior supplemented by non-rigid motion simulations, and simulated intra-fractional 3D estimation. The network employs a modified Attention U-Net with a channel-to-depth bottleneck and a triple feature concatenation to map the 2D to 3D spatial domain. Results The proposed model demonstrated a statistically significant improvement in structural tracking capabilities compared to a static uncompensated baseline. Furthermore, the performance variance across patients was substantially compressed, enhancing reliability against setup uncertainties while achieving high spatial concordance in the complex spinal anatomy. The inference throughput reached approximately 10 frames per second. Conclusions This proof-of-concept study establishes the technical feasibility of data-efficient, patient-specific onboard volumetric tracking using a single volumetric prior by successfully resolving anatomical deformations from a single 2D projection in near real-time.

title: Diagnostic accuracy of Neuromelanin-sensitive MRI for Parkinson Disease: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Introduction Objective: The diagnosis of Parkinson's disease (PD) remains challenging due to clinical overlap with other parkinsonian syndromes and the absence of widely available imaging biomarkers. Neuromelanin-sensitive MRI (NM-MRI) enables in vivo visualization of neuromelanin in the substantia nigra (SN) and locus coeruleus (LC), where signal loss reflects dopaminergic neurodegeneration in the SN and noradrenergic neurodegeneration in the LC. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of NM-MRI in differentiating PD from healthy controls. Materials and methods PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to February 2025. Studies evaluating the diagnostic accuracy of NM-MRI in PD versus healthy controls were included. Two independent reviewers extracted data and assessed methodological quality using QUADAS-2. Pooled sensitivity and specificity were estimated using a random-effects bivariate model, with construction of a summary receiver operating characteristic (SROC) curve. Subgroup analyses were performed by anatomical region (SN, LC) and imaging parameter (volume, area, signal intensity, contrast ratio, subjective assessment), along with meta-regression and Deeks' funnel plot for publication bias. This review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251088071). Results Twenty-eight studies comprising 2,268 participants were included. Pooled sensitivity and specificity were 88.0 % (95 % CI, 85.3-90.2 %) and 84.4 % (95 % CI, 80.6-87.5 %), respectively, with an area under the SROC curve of 0.901 and low heterogeneity (I 2 = 3.6 % for sensitivity, 9.2 % for specificity). Volumetric analysis of the SN yielded robust and reproducible performance (sensitivity 88.0 %, specificity 85.5 %), while subjective visual assessment achieved the highest sensitivity (90.8 %) but lower reproducibility. Meta-regression identified no significant effect of MRI acquisition parameters on diagnostic accuracy, and no significant publication bias was detected. Conclusion NM-MRI demonstrates high diagnostic accuracy for differentiating PD from healthy controls, with volumetric analysis of the substantia nigra offering a robust and reproducible imaging biomarker. As the included studies compared PD with healthy controls rather than with other parkinsonian syndromes, these findings should not yet be extrapolated to the differential diagnosis of PD from other forms of parkinsonism.

Meta-regression identified no significant effect of MRI acquisition parameters on diagnostic accuracy, and no significant publication bias was detected.

Conclusion

NM-MRI demonstrates high diagnostic accuracy for differentiating PD from healthy controls, with volumetric analysis of the substantia nigra offering a robust and reproducible imaging biomarker. As the included studies compared PD with healthy controls rather than with other parkinsonian syndromes, these findings should not yet be extrapolated to the differential diagnosis of PD from other forms of parkinsonism.

title: Upper airway morphometry in acute neck infections: Clinical associations and deep learning-based segmentation.
abstract: Objectives Upper airway (UA) compromise is a significant and potentially life-threatening complication of acute neck infection (ANI), but objective, quantitative imaging features are lacking. This study aimed to evaluate the association between UA morphometry in emergency neck MRI and disease severity in ANI, and to develop and evaluate a deep learning (DL)-based model for automatic UA segmentation in ANI patients. Materials and methods A total of 322 patients were included. UA lumen was manually segmented, and prespecified morphometric features were extracted. UA morphometry was correlated with clinical outcomes. Interobserver agreement for all extracted features was evaluated with the Intraclass Correlation Coefficient (ICC). An nnU-Net model was trained on manually segmented data, and its performance was evaluated using the Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) and feature-specific ICCs. Results ICU admission occurred in 33/322 patients (10.2 %) and prolonged stay (>5 days) in 47/319 (14.7 %). Minimum cross-sectional area, compactness, maximum midline shift, and length of airway narrowing were associated with ICU admission (false-discovery-rate q ≤ 0.008) but not with prolonged stay, and did not significantly improve an established clinical model (AUC 0.80 to 0.84, DeLong p = 0.07 to 0.12). Interobserver agreement was moderate-to-excellent. The nnU-Net reached a median DSC of 0.920 with ICCs of 0.853 to 0.973 and reproduced the ICU associations. Conclusion Quantitative UA morphometry in ANI is reproducible. A narrow caliber, a long narrowed segment, and lateral displacement of the airway are associated with ICU admission, without demonstrated incremental value over established predictors in the prespecified comparison. nnU-Net segmentation reproduces the features and their univariable associations.

title: Impact of BRCA2, BRCA1, and Other Individual Homologous Recombination Repair Alterations on Survival in Metastatic Castration-resistant Prostate Cancer.
abstract: Background and objective The clinical significance of homologous recombination repair (HRR) alterations beyond BRCA2 in advanced prostate cancer is poorly understood. We investigated the association of individual non-BRCA2 HRR alterations with outcomes of patients treated with first-line therapy for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. Methods Eligible patients from the prospective CAPTURE study underwent somatic/germ line DNA analyses using a next-generation sequencing panel including ATM, BRCA1, BRCA2, BRIP1, CDK12, CHEK2, FANCA, HDAC2, PALB2, RAD51B, and RAD54L. Association with overall survival (OS) and radiographic progression-free survival was assessed using multivariable Cox regression models comparing individual non-BRCA2 HRR alterations to those in patients with BRCA2 alterations or without HRR alterations. Key findings and limitations A total of 1010 patients were included, with BRCA2 and non-BRCA2 HRR alterations found in 122 (12%) and 191 (19%) patients, respectively. BRCA1, ATM, FANCA, HDAC2, CHEK2, CDK12, and BRIP1 alterations were observed in 19 (1.9%), 69 (6.8%), 34 (3.4%), 24 (2.4%), 23 (2.3%), 20 (2%), and 15 (1.5%) patients, respectively. Patients with ATM (hazard ratio [HR] 1.66; 95% confidence interval [CI] = 1.20-2.30; p = 0.002) or CHEK2 (HR 1.71; 95% CI = 1.03-2.90; p = 0.039) alterations showed improved OS compared to patients with BRCA2 alterations, with similar outcomes to patients without HRR alterations. BRCA1 (HR 0.49; 95% CI = 0.30-0.80; p = 0.004), FANCA (HR 0.61; 95% CI = 0.42-0.89; p = 0.011), and CDK12 (HR 0.57; 95% CI = 0.35-0.93; p = 0.025) were associated with worse OS compared to patients without HRR alterations, with similar outcomes to patients with BRCA2 alterations. Conclusions and clinical implications Prognostic associations differ across individual HRR alterations. Although BRCA1, FANCA, or HDAC mutations were associated with a prognosis similar to that associated with BRCA2 alterations, prognosis in patients with ATM or CHEK2 alterations was similar to that in patients without HRR alterations. In the research setting, non-BRCA2 HRR alterations should be analyzed and reported as individual entities whenever possible.

title: An OCT-based Structural Evaluation Framework for Laser-Induced Retinal Lesions in Mice and Exploratory Application Under ALDH2 Modulation.
abstract: Laser-induced retinal injury models require structural assessments that capture lesion heterogeneity. We developed a five-dimensional optical coherence tomography (OCT) framework and explored its application under aldehyde dehydrogenase 2 (ALDH2) modulation. Following 532-nm left-eye photocoagulation, mice received dimethyl sulfoxide vehicle, Alda-1, or Daidzin intraperitoneally for seven days. OCT, fundus photography, and fluorescein angiography were performed 24 h after the final dose. The framework integrated morphologic classification, five-domain severity scoring, lesion geometry, layer-specific thickness and normalized area under the thickness-distance curve (AUC), and anatomically matched contralateral comparisons. Thirty-six lesions from nine mice were analyzed. Classification and scoring showed high interobserver agreement (κ = 0.839; intraclass correlation coefficient = 0.925). After Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment, severity score was the only tested outcome differing significantly among subtypes; eight of 45 structural correlations were significant. In 32 matched pairs, all six thickness comparisons showed significantly lower lesion-eye values. Correlations between local thickness and normalized AUC were significant after contralateral subtraction for outer retinal and outer nuclear layer measurements at the lesion level, whereas absolute correlations were nonsignificant; only the former remained significant at the mouse level. Alda-1 and Daidzin differed in subtype composition. Mouse-clustered models indicated lower scores, greater outer nuclear layer first-point thickness, and larger margin angles with Alda-1, but mouse-level comparisons were nonsignificant. Normalized AUC and its contralateral differences showed no significant treatment differences at either level. This framework integrates qualitative, semiquantitative, and quantitative assessments to characterize OCT-visible structural features in mouse retinal laser injury models.

title: Ring-based OCT protocol for retinal ganglion cell complex thickness analysis in mice.
abstract: Optical coherence tomography (OCT) enables non-invasive, high-resolution imaging of retinal layers and is widely used to assess structural changes in preclinical models of retinal and optic nerve disease. However, OCT-based retinal thickness measurements in rodents remain insufficiently standardized, with differences in measurement location and segmentation methodology potentially limiting reproducibility and comparability across studies. We describe a standardized OCT-based protocol for ganglion cell complex (GCC) thickness measurement in mice using predefined retinal landmarks and manual segmentation. Six radial OCT scans separated by 30° are acquired around the optic nerve head, and GCC thickness is measured using ImageJ at three nominal radial distances on each side of the optic nerve: 1000, 1500, and 2000 μm. The applicability of the protocol was evaluated in a murine optic nerve crush (ONC) model. GCC thickness decreased significantly over time, from 68.8 ± 5.2 μm at baseline to 60.7 ± 8.0 μm at day 15 and 60.6 ± 9.8 μm at day 24. Radius- and quadrant-specific analyses further demonstrated the ability of the protocol to detect regional patterns of GCC thinning. This protocol provides a structured approach for OCT-based GCC thickness assessment in mice and may improve consistency and comparability across preclinical studies.

title: Adiposity measures in relation to cognitive screening performance and MRI-derived brain age gap in middle-aged and older adults.
abstract: Background Adiposity has pernicious health implications, notably contributing to cognitive decline and neuroanatomical alterations. Research regarding which measures of adiposity are most related to cognition and the brain is inconsistent. This study explores the relationships between 1) multiple adiposity measures, 2) adiposity measures and cognitive screening performance, and 3) adiposity measures and a machine-learning predicted brain age gap (BAG). Methods Cross-sectional data were combined from two multi-site studies, including 641 non-Hispanic black and non-Hispanic white adults (45-85 years old). Adiposity measures included Body Mass Index (BMI), waist circumference (WC), waist-to-hip ratio (WHpR), waist-to-height ratio (WHtR), and A Body Shape Index (ABSI) z-score. Cognition was assessed using the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) and Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA). MoCA scores were converted to equivalent MMSE scores. The predicted BAG was obtained using DeepBrainNet (n = 204) from T1-weighted brain MRI. Results Adiposity measures were significantly correlated, except for BMI and ABSI. After covariate adjustment, cognitive screening associations were small and inconsistent, with a linear association for BMI and nonlinear associations for WC and WHtR. BAG associations depended on model form, with nonlinear patterns for BMI, WC, and WHtR and higher predicted BAG at higher versus intermediate adiposity levels. Combining adiposity measures showed little additional predictive value. Conclusions Anthropometric adiposity measures, particularly BMI, WC, and WHtR, were more consistently related to MRI-derived brain age gap than to brief cognitive screening performance in a cohort of middle-aged and older adults. These findings describe cross-sectional associations with older predicted brain age, especially at higher adiposity levels.

title: PSMA PET Before Prostate Biopsy: From Lesion Detection to Biopsy Avoidance.
abstract: Introduction Prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) positron emission tomography (PET) may refine biopsy selection when magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is equivocal or nonsuspicious despite persistent clinical concern. This review aims to examine the prospective evidence and to distinguish diagnostic accuracy from biopsy avoidance. Methods Selected prospective cohorts and randomized trials evaluating PSMA PET before prostate biopsy were synthesized narratively, alongside relevant systematic reviews and guidelines. Interpretation focused on patient selection, clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa) definitions, biopsy protocols, and verification of PET-negative findings. Results Combining PSMA PET with MRI improves sensitivity and negative predictive value in several prospective studies, particularly in men with equivocal findings. PET-targeted biopsy can improve sampling, but this does not establish the safety of omitting biopsy. In PRIMARY2, a PET-guided pathway achieved noninferior csPCa detection compared with systematic biopsy (12% versus 16%; prespecified noninferiority margin, 10 percentage points), while 49% of men in the PET arm avoided biopsy within 6 months. PET-negative men did not undergo routine immediate biopsy, so the trial does not establish histologically verified negative predictive value. Study heterogeneity and limited follow-up constrain generalization. Conclusions PSMA PET may complement MRI in selected men with residual diagnostic uncertainty. Broader implementation requires validated clinical thresholds, longer follow-up after biopsy deferral, and evidence of cost-effectiveness.

title: [Place of clinical breast examination in breast cancer screening strategies. French College of Gynecologists and Obstetricians (CNGOF) recommendations for clinical practice].
abstract: France, like many countries around the world, is facing a rise in the incidence of breast cancer. Numerous studies have shown that the risk of death is linked to the initial stage of the tumor. In this context, mammographic screening for breast cancer aims to diagnose cancers at a subclinical stage, to limit treatment-related morbidity and reduce mortality. In France, this screening is recommended every two years for women aged 50 to 74, while clinical breast examination (CBE) by a healthcare professional is recommended by the Haute Autorité de Santé (HAS) starting at age 25, to be performed annually with no upper age limit. However, the practice of CBE needs to be updated, particularly regarding its impact on the number of cancers diagnosed, their stage, and mortality, considering new data from international literature. Design The GRADE (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation) method was used to assess the quality of the evidence on which these recommendations were based. Methods The Senology Commission (SC) of the French College of Gynecologists and Obstetricians examined 16 questions regarding CBE, distinguishing four groups of women (the general population with or without mammography screening, women over 70 years of age, high or very-risk women, and women previously treated for breast cancer). For each scenario, it was determined whether performing a CBE, compared with not performing it, led to the detection of more breast cancers, reduced tumor size, or improved survival. One question addressed the training requirements for CBE. Results The SC issued three recommendations aimed at: 1) recommending annual CBE for women in the general population aged 30 to 74, 2) recommending annual CBE for women who have previously been treated for breast cancer, 3) recommending that CBE be performed by a trained healthcare professional. The SC issued four position statements aimed at: 1) not advising CBE for women in the general population under the age of 30, as the procedure carries a risk of unnecessary follow-up tests in a group of women where the incidence of breast cancer is very low. 2) advising performing a CBE during breast cancer screening; 3) advising an annual CBE for women over 75 years of age, with the discontinuation of this practice depending on comorbidities and life expectancy. 4) advising annual CBE for women at high and very high-risk starting at age 20. According to the experts of the CNGOF's Scientific Committee, a CBE should be performed only after obtaining explicit consent following the provision of information on its benefits and risks. The SC urges all women who notice a change or abnormality in their breasts to consult their doctor without delay to undergo a clinical breast exam.

title: Prognostic Value of Late Gadolinium Enhancement in Non-Ischemic Dilated Cardiomyopathy: A Prospective Observational Study from India.
abstract: Background Non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy (NIDCM) represents a significant cause of heart failure and sudden cardiac death (SCD). Current risk stratification relies heavily on left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), which has limitations in predicting adverse outcomes. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) on cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging may provide additional prognostic information. Methods This prospective observational study enrolled 88 consecutive NIDCM patients who underwent CMR imaging at our institution. Patients were followed for a minimum of 6 months and thereafter until a common study closure date, giving a mean follow-up of 337±173 days. The primary endpoint was a composite of major adverse cardiac events (MACE), defined as sudden cardiac death, heart failure death, aborted sudden cardiac death, sustained ventricular tachycardia, and heart failure hospitalization. Results LGE was present in 44 patients (50%). The most common pattern was mid-myocardial enhancement (40.9%), followed by a combination of patterns (25.0%) and transmural enhancement (22.7%); the interventricular septum was the most frequently involved segment (81.8%). MACE occurred in 22.7% of LGE-positive patients versus 13.6% of LGE-negative patients. ROC curve analysis identified LGE extent >26% of LV volume as the optimal threshold for predicting MACE (sensitivity 70%, specificity 73.5%, AUC 0.75). Patients with LGE >26% had significantly higher event rates (43.7% vs 10.7%; unadjusted OR 6.48, 95% CI 1.45-28.9; p=0.02). Conclusions Greater LGE extent was associated with adverse cardiac events in NIDCM patients. CMR-based risk stratification may help identify high-risk patients who could benefit from ICD, but external validation in larger cohorts is required before using this threshold clinically.

title: Clinical utility of computed tomography angiography in assessing internal maxillary artery position during temporomandibular joint ankylosis surgery.
abstract: Temporomandibular joint (TMJ) ankylosis surgery carries a high risk of intraoperative bleeding due to the close anatomical relationship between the ankylotic mass and the internal maxillary artery (IMA). Although computed tomography angiography (CTA) is widely used for preoperative vascular assessment, its reliability in predicting the intraoperative IMA course in TMJ ankylosis surgery remains uncertain. This exploratory prospective case series included 34 patients (22 males, 12 females; mean age 19.6 ± 2.5 years) with TMJ ankylosis involving 48 joints treated with 1 cm gap arthroplasty. CTA identified three IMA-ankylotic mass relationships: close contact (n = 20, further subdivided into medial, n = 8; posterior, n = 12), enclosed (n = 13), and no contact (n = 15). Overall concordance between preoperative CTA-based IMA classification and intraoperative findings was 56.3%, with discordance in 43.7% of joints (Cramér's V = 0.069; P = 0.97). Concordance varied across CTA categories, with the lowest concordance observed in the no contact group (53.3%). Despite differences in preoperative CTA-based IMA classification, intraoperative outcomes did not differ significantly among groups. Ankylotic mass resection time was comparable across categories (median 23-24 min; P = 0.085), and no significant differences were observed in estimated blood loss, vascular control measures, or blood transfusion requirements. In conclusion, CTA demonstrates limited concordance with the clinically observed intraoperative course of the IMA in TMJ ankylosis surgery and does not significantly stratify intraoperative outcomes. Therefore, it may be considered a complementary tool for preoperative planning rather than a definitive predictor of intraoperative vascular anatomy.

title: Prevalence of Muscle loss during and after Pelvic Radiotherapy in Gynecological Cancer Patients.
abstract: Introduction Women undergoing pelvic radiotherapy are at risk of developing sarcopenia, defined by muscle loss. In patients treated with radiotherapy for cervical cancer, post-treatment muscle loss has been associated with poorer cancer-specific and overall survival. This study aimed to longitudinally assess sarcopenia and changes in muscle during radiotherapy and follow-up, and to evaluate whether bioelectrical impedance analysis can serve as an accurate bedside alternative to computed tomography (CT) for sarcopenia assessment. Methods and materials This prospective cohort study included women with histologically confirmed primary cervical, endometrial, vulvar, or vaginal cancer, all scheduled to undergo external beam radiotherapy (EBRT) with curative intent. Sarcopenia was assessed at baseline, during the last week of EBRT, and at the three- and six-month follow-up. Two methods were used to evaluate sarcopenia: lumbar skeletal muscle index measured via CT scan (gold standard) and appendicular skeletal muscle mass via bioelectrical impedance analysis. Fisher's exact test and the Mann-Whitney U test were used to compare baseline characteristics between women with and without sarcopenia during the last week of radiotherapy. Results A total of 31 women were included. Based on CT scans, the prevalence of sarcopenia was 23% at baseline, 32% at the last week of radiotherapy, and 42% at the three-month follow-up. At the six-month follow-up, 29% of the women were sarcopenic. Bioelectrical impedance analysis detected sarcopenia in only 0% to 50% of cases across the various time points. Patients with FIGO stage III were significantly more frequently sarcopenic based on their appendicular skeletal muscle index as assessed by CT scan during the last week of EBRT. Conclusions The prevalence of sarcopenia is high in women treated with radiotherapy for gynecological cancer. An increase in the prevalence of sarcopenia was observed, reaching its highest point at the three-month follow-up. Sarcopenia may be underestimated when assessed using bioelectrical impedance analysis, as indicated by the low sensitivity observed.

title: RESPONSE-ADAPTIVE STEREOTACTIC BODY RADIOTHERAPY BOOST AFTER CONCURRENT CHEMORADIOTHERAPY IN UNRESECTABLE STAGE III NSCLC: A PROSPECTIVE SINGLE-CENTRE COHORT STUDY.
abstract: Objective This study aimed to escalate the dose to the residual primary tumor with an adaptive stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) boost after concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CRT) in unresectable stage III non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), and to explore, within this cohort, whether a higher cumulative dose to the residual primary was associated with better locoregional control (LRC) and whether this translated into a difference in overall survival (OS). Materials and methods In this single-center, prospective, single-arm cohort, 51 patients received concurrent CRT (50 Gy/25 fractions with weekly carboplatin and paclitaxel) followed by an adaptive boost (30 Gy/5 fractions to the residual primary, 10 Gy/5 fractions to residual nodes), without consolidation durvalumab. Doses were summed by deformable registration and reported as EQD2. Response was assessed at 3 months with FDG-PET/CT (PERCIST), and toxicity with CTCAE v5.0. Outcomes estimated by Kaplan-Meier; predictors by Cox regression. Results At a median follow-up of 26 months, 2-year OS and LRC were 61.5% and 62.8%. The median PFS and DMFS were 13 and 16 months, and distant metastasis was the dominant failure pattern (41.2%). Cumulative dose below 94.77 Gy (EQD2) to the residual primary independently predicted worse LRC (HR 5.86), and a 3-month locoregional SUVmax ≥4.55 predicted worse LRC (HR 5.04). OS was independently associated with residual nodal volume, 3-month metabolic progression, and subsequent locoregional progression. Grade 3-4 pneumonitis occurred in 7.8%, grade 3 esophagitis in one patient (2%), and hemoptysis in five (9.8%). Conclusion The SBRT boost achieved encouraging locoregional control, including in bulky and node-advanced disease, without immunotherapy, and higher cumulative dose to the residual primary was associated with better locoregional control. Hemoptysis was the main safety concern and occurred predominantly in patients with pre-existing hemoptysis, supporting careful selection and strict bronchial constraints. Local escalation alone did not overcome the competing risk of distant failure.

title: Management of Coronary Calcified Nodules: A Position Statement.
abstract: Coronary calcified nodules are an uncommon but important substrate for acute coronary syndromes, stent underexpansion, and recurrent target lesion revascularization. This consensus integrates pathologic, imaging, prognostic, and interventional evidence to guide practical decision-making. Intravascular imaging is essential for diagnosis, mechanism definition, and procedural optimization. Optical coherence tomography provides superior assessment of cap disruption and thrombus, whereas intravascular ultrasound remains valuable when contrast exposure or lesion crossing limits optical coherence tomography. Treatment should be tailored to lesion crossability, calcium distribution, and the need for mechanical scaffolding. No calcium-modification device or drug-eluting stent vs drug-coated balloon strategy has demonstrated consistent superiority. The proposed type IIa/IIb framework is hypothesis-generating and requires prospective validation. Calcified nodule-related target lesion failure should be managed by correcting the dominant mechanical mechanism before antiproliferative therapy. These recommendations emphasize individualized, imaging-guided percutaneous coronary intervention and identify priorities for prospective comparative research.

title: Transcatheter Solution to Atypical Anomalous Pulmonary Venous Drainage in a Single Ventricle Patient.
abstract: Background Partial anomalous pulmonary venous drainage (PAPVD) is typically incompatible with single ventricle physiology if left unrepaired before cavopulmonary connection. This report describes a rare anatomical variant and novel interventional solution. Case summary An 8-month-old female with hypoplastic left heart variant developed profound cyanosis following bidirectional Glenn because of unrepaired PAPVD of the right upper pulmonary vein to the superior vena cava (SVC). Retrospective 3-dimensional reconstruction of the patient's neonatal computed tomography angiogram revealed a small interlobar vessel between the anomalous pulmonary vein and the anatomically normal right lower pulmonary vein. This interlobar vessel's gross dilatation and anatomical features permitted percutaneous device occlusion of the PAPVD connection to the SVC, isolating SVC return to the cavopulmonary circulation while preserving unobstructed pulmonary venous return to the atrium. Discussion Surgical and interventional solutions are reviewed in the context of this unusual anatomical variant. Take-home messages In the uncommon circumstance of an unrecognized anomalous pulmonary vein with connections to both systemic and pulmonary venous circulations, consideration may be given to interventional occlusion of the PAPVD connection to the systemic vein. Retrospective application of contemporary 3-dimensional reconstruction tools can add great value in delineating complex or unusual anatomy.

title: Sarcomatoid Renal Cell Carcinoma With Cardiac Metastasis Causing Right Ventricular Outflow Tract Obstruction.
abstract: Background Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) rarely metastasizes to the heart, and an aggressive histologic transformation known as sarcomatoid dedifferentiation confers a poor prognosis. Case summary A patient presented with progressive exertional dyspnea. Initial laboratory studies revealed elevated troponin and elevated D-dimer. Computed tomography pulmonary angiography showed a right ventricle (RV) filling defect. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated a large lobulated mass extending from the RV free wall into the outflow tract, encroaching on the pulmonic valve with an ejection fraction of <20%. Abdominal magnetic resonance imaging revealed a right renal mass. The patient suffered a fatal arrest because of obstructive shock from severe RV outflow tract obstruction. Discussion Postmortem examination confirmed metastatic sarcomatoid RCC. Patients typically present with advanced disease, and survival is <1 year. Combination immunotherapy is approved for metastatic RCC. Initiating immunotherapy would not have addressed the patient's acute hemodynamic compromise. Take-home message Early recognition of metastatic RCC is crucial for potential therapeutic intervention, though prognosis remains poor in advanced cases.

title: Development of an Electronic Clinical Quality Measure for Excessive Radiation Dose or Inadequate Image Quality in Diagnostic CT in Adults.
abstract: The Excessive Radiation Dose or Inadequate Image Quality for Diagnostic CT in Adults (ExRad) measure is the first automated radiology outcome measure adopted by CMS. We describe its development, specification, calculation, and adoption. Beginning in 2018, the measure was developed under a CMS cooperative agreement following the Measures Management System Blueprint, with oversight from a multidisciplinary Technical Expert Panel. ExRad evaluates each adult diagnostic CT examination in three steps. First, the examination is assigned to 1 of 19 CT categories defined by anatomic region and clinical indication using International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision, Clinical Modification and Current Procedural Terminology codes. Second, size-adjusted radiation dose and image noise are computed from the DICOM dose report and pixel data; because clinical and radiology data reside in separate systems, translation software inside the hospital firewall performs the linkage and calculations automatically. Third, dose and noise are compared with category-specific thresholds derived from a reader study in which 125 radiologists rated the image quality of 734 CT examinations. An examination is out of range if either value exceeds its threshold, and the measure score is the percentage of eligible examinations that are out of range. Testing across 32 facilities in eight health systems confirmed the availability, accuracy, validity, and reproducibility of all data elements, and the National Quality Forum endorsed the measure in 2021. CMS adopted ExRad in 2023 into hospital inpatient, hospital outpatient, and clinician quality reporting programs, with voluntary reporting beginning in 2025. It is the sole outcome measure in the Diagnostic Radiology MIPS (Merit-Based Incentive Payment System) Value Pathway.

title: CT-Based Deep Learning Assessment of Aortic Valve Fibrosis and Calcification: Development and Multicenter External Validation Against Experts, Histology, and Outcomes.
abstract: Background Computed tomography angiography (CTA) enables assessment of aortic valve tissue composition, providing insights into disease progression and helping predict outcomes in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement for severe aortic stenosis (AS). The authors aimed to develop a deep learning system for CTA-based quantification of aortic fibrotic and calcific tissue, validate its agreement with expert manual analysis and histopathology, and evaluate its value for outcome prediction. Methods This international, multicenter study included 1,674 patients who underwent CTA at 9 sites. A deep learning model based on the nnU-Net architecture was trained in 468 patients and applied to an external test set of 1,206 patients, including 29 with valve histology and 12 with serial CTA. In 1,165 patients with clinical outcomes, prognostic value was assessed adjusting for clinical, echocardiographic, and procedural covariates. Results Deep learning-enabled tissue composition analysis was rapid (1.35 ± 0.4 min vs 7.2 ± 1.2 min for experts) with excellent agreement vs expert assessment (r = 0.915; intraclass correlation coefficient [ICC] = 0.913), histology (r = 0.909; ICC = 0.905), and scan-rescan reproducibility (r = 0.999; ICC = 0.999). In the external cohort, 469 patients (40%) died over 4.1 ± 1.1 years of follow-up. Fibrotic tissue volume (adjusted HR [aHR] 1.42 per IQR increase; P < 0.001), calcific tissue attenuation (aHR 1.02 per 25 HU increase; P = 0.005), left ventricular ejection fraction (aHR 1.10 per 5% decrease; P < 0.001), life-threatening bleeding (aHR: 1.96; P = 0.003), major vascular complication (aHR: 1.51; P = 0.042) and postprocedural peak pressure gradient (aHR 1.03 per 1 mm Hg increase; P < 0.001) independently predicted mortality. Patients in the highest tertile of fibrotic tissue volume (>0.940 cm 3 ) had a 2-fold higher risk of death (aHR: 2.0; P < 0.001), whereas patients with dense calcific tissue attenuation (>885 HU) had a 1.5-fold higher risk of death. Conclusions Deep learning enables rapid quantification of aortic valve fibrotic and calcific tissue from CTA, demonstrating excellent agreement with both expert CTA and histological assessments. Quantitative analysis of aortic tissue composition provides additional prognostic value for all-cause mortality after transcatheter aortic valve replacement in multicenter external evaluation.

Fibrotic tissue volume (adjusted HR [aHR] 1.42 per IQR increase; P < 0.001), calcific tissue attenuation (aHR 1.02 per 25 HU increase; P = 0.005), left ventricular ejection fraction (aHR 1.10 per 5% decrease; P < 0.001), life-threatening bleeding (aHR: 1.96; P = 0.003), major vascular complication (aHR: 1.51; P = 0.042) and postprocedural peak pressure gradient (aHR 1.03 per 1 mm Hg increase; P < 0.001) independently predicted mortality. Patients in the highest tertile of fibrotic tissue volume (>0.940 cm3) had a 2-fold higher risk of death (aHR: 2.0; P < 0.001), whereas patients with dense calcific tissue attenuation (>885 HU) had a 1.5-fold higher risk of death.

Conclusions

Deep learning enables rapid quantification of aortic valve fibrotic and calcific tissue from CTA, demonstrating excellent agreement with both expert CTA and histological assessments. Quantitative analysis of aortic tissue composition provides additional prognostic value for all-cause mortality after transcatheter aortic valve replacement in multicenter external evaluation.

title: Clinical and functional outcomes following transoral endoscopically-assisted treatment of mandibular subcondylar fractures: A single-center experience.
abstract: Purpose Evidence on the outcomes of transoral endoscopically-assisted treatment of mandibular subcondylar fractures remains limited. The primary aim of this study was to evaluate surgical outcomes, complication rates, revision rates, and long-term functional results following transoral endoscopically-assisted treatment of subcondylar fractures. The secondary aim was to identify predictors of postoperative complications, revision surgery, and craniomandibular dysfunction. Methods This monocentric observational study comprised a retrospective and a prospective study arm. The retrospective cohort included all patients with mandibular subcondylar fractures treated by transoral endoscopically-assisted open reduction and internal fixation without transbuccal trocars between December 2014 and August 2024. Fractures were classified using the AO CMF and Spiessl-Schroll Classification Systems based on preoperative CT imaging. Demographic, clinical, radiographic, surgical, and postoperative data were collected. The prospective cohort consisted of patients who underwent standardized clinical follow-up at least 12 months after surgery, including assessment of temporomandibular disorders, mandibular function, occlusion, pain, and maximum mouth opening using standardized DGFDT examination protocols. Primary outcomes were postoperative complications and revision surgery; long-term functional outcome was evaluated as a tertiary endpoint. Descriptive statistics, exploratory bivariate analyses, and multivariable logistic regression were performed to identify factors associated with postoperative complications. Results A total of 132 patients with 144 subcondylar fractures were included. Postoperative complications occurred in 43.8 % of fractures, whereas intraoperative revision following 3D C-arm imaging and postoperative revision surgery were required in 15.3 % and 2.8 % of cases, respectively. The most common complications were malocclusion (20.1 %), osteosynthesis material failure (15.3 %), and wound infection (14.6 %). Multivariable analysis identified longer intermaxillary fixation as the only independent predictor of postoperative complications (OR 1.052, 95 % CI 1.008-1.109; p = 0.036). Follow-up examinations demonstrated generally favorable long-term functional outcomes, although 22.7 % of patients showed signs of temporomandibular disorders and 31.8 % presented with objective occlusal disturbances. Conclusions Transoral Endoscopically-assisted open reduction and internal fixation provided reliable surgical management of subcondylar mandibular fractures, with a low revision rate and favorable long-term functional outcomes. Prolonged postoperative intermaxillary fixation was the only independent predictor of postoperative complications, while routine intraoperative 3D imaging supported accurate fracture reduction and implant positioning.

title: Engineering long-circulating deferoxamine targeting the innate immunity of neutrophil ferroptosis for systemic lupus erythematosus treatment.
abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is characterized by dysregulation of both innate and adaptive immunity, in which ferroptosis-mediated neutrophil death has been implicated in disease progression. However, the clinical application of ferroptosis inhibitors remains limited by rapid systemic clearance and poor pharmacokinetic profiles. Here, we report a full positron emission tomography (PET)-guided strategy for pharmacokinetic engineering of ferroptosis inhibitors through albumin hitchhiking. By incorporating an albumin-binding motif into deferoxamine (DFO), we developed a series of albumin-hitchhiking conjugates and employed in vivo PET imaging-assisted evaluation to identify a long-circulating molecule, termed LAC NE . Blood pharmacokinetic analysis showed that LAC NE exhibited an estimated terminal blood half-life of 235.94 min, approximately 17-fold longer than that of DFO (13.74 min). Mechanistically, LAC NE was preferentially taken up by activated neutrophils via Fcγ receptor-mediated internalization under inflammatory conditions, resulting in effective suppression of neutrophil ferroptosis. Consequently, LAC NE reduced autoimmune responses, alleviated renal injury, and improved disease manifestations in lupus-prone mice. Collectively, these findings establish a PET-guided albumin-hitchhiking approach for pharmacokinetic optimization and targeted delivery of ferroptosis inhibitors, providing a promising strategy for precision treatment of SLE.

title: A Systematic Review of Bias, Validation, and Explainability in Artificial Intelligence Algorithms for Dental Diagnostics.
abstract: Objectives To critically evaluate the current role of artificial intelligence (AI) in dental diagnosis across multiple dental disciplines, assessing diagnostic performance, methodological quality, risk of bias, validation, explainability, and clinical applicability. Data and sources This systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines and registered in PROSPERO (CRD42025639340). PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Embase, LILACS, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Web of Science, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched up to December-2025. Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment. Risk of bias in diagnostic accuracy studies was assessed using QUADAS-2-tool, evaluating the domains of patient selection, index test, reference standard, flow and timing whilst randomised studies were assessed using Cochrane RoB 2-tool. Reporting quality and transparency of AI-model development and validation were assessed using the selected items from TRIPOD-AI reporting guideline. Methodological quality and risk of bias in AI model development and evaluation were additionally assessed using PROBAST+AI. Study selection Ninety-six studies met the inclusion criteria, of which 90.6% were retrospective. Convolutional neural networks (CNN) were the most frequently used architecture (82.3%). Sixteen studies failed to specify the CNN architecture used. Reported diagnostic accuracy ranged from 81% to 99% across dental specialties, with high performance in implantology (92-99%), orthodontics (88-99%), endodontics (87-99%). Panoramic radiographs and cone-beam computed tomography were the most used imaging modalities. QUADAS-2 analysis indicated that high-risk of bias in 55.2% of studies and most lacked external validation, whilst Assessment using selected TRIPOD+AI items identified important gaps in reporting completeness and transparency, particularly in sample-size justification, missing-data handling, protocol availability, study registration, and data or code availability. Conclusions AI demonstrates substantial technical capability to enhance diagnostic accuracy and efficiency. However, the predominance of retrospective designs, limited external validation, and methodological weaknesses constrain the strength of current evidence. Clinical significance The use of AI is potentially considered as a decision-support tool rather than replacement for clinical judgement.

title: Evaluation of knowledge, attitudes, and perceptions of interventional radiology among the Jordanian population.
abstract: Background Interventional Radiology (IR) comprises multiple minimally invasive techniques that aid in the diagnosis and treatment of a plethora of conditions. However, some studies worldwide indicate low public awareness, with IR often conflated with Diagnostic Radiology (DR). No prior study has evaluated this knowledge gap in Jordan. This study aims to assess the knowledge, attitudes, and perceptions of IR among the Jordanian population. Methods A cross-sectional, questionnaire-based survey was distributed via social media and convenience sampling. The survey, available in both English and Arabic, assessed demographics, awareness, procedural knowledge, and attitudes toward IR. A total of 429 participants were analyzed using R software. Statistical analyses included descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, and multivariable logistic regression. Results Slightly over half (52.2%) of participants had heard of IR. Self-assessed knowledge was low (67.6% "Poor/Very poor"), and 73.9% were confused about the difference between IR and DR. While 72.0% preferred IR over surgery in a hypothetical choice, only 44.1% definitively agreed to undergo an IR procedure when advised. Awareness was significantly lower among females and those in non-medical occupations. High rates of misattribution were observed, with only 18.2% correctly identifying MRI as a DR procedure. Conclusion There is a significant public knowledge gap regarding IR in Jordan, creating an "awareness-preference paradox." Despite a theoretical preference for minimally invasive IR treatments, a lack of concrete knowledge hinders real-world acceptance. Targeted educational initiatives are needed to clarify the role of IR and improve the utilization of these therapeutic options. Plain language summary Interventional radiology uses minimally invasive procedures guided by medical imaging and can offer an alternative to some types of surgery. This study surveyed people in Jordan to understand their knowledge and views of interventional radiology and related imaging services. This study found that awareness and understanding of interventional radiology were generally low, many people confused it with diagnostic imaging, but most said they would prefer a minimally invasive treatment option. This matters because better public education could help people make informed healthcare decisions and improve access to available treatment options.

title: A reproducible pipeline for simulating individual and inter-brain neural dynamics from structural connectivity.
abstract: Background Computational models can link anatomical structure to neural dynamics. However, there is no validated, reproducible pipeline that simulates individual and inter-brain EEG-like dynamics from an individual's own structural connectome. New method To address this, we developed a comprehensive computational pipeline that combines probabilistic tractography from Diffusion Magnetic Resonance Imaging (dMRI) with dynamical systems modeling to simulate EEG-like neural dynamics from individual connectomes. It extracts anatomical connectivity, intra-individual functional connectivity, and inter-individual (two-brain) functional coupling features. It then evaluates their group-discriminative information with random-forest classification under repeated nested cross-validation. Simulated phase-locking values are calibrated against empirical resting-state EEG. Results In a test sample of individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and matched controls (16 each), simulated intra-individual synchrony added classification information beyond anatomy, raising accuracy from 71.2% (AUC 0.843) to 77.6% (AUC 0.871), in a sample where groups did not differ in mean structural connectivity. Comparison with existing methods Unlike current single-brain simulations, this pipeline generates and jointly simulates two individual brain models within a single system, and reports the contribution of each feature level explicitly. Conclusions The pipeline provides a reproducible, extensible framework for deriving informative individual-level dynamic features from anatomy. The two-brain extension generates and ranks candidate inter-brain features, providing a principled way to identify between-brain measures for hypothesis-driven testing.

title: Workflow-friendly free-breathing whole-chest cardiovascular MRI using inner-volume balanced T1 relaxation-enhanced steady-state.
abstract: Background Free-breathing cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) may provide useful volumetric information. This study evaluated acquisition time and the feasibility of incorporating highly accelerated free-breathing inner-volume balanced T1 relaxation-enhanced steady-state (bT1RESS) imaging into a standard CMR protocol during the post-contrast interval before late gadolinium enhancement (LGE). Methods A prototype ECG-gated, navigator-gated inner-volume bT1RESS sequence was added to 1.5T CMR examinations in 45 patients; 30 were included in the paired comparison with breath-hold bT1RESS. Series-start timing was assessed in 14 of the 45 patients. Three readers assessed image quality. Aortic diameters were compared between bT1RESS protocols and, in an additional cohort of 15 subjects, with CEMRA. Agreement was assessed separately at five aortic levels using Bland-Altman analysis. Results Median inner-volume bT1RESS acquisition time was 1.82minutes (range, 0.78-3.72). In the series-start timing subset, median intervals from perfusion/CEMRA start to TI scout and first LGE series were 6.49minutes (n=13) and 8.46minutes (n=14), respectively. Reader preferences favored the inner-volume over breath-hold bT1RESS protocol. In the CEMRA comparison, mean differences (inner-volume bT1RESS minus CEMRA) ranged from 0.00 to 0.93mm; the lower and upper 95% limits of agreement ranged from -2.47 to -1.16mm and from 2.06 to 3.02mm, respectively. Conclusion Inner-volume bT1RESS provided rapid volumetric cardiovascular imaging within the evaluated post-contrast workflow. A primary benefit is the capability for 3D vessel measurement without a separate first-pass CEMRA acquisition. The technique may also help identify coronary artery origins, characterize morphological abnormalities in congenital heart disease and other cardiovascular disorders, and help to detect and characterize extracardiac lesions. Larger studies are needed to establish reproducibility and diagnostic performance.

title: Dynamic Fractional Myocardial Blood Volume Mapping Using Ferumoxytol-enhanced CMR Multitasking with Subspace Dose Harmonization.
abstract: Background Fractional myocardial blood volume (fMBV) represents the vascular compartment within myocardial tissue and may reflect changes in microvascular status and health. Conventionally derived from multi-dose Modified Look-Locker Inversion (MOLLI) recovery T1 mapping with ferumoxytol, MOLLI-based fMBV requires repeated breath-holds, inter-dose image registration, and static end-diastolic estimates. CMR Multitasking enables free-breathing, non-electrocardiogram (ECG)-gated imaging and offers a subspace that captures shared motion and contrast dynamics. This subspace representation can be exploited to harmonize multi-dose acquisitions directly in parameter space, enabling motion-resolved dynamic fMBV mapping while reducing reliance on post-hoc image-space registration. Methods Thirteen healthy volunteers (11 females, 28.2±10.0 years) and twelve ischemic heart disease (IHD) patients (1 female, 67.2±7.1 years) underwent multi-dose ferumoxytol imaging at 3.0T using both breath-held ECG-triggered 5(3)3(3)3 MOLLI and free-running 2-dimensional Multitasking T1 mapping sequences. MOLLI-Multitasking agreement was assessed in healthy volunteers; patient data were used for exploratory dynamic fMBV analysis. Multitasking data were harmonized across respiratory- and cardiac-motion subspace dimensions for cross-dose alignment. Pixel-wise fMBV was estimated using a two-compartment water exchange model. fMBV agreement with MOLLI was assessed using Bland-Altman analysis. Dynamic fMBV changes were also evaluated from the Multitasking data. In IHD patients, fMBV kinetic metrics (upslope and diastolic-to-systolic distribution) for cycle-dependent variation in dynamic fMBV were computed to assess systolic compression and diastolic recoil. Cardiac positron emission tomography (PET) derived perfusion and CMR-derived strain and late gadolinium enhancement served as references. Results In healthy volunteers, Multitasking produced motion-resolved fMBV maps with strong MOLLI agreement (bias -0.11%, p=0.84). Subspace harmonization reduced cross-dose variability and aligned cardiac phases. Healthy subjects showed significant diastolic-to-systolic variation (10.55±2.12% vs. 7.73±2.76%, p=0.0004). In IHD patients, ischemic segments exhibited elevated diastolic fMBV with significant systolic compression (16.36±3.44% vs. 10.01±2.24%, p=0.013), remote myocardium showed similar phasic variation (11.16±0.68% vs. 7.98±0.57%, p<0.0001). At the same time, scar demonstrated reduced fMBV with attenuated modulation (7.74±1.95% vs. 5.59±1.97%, p=0.099). Abnormal dynamic fMBV regions corresponded to PET defects and impaired circumferential strain. Conclusion Ferumoxytol-enhanced Multitasking with subspace harmonization enables free-breathing, cardiac-resolved dynamic fMBV mapping, overcoming practical limitations of MOLLI-derived fMBV. This approach enables non-invasive assessment of dynamic myocardial blood volume across the cardiac cycle, with potential utility for characterizing microvascular function in ischemic heart disease.

title: Precision localization of spinal cord lesions during surgery: Current technologies and future directions for targeted therapies.
abstract: Background Accurate intraoperative localization is essential for safe spinal cord surgery. Although numerous imaging, navigation, and neurophysiological technologies are available, their contributions are generally discussed individually rather than according to the information they provide for surgical decision-making. Emerging targeted intramedullary therapies introduce additional requirements for precise therapeutic delivery. Objective To critically review established and emerging intraoperative guidance technologies in spinal cord surgery and propose an information-centered framework supporting indication-specific surgical decision-making and precision therapeutic targeting. Methods A narrative review of the literature was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE, supplemented by relevant references from selected publications. Technologies were evaluated according to their clinical applications, supporting evidence, limitations, and contribution to intraoperative guidance. Results Five complementary information domains were identified: anatomical localization, morphological characterization, functional localization, tissue characterization, and precision therapeutic targeting. Established techniques, particularly intraoperative ultrasound and neurophysiological monitoring, provide clinically relevant guidance in selected spinal cord procedures. Fluorescence imaging offers additional vascular or tumor-associated information, whereas advanced optical imaging, multimodal fusion, artificial intelligence, and robotic assistance remain insufficiently validated for routine intramedullary applications. The proposed framework emphasizes that these domains are neither mandatory nor sequential and that additional technological complexity does not necessarily translate into improved clinical outcomes. Emerging targeted therapies further highlight the distinction between instrument positioning accuracy, therapeutic deposition, and effective biological exposure. Conclusions An information-centered approach may help guide the selection and integration of intraoperative technologies according to surgical objectives and clinical evidence. Future developments should prioritize validated, indication-specific strategies demonstrating improvements in procedural safety, targeting accuracy, and patient-relevant outcomes.

title: Proceedings from the 2025 International Consensus Meeting on Orthopedic Infections: Diagnosis of Periprosthetic Shoulder Infection.
abstract: Background Prosthetic joint infection (PJI) following shoulder arthroplasty is difficult to diagnose because clinical findings are often nonspecific, conventional diagnostic tests have variable sensitivity, and Cutibacterium acnes (C. acnes) may cause indolent infection with limited systemic inflammatory response. Diagnostic criteria have also largely been adapted from hip and knee arthroplasty with limited shoulder-specific validation. This International Consensus Meeting (ICM) reviewed the available evidence and developed consensus recommendations for the diagnosis of shoulder PJI. Methods The Shoulder Group of the 2025 ICM on Orthopedic Infections included international shoulder surgeons, infectious disease physicians, and microbiology experts experienced in shoulder arthroplasty and PJI. Thirty-two diagnostic questions underwent question-specific literature review, presentation to the consensus group, discussion, and voting. A modified Delphi process was used to establish consensus. Delegates voted to agree, disagree, or abstain. Consensus was categorized by percentage agreement, while strength of recommendation was assessed separately based on evidence quality, consistency, and directness. Results Consensus was achieved for 31 analyzed questions, with agreement ranging from 72% to 100%; 29 resulted in recommendations for clinical practice and 2 were identified as requiring further research. Question 47, which addressed the definition of PJI, was reported separately. Humeral component loosening, erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), and C-reactive protein (CRP) were supported as components of the diagnostic criteria, whereas cloudy fluid, postoperative stiffness, serum WBC count, and D-dimer were not supported as independent criteria. Arthroscopic tissue biopsy, frozen section, and selective ultrasound-guided aspiration or synovial biopsy were supported as adjuncts to diagnosis. Five intraoperative tissue specimens, prolonged aerobic and anaerobic culture incubation, and routine perioperative antibiotic prophylaxis were supported. Next-generation sequencing (NGS) and synovial neutrophil testing were supported as adjuncts; alpha-defensin was considered potentially useful but insufficiently validated for formal inclusion; and leukocyte esterase inclusion was not recommended. Routine use of bone scintigraphy, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), computed tomography (CT), single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT), or positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) was not supported. Evidence remained insufficient to determine the clinical significance of polymicrobial molecular results or routine negative control samples. Conclusion The 2025 ICM provides a consensus framework for the diagnosis of shoulder PJI, identifying several measures that can be incorporated into current clinical practice. However, substantial uncertainty remains because most recommendations are supported by limited evidence and several diagnostic tests lack sufficient sensitivity. Prospective, shoulder-specific studies are needed to define diagnostic thresholds and determine the role of emerging molecular, biomarker, and imaging modalities.
