title: Transthoracic Electromechanical and Mechanical Cardiac Function Imaging in Acute and Chronic Myocardial Infarction Progression.
abstract: Rationale Accurate and precise quantitative functional echocardiographic assessment remains a clinical challenge. Myocardial elastography (ME) and electromechanical wave imaging (EWI) are ultrasound-based elastographic myocardial strain estimation methods that, in tandem, aim to aid in the diagnosis and monitoring of cardiac diseases. Until now, these modalities have been used separately. In this study, we explore their compatibility to localize and detect both the electromechanical and mechanical effects of ischemia. Methods A longitudinal myocardial infarction model was studied in canine subjects (n = 9) for either 4 days (4-d; n = 6) or 5 week (5 wk; n = 3) to investigate the ability of ME and EWI to detect, locate and monitor collateral perfusion recovery from infarction generated via ligation of the left anterior descending coronary artery (LAD). Canine subjects were imaged with both a 300 frames/s and a 2000 frames/s ultrasound radiofrequency acquisition scheme for ME and EWI, respectively, at baseline, daily (n = 9) for 1 week and on a weekly basis (n = 3) for 4 weeks. Both techniques were performed on the acquired data and then segmented by coronary perfusion region. ME displacements were calculated with 1-D normalized cross-correlation in the axial and lateral directions (4.6 mm window, 80% window overlap, 3× lateral re-correlation), and EWI displacements were calculated with the 1-D normalized cross-correlation (5 mm window, 90% window overlap). Strains were computed using a least-squares estimator, resulting in ME cumulative radial strains and EWI interframe axial strains. The means and standard deviations were calculated by day for each technique and observed for the duration of the study. The differences in the cumulative systolic strain and the systolic activation timings between each treatment day and baseline were calculated between each perfusion segment. Results In the 4-d experiments, the difference between baseline and treatment days was significantly greater in the LAD segment than in the right coronary artery or left circumflex coronary artery (LCX) for both ME (p < 0.005, mixed-effects analysis with Geisser-Greenhouse correction and Tukey's multiple comparisons) and EWI (p < 0.001, mixed-effects analysis with Geisser-Greenhouse correction and Tukey's multiple comparisons). Over the duration of the 4 d study, the LAD showed the most significant electromechanical delay from baseline imaging. The same trend was observed in the 4 wk studies, where the LAD segment showed the most significant difference (ME: -25.8% ± 15.2%; EWI: 58.2 ± 39.5 ms) from baseline for both ME (LCX: -10.0% ± 22.2%, p < 0.01, Kruskal-Wallis test with Dunn's multiple comparisons) and EWI (right coronary artery: 31.4 ± 36.6 ms, p < 0.01, Kruskal-Wallis test with Dunn's multiple comparisons; LCX: 33.6 ± 40.1 ms, p < 0.01, Kruskal-Wallis test with Dunn's multiple comparisons). The LAD segment showed a more significant electromechanical delay between baseline and each treatment day for EWI over the 4 wk studies. This was also observed with an increased EWI systolic activation time delay between baseline and week 4. Conclusions Both ME cumulative radial strain and EWI systolic activation timing showed the ability to monitor myocardial infarction recovery over both an acute (4 d) and a chronic (4 wk) period. ME also showed substantial collateral reperfusion of the canine myocardium in the recovery of radial strain magnitude, while an electromechanical delay remained throughout both phases of the study over the LAD perfusion segment. Taken together, these findings indicate that even after apparent recovery of cumulative radial strain to baseline values, there is a remaining functional deficit in the form of electromechanical activation. EWI showed the ability to complement ME by providing insight into the electromechanical recovery of the myocardium in addition to the radial strain magnitude.

title: Focused Ultrasound in Parkinson's Disease: From Mechanisms to Precision Therapy.
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder that markedly impairs motor function and quality of life. As conventional pharmacotherapy and deep brain stimulation are increasingly limited by waning efficacy, treatment-related complications or surgical ineligibility, focused ultrasound (FUS) has emerged as a versatile, non-invasive platform that delivers acoustic energy with high spatiotemporal precision. Prior investigations of FUS for PD have often remained fragmented within two largely disconnected domains: clinical application and laboratory-based mechanistic validation. To bridge the gap between these two disconnected domains, a narrative and translational review was conducted that integrates the latest advances from both fields into a unified framework. A structured literature search of PubMed and Web of Science for articles published between January 2004 and November 2025 was conducted. After applying pre-defined inclusion criteria and exclusion criteria, a total of 114 articles were identified and constitute the evidence base for this review. Reference lists of included articles were manually screened to identify additional relevant publications. Our findings critically benchmark thermal ablation, transcranial ultrasound stimulation and BBB opening against established therapies, while appraising their key technical limitations. Looking forward, this review highlights three engineering trajectories poised to propel the field from empirical trial-and-error toward precision medicine: predictive numerical simulations for individualized treatment planning, standardization of sonication protocols and regulatory frameworks, and the evolution from open-loop to real-time closed-loop intelligent control for personalized adaptive therapy. By integrating mechanistic insights, clinical evidence and emerging technologies, this review provides a comprehensive roadmap for advancing FUS-based precision management of PD.

title: Volumetric Tissue Organization Mapping Using Backscatter Tensor Imaging With a Row Column Addressing Transducer.
abstract: Introduction Alterations in tissue organization are involved in numerous pathologies and may influence disease progression and therapeutic response. Backscatter Tensor Imaging (BTI), an emerging ultrasound (US) technique based on local spatial coherence, can be used to map tissue structure in a whole volume. However, previous volumetric implementations were limited by prolonged acquisition times or required high channel count systems. Row Column Addressing transducers (RCA) achieve volumetric acquisitions with a low channel count, making it potentially compatible with clinical settings, but have never been used for BTI. Here, we aimed to evaluate the feasibility of mapping tissue organization with an RCA probe. Methods This was done using a 6 MHz RCA probe driven by a 256-channel programmable US machine. A rotation motor was used to image the medium at 36 angular positions with respect to a reference position. The local spatial coherence of backscattered signals was calculated at each position, and the coherence values used to determine the medium orientation and fractional anisotropy. This methodology was validated in vitro in a metal needle immersed in water to test for its ability to identify a highly organized medium. We then tested the ability of our method to accurately map complex medium organization in an agar phantom consisting of fishing lines wrapped around a cylindrical structure, and an ex vivo phantom of orthogonally stacked chicken breasts. Results The measured coherence was significantly higher in the organized needle structure than in water (+20.8%, p = 0.0167). In the cylindrical phantom, measured medium orientations at the location of the fishing lines followed the expected circumferential organization, yielding a regression slope of 0.836, a bias of 9.0°, and a regression coefficient R 2 of 0.979. In ex vivo tissue, the measured organization agreed visually with the fiber orientation observed on corresponding tissue sections. Acquisitions required approximately 5 min and covered a cylindrical imaging volume with a radius of 12.8 mm and a depth of 50 mm. Conclusion These results demonstrate the feasibility of volumetric BTI using an RCA transducer for the characterization of medium organization. Future work will focus on eliminating probe rotation to enable more practical clinical implementation.

Here, we aimed to evaluate the feasibility of mapping tissue organization with an RCA probe.

This was done using a 6 MHz RCA probe driven by a 256-channel programmable US machine. A rotation motor was used to image the medium at 36 angular positions with respect to a reference position. The local spatial coherence of backscattered signals was calculated at each position, and the coherence values used to determine the medium orientation and fractional anisotropy. This methodology was validated in vitro in a metal needle immersed in water to test for its ability to identify a highly organized medium. We then tested the ability of our method to accurately map complex medium organization in an agar phantom consisting of fishing lines wrapped around a cylindrical structure, and an ex vivo phantom of orthogonally stacked chicken breasts.

Results

The measured coherence was significantly higher in the organized needle structure than in water (+20.8%, p = 0.0167). In the cylindrical phantom, measured medium orientations at the location of the fishing lines followed the expected circumferential organization, yielding a regression slope of 0.836, a bias of 9.0°, and a regression coefficient R2 of 0.979. In ex vivo tissue, the measured organization agreed visually with the fiber orientation observed on corresponding tissue sections. Acquisitions required approximately 5 min and covered a cylindrical imaging volume with a radius of 12.8 mm and a depth of 50 mm.

Conclusion

These results demonstrate the feasibility of volumetric BTI using an RCA transducer for the characterization of medium organization. Future work will focus on eliminating probe rotation to enable more practical clinical implementation.

title: Molecular profiling of renal mass biopsy tissue: A review of feasibility and clinical utility.
abstract: Conventional preoperative assessment of renal masses may not fully capture biologic aggressiveness, particularly for small or indeterminate lesions where reliance on imaging, histopathology, and tumor size can limit individualized risk assessment. As molecular classification becomes increasingly utilized in renal tumor diagnosis, renal mass biopsy (RMB) tissue provides an opportunity to preoperatively address this gap to support patient-specific management. We reviewed the feasibility and potential clinical relevance of molecular profiling performed on RMB tissue. PubMed and Embase were searched for English-language human studies published from January 1, 2010, to February 19, 2026. Eligible studies included adults with primary renal masses who underwent genomic, transcriptomic, or proteomic analysis of biopsy-derived solid tissue. Findings were synthesized descriptively by profiling modality, technical feasibility, molecular findings, reported diagnostic, prognostic, or management implications. Exploratory quantitative synthesis was performed for studies with extractable technical-feasibility denominators. Thirteen studies were included, evaluating DNA-based, RNA-based/transcriptomic, and proteomic or multi-omic profiling approaches. Nine studies with extractable technical feasibility or tissue adequacy outcomes reported high observed approach-specific success rates: DNA-based 97% (482/496), RNA-based 100% (254/254), and proteomic/multi-omic 100% (22/22). Biopsy-derived profiling identified molecular features relevant to benign-malignant discrimination, subtype refinement, small renal mass risk stratification, and characterization of biologic programs associated with aggressive tumor behavior. Molecular profiling of RMB tissue appears feasible and may provide biologically meaningful information beyond imaging and histopathology. Prospective studies using standardized preoperative RMB workflows are needed to determine whether biopsy-derived profiling improves risk stratification and supports precision management.

title: Central nervous system involvement, sequelae, and prognostic markers in children with severe hand-foot-and-mouth disease: A multicenter cohort study across four Chinese cities.
abstract: Approximately 10% of severe hand-foot-mouth disease (HFMD) cases develop post-recovery sequelae such as language and cognitive impairments, posing major social and family burdens. However, large-scale evidence on long-term outcomes is limited. This multicenter cohort study retrospectively analyzed hospitalized HFMD cases between January 1, 2015, and December 31, 2023, in four cities (Zhengzhou, Changchun, Xi'an, and Zhoukou). Among 25,536 medical records, all severe HFMD inpatients were identified, and mild HFMD inpatients from the same period were randomly selected as controls at a 1:1 ratio, resulting in 1,909 patients in each group. Sequelae were assessed through long-term follow-up, and potential prognostic markers were examined using Kaplan-Meier survival analysis and multivariable Cox proportional hazards models. The result showed that severe HFMD was associated with a significantly higher risk of long-term sequelae compared with mild cases, including motor disorders, epilepsy, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, tic disorders, language disorders, developmental delays, psychiatric disorders, intellectual disabilities, and social impairments. Independent predictors of sequelae were peak fever, feeding mode, serum creatinine, serum sodium, and complement C3 levels, which together provided effective prediction of the 6-year cumulative risk. Abnormal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and electroencephalography (EEG) findings during the acute phase were strongly correlated with subsequent sequelae. Furthermore, learning disabilities were more common among patients with severe HFMD, further highlighting the potential long-term neurological and neurodevelopmental burden of the disease. Together, these findings underscore the importance of long-term follow-up and further research to improve early identification of children at risk and inform strategies to reduce the long-term effect of HFMD.

title: Awake Craniotomy for Eloquent and Near-Eloquent Brain Tumors Without MRI or Intraoperative Neuromonitoring During the Gaza War: A Six-Patient Case Series.
abstract: Objective To describe patient selection, intraoperative neurological assessment, and postoperative observations in six awake brain tumor resections performed without MRI or electrical stimulation mapping during the Gaza war. Methods We reviewed six awake procedures undertaken at two Gaza neurosurgical services between February 2025 and July 2026. CT guided anatomical planning; patients remained awake with scalp block, local infiltration, and anesthesiologist-supervised sedation. The operating surgeon performed motor or language assessment appropriate to the lesion location. Operative records, available CT descriptions, and subsequent clinical clarifications informed the analysis. Results Among 125 tumor craniotomies reported by the participating services, six were performed awake; the number eligible for awake surgery was not recorded. All six procedures were completed without conversion to general anesthesia or a reported intraoperative clinical functional change. Five resections were judged complete by the surgeon and one intentionally subtotal, without MRI-based volumetric verification. One patient developed postoperative right hemiplegia with only partial improvement reported about one week later and died three months after surgery. The five other patients had reported follow-up of 1-18 months (median, 9 months). CT lesion dimensions were supplied for all cases, but source imaging was not independently re-reviewed. The surgeon recalled operative durations of approximately two to three hours. Conclusions Awake clinical examination provided limited real-time functional feedback when standard mapping tools were unavailable. These observations do not establish comparative safety, complete resection, or equivalence to stimulation mapping. Their relevance lies in the operative choices, limitations, and postoperative morbidity documented under resource constraints.

title: Unimodal imaging foundation models and vision-language models in MRI: A systematic review of emerging methods and clinical applications.
abstract: Artificial intelligence in medical imaging is shifting from task-specific algorithms toward adaptable foundation models (FMs) and vision-language models (VLMs). However, applying these models to MRI remains challenging because clinical interpretation requires integrating multi-parametric, volumetric imaging across multiple sequences with clinical context. This systematic review evaluates 35 studies on unimodal FMs and multimodal VLMs in MRI, summarizing emerging architectures, downstream applications, and challenges to clinical translation. Current research is concentrated in neuroimaging, with diagnostic classification representing the most mature application. Segmentation and outcome prediction also show promise, whereas automated report generation remains limited by poor clinical fidelity despite strong linguistic fluency. Broader adoption is hindered by heterogeneous MRI acquisition, limited large-scale paired image-text datasets, and inadequate safety-focused evaluation metrics. Advancing clinical translation will require standardized multicenter datasets, stronger integration with electronic health records and pathology, robust evaluation frameworks, and improved model explainability.

title: Spatial omics in cancer: a review of computational approaches and vision of AI-driven analysis.
abstract: Predicting patient response to cancer treatments remains a challenge due to tumor heterogeneity and complex tumor microenvironments (TMEs). Modern spatial genomics technologies enable gene expression profiling alongside histological frameworks, but comprehensive analysis and clinical translation of these high-dimensionality datasets will benefit from Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML). This review synthesizes computational approaches that address challenges of spatial data by examining deep-learning architectures such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for histological feature extraction and Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for modeling cell-cell interactions. We then explore the paradigm of Foundation Models that bridge histopathology with transcriptomics to accelerate the identification of spatially resolved biomarkers, improve patient stratification for immunotherapy and targeted treatments, and advance the clinical translation of mechanistic insights derived from the tumor microenvironment.

title: Novel orthotopic uterine leiomyosarcoma model demonstrated enhanced tumor growth, metastasis, and chemosensitivity compared to subcutaneous counterparts.
abstract: Objective Uterine leiomyosarcoma (uLMS) maintains a poor prognosis due to its aggressive behavior and limited therapeutic response. Preclinical progress is severely hindered by traditional subcutaneous models that often fail to metastasize, despite one-third of uLMS patients displaying metastases at diagnosis. This study aimed to establish a reproducible, physiologically accurate orthotopic uLMS murine model that faithfully recapitulates disease progression and chemotherapeutic response. Methods Primary subcutaneous tumors were established via SK-LMS-1 cell injections in NOD/SCID mice. Harvested xenografts were surgically implanted heterotopically (subcutaneous flank) or orthotopically (uterine myometrium). Eight days post-implantation, mice were randomized to receive intraperitoneal doxorubicin (1.2 mg/kg twice weekly) or vehicle control for 3 weeks. Tumor growth was tracked longitudinally via MRI (orthotopic) or caliper measurement (subcutaneous). Immunohistochemistry evaluated tumor vitality, microenvironment hypoxia, vascular density, and metastatic spread. Results Orthotopic tumors exhibited significantly accelerated growth kinetics compared to subcutaneous counterparts. This expansion was supported by co-option of host uterine vasculature, resulting in ample tumor perfusion, suppressed tissue hypoxia, and robust proliferation. Crucially, 37% of primary orthotopic tumors developed spontaneous, multi-organ metastases to pulmonary, omental, and intraperitoneal sites by 4 weeks. Orthotopic tumors demonstrated heightened sensitivity to doxorubicin, achieving a 55% volume reduction compared to 44% in subcutaneous controls, mediated by superior intratumoral drug delivery supported by increased cleaved caspase-3-dependent apoptosis. Conclusions Surgical orthotopic xenografting recapitulates clinical uLMS, demonstrating site-dependent vascular co-option, spontaneous systemic metastasis, and enhanced chemosensitivity. By mimicking physiological characteristics of human uLMS, this orthotopic model offers significant potential for enhancing understanding of uLMS and evaluating novel therapies.

title: Deep learning denoising and positron range correction of clinical [<sup>68</sup>Ga]Ga-DOTA-TOC PET images.
abstract: PET image quality degradation due to positron range effects in high-energy positron-emitting radionuclides such as Gallium-68 ( 68 Ga) can be mitigated by applying positron range correction (PRC). Deep learning (DL) models have been shown to improve image quality by reducing image noise. This study aimed to evaluate a DL model for simultaneous denoising and 68 Ga-specific PRC in clinical [ 68 Ga]Ga-DOTA-TOC PET scans. Three different U-Net-based DL models were trained to map reduced-count PET images reconstructed without PRC (25%, 33%, or 50% of acquired counts) to full-count PET images reconstructed with tissue-independent PRC (FC-PRC). The generated reduced-count-enhanced images (RCE-25%, RCE-33%, RCE-50%) were evaluated using the mean standardized uptake value (SUV mean ) in liver and lung, noise levels in liver, and maximum standardized uptake value (SUV max ) and contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) of soft tissue lesions. Three experienced nuclear medicine physicians assessed the overall image quality (OIQ), overall diagnostic confidence (ODC), and lesion detectability (sensitivity, specificity, accuracy). Compared to FC-PRC, RCE-33% and RCE-50% exhibited similar noise, whereas RCE-25% showed substantial residual noise. CNR was reduced for RCE-33% (-5.6%, p=0.001) and RCE-25% (-8.0%, p<0.001), but was comparable for RCE-50%. All reduced-count-enhanced images demonstrated lower SUV max (RCE-25%: -3.8%, p=0.02; RCE-33%: -7.0%, p<0.001; RCE-50%: -5.2%, p<0.001). RCE-33% and RCE-50% achieved non-inferior OIQ and ODC compared to FC-PRC, while RCE-25% demonstrated only non-inferior ODC. All reduced-count-enhanced images showed high sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy (>90%). The proposed DL-based approach achieved comparable noise and image quality down to 50% of counts. Although it did not outperform the reconstruction-based PRC, its benefit lies in simultaneous denoising and PRC in a single step.

title: Activity and safety of first-line pumitamig plus nab-paclitaxel in triple-negative breast cancer: a single-arm, phase 1b/2 trial.
abstract: Background Pumitamig, an investigational bispecific antibody targeting programmed death ligand-1 and vascular endothelial growth factor A, has shown preliminary efficacy across several tumour types. We aimed to evaluate the safety and activity of pumitamig plus nab-paclitaxel as first-line treatment in patients with advanced or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer. Methods In this single-arm, phase 1b/2 trial conducted at ten sites (hospitals and cancer centres) in China, patients aged 18-75 years with histologically documented, unresectable, locally advanced or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer, an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 1 or less, and one or more measurable lesion (as per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumours, version 1.1) received first-line pumitamig (20 mg/kg intravenously once every 2 weeks) plus nab-paclitaxel (100 mg/m 2 intravenously on days 1, 8, and 15 of each 28-day cycle) until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. In phase 1b, six patients received pumitamig (20 mg/kg once every 2 weeks intravenously plus nab-paclitaxel 100 mg/m 2 intravenously on days 1, 8, and 15 of each 28-day cycle) and were monitored for treatment-emergent adverse events, before subsequent enrolment in phase 2. The primary endpoints were confirmed objective response rate and safety, assessed in the efficacy-evaluable population, defined as all patients who received one or more doses of study drug and had measurable disease at baseline and at least one efficacy assessment. This trial is registered with chictr.org.cn (ChiCTR2200060400) and ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05918133), and is closed to recruitment. Findings Between June 27, 2022, and March 15, 2023, 42 patients were enrolled, received one or more doses of pumitamig plus nab-paclitaxel (median duration of exposure 9·0 months, 95% CI 6·9-11·7) and had one or more tumour assessments. All patients were Chinese and female; median age was 53 years (IQR 41-60). At a median follow-up of 35·2 months (95% CI 33·0-36·1), the confirmed objective response rate was 73·8% (95% CI 58·0-86·1; 31 of 42 patients), including one complete response and 30 partial responses. The most frequent treatment-related adverse events of grade 3 or worse were decreased neutrophil count (13 [31%] of 42 patients), decreased white blood cell count (11 [26%]), proteinuria (six [14%]), and febrile neutropenia (five [12%]). Nine (21%) patients reported 14 treatment-related serious adverse events (alanine aminotransferase increased n=2; febrile neutropenia n=2; pancreatitis n=2; and ascites, aspartate aminotransferase increased, abdominal distension, γ-glutamyltransferase increased, blood alkaline phosphatase increased, cataract, macular oedema, and retinal vein occlusion all n=1). Treatment-related adverse events led to discontinuation of both nab-paclitaxel and pumitamig in four (10%) patients, discontinuation of nab-paclitaxel only in three (7%) patients, and discontinuation of pumitamig only in two (5%) patients. There were no treatment-related deaths. Interpretation Treatment with first-line pumitamig plus nab-paclitaxel showed encouraging antitumour activity in patients with advanced or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer and a safety profile consistent with the mode of actions of both agents. These findings warrant further clinical evaluation in global phase 2 and 3 trials. Funding Biotheus (BioNTech group). title: Cancer in the Commonwealth: a Lancet Oncology Commission.
abstract: Cancer is now one of the defining health and development challenges of our time. The 56 nations of the Commonwealth, home to 2·7 billion people, mirror this global burden. Recorded cancer cases across member states rose by 35% in 2008-18 and the number of deaths reached almost 1·7 million in 2018. The Lancet Oncology Commission on cancer in the Commonwealth was convened to ask a deceptively simple question: how can 56 diverse nations act collectively to close the widening gap between the burden of cancer and the capacity of each country to respond? 80 researchers, clinicians, policy makers, and civil society members, organised into five working groups and ten research streams, spent 2 years assembling the evidence base for this report. Using a validated microsimulation model, we estimate that 5-year net survival across eleven common cancers in the Commonwealth stood at just 30·7% in 2020, ranging from 4·1% in low-income countries (LICs) to 59·0% in high-income countries (HICs), driven overwhelmingly by late-stage presentation, which affects 62% of patients in LICs compared with 43% in HICs. This difference in survival is compounded by chronic underinvestment. Infrastructure gaps are equally stark: only 12% of countries meet international benchmarks for CT imaging, 22% for hospital density, and 40% for radiotherapy. Governance is underdeveloped too: barely one-third of Commonwealth countries have a national cancer control plan meeting basic quality criteria. Research investment also mirrors these inequities: between 2016 and 2023, Commonwealth countries collectively invested only US$165 per cancer-related disability adjusted life year. Yet the case for investment is unambiguous. Our modelling shows that a comprehensive scaleup of treatment, imaging, and quality of care could raise 5-year net survival across the Commonwealth from 30·7% to 52·9%, averting an estimated 5·8 million deaths and adding 113 million life-years between 2025 and 2035, at an incremental cost of $36·7 billion, delivering a return of between four and twenty dollars on every dollar invested. Crucially, this investment need not depend chiefly on external aid, which is contracting sharply at present. Our modelling for 38 low-income and middle-income Commonwealth countries suggests that up to $701 billion in additional domestic fiscal space could be mobilised between 2025 and 2030, through budget reprioritisation, macroeconomic growth, targeted taxation, and prudent borrowing. On this evidence, the Commission proposes six priority actions. These commitments are ambitious, set against an unusually turbulent geopolitical backdrop of declining official development assistance, fiscal retrenchment, and contested multilateralism. Yet it is precisely this backdrop that gives the Commonwealth its distinctive advantage: a voluntary association spanning every income level and continent, bound by common legal and regulatory traditions, capable of collective action that neither purely bilateral aid nor multilateral institutions under strain can easily replicate.

title: Contralateral tonsillectomy in oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma: diagnostic yield and procedural burden.
abstract: Objective Unilateral radiotherapy for well-lateralised oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma reduces treatment toxicity. This study evaluated whether routine contralateral tonsillectomy, performed to look for synchronous tonsillar malignancies, is justified. Methods A retrospective analysis was conducted of 81 patients treated with curative intent for oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma at a tertiary centre (2022-2024). All patients underwent positron emission tomography computed tomography. Contralateral tonsillectomy was performed in candidates for unilateral radiotherapy. Results Forty-two patients underwent contralateral tonsillectomy. Synchronous contralateral squamous cell carcinoma was identified in one patient (2.4 per cent) who required bilateral cervical chemoradiation because of extranodal extension found on neck dissection. Eleven patients (26 per cent) underwent staged procedures after a median interval of 21 days. Post-tonsillectomy haemorrhage requiring hospital re-admission occurred in one patient (2.4 per cent). Conclusion Routine contralateral tonsillectomy did not yield any findings that altered the laterality of treatment in any patient. This suggests that omitting contralateral tonsillectomy may complement de-escalation strategies.

title: Acid-Catalyzed Synthesis of Octacosanyl Fatty Acid Esters and Their In Vivo Biological Activities.
abstract: Octacosanol (C28), mainly found in rice bran and sugar cane, possesses cholesterol-lowering properties but is limited by poor bioavailability. This study optimized the sulfuric acid-catalyzed synthesis of lauric acid-esterified octacosanol (LEO) and oleic acid-esterified octacosanol (OEO) to enhance their bioactivity. Under optimized conditions (140-150 °C for 3 h), esterification rates reached 97.8% for LEO and 90.6% for OEO, with structures confirmed via gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS), nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), and Fourier transform infrared spectrometer (FTIR). In high-fat diet-induced obese C57BL/6J mice, both esters significantly improved serum lipid profiles compared to nonesterified octacosanol, with OEO showing the strongest efficacy in reducing total cholesterol and elevating HDL-c. Furthermore, a 28-day subacute toxicological assessment in ICR mice revealed no clinical, biochemical, or hematological abnormalities, indicating a favorable preliminary safety profile for OEO. These results suggest that OEO is a promising functional ingredient for mitigating hyperlipidemia and cardiovascular disease risk, offering improved application potential in dietary supplements.

title: Development and Preclinical Evaluation of [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-L3: A Novel PET Tracer for Quantitative Imaging of Carbonic Anhydrase IX.
abstract: Carbonic anhydrase IX (CA IX) is a key biomarker for tumor hypoxia and a promising target for molecular imaging. In this study, we developed [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-L3, a novel small-molecule CA IX-targeted PET tracer. The radiolabeling was optimized to consistently achieve a radiochemical purity of >98% (10 μg precursor, 90 °C, pH 4.5, 10 min), with excellent stability in saline and FBS up to 240 min. In vivo studies demonstrated rapid blood clearance and predominant renal excretion. Surface plasmon resonance analysis demonstrated high-affinity binding of the DOTA-L3 precursor toward CA IX (Kd = 7.60 ± 0.37 nM) with highest affinity observed for CA IX among the tested isoforms. MicroPET/CT imaging (30-240 min p.i.) showed robust tumor accumulation in OSRC-2 (SUVmean = 1.47 ± 0.21) and HT-29 (SUVmean = 1.03 ± 0.12) xenografts, while minimal uptake was observed in CA IX-low FTC-238 tumors (SUVmean = 0.21 ± 0.05) at 60 min p.i. PET-derived tumor uptake showed a strong linear correlation with CA IX expression levels (R2 = 0.976, P < 0.001) across the three tumor models. High tumor-to-muscle and tumor-to-blood ratios further confirm favorable imaging contrast (T/M = 27.53 ± 1.89 and T/B = 24.61 ± 2.35 at 240 min p.i. for OSRC-2 model). These results support [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-L3 as a promising candidate for non-invasive assessment of CA IX-associated hypoxia and as a scaffold for future theranostic development.

title: Comparing MRI-based scoring systems for neuroprognostication in neonatal encephalopathy.
abstract: Background Neonatal encephalopathy (NE) remains a significant cause of neurodevelopmental impairment. However, which MRI-based scoring system best predicts 36-month outcomes remains unclear. Methods A prospective cohort of 102 neonates ≥36 weeks gestation with NE underwent early postnatal brain MRI. Images were scored using five established systems: Barkovich, Weeke, Trivedi, Rutherford, and NICHD-NRN. Neurodevelopmental outcomes were evaluated at 36 months. Prognostic performance was analyzed using logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic curves. The best predictive model was determined using pairwise correlation to reduce highly correlated variables, and then backward selection to optimize the linear regression model. Results The Weeke total score showed the highest predictive accuracy for Bayley Scales of Infant Development motor outcomes (AUC 0.7647). The Weeke gray matter subscore was most predictive of Child Behavior Checklist internalizing problems (AUC 0.7735). No scoring system reliably predicted cognitive, language, or externalizing problems (AUC < 0.7). The optimal motor outcomes prediction model included 5 Weeke variables: basal ganglia, posterior limb of internal capsule, perirolandic cortex, cerebellar hemorrhage location, and basal ganglia lactate. Conclusions MRI-based scoring systems have limited prognostic value beyond motor outcomes after NE. The Weeke score offers the most reliable motor prediction, achievable using only five parameters. Impact Existing MRI scoring systems have limited prognostic value beyond motor outcomes after neonatal encephalopathy. The Weeke score offers the most reliable motor prediction. Only 5 Weeke scoring system variables are needed to optimize motor prediction. Deep gray matter injury is associated with internalizing behavioral outcomes. A simplified, user-friendly prognostic model can support accurate outcome prediction by a broader range of clinicians.

title: Distribution patterns and temporal detection profiles of MRI-visible tract-specific wallerian degeneration after traumatic cervical spinal cord injury.
abstract: Study design Retrospective study. Objectives To characterize the distribution patterns, associated clinical factors, and temporal detection profiles of tract-specific MRI-visible Wallerian degeneration (WD) in patients with traumatic cervical spinal cord injury (tCSCI). Setting China Rehabilitation Research Center, Beijing, China. Methods Medical records of patients with tCSCI admitted between January 2015 and December 2024 were reviewed. Primary analyses used the first eligible post-injury MRI. WD was identified on T2-weighted MRI as tract-specific hyperintensity remote from the injury epicenter. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed for dorsal column WD (DC-WD), spinothalamic tract WD (ST-WD), and corticospinal tract WD (CS-WD). Temporal detectability was assessed across five injury-to-MRI interval categories. Results Of 238 patients, DC-WD was detected in 122 (51.3%), ST-WD in 103 (43.3%), and CS-WD in 64 (26.9%). ST-WD occurred only with DC-WD, and CS-WD only with concurrent DC-WD and ST-WD, forming a nested pattern of MRI-visible tract involvement. After multivariable adjustment, the log-transformed injury-to-MRI interval was significantly associated with all three WD subtypes (DC-WD: aOR = 12.74; ST-WD: aOR = 7.96; CS-WD: aOR = 6.45; all p < 0.001). The model-estimated injury-to-MRI intervals corresponding to a 50% predicted probability of MRI-visible WD were 59.1 days for DC-WD, 79.1 days for ST-WD, and 152.9 days for CS-WD. Conclusions Tract-specific MRI-visible WD after tCSCI showed a nested distribution and interval-dependent detectability. These exploratory, cross-sectional estimates should not be interpreted as longitudinal detection times but may provide reference data for MRI interpretation after tCSCI.

title: Radiographic appearance of proximal resin composite restorations bonded with a radiopaque or radiolucent universal adhesive: a randomized clinical trial.
abstract: Objectives This trial evaluated the radiographic appearance of resin composite restorations bonded with a radiopaque universal adhesive compared with a radiolucent universal adhesive, assessed by digital radiography based on modified USPHS criteria. Materials and methods Seventy-four participants with class II cavities were randomly assigned to two groups (n = 37). The intervention group received radiopaque universal adhesive (Scotchbond Universal Plus, 3M ESPE, St. Paul, USA), while the control group received radiolucent universal adhesive (Single Bond Universal adhesive, 3M ESPE, St. Paul, USA). Selective enamel etching was performed, followed by adhesive application and restoration with nanofilled resin composite (Filtek Z350XT, 3M ESPE, St. Paul, USA). Postoperative periapical radiographs were used to evaluate the appearance of the tooth-restoration interface according to modified USPHS criteria, classifying restorations as Alpha (absence of radiolucent line) or Bravo (presence of radiolucent line). Categorical data were analyzed using Fisher's exact test. Absolute risk reduction (risk difference) with 95% confidence interval was calculated to estimate the difference in the risk of detecting a radiolucent adhesive line between the two groups. Results A statistically significant difference was observed between the two groups (P = 0.025). Restorations bonded with the radiopaque adhesive demonstrated a 16.2% absolute reduction in the risk of exhibiting a radiolucent line at the tooth-restoration interface compared with those bonded using the radiolucent adhesive (95% CI: 3.71-28.73%). Conclusions The radiopaque universal adhesive resulted in significantly fewer restorations with visible radiolucent lines at the tooth-restoration interface immediately after restoration placement and may facilitate radiographic interpretation of proximal resin composite restorations. Trial registration https://clinicaltrials.gov/ , (NCT05907928).

title: [<sup>18</sup>F]FET PET enables histopathology-validated detection of non-contrast-enhancing glioblastoma.
abstract: Accurate visualization of glioblastoma is essential for guiding biopsy, resection and radiotherapy. Contrast-enhanced MRI is routine in clinical practice, yet it can miss metabolically active tumor outside areas of blood-brain barrier disruption. In a histopathology-validated cohort with 472 tissue samples of 61 patients with IDH-wildtype glioblastoma, we show that O-(2-[¹⁸F]fluoroethyl)-L-tyrosine PET ([ 18 F]FET PET) depicts tumor tissue significantly better than contrast-enhanced MRI (CE-MRI), especially in regions that show no enhancement on MRI. [ 18 F]FET PET achieves substantially higher sensitivity for tumor detection (91.2% vs 52.6%) and maintains high reliability in non-enhancing tissue (positive predictive value 98.3%), findings that are consistent across newly diagnosed and recurrent disease and in both cohorts undergoing either resection or biopsy. These results indicate that [ 18 F]FET PET complements MRI by revealing MRI-occult tumor burden. Incorporating amino acid PET into routine planning may therefore improve the accuracy of tumor visualization and, ultimately, patient management.

[<sup>18</sup>F]FET PET achieves substantially higher sensitivity for tumor detection (91.2% vs 52.6%) and maintains high reliability in non-enhancing tissue (positive predictive value 98.3%), findings that are consistent across newly diagnosed and recurrent disease and in both cohorts undergoing either resection or biopsy. These results indicate that [<sup>18</sup>F]FET PET complements MRI by revealing MRI-occult tumor burden. Incorporating amino acid PET into routine planning may therefore improve the accuracy of tumor visualization and, ultimately, patient management.

title: Re-timing mortality risk through individualized modelling of lifespan trajectories.
abstract: There is an urgent global need for affordable, large-scale health screening to enhance preventive care in the ageing population. Using low-cost, non-invasive retinal photographs and leveraging large foundation models, we developed a deep learning-based biomarker, Retinal Mortality Equivalent (RetiME), that directly mapped retinal features to individual mortality risk. Trained on a European cohort and externally validated across three independent external cohorts spanning Southeast Asia, Eurasia and North America, RetiME showed robust associations with all-cause and cause-specific mortality and predicted the incidence of a wide range of systemic and ocular diseases. Crucially, beyond static risk estimation, RetiME re-timed mortality risk by reconstructing personalized lifespan trajectories that were associated with observed mortality outcomes (for example, age of death). Clustering of these trajectories revealed distinct mortality patterns, spanning cancer-predominant, cardiometabolic and neurodegenerative risks, reflecting diverse ageing pathways captured by RetiME. Interpretability analyses showed that RetiME captures diverse biological and retinal features underlying mortality risk. Genome-wide analyses further identified genetic loci associated with RetiME. Collectively, these findings support further evaluation of retinal imaging and trajectory modelling as one component of a comprehensive assessment of mortality risk.

title: Synchrotron X-ray Data of non-diseased and diabetic Human Pancreas Tissue and Islet Segmentation Model.
abstract: Three-dimensional virtual histology using synchrotron radiation micro-computed tomography enables non-destructive visualization of biological tissue microarchitecture with isotropic resolution. To support quantitative studies of human pancreatic morphology, we provide high-resolution 3D X-ray imaging datasets of 55 pancreatic tissue cores from 32 individuals. The collection comprises histologically non-diseased pancreatic tissue from organ donors and non-neoplastic regions of surgical resection specimens from patients with pancreatic cancer, including subgroups with insulin-dependent diabetes or following neoadjuvant chemotherapy. Formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded tissue cores with a diameter of 1 mm were imaged at 650 nm isotropic voxel size, yielding a mean effective spatial resolution of 1.66 µm. The cohort includes reconstructed volumes, corresponding immunohistochemistry, clinical metadata, expert-validated annotations, and dataset-specific example 2.5D U-Net models for automated segmentation of islets of Langerhans. A representative co-registered section yielded a Dice similarity coefficient of 0.81 and intersection-over-union of 0.67. This openly accessible, FAIR-compliant resource supports quantitative analysis of endocrine, exocrine, ductal, and stromal architecture and provides a reproducible reference framework for three-dimensional virtual histology of human pancreatic tissue and computational benchmarking.

title: PFH-loaded hollow iron oxide nanoparticles suppress breast cancer progression through magnetothermal ferroptosis and inhibition of TGF-β1/Smad-driven EMT.
abstract: Breast cancer metastasis remains a major cause of mortality, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) is a key process driving tumor progression. Here, we developed perfluorohexane-loaded hollow iron oxide nanoparticles (PFH-HIONs) as a magnetothermal phase-transition platform for image-guided breast cancer therapy. PFH-HIONs were synthesized by vacuum-assisted loading of PFH into hollow iron oxide nanoparticles and characterized for morphology, size, zeta potential, magnetothermal performance, and ultrasound phase-transition behavior. Their antitumor effects were evaluated in MCF-7 cells and in a xenograft model. Ferroptosis-related changes, EMT-associated signaling, macrophage polarization, and immune-related responses were further assessed. PFH-HIONs showed a hollow nanostructure, AMF-responsive heating, and stimulus-triggered ultrasound contrast enhancement. PFH-HIONs combined with AMF reduced MCF-7 cell viability and increased apoptotic cell death. This treatment also induced ferroptosis-related changes, including GPX4 downregulation, 4-HNE and ACSL4 upregulation, and ROS accumulation. In TGF-β1-treated MCF-7 cells, PFH-HION plus AMF suppressed Smad2/3 phosphorylation, reversed EMT-associated protein and transcription factor expression, and these effects were partially attenuated by ferrostatin-1. In addition, PFH-HIONs plus AMF promoted a more pro-inflammatory macrophage phenotype, and conditioned medium from treated tumor cells induced a similar macrophage reprogramming. In vivo , PFH-HIONs plus AMF inhibited tumor growth, increased necrosis, reduced Ki67, and were associated with increased intratumoral infiltration of CD8-positive lymphocyte-like cells and elevated IFN-γ levels, with acceptable short-term biosafety. PFH-HIONs function as a magnetothermal phase-transition nanoplatform with antitumor activity associated with ferroptosis, EMT suppression, and immune-related tumor microenvironment changes, supporting further investigation for image-guided breast cancer therapy.

title: Comparative efficacy of ultrasound versus elbow arthrography in treating Monteggia fractures in young children.
abstract: Purpose This study aims to compare the effectiveness and clinical value of ultrasound-assisted and arthrography-assisted treatment for acute Monteggia fractures in young children. Methods We conducted a retrospective analysis of 40 cases of acute Monteggia fractures in children treated with Kirschner wire or elastic intramedullary nail fixation between April 2020 and April 2025. Among these cases, 19 were treated under arthrography assistance (Group A), and 21 were treated under ultrasound guidance (Group B). We recorded baseline data for both groups, including gender, age, fracture side and type, associated injuries, time from injury to surgery, internal fixation device, fluoroscopy time, surgical duration, follow-up duration, and internal fixation removal time. Postoperative X-ray examination was performed to assess the quality of fracture reduction. Results Fluoroscopy time and surgical duration in Group B were significantly lower than in Group A (P < 0.05). Based on the evaluation criteria for assessing reduction quality, 17 cases were graded excellent, and 2 were considered good in Group A, while in Group B, 20 cases were deemed excellent and 1 was considered good. At the final follow-up, there was no significant difference in the range of elbow flexion, extension, pronation, and supination between the affected limbs of Group A and Group B (P > 0.05). Conclusion Ultrasound not only saves surgical time and reduces intraoperative radiation exposure for the patients but also enables the exploration of peripheral nerves, vessels, and soft tissue compressions.

title: Radiographic manifestations of pneumatosis intestinalis and construction of an AI-assisted diagnostic system.
abstract: Pneumatosis intestinalis (PI) has a wide range of etiologies, and the imaging differentiation between benign and ischemic PI is difficult, leading to a high risk of missed diagnosis. This study systematically summarizes the CT (Computed Tomography) imaging manifestations of PI and constructs an AI (Artificial Intelligence)-assisted diagnostic model that integrates multidimensional features. This study retrospectively collected CT and x-ray data from 612 patients with PI (398 benign and 214 ischemic cases) from three tertiary hospitals, and included an external validation set of 106 cases. Imaging analysis established a five-level PI-CT severity scoring system based on gas morphology, distribution, portal venous gas (PVG), intestinal wall enhancement, mesenteric edema, and ascites. The AI system adopted a two-level architecture: The first level used EfficientNet-B3 for rapid screening on x-ray films; the second level used 3D nnU-Net (No-new-Net) to segment intestinal wall gas, and then fused the data through a three-branch network (gas morphology, accompanying signs, and clinical metadata) via cross-attention to output the probability of ischemic PI. In the internal test set, the model achieved an AUC (Area Under the Curve) of 0.947 for ischemic PI (sensitivity 91.3%, specificity 93.6%), significantly outperforming senior radiologists (AUC = 0.876); the AUC on the external validation set was 0.931. SHapley Additive exPlanations analysis showed that PVG and blood lactate were the most important predictors. This two-tiered AI system can significantly improve the early identification of the causes of critical PI, providing a reliable method for intelligent diagnosis of emergency imaging.

title: Should the carbon footprint of imaging be considered to ensure an effective, sustainable supplementary breast screening strategy for women with dense breasts?
abstract: Breast density is an independent risk factor for breast cancer and reduces the sensitivity of mammography, increasing the chance of a missed breast cancer. Notifying women of their breast density aims to increase their awareness about their breast cancer risk and support discussions about supplemental screening (e.g. ultrasound or magnetic resonance imaging) with their healthcare providers. Although supplemental screening may improve cancer detection, it also brings challenges, including lack of international consensus on how best to manage screening in women with dense breasts. The implementation of breast density notification and supplemental screening will significantly impact global screening programs, and provides an opportunity to re-evaluate screening pathways, not only in terms of benefits and harms, but also environmental sustainability. In this perspective, we discuss the benefits and harms of supplemental screening for women with dense breasts, including the carbon footprint of screening, and considerations for clinicians, consumers and policymakers.

title: Clinical and behavioral delineation of cochlear implant non-users: a 20-year retrospective descriptive analysis.
abstract: Background Although cochlear implants (CIs) effectively restore hearing, device abandonment ('non-use') remains a critical challenge limiting long-term auditory rehabilitation. Aims/objectives This study aimed to evaluate the prevalence, clinical and radiological characteristics, and patient-reported reasons for CI non-use, comparing pre-lingually and post-lingually deafened individuals to inform long-term retention strategies. Material and methods We retrospectively reviewed 545 CI recipients implanted between 2002 and 2023 (excluding 24 patients lost to follow-up or with incomplete data). Clinical features, temporal bone CT, internal auditory canal MRI, and speech-language therapy records of 36 non-users were analyzed. Results Overall non-use rate was 6.6% (36/545), comprising 8.7% (25/287) in pre-lingual and 4.3% (11/258) in post-lingual recipients. Inner ear anomalies were identified in 11 pre-lingual non-users, including two with isolated cochlear nerve deficiency. Primary non-use reasons were sound maladaptation (48.0% pre-lingual vs. 36.4% post-lingual) and lack of subjective listening effect (48.0% vs. 18.2%). Post-lingual non-users presented distinct adult-specific psychosocial barriers (27.3%), including depression and cognitive decline. Conclusions and significance CI non-use is driven by distinct physiological, psychological, and socioeconomic factors depending on deafness onset. Delineating these onset-specific profiles provides essential guidance for tailored preoperative counseling and age-appropriate post-implantation monitoring to minimize long-term device abandonment.

title: Exoscope-assisted resection of spinal tumors: volumetric efficacy, safety and learning curve analysis in 47 consecutive cases.
abstract: Objective To evaluate the clinical outcomes, volumetric extent of resection, safety profile, and skill acquisition dynamics of 3D-4K digital exoscope-assisted spinal tumor resection. Methods A retrospective analytical single-center study was conducted on 47 consecutive patients undergoing exoscope-assisted resection across intramedullary (IM, n = 7), intradural extramedullary (IDEM, n = 34), and extradural (ED, n = 6) compartments. Extent of resection was determined via blinded postoperative subtraction MRI. Surgical skill acquisition was modeled using sequential Cumulative Sum (CUSUM) analysis of intraoperative blood loss. Results Mean age was 49.1 ± 17.3 years (63.8% female). Overall Gross Total Resection (GTR > 95%) was achieved in 85.1% ( n = 40/47), reaching 100% in IM lesions ( n = 7/7) and 82.4% in IDEM tumors ( n = 28/34, p = 0.567). Postoperative CSF fistula occurred in 6.4% ( n = 3/47), restricted exclusively to IDEM Schwannomas. Median operative time was 3.27 hours (IQR: 2.68-5.05; n = 32/47). Median hospital stay was 3.0 days (IQR: 3.0-5.0). At 6-month follow-up, paired evaluations demonstrated significant functional and pain improvements (mMs and ODI/NDI, p < 0.001). Sequential CUSUM analysis identified a structural break at case 28, marking the transition to technical mastery without blood loss inflation during early cases ( p = 0.553). Conclusions Resection of spinal tumors using the 3D-4K exoscope is safe, effective, and yields high volumetric resection rates. Skill acquisition follows a patient-safe learning curve, achieving technical proficiency at case 28.

title: Hyper-acute orbital edema and vision loss following palliative radiotherapy of the lacrimal gland.
abstract: Breast carcinoma is the most common primary malignancy to metastasize to the orbit. While mild delayed orbital edema is a recognized complication of orbital radiotherapy, hyper-acute severe edema resulting in transient vision loss is rare. A 48-year-old woman with metastatic invasive lobular breast carcinoma and left orbital involvement received a first-dose palliative radiation fraction of 8 Gy to the left orbit. Within 5 hours, she developed severe proptosis, chemosis, elevated intraocular pressure, and monocular vision loss. Computed tomography demonstrated proptosis of the left globe and optic nerve stretching. She received 8 mg of intravenous dexamethasone, and her vision rapidly recovered to baseline with the resolution of her acute compressive symptoms without any change in tumor-directed therapy. This case highlights the rare risk of hyper-acute post-radiation orbital edema within hours of radiotherapy and demonstrates that early, prompt medical management can successfully rescue compressive optic neuropathy.

title: Association of HIV infection with short-term major adverse cardiovascular events among Chinese patients with carotid atherosclerosis: a single-center retrospective cohort study.
abstract: Background People living with HIV (PLWH) suffer accelerated atherosclerotic injury, but real-world Chinese cohort data excluding patients with pre-existing cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases remain scarce regarding HIV-related incident major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). This study aimed to explore the independent associations between HIV infection and 2-year incident MACE among Chinese patients with carotid atherosclerosis free of prior cardiovascular events, and identify correlated metabolic and renal factors. Methods A retrospective single-center cohort design was adopted. We enrolled patients with ultrasound-confirmed carotid atherosclerosis from January 2020 to June 2023, excluded individuals with prior coronary heart disease, ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack, and conducted standardized 2-year follow-up for all eligible participants. Univariate statistical tests screened variables correlated with MACE; variables with univariate p < 0.05 plus core clinical confounders (age, sex, hypertension, diabetes) were incorporated into multivariate binary logistic regression to identify independent correlates of new-onset MACE. Results Patients with HIV infection showed significantly younger age compared with HIV-negative counterparts (63.55 ± 10.81 years vs 70.61 ± 9.75 years, p < 0.001). The cumulative 2-year occurrence rate of MACE was markedly higher in the HIV-positive group (40.4% versus 22.9%, p = 0.023). Multivariate regression analysis verified four independent risk markers for incident MACE: HIV seropositivity (OR = 2.24, 95%CI 1.19-4.22, p = 0.012), baseline active smoking (OR = 1.98, 95%CI 1.07-3.66, p = 0.028), reduced estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) (OR = 2.15, 95%CI 1.15-4.02, p = 0.017) and hyperuricemia (OR = 1.89, 95%CI 1.02-3.51, p = 0.043). Conclusion Chinese people living with HIV (PLWH) combined with carotid atherosclerosis develop atherosclerotic lesions at an earlier age and carry elevated short-term MACE risk. Integrated intervention strategies covering HIV viral control, smoking cessation, renal function protection and serum uric acid management can effectively improve cardiovascular long-term prognosis for this special population.

title: Association between pancreatic ectopic fat deposition and QCT-assessed bone mass status in patients with chronic kidney disease: a cross-sectional study.
abstract: Background Patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) are at increased risk of bone abnormalities. Beyond disturbances in mineral metabolism, ectopic fat deposition may also be associated with skeletal abnormalities in CKD. However, the relationship between pancreatic fat and bone mass status remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the association between mean pancreatic fat fraction and quantitative computed tomography (QCT)-assessed bone mass status in patients with CKD. Methods This retrospective cross-sectional study included 327 patients with CKD. Vertebral volumetric bone mineral density was measured using QCT to classify bone mass status as normal bone mass, osteopenia, or osteoporosis. Mean pancreatic fat fraction was quantified from CT images. Ordinal logistic regression, restricted cubic spline (RCS), subgroup analyses, and sensitivity analyses were performed to evaluate its association with bone mass status. Results Mean pancreatic fat fraction was highest in patients with osteoporosis ( p < 0.001). In the fully adjusted model, each 5-percentage-point increase in mean pancreatic fat fraction was associated with higher odds of a more severe bone mass category (OR = 1.481, 95% CI: 1.152-1.905, p = 0.002). RCS analysis showed a significant overall association ( p = 0.009), with no evidence of nonlinearity ( p = 0.290). No statistically significant interactions were detected for sex, age, diabetes status, or CKD stage. Conclusion A higher mean pancreatic fat fraction was associated with more severe bone mass categories in patients with CKD after adjustment for the measured covariates. QCT-based pancreatic fat assessment may provide additional information on metabolic features associated with bone mass abnormalities in CKD.

title: Efficacy of hysteroscopic curettage and niche resection in type II and III cesarean scar pregnancies.
abstract: Introduction To evaluate the efficacy and safety of hysteroscopic curettage combined with cesarean scar diverticulum canal-opening after focused ultrasound ablation surgery (FUAS) pretreatment in patients with type II and III cesarean scar pregnancy (CSP). Methods Clinical data of 105 patients with type II/III CSP treated between January 2019 and October 2022 were retrospectively analyzed. All patients received FUAS pretreatment. The observation group ( n = 47) underwent hysteroscopic curettage combined with niche canal-opening, while the control group ( n = 58) received hysteroscopic curettage alone. Surgical parameters, postoperative recovery, complications, reintervention rates, and menstrual outcomes were compared. Results The observation group had significantly shorter operation time [20 (15,25) vs. 25 (20,31) min, p = 0.001], less intraoperative blood loss [5 (5,10) vs. 10 (10,50) mL, p = 0.002], lower complication rate [4.3% vs. 17.2%, p = 0.038], and lower reintervention rate [4.3% vs. 19.0%, p = 0.023]. No between-group differences were observed in postoperative hemoglobin decline, hospital stay, vaginal bleeding duration, human chorionic gonadotropin normalization time, menstrual recovery time, or residual scar myometrial thickness (all p > 0.05). Among patients with preoperative prolonged menstruation, menstrual duration improved in both groups ( p < 0.05), with a higher improvement rate in the observation group [75.0% vs. 23.1%, p = 0.005]. Conclusions FUAS pretreatment combined with hysteroscopic surgery is safe and effective for type II/III CSP. Adding diverticulum canal-opening to hysteroscopic curettage further optimized surgical outcomes by reducing operation time, intraoperative blood loss, complication rates, and the need for reintervention, while also significantly improving prolonged menstruation. This combined strategy may serve as an optimized minimally invasive alternative for patients desiring fertility, though long-term reproductive safety requires further verification.

title: Combined radiofrequency electromagnetic and pulsed magnetic field exposure attenuates histological and molecular markers of acute colonic injury in young rats.
abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease involves epithelial injury, ulceration, apoptosis, inflammation, and oxidative-stress dysregulation. Although bioelectromagnetic fields may modulate tissue responses, their effects on acute colitis remain unclear. This exploratory study assessed histological and molecular changes associated with combined radiofrequency electromagnetic field (RF-EMF) and pulsed magnetic field (PMF) exposure in acetic-acid-induced colitis.Thirty-two young female Wistar albino rats were allocated to Control, Colitis, Colitis+RF-EMF+PMF, or RF-EMF+PMF groups (n=8 each). Colitis was induced intrarectally with 4% acetic acid. Exposure comprised RF-EMF (27.12 MHz, 30 min/session, 12 cycles/day) and PMF (0.5 mT, continuous). After seven days, distal colonic specimens underwent semiquantitative histopathology, crypt morphometry, immunohistochemistry for CAS-3, IL-6, and TNF-α, and RT-qPCR for SIRT-1, NRF-2, and HO-1. Colitis caused histological injury, reduced crypt dimensions, increased CAS-3, IL-6, and TNF-α immunopositivity, and decreased SIRT-1, NRF-2, and HO-1 expression. Compared with untreated colitis, combined exposure increased crypt depth and width and reduced all three immunohistochemical markers (all Tukey-adjusted p<0.001). Overall histopathological injury was lower but not statistically significant (Dunn-adjusted p=0.068), whereas submucosal inflammatory infiltration decreased significantly (p=0.048). NRF-2 expression increased (Tukey-adjusted p=0.002); SIRT-1 and HO-1 increased numerically without statistical significance (p=0.057 and 0.134).Combined RF-EMF+PMF exposure was associated with preserved crypt architecture, reduced apoptotic and inflammatory immunopositivity, and increased NRF-2 expression. Absent barrier-function testing and incomplete RF dosimetry preclude conclusions regarding restored epithelial barrier function or established therapeutic efficacy.

title: Targeting Accelerated Aging in COPD: The AMICO (A Trial of Metformin In COpd) Trial Design.
abstract: Introduction Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is increasingly recognized as a disease of accelerated biological aging characterized by progressive lung function decline, emphysema progression and multiple age-related comorbidities. Current therapies improve symptoms and reduce exacerbations but have limited effects on disease progression. Metformin has demonstrated anti-aging properties through modulation of pathways involved in oxidative stress, inflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction and cellular senescence, making it a potential disease-modifying treatment in COPD. Methods AMICO (A Trial of Metformin In COPD) is an investigator-initiated, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase III trial conducted in anonymous . A total of 212 patients with clinically stable COPD, centrilobular emphysema on computed tomography, post-bronchodilator FEV 1 40%-70% predicted and accelerated FEV 1 decline (>40 mL·year -1 ) will be randomized (1:1) to receive metformin (850 mg twice daily) or matching placebo for 36 months in addition to standard COPD treatment. Assessments include pulmonary function, chest computed tomography, exercise capacity, health status, muscle strength, body composition, age associated comorbidities development and aging-related biomarkers.The primary endpoint is the annual rate of FEV 1 decline over 36 months. Secondary endpoints include emphysema progression, changes in diffusing capacity, COPD Assessment Test score, 6-minute walk distance, BODE index, handgrip strength, exacerbations, major cardiovascular events, cancer incidence and renal dysfunction. Conclusions AMICO is the first randomized trial specifically designed to evaluate metformin as a gerotherapeutic and disease-modifying intervention in COPD. The study may provide novel evidence supporting geroscience-based approaches to slow disease progression and improve long-term outcomes in patients with COPD.

title: Progression-free survival prediction in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma: where can we further improve?
abstract: Introduction Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) is a biologically heterogeneous disease in which approximately one-third of patients experience primary refractoriness or relapse despite modern chemoimmunotherapy. Although clinical prognostic indices remain the cornerstone of risk stratification, they incompletely capture the biological complexity underlying disease progression. Accurate prediction of progression-free survival (PFS) is essential to support personalized treatment strategies. Areas covered This review summarizes advances in PFS prediction in DLBCL, including clinical prognostic models, quantitative PET imaging, molecular and transcriptomic classification, genomic classifiers, tumor microenvironment profiling, circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA)-based biomarkers, and integrated multimodal prognostic models. Relevant literature was identified through PubMed, with ClinicalTrials.gov searched for ongoing clinical trials; searches were updated through 3 October 2026. We discuss the strengths, limitations, and clinical applicability of these approaches. Expert opinion Future prognostic models will increasingly rely on integrated multimodal frameworks combining clinical, imaging, molecular, immune, and dynamic response biomarkers. Among these, ctDNA has emerged as one of the most promising tools for measurable residual disease assessment. However, improving patient outcomes will require moving beyond prognostic accuracy toward predictive biomarkers capable of guiding personalized treatment selection across an evolving therapeutic landscape. Prospective validation, assay standardization, and demonstration of clinical utility will be essential for translating these approaches into routine practice.

title: A Belgian study assessing relapsing multiple sclerosis activity through automated magnetic resonance imaging volumetry.
abstract: Aim This study assessed to what extent ico brain ms , a commercially available artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) volumetry software, detected disease activity in patients with clinically and radiologically stable relapsing multiple sclerosis (RMS), and estimated its impact on radiologists' assessments. Patients and methods We retrospectively enrolled 111 RMS patients with two consecutive MRI scans at one year interval, without relapses, progression or radiological changes while remaining on stable therapy. MRI scans were analyzed by four radiologists acting independently, and by ico brain ms . The radiologists performed their assessments both without and with ico brain ms support and categorized patient status based on lesion and brain volume changes. Results Radiologists' detection of lesion activity non-significantly increased from 6.8% to 8.6% (McNemar p = 0.215; ordinal regression p = 0.06; sign-test p = 0.08) using ico brain ms . Detection of accelerated brain volume loss increased from 2.0% to 7.7% (all p < 0.01). Inter-reader agreement improved from 36% to 56% for lesions, and from 26% to 40% for brain loss (Kendall's W, p < 0.001). Ico brain ms detected new or significantly enlarged lesions in 16.2% and accelerated brain volume loss in 6.3% of participants. Conclusion AI-assisted MRI volumetry may support radiologists to detect subclinical disease activity in patients characterized as having stable disease.

title: Instance-Specific Brain Image Registration: Learning Deformable Fields from a Single Image Pair without External Datasets.
abstract: Objective To eliminate the reliance on large-scale external training datasets and achieve high-precision alignment for complex brain structures by overcoming the prevalent challenges of data scarcity and domain shifts in current deep learning-based registration methods. Approach: We propose a novel Instance-Specific Deep Brain Registration Framework that independently trains a dedicated model for each specific image pair. By reconceptualizing a single image pair as an internal dataset generator, we introduce a Multi-Scale Random Patch Learning strategy to construct a diverse local-to-global sample space. Architecturally, we design a Context-Aware Flow Predictor integrated with a Recurrent Context Transfer mechanism within a coarse-to-fine paradigm. Furthermore, a Topology-Aware Adaptive Optimization strategy is incorporated during the inference phase. By dynamically tracking the local spatial folding status, it adaptively adjusts spatial regularization to effectively suppress topological distortions while maximizing voxel-level accuracy. Main results: Extensive experiments on mono-modal, multi-modal, and pathological brain MRI datasets demonstrate that our method can handle large anatomical deformations without relying on external training datasets. It achieves highly competitive registration performance compared to mainstream population-based and implicit neural representation methods. Crucially, it balances this alignment precision with effective numerical topology preservation. Significance: This framework challenges the traditional population-based learning paradigm, offering a highly flexible, robust, and promising solution for practical neuroimage analysis, particularly in clinical scenarios characterized by extreme data scarcity and complex cross-modality variations.

title: Volumetric Chest CT Report Generation via State-Space Visual Prompting and Clinical-Fact Alignment.
abstract: Objective To address the memory bottlenecks of 3D sequence modeling and the factual hallucinations associated with cross-entropy optimization in automated 3D chest CT report generation. Approach We propose an end-to-end framework that couples perception refinement with clinical-fact alignment. First, a hybrid perception module integrates spatial visual encoding with a bidirectional state-space model to capture global anatomical topology at linear computational complexity. Second, a lesion-aware visual prompting module extracts key pathological signals through cross-view synergy and adaptive residual gating. Finally, the text decoder is fine-tuned with the Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) algorithm under an asymmetric composite reward, reducing its reliance on normal templates. Main results Experiments on the CTRG-Chest-548K dataset show that the proposed method achieves competitive natural language generation performance and, more importantly, a substantial improvement in clinical accuracy. The RadGraph F1 score increases from 41.89 to 44.63 relative to the strongest baseline, indicating reduced factual hallucination. Significance Combined with a 71% reduction in peak inference memory, these results indicate that the framework is a practical step toward deployable and clinically reliable automated CT interpretation.

title: 3D ultrasound shear wave elastography quantifies myocardial stiffness and anisotropy in the human heart.
abstract: Myocardial stiffness (MS) is a key property of diastolic cardiac function which is altered in various cardiomyopathies. Its quantitative evaluation remains challenging due to the myocardium's complex anisotropic fiber architecture and dynamic contraction. We developed a novel 3D shear wave elastography (3D-SWE) system suitable for clinical translation based on 3D ultrafast volumetric imaging for the quantitative assessment of myocardial stiffness in the human heart. Validation was performed on calibrated phantoms and ex vivo in porcine hearts compared to standard 2D-SWE. In vivo feasibility was demonstrated on healthy volunteers and patients with transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis. We demonstrated that 3D shear wave propagation can be observed in vivo and that 3D-SWE provides quantitative assessment of myocardium anisotropy through shear wave velocities along and across fibers and fractional anisotropy. In addition, myocardial stiffness was significantly elevated in cardiac amyloidosis patients compared to normal myocardium, whereas the fractional anisotropy was decreased. The feasibility of volumetric myocardial stiffness mapping on the human heart was demonstrated showing the potential of 3D-SWE as a clinically oriented tool for early diagnosis of cardiomyopathies such as cardiac amyloidosis.

title: 3D non-rigid motion correction using doppler-regularized optical flow for coronary ultrasound localization microscopy in beating heart.
abstract: Objectives Coronary microvascular disease, involving vessels smaller than 300 µm, contributes significantly to cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. However, direct visualization of coronary microcirculation remains challenging because current clinical imaging modalities lack the spatial and temporal resolution required to resolve the microvascular network. Ultrasound Localization Microscopy (ULM) enables imaging beyond the diffraction limit and can reveal coronary microvascular structures but is altered by large motion. This work addresses 3D non-rigid motion in coronary ULM to enable more accurate reconstruction and visualization of the coronary microvascular network. Approach: Here we developed a 3D non-rigid motion correction framework based on Optical Flow with Doppler velocity regularization to compensate for cardiac motion in 3D ULM of beating rat hearts. Main results: The method was validated in perfused ex vivo beating rat hearts imaged with ultrafast 3D ultrasound. Motion correction enhanced microbubbles tracking density and vessels delineation, enabling visualization of microvessels below 100 µm and velocity measurements with spatial resolution of at least 40 µm. Significance: This framework advances volumetric assessment of coronary microcirculation, facilitating longer acquisition windows and may support future cardiovascular research and clinical applications by overcoming motion-induced limitations in 3D coronary ULM.

title: Motion-guided semi-supervised learning with dynamic kernels for cardiac cine segmentation.
abstract: Objective Accurate segmentation of full cardiac cine magnetic resonance (CMR) sequences is crucial for clinical diagnosis. Although deep learning models have become the standard for this task, they typically require exhaustive frame-by-frame supervision, making manual data annotation prohibitively time-consuming. Approach To address this, we propose a novel motion-guided semi-supervised spatiotemporal framework that propagates sparse supervision from the label of the end-diastolic (ED) frame to the entire sequence. Our framework jointly optimizes motion estimation and segmentation. First, a motion decoder estimates dense displacement fields to warp the ED label, generating high-fidelity pseudo-labels for unannotated frames. Concurrently, the segmentation network employs a Temporal Kernel Segmentation (TKS) module with dynamic convolutions to adaptively capture rapid cardiac deformations, alongside a Multi-Scale Spatial Propagator (MSP) to recover fine anatomical boundaries. The motion-derived pseudo-labels directly supervise the segmentation network, ensuring temporal coherence. Main results Extensive experiments on a multi-center cohort from three clinical centers demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms the compared methods, achieving superior segmentation accuracy and robust generalization capabilities. Significance The proposed framework effectively mitigates the burden of manual data annotation while providing temporally coherent full-cycle cardiac analysis, holding significant potential for efficient and reliable clinical assessment of cardiovascular diseases.

Although deep learning models have become the standard for this task, they typically require exhaustive frame-by-frame supervision, making manual data annotation prohibitively time-consuming.
