title: VQ-CSDN: A Vector Quantized Content-Stain Decoupling Network for Stain Normalization of H&E Histopathology Images.
abstract: Stain normalization is a fundamental preprocessing technique in digital and computational pathology, and it is important for improving the consistency of clinical diagnosis by reducing color heterogeneity. However, existing stain normalization methods are often limited by content-stain entanglement and an ambiguously modeled content-stain relationship, resulting in unstable structural preservation, cross-center adaptation burden, and sensitivity to template selection. To address these limitations, we propose a Vector-Quantized Content-Stain Decoupling Network (VQ-CSDN) that decouples structure-defining content from stain appearance and learns a center-specific content-to-stain mapping, enabling structure-preserving, template-free stain transfer from unseen source centers without source-specific retraining. VQ-CSDN employs two independent encoders to extract content and stain features respectively and a generator for reconstruction. To better characterize cross-center content feature spaces and capture staining styles, we introduce vector quantization with a global content codebook shared across centers and center-specific stain codebooks. Moreover, a content-to-stain module directly infers stain features from the content feature and a target staining style, enabling end-to-end stain transfer without template selection. To further promote structural fidelity and enhance staining style separability, we propose center-specific gradient-driven discriminators that jointly assess center-level stain conformity and the morphological consistency of generated images. Extensive experiments on multiple public and private pathology datasets show that VQ-CSDN consistently enhances normalization quality, reflected by increased SSIM/PSNR and decreased FID, and further improves downstream benign-malignant classification performance (AUC 0.9738) over state-of-the-art methods.

title: Synergizing SAM2 and U-Mamba as Mutual Teachers in a Dual-Branch Dynamic Knowledge Transfer Network for Orbital Segmentation.
abstract: Accurate segmentation of orbital structures in thyroid eye disease (TED) is critical for clinical staging and surgical planning. However, as an under-explored task, orbital multi-organ segmentation suffers from inherent data scarcity, resulting in substantial domain gaps when directly applying general-purpose segmentation models. These foundation models often lack sufficient exposure to orbital imaging data, producing anatomically implausible yet overconfident predictions. To address this challenge, we propose a Dual-Branch Dynamic Knowledge Transfer Network (DDKTN), which integrates the global semantic generalization capability of SAM2 with the fine-grained structural modeling strength of U-Mamba. Specifically, a Dynamic Feature Interaction (DFI) mechanism enables adaptively controlled inter-branch knowledge transfer, facilitating a progressive transition from SAM2-guided global semantics to U-Mamba-driven structural refinement. Moreover, a Bidirectional Consensus Confidence (BCC) regularization mechanism identifies consensus and discrepancy regions between the foundation and domain-specific branches, enforcing anatomy-aware consistency via mutual supervision. In addition, a Prompt Adaptation Module (PAM) leverages the anatomical sensitivity of the domain-specific branch to automatically generate structured prompts, thereby injecting reliable anatomical priors into SAM2. Experiments conducted on a private orbital CT dataset and a public coronal MRI benchmark demonstrate that DDKTN achieves superior performance, with average Dice scores of 93.68% and 94.65%, respectively. Ablation studies further validate the effectiveness of each component in improving generalization and anatomical fidelity. The implementation of our method is available at https://github.com/zltshadow/DDKTN.

title: Identification of local nonlinear shear-wave dynamics using Volterra kernels: application to prostate cancer detection.
abstract: Cancer remains a major health concern worldwide. Shear-wave elastography (SWE) holds promise for cancer detection by quantifying linear elastic changes in tissue through shear-wave (SW) velocity estimation. However, shear viscosity and nonlinearity are often over-looked, despite their potential as additional biomarkers. This study evaluates the visco-hyperelastic properties of soft tissue, including linear shear modulus, shear viscosity, and shear nonlinearity. We propose using Volterra kernels to characterize local nonlinear SW dynamics, with kernel identification based on SW particle velocity measurements at adjacent locations. The method was validated using in-silico simulations and in-vitro gelatin phantoms. To evaluate its clinical relevance, we applied the method for prostate cancer (PCa) detection. To our knowledge, this is the first in-vivo assessment of voxel-based visco-hyperelastic properties of the prostate. In 90 patients, our results indicated that the linear kernel correlated with the linear shear modulus, while the quadratic kernel reflected both viscosity and nonlinearity. A convolutional neural network trained on these parameters with registered histopathology as ground truth achieved area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values of 0.60 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.57, 0.62) and 0.66 (95% CI: 0.64, 0.68) for PCa detection, respectively-both significantly outperforming the linear shear modulus (AUC of 0.54; 95% CI, 0.52 to 0.56). Our findings suggest that Volterra kernels reflect information related to the visco-hyperelastic properties of prostate tissue, highlighting the potential of viscosity and nonlinearity as additional biomarkers for PCa detection.

title: Does More Speech Therapy Lead to Better Results in Childhood Apraxia of Speech? A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of the Available Evidence.
abstract: Background In recent years there has been a significant increase in the number and quality of childhood apraxia of speech (CAS) treatment research published. Much of this research has focussed on establishing treatment efficacy and identifying treatment components. A smaller subset of the literature has looked at treatment intensity, such as comparing therapy delivered twice per week with four times per week, however this literature has not been compared across interventions. Aims This systematic review and meta-analysis examines cumulative intervention intensity and its components (dose per session, dose frequency, intervention duration-number of weeks) and reported treatment effects to understand whether there is a relationship between dose and effect in specific treatments or overall. Methods A systematic search and review was registered with Prospero (CRD420251107259). Twelve electronic databases were searched supplemented by handsearching references lists. Included studies were coded for CAS diagnosis confidence, methodological quality, dose characteristics, and treatment outcomes. Standard mean difference (SMD), an effect size metric equivalent to Cohen's d, was calculated for 25 included papers and weighted Pearson's correlations performed to identify relationships between dose characteristics and treatment outcomes. Main contribution This paper is the first to (1) create omnibus standard effect sizes across diverse interventions and (2) show the relationship between intensity and treatment outcome in children with CAS. The omnibus SMD across studies with three or more participants for treated items was 1.22 (confidence interval 0.76-1.67), a large effect, and for generalisation items was 0.66 (confidence interval 0.46-0.85) which is a moderate effect. These results show that CAS treatment works in well-controlled studies when delivered at least twice per week for at least 45 min per session. The relationship between intensity variables and generalisation SMD was less clear with weeks of therapy being moderately correlated (r = 0.39) and none of the other variables showing any relationship with study SMD. These results should be interpreted carefully as there was significant missing data and limited range in some variables. Researchers need to include more standard intensity information in reporting their results. Conclusions Treatment for CAS is effective and leads to moderate generalisation; more weeks of therapy leads to stronger gains than fewer weeks of therapy. What this paper adds What is already known on this subject CAS is a neurological-based motor speech disorder that originates in childhood for which there are a number of effective treatments. For this population, high intensity treatment is recommended-over 100 production trials per session, 2-5 sessions per week, across an extended period. In studies which directly compare intensity of variables, more therapy (e.g. 20 sessions) results in greater improvement than less therapy (e.g. 10 sessions). There are no previous meta-analyses of intensity variables-dose, dose frequency, treatment duration, or cumulative intervention intensity in CAS What this study adds to the existing knowledge This study compiles data from 25 studies with a low risk of bias and high CAS diagnostic confidence in a meta-analysis of the dose effects of CAS treatment. The meta-analysis shows that CAS treatment in general works. Most studies had 2-4 sessions per week across 3-12 weeks. Within this narrow band of intensity, a significant correlation was shown between the number of weeks of therapy and outcome. There is no significant evidence for CAS therapy less frequently than twice per week at this time. Eight different treatments demonstrated efficacy for improving speech outcomes in children with CAS. What are the clinical implications of this study? Provided they are delivered at least twice per week for at least 12 sessions, with greater improvements when treatment extends over more weeks, selection of any of the included treatments should result in improved speech where the child being treated is similar to children in the research. The following treatments were shown to be effective for CAS: Integral stimulation treatments including Dynamic Temporal and Tactile Cueing, Kaufman-Speech to Language Protocol, Motor Speech Treatment Protocol, Nuffield Dyspraxia Programme-3rd Edition, Rapid Syllable Transition Treatment, Speech Motor Chaining and Ultrasound Biofeedback alone and the combination of Speech Motor Chaining with Ultrasound Biofeedback. Practitioner points Therapy must be sufficiently frequent and sustained: Evidence shows that CAS treatment is effective when therapy is provided at least twice per week, over a minimum of 12 sessions, for 45 min per session with total weeks of therapy being the only intensity variable consistently associated with treatment outcomes. Dose matters, both within and across sessions: Clinicians should prioritise the number of production trials and ensure adequate cumulative intervention intensity. Sessions with low active practice time or insufficient trials are unlikely to produce meaningful change. Eight treatments are effective for CAS: Integral Stimulation including Dynamic Temporal and Tactile Cueing (DTTC), Kaufman Speech to Language Program (K-SLP), Motor Speech Treatment Protocol (MSTP), Nuffield Dyspraxia Programme (3rd ed; NDP3), Rapid Syllable Transition Treatment (ReST), Speech Motor Chaining (SMC), Ultrasound Biofeedback, and SMC + Ultrasound Biofeedback combined. Clinicians should consider the client's speech needs and overall profile when selecting from the treatments that have demonstrated effectiveness.

There is no significant evidence for CAS therapy less frequently than twice per week at this time. Eight different treatments demonstrated efficacy for improving speech outcomes in children with CAS. What are the clinical implications of this study? Provided they are delivered at least twice per week for at least 12 sessions, with greater improvements when treatment extends over more weeks, selection of any of the included treatments should result in improved speech where the child being treated is similar to children in the research. The following treatments were shown to be effective for CAS: Integral stimulation treatments including Dynamic Temporal and Tactile Cueing, Kaufman-Speech to Language Protocol, Motor Speech Treatment Protocol, Nuffield Dyspraxia Programme-3rd Edition, Rapid Syllable Transition Treatment, Speech Motor Chaining and Ultrasound Biofeedback alone and the combination of Speech Motor Chaining with Ultrasound Biofeedback.

Practitioner points

Therapy must be sufficiently frequent and sustained: Evidence shows that CAS treatment is effective when therapy is provided at least twice per week, over a minimum of 12 sessions, for 45 min per session with total weeks of therapy being the only intensity variable consistently associated with treatment outcomes. Dose matters, both within and across sessions: Clinicians should prioritise the number of production trials and ensure adequate cumulative intervention intensity. Sessions with low active practice time or insufficient trials are unlikely to produce meaningful change. Eight treatments are effective for CAS: Integral Stimulation including Dynamic Temporal and Tactile Cueing (DTTC), Kaufman Speech to Language Program (K-SLP), Motor Speech Treatment Protocol (MSTP), Nuffield Dyspraxia Programme (3rd ed; NDP3), Rapid Syllable Transition Treatment (ReST), Speech Motor Chaining (SMC), Ultrasound Biofeedback, and SMC + Ultrasound Biofeedback combined. Clinicians should consider the client's speech needs and overall profile when selecting from the treatments that have demonstrated effectiveness.

title: Prognostic Value of Early Dynamic Changes in Skeletal Muscle Index for Unresectable Lung Squamous Cell Carcinoma: A Prospective Landmark Analysis.
abstract: Objectives To investigate the prognostic value of early dynamic skeletal muscle index (ΔSMI) changes in unresectable lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC) and explore associations with systemic inflammatory and nutritional markers. Materials and methods This prospective study enrolled 76 patients with unresectable Stage III/IV LUSC. Routine computed tomography images at the fourth thoracic vertebra were analyzed before and 90 days posttreatment to quantify body composition changes. Progression-free survival (PFS) was evaluated using landmark analysis to prevent immortal time bias. Multivariate Cox regression identified independent prognostic factors utilizing optimal cut-offs from the maxstat algorithm. Results Only rapid skeletal muscle depletion (ΔSMI ≤ -5.0%) emerged as an independent predictor of adverse PFS (HR = 2.030, 95% CI: 1.132-3.642, p = 0.018), alongside clinical Stage IV (p < 0.001); overall ΔBMI lacked prognostic significance. Patients with rapid muscle loss exhibited persistently elevated C-reactive protein and steeper hemoglobin declines, reflecting an unresolved inflammatory and hypercatabolic state. Subgroup analyses confirmed ΔSMI's consistent prognostic value across age, sex, and stage (all P-interaction > 0.05). Conclusion Early ΔSMI loss, not overall weight variation, independently predicts poor PFS in unresectable LUSC. Routine CT-based body composition monitoring provides a critical window to identify high-risk patients for interventions targeting the muscle-inflammation axis. Trial registration Chinese Clinical Trial Registry: ChiCTR2500104777.

title: WIse CHoices in the ICU (WICH-ICU): Protocol and Statistical Analysis Plan for a Stepped-Wedge Cluster Randomized Trial of Choosing Wisely Interventions in Swedish Intensive Care Units.
abstract: Background Healthcare overuse, including unnecessary diagnostic testing and procedures, contributes to patient harm, increased healthcare costs, and resource waste. The Choosing Wisely initiative aims to reduce low-value care through evidence-based recommendations. However, limited evidence exists regarding the safety and effectiveness of implementing Choosing Wisely recommendations in intensive care settings. Methods The WICH-ICU is a registry-based stepped-wedge cluster randomized controlled trial designed to evaluate the implementation of specific Choosing Wisely interventions in Swedish intensive care units (ICUs). The study will include adult patients treated in participating Swedish ICUs. The intervention consists of three parts of the Choosing Wisely recommendations: (1) reduced frequency of arterial blood gas sampling, (2) reduced routine laboratory testing, and (3) reduced routine chest radiography. The primary outcome is 30-day mortality. Secondary outcomes include ICU length of stay, duration of mechanical ventilation (invasive and noninvasive), continuous renal replacement therapy duration, and ICU readmission within 72 h. Intervention data, testing intensity (arterial blood gas samples, laboratory tests, and chest radiographs per patient-day), will be collected through local monitoring, while outcome data will be obtained from the Swedish Intensive Care Registry (SIR). The stepped-wedge design allows each participating ICU to serve as its own control, with randomized timing of intervention implementation. Discussion This study will provide evidence on the safety and effectiveness of implementing Choosing Wisely recommendations in intensive care settings. The stepped-wedge cluster randomized design minimizes contamination while allowing all participating sites to eventually receive the intervention. The results will inform evidence-based de-implementation strategies in critical care. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT07013175.

title: Long-Term Fate of Resorbed Adjacent Teeth Associated With Impacted Maxillary Canines Following Orthodontic Treatment: A Systematic Review.
abstract: Limited evidence exists on the long-term prognosis of resorptive lesions in teeth adjacent to impacted maxillary canines' post-orthodontic treatment. To systematically evaluate the long-term radiographic status of resorbed maxillary incisor roots following orthodontic correction of adjacent ectopically erupting canines. Comprehensive electronic and manual searches across five databases identified retrospective or prospective studies assessing long-term Cone Beam Computed Tomography (CBCT) or radiographic follow-up of resorbed adjacent teeth. Data selection, extraction and bias assessment were performed independently. Five studies with moderate risk of bias met inclusion criteria. The combined sample consisted of 54 male and 123 female. Findings indicate that orthodontic management of impacted canines carries minimal risk of progressive root resorption or periodontal deterioration in adjacent incisors. Resorbed incisors largely retained vitality and functional stability, with no mobility beyond Grade 1 and resorption lacunae often became shallower over time. Marked heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis. Long-term outcomes are favourable, with most resorbed root surfaces showing natural remodelling and minimal need for endodontic intervention. title: Clinical Trial: Capsule Sponge as a Non-Endoscopic Monitoring Tool in Eosinophilic Oesophagitis-A Prospective Real-World Multicentre Study.
abstract: Background and aims Eosinophilic oesophagitis (EoE) is a chronic inflammatory condition requiring repeat endoscopy and biopsy for histological monitoring, which is invasive, resource-intensive and burdensome for patients. The capsule sponge (CS) offers a potential non-invasive alternative. We evaluated the diagnostic accuracy, feasibility and patient acceptability of CS versus endoscopic biopsies for monitoring disease activity in adult patients. Methods A real-world prospective multicentre cohort study was conducted across three NHS sites in England from August 2023 to June 2025. Adults with established EoE without oesophageal strictures underwent same-day endoscopy and CS using the Endosign device. Histological activity was defined as ≥ 15 eosinophils per high-power field or 0.3 mm 2 on endoscopic biopsy histology and CS respectively. Symptom burden was assessed using the Dysphagia Symptom Questionnaire, endoscopic severity using the EoE Endoscopic Reference Score and patient acceptability via structured questionnaire. Results 136 patients (164 paired episodes) from three secondary care hospitals successfully swallowed CS with sufficient sampling; CS swallowing success rate was 92.7%. Median age was 45 years (IQR 34.8-56); 92/136 (67.6%) were male. CS demonstrated sensitivity 76.3%, specificity 89.5%, PPV 80.4%, NPV 87.0% and overall accuracy 84.8% (Cohen's κ = 0.67). AUC was 0.904 (95% CI 0.856-0.953). Patient acceptability recorded 96.7% found CS acceptable, 78.8% preferred it over endoscopy, and 90.8% would repeat the procedure. No complications occurred. Conclusions CS is a safe, feasible, accurate and highly acceptable less-invasive tool for monitoring EoE. Its implementation could improve care pathways, reducing the need for repeated endoscopic biopsies while maintaining diagnostic reliability, with potential to reduce service burden, carbon emissions and improve patient experience. Trial registration CoSiE: IRAS number: 314770; ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT06501274; QuBiE: UK Clinical Trial registry identifier: ISRCTN14071734; Trial number: 10083253.

title: Association of Polygenic Risk Score for Suicidal Behavior With Ventral Prefrontal Morphology in Bipolar Disorder.
abstract: Background Bipolar disorder (BD) studies consistently implicate the ventral prefrontal cortex (VPFC) in association with suicidal behaviors. A suicidal behavior polygenic risk score (PRS) can now be computed to test whether elevated genetic risk for suicidal behavior is associated with variation in VPFC gray matter and/or suicidal behavior history. Methods We explored relationships among a PRS previously associated with suicidal behavior, VPFC morphology, and suicidal behavior in 376 individuals of European ancestry (mean age 30y; 57% female): 225 with BD (76 suicide attempters (SAs), 149 non-suicide attempters (NSAs)) and 151 healthy control individuals (HCs). We calculated PRS and performed magnetic resonance imaging to assess VPFC (inferior frontal gyrus (IFG) and orbitofrontal cortex) cortical thickness and surface area. Associations were examined among PRS, diagnosis, suicide attempt history, and brain measures. Results Among individuals with BD, those with higher PRS showed decreased right VPFC surface area, primarily due to IFG reductions (p < 0.01). A significant group (SA, NSA, HC)-by-PRS interaction was observed for right IFG cortical surface area (p < 0.05); NSAs with high vs. low PRS had significantly smaller right IFG surface area. The mean PRS was highest for SAs, then NSAs, and lowest for HCs; however, differences did not reach significance. Conclusions These findings suggest this suicide PRS may reflect genetic mechanisms influencing IFG differences in BD. Given the modest sample size, replication of these preliminary findings in large-scale diverse cohorts is required to determine whether including this PRS and/or the corresponding IFG values could improve multimodal BD suicidal behavior prediction algorithms.

title: Automated urine analysis of atypical urothelial cells for urothelial carcinoma: a prospective study.
abstract: Objectives To prospectively evaluate the diagnostic value of atypical urothelial cells (Atyp.C), an automatically determined quantitative parameter of the Sysmex UF-5000 urine particle analyser (Sysmex Corp., Kobe, Japan), as a non-invasive biomarker for urothelial carcinoma (UC). Early diagnosis of UC remains challenging despite advances in diagnostic techniques. While non-invasive urine cytology has high diagnostic value, clinical evidence for Atyp.C in urine remains unclear. Quantification of Atyp.C in urine may improve non-invasive UC disease diagnostics. Patients and methods Urine samples from 234 patients who underwent invasive urological intervention for non-malignant conditions (control group [CG]) or UC (intervention group [IG]) were considered. Based on histopathology, the IG was subclassified into low-grade (LG) and high-grade (HG) UC and was further grouped into non-muscle-invasive (non-MI) and MI UC. Patients who received neoadjuvant chemotherapy were analysed separately. Atyp.C of ≥0.1 Atyp.C/μL were defined as positive and were automatically quantified using the Sysmex UF-5000 urine particle analyser, which classifies epithelial cells with disproportionately high nucleic acid content relative to cell size. Smoking state, urinary tract infection (UTI), and micro-/macrohaematuria, were evaluated as potential confounding factors. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was performed to assess explorative diagnostic Atyp.C performance. Results The Atyp.C concentration was higher in the IG than in the CG (mean [SEM] 0.53 [0.1] vs 0.29 [0.1] Atyp.C/μL; P = 0.004), with a sensitivity of 0.59. HGUC exhibited higher Atyp.C levels (mean [SEM] 0.85 [0.2] Atyp.C/μL, P < 0.001) and a sensitivity of 0.73. MI UC showed the highest Atyp.C concentrations (mean [SEM] 0.95 [0.4] Atyp.C/μL; P = 0.004) and sensitivity of 0.78. ROC analysis demonstrated the highest diagnostic accuracy for MI UC (area under the ROC curve = 0.75). ROC analysis was exploratory and lacked external validation. UTI was a significant confounder for Atyp.C quantification. Conclusion The Atyp.C are elevated in HGUC, particularly in MI disease, supporting their potential as a non-invasive diagnostic biomarker in UC condition.

title: DFDBA With or Without Platelet-Rich Fibrin in Maxillary Sinus Augmentation: A Randomized Split-Mouth Clinical Trial.
abstract: Objectives To compare histologic and histomorphometric outcomes after bilateral lateral maxillary sinus augmentation with demineralized freeze-dried bone allograft (DFDBA) alone versus DFDBA combined with platelet-rich fibrin (PRF), and to report 1-year prosthetic follow-up of the restored implants. Materials and methods This randomized split-mouth clinical trial included subjects requiring bilateral lateral maxillary sinus augmentation before implant placement. In each subject, one sinus was randomly assigned to DFDBA alone and the contralateral sinus to DFDBA combined with leukocyte- and platelet-rich fibrin (L-PRF) and injectable PRF (i-PRF). Bone biopsy specimens were harvested at the clinically relevant 6-month implant placement time point. The primary outcome was newly formed bone. Secondary histomorphometric outcomes were residual graft material, connective tissue, and fibrosis; inflammation and necrosis were assessed histologically. Clinical and radiographic prosthetic follow-up was performed 1 year after definitive prosthetic loading. Paired comparisons were performed using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test. Median newly formed bone was 48.72% (IQR, 33.33%-63.33%) on the PRF side and 45.76% (IQR, 37.14%-54.90%) on the non-PRF side (p = 0.5). The lower connective tissue proportion on the PRF side may suggest altered tissue maturation; however, this secondary finding should be interpreted cautiously. Definitively restored implants showed 100% prosthetic survival during 1-year follow-up. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT07348198; https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07348198. This clinical trial was not registered prior to participant recruitment and randomization.

title: Fully automated AI-based quantification of tumour volume on PSMA PET-CT images is associated with overall survival in prostate cancer.
abstract: Introduction Artificial intelligence (AI)-based models can quantify tumour volume in positron emission tomography (PET) examinations using prostate specific membrane antigen (PSMA). It is, however, unknown whether this measurement of tumour volume contains prognostic information. The purpose of this study was to examine whether tumour volume measured by AI is associated with overall survival in patients with prostate cancer. Methods Patients who had undergone [ 18 F]PSMA-1007 PET-CT due to primary staging or biochemical recurrence (BCR) of prostate cancer at our centre were retrospectively included and followed for 5 years. Automatic quantification of tumour volume was performed using a previously developed fully automated AI model from our research group for PSMA PET-CT analysis, without manual corrections. The tumour volume for the prostate, lymph nodes, and bone was calculated and summarized as Total Lesion Volume (TLV) and divided categorically (no detectable tumour, low, and high) as well as aggregated to whole-body TLV and divided into tertiles (low, intermediate, and high). Mortality rates were compared using Cox-regression and adjusted for age. Results Among 267 patients in the final analysis, 48 (18%) died during follow-up. Whole-body TLV was significantly associated with mortality in the combined cohort (p = 0.001) and in the primary staging cohort (p = 0.014) but did not reach statistical significance in the BCR cohort (p = 0.061). Conclusions Fully automated AI-derived TLV from PSMA PET-CT was associated with overall survival. These findings support the potential role of AI-based tumour quantification as a potential prognostic biomarker in prostate cancer.

title: Early Changes in Peripancreatic Mesenteric Fat Beyond Weight Loss Predict Durability of Hepatic Improvements in MASLD.
abstract: Aims Various visceral adipose tissue depots exhibit heterogeneous metabolic properties. This study aims to explore whether specific abdominal fat compartments differentially predict loss of sustained treatment response to lifestyle interventions in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). Materials and methods Consecutive treatment-naïve MASLD patients were prospectively enrolled from January 2015 to March 2024, with a 96-week follow-up period. Liver fat content, preperitoneal fat thickness (PFT), peripancreatic mesenteric fat thickness (MFT1), periumbilical mesenteric fat thickness (MFT2) and perirenal fat thickness (PrFT) were quantified using magnetic resonance imaging. Liver stiffness measurement (LSM) was assessed by 2D-SWE. Treatment responses were evaluated at 48 and 96 weeks, and the primary outcome was loss of response at 96 weeks. Results A total of 631 MASLD patients (mean age: 41.5 ± 13.8 years; 72.0% male) were included. Logistic regression analyses revealed that a greater 48-week relative decrease in MFT1 (per 10% relative reduction), rather than in MFT2, PFT or PrFT, was independently associated with lower odds of losing MRI-PDFF response (OR: 0.48, 95% CI: 0.34-0.69, p < 0.001) and LSM response (OR: 0.53, 95% CI: 0.28-0.99, p = 0.046) at 96 weeks. Receiver operating characteristic curve analyses indicated that relative changes in MFT1 showed discriminatory ability for the loss of MRI-PDFF and LSM responses, with areas under the curves of 0.70 (95% CI: 0.64-0.76) and 0.77 (95% CI: 0.67-0.88), respectively. Conclusions Early changes in MFT1 were associated with subsequent loss of response in hepatic steatosis and fibrosis, suggesting potential prognostic value for hepatic response durability in MASLD.

title: Cognitive Cerebellum Structure and Functional Connectivity in Relation to Executive Functions in Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder.
abstract: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) has been primarily linked to abnormalities within the cortico-striato-thalamo-cortical circuit; however, recent evidence suggests that the posterior cerebellum may contribute to the executive dysfunction observed in the disorder. In 56 adults (28 OCD, 28 controls), we assessed executive functions using the BANFE-2 battery and integrated structural MRI (T1) and resting-state fMRI. Although the Global Executive Index did not differ significantly between groups, patients with OCD showed significantly lower scores in the inhibitory control/decision-making domain relative to controls. We quantified cortical thickness and volume (% intracranial volume) in Crus I/II and lobule VI using CERES and examined resting-state functional connectivity (seed-to-voxel) in CONN, adjusting for age, sex, medication, and depression. Compared with controls, patients with OCD showed reduced bilateral cortical thickness in Crus I/II and lobule VI (false discovery rate-corrected q < 0.05; β_OCD - Control = -0.27 to -0.59; ηp 2 = 0.34-0.55), with no significant volumetric differences after correction for multiple comparisons. Functional connectivity results revealed a mixed pattern, including focal hyperconnectivity (e.g., left Crus I with primary auditory cortex; left Crus II with occipital cortex) and widespread intracerebellar hypoconnectivity. In addition, significant Group × executive-function interactions (p-family-wise error < 0.05) emerged mainly for bilateral Crus I (Global Executive Index and working memory/flexibility) and left lobule VI (inhibition/decision-making), indicating that the relationship between cerebellar connectivity and executive performance differs in OCD relative to controls. These findings support an expanded model of executive circuits in OCD that incorporates the posterior cerebellum as a relevant node.

title: Convergence of Cerebrospinal Fluid Neuronal Biomarker Burden and MRI Lesion Pattern and Its Association With Short-Term Outcome in Neuroinfectious Diseases.
abstract: Background Neuroinfectious diseases (NDs) are potentially treatable conditions associated with substantial morbidity, but their clinical course remains difficult to predict. While specific MRI patterns are characteristic of distinct aetiologies, their prognostic value remains poorly investigated. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) biomarkers of neuroaxonal and synaptic damage have been linked to clinical outcome. We investigated the association of CSF biomarkers and MRI findings with short-term outcome in NDs. Methods In this multicentre cohort study, CSF was analysed in 123 patients with NDs and in 95 non-neuroinflammatory controls. Concentrations of beta-synuclein, SNAP-25, neurogranin and neurofilament light chain protein (NfL) were measured. MRI findings were classified by topography and lesion pattern. Clinical outcome at discharge was assessed using the modified Rankin Scale and degree of recovery. Results All CSF biomarkers were higher in ND patients with MRI abnormalities than in those without MRI abnormalities and/or controls, also within the (meningo-)encephalitis group. Temporal lobe involvement was the MRI pattern most consistently associated with elevated CSF biomarkers, even after multivariable adjustment including aetiology, and was independently associated with poor functional outcome and incomplete recovery. A global neuronal biomarker burden derived by principal component analysis (PC1) improved the fit of outcome models including MRI lesion pattern, with both temporal lobe involvement and PC1 remaining independently associated with outcome at discharge. Conclusions MRI lesion pattern and CSF biomarkers of synaptic and neuroaxonal damage were independently associated with short-term outcome in NDs, suggesting that they capture complementary aspects of disease severity. Prospective studies are needed to establish their prognostic value.

title: Clinical Diagnosis Versus Plain Radiography for Diabetic Foot Osteomyelitis: A Prospective Study of Diagnostic Agreement in a Resource-Limited Settings.
abstract: Diabetic foot osteomyelitis (DFO) is a serious complication of diabetic foot ulcers, particularly in advanced infections. In low-resource settings, access to medical imaging may be limited. This study evaluated the diagnostic agreement between a composite clinical approach (clinical assessment plus probe-to-bone test) compared with plain radiography for diagnosing DFO, including performance across ulcer categories. A prospective cohort study was conducted from December 2021 to January 2025 among patients with suspected DFO. Participants underwent clinical evaluation, risk factor assessment, ulcer history, SINBAD classification, probe-to-bone testing and plain radiography. Diagnostic performance measures were calculated. Given the absence of a gold standard reference test (bone biopsy) in this low-resource setting, performance measures represent comparative diagnostic agreement with plain radiography rather than absolute diagnostic accuracy. A total of 166 patients with deep foot ulcers were enrolled. Composite clinical diagnosis identified osteomyelitis in 117 patients and excluded it in 49. Plain radiography was positive in 96 of 117 composite positive cases, while 21 were discordant; all 49 composite negative cases were radiographically negative. The composite approach showed 100% sensitivity, 70% specificity and 87.3% overall agreement. Sensitivity remained 100% across ulcer categories, while specificity increased significantly from 63.8% in SINBAD-4 ulcers to 77.8% in SINBAD-5 ulcers, improving agreement from 86.1% to 89.7%. In conclusion, composite clinical diagnosis demonstrates substantial agreement with plain radiography in this cohort of patients with suspected DFO. This can provide a practical adjunct for clinical assessment in resource-limited settings where imaging is unavailable or difficult to interpret but should not be considered a definitive diagnostic test in the absence of an independent reference standard.

title: Radiotherapy for Cervical Cancer: Technical Advances, Clinical Applications, and Future Perspectives.
abstract: Radiotherapy is an essential treatment modality for cervical cancer and has evolved substantially with advances in image guidance and treatment delivery. This review summarizes recent technological developments in external beam radiotherapy and brachytherapy, their clinical applications, and future directions, with particular consideration of Japanese practice in an international context. In external beam radiotherapy, conventional techniques incorporating central shielding are increasingly being replaced by intensity-modulated radiotherapy (IMRT) and volumetric-modulated arc therapy (VMAT). Daily three-dimensional image-guided radiotherapy (3D-IGRT) is essential for the safe implementation of these techniques because of substantial uterine motion and deformation. In brachytherapy, the transition from two-dimensional point-based prescription to three-dimensional image-guided treatment has enabled individualized assessment of target coverage and doses to organs at risk. Although magnetic resonance imaging-based brachytherapy is internationally recommended, computed tomography-based planning predominates in Japan and has achieved favorable outcomes, despite some studies reporting lower cumulative target doses than those recommended internationally. Intracavitary/interstitial brachytherapy (IC/IS BT) further improves dose distribution by combining intracavitary applicators with interstitial needles, particularly when adequate target coverage cannot be achieved with standard intracavitary brachytherapy alone. Future advances may include artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted treatment planning and adaptive workflows, tissue spacers to overcome anatomical constraints, and the incorporation of genomic, multi-omics, and radiomics information. Integrating these approaches may enable cervical cancer radiotherapy to progress beyond increasingly safe and precise treatment toward personalized care tailored to individual patient and tumor characteristics.

title: Hepatic Steatosis in People With Chronic Hepatitis B in Africa: Prevalence, Correlates, and Clinical Significance.
abstract: To address data gaps around metabolic liver disease in Africa, within the Hepatitis B in Africa Collaborative Network (HEPSANET), we evaluated participants with chronic hepatitis B virus infection (CHB) for steatotic liver disease (SLD) using transient elastography with controlled attenuation parameter (CAP). Using multivariable logistic regression, we identified sociodemographic, anthropometric, and clinical associations with SLD (CAP ≥ 248 dB/m), and evaluated whether SLD severity was independently associated with fibrosis. Short-term impacts of SLD on mortality were also assessed with Cox proportional hazards analysis. We also evaluated the diagnostic performance of B-mode ultrasound for SLD, with CAP as reference. Across 6 countries and 1601 participants (age range, 12-80 years; 39.5% female; 4% with diabetes; 11% unhealthy alcohol use; median body mass index, 24.4), 421 (26.3%) had SLD; 219 (13.7%) had severe steatosis (CAP ≥ 280 dB/m). Older age, male sex, overweight and obesity, and HIV-negative status were associated with SLD. After adjusting for age, sex, HIV status, HBV treatment, and country, severe steatosis, but not mild and moderate forms (i.e., 248-279 dB/m), was associated with a 8.4% (95%, 1.9%-14.9%) increased probability of fibrosis. Over limited follow-up (median 2.69 years) and small number of deaths, SLD was not associated with all-cause or liver-related mortality. B-mode ultrasound had low sensitivity for SLD, overall or when severe, but specificity was 95%. In conclusion, SLD was common in people with CHB in Africa and its severe form was associated with liver fibrosis. These data support screening for metabolic comorbidities as part of HBV care and treatment in Africa.

title: Application of Combined Gastric Tube Tip Manometry and Auscultation for Nasogastric Tube Positioning in Neurocritical Care Patients With Artificial Airways: A Prospective Diagnostic Pilot Study.
abstract: Background Nasogastric tube placement is central to enteral nutrition support in neurocritical care patients. However, tube malposition, particularly accidental placement into the airway, can lead to fatal complications. Aim To assess the accuracy of a combined gastric tube tip manometry and auscultation approach for confirming nasogastric tube placement in neurocritical care patients with artificial airways. Study design This prospective study enrolled patients who underwent nasogastric tube insertion in the neurocritical care unit of a tertiary hospital in China between January 2025 and May 2025. Using chest X-ray as the reference standard, we compared the sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), negative predictive value (NPV), positive likelihood ratio (PLR) and negative likelihood ratio (NLR) for gastric tube tip manometry alone, auscultation alone and their combination. Results In total, 120 patients participated. X-ray confirmed correct nasogastric tube positioning in 119 patients and malposition in 1 patient. For gastric tube tip manometry alone, the sensitivity was 97.48%, with a specificity of 0%, a positive predictive value (PPV) of 99.15% and a negative predictive value (NPV) of 0%. Auscultation alone yielded a sensitivity of 90.76%, a specificity of 100%, a PPV of 100% and an NPV of 8.33%. The combined manometry-plus-auscultation approach had a sensitivity of 88.24%, a specificity of 100%, a PPV of 100% and an NPV of 6.67%. Conclusions The combined gastric tube tip manometry and auscultation method might serve as an adjunctive bedside strategy for confirming nasogastric tube placement in neurocritical care patients with artificial airways. However, only one malpositioned tube was observed in this study; the specificity and NPV should be interpreted with caution. Relevance to clinical practice When gastric aspirate cannot be obtained or immediate chest radiography is impractical, combined gastric tube tip manometry and auscultation provide a feasible, radiation-free bedside pathway for confirming nasogastric tube position; equivocal or negative bedside findings should still be verified radiographically before feeding. Trial registration The study was registered with the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2300078001).

title: Balancing Iliac Crest Avoidance and Neural Safety in L5/S1 TELD: Quantitative Identification of a Candidate Balanced Trajectory Window Using AI-Assisted 3D MRI Reconstruction.
abstract: Objective Transforaminal endoscopic lumbar discectomy (TELD) at L5/S1 is challenging due to the iliac crest barrier. Conventional planning relies on CT or 2D imaging, inherently lacking soft-tissue contrast to visualize neural structures. This study aimed to define a quantitative candidate balanced trajectory zone using AI-assisted 3D MRI reconstruction to simultaneously evaluate iliac crest obstruction and neural safety constraints. Methods A deep learning model was trained on 50 thin-slice lumbar MRIs to achieve precise segmentation and 3D reconstruction of neural, dural, and osseous structures. Thirty lumbar models were selected after image- and reconstruction-quality screening for surgical puncture simulation. Using a 5° increment as the angular increment, 49 virtual working trajectories (coronal plane angles, CPA 0°-30° and cross-sectional angles, CSA 0°-30°) were established for each bilateral intervertebral foramen, yielding a total of 2940 trajectories. Intersection volumes between each trajectory and the iliac crest, L5 nerve root, dural sac, and articular processes were quantitatively analyzed. Results The model achieved an 86.4% mean Dice coefficient (73.2%-92.4%). Among 2940 trajectories, 1207 (41.1%) completely avoided the iliac crest. Spatial analysis revealed a trade-off: increasing CSA reduced iliac and S1 superior articular process obstruction but increased L5 osseous removal, whereas steeper CPAs spared the L5 nerve root but risked the L5 inferior articular process. Quantitative analysis identified a candidate balanced trajectory window (CPA 20°-25°, CSA 25°-30°) that achieved a balance between iliac crest avoidance, neuro-osseous preservation, and facet integrity. Conclusions This candidate trajectory window (CPA 20°-25°/CSA 25°-30°) may provide a useful reference for balancing iliac crest avoidance with neuro-osseous safety. These findings provide quantitative constraints for manual planning and for the future development of computer-assisted trajectory-planning systems.

title: Concurrent Long Thoracic and Lateral Cutaneous Intercostal Nerve Entrapment After Chest Tube Thoracostomy Causing Scapular Winging and Chest Wall Pain: Diagnosis With Ultrasound and Treatment With Hydrodissection.
abstract: Background Chest tube thoracostomy may cause iatrogenic nerve injury, resulting in persistent pain and functional impairment. Long thoracic nerve (LTN) palsy after chest tube placement has been described, but concurrent involvement of the LTN and the lateral cutaneous branch of an intercostal nerve (LCIN) appears to be rarely reported. We describe a patient with persistent post-thoracostomy chest wall pain and scapular winging in whom musculoskeletal ultrasonography identified entrapment of both nerves. Case presentation A 43-year-old man presented with severe left shoulder and chest wall pain 6 months after chest tube placement for traumatic hemopneumothorax. Examination demonstrated focal tenderness, dysesthesia, and mechanical allodynia at the chest tube scar, along with medial/inferior scapular winging during serratus anterior provocative testing. Shoulder range of motion was full on examination; however, forward flexion beyond 15° markedly aggravated pain, resulting in pain-related reluctance to move the shoulder. Manual muscle testing was 4+/5 before treatment because pain limited force generation. Musculoskeletal ultrasound demonstrated focal abnormality of the LTN where it pierced the axillary fascia over the sixth rib, with loss of fascicular definition and reduced glide, and tethering/thickening of the LCIN within scar tissue at the prior tube insertion site. Symptom reproduction with sonopalpation supported the clinical relevance of both findings. Intervention and results Ultrasound-guided hydrodissection using 5% dextrose in water was performed around both nerves. A total of approximately 40 mL of 5% dextrose in water was used, with 20 mL administered per nerve. Immediately after the first procedure, pain improved from NRS 9/10 to 2/10, with marked reduction in pain during shoulder movement, including forward flexion. The patient subsequently underwent 5 treatment sessions at 2-week intervals over 10 weeks. During follow-up, manual muscle testing improved to 5/5 without pain, scapular winging was no longer evident on provocative testing, and the Shoulder Pain and Disability Index improved from pain/disability scores of 25/15 to 6/4. At the sixth follow-up visit, pain and function were satisfactory, and the patient elected continued monitoring without further intervention. At 1-year follow-up, treatment efficacy remained sustained without recurrence. Conclusion In patients with persistent shoulder or chest wall pain after chest tube thoracostomy, iatrogenic peripheral nerve entrapment should be considered. This case highlights the value of a focused neuromuscular examination and musculoskeletal ultrasound for identifying concurrent motor and sensory nerve involvement and suggests that ultrasound-guided hydrodissection may be a useful minimally invasive treatment. Because electrodiagnostic studies were not performed, the findings are most consistent with entrapment/neurapraxia with dynamic tethering rather than electrodiagnostically proven axonal palsy.

title: Meibomian Gland Epithelioma Mimicking Eyelid Squamous Cell Carcinoma in a Hereford-Cross Steer.
abstract: Objective To describe the clinical presentation and histopathology of a meibomian gland epithelioma that clinically resembled squamous cell carcinoma in a steer. Animal studied A 15 year-old Hereford-Lowline cross steer presented for evaluation of an approximately 2 × 4 cm ulcerated, pedunculated eyelid mass arising from the right inferior eyelid margin. Procedures Excision of the mass followed by adjunctive cryotherapy was performed. The mass was submitted for histopathologic analysis. Results Histopathologic evaluation revealed the mass to be consistent with a meibomian gland epithelioma, a neoplastic proliferation of the basal/reserve cells of the meibomian gland. The steer recovered routinely from the procedure with no evidence of regrowth of the mass at 13 months post-operatively. Conclusion Meibomian gland epitheliomas are one of the most common eyelid tumors of dogs; however, this is the first known report of a histologically confirmed meibomian gland epithelioma in cattle. Clinically, the mass resembled the appearance of squamous cell carcinoma, a common eyelid tumor in Hereford cattle. title: Idiopathic Granulomatous Inflammation of the Periocular Structures in Four Dogs: Clinical, Histopathological, and Imaging Findings and Therapeutic Outcome.
abstract: Purpose To describe cases of canine idiopathic periocular granulomatous inflammation. Material and methods Clinical records were reviewed. Animal studied At the time of presentation, the four patients (German Shepherd dog, mixed breed, Magyar Vizsla, Hovawart) were 1.5-5 (mean 3.75) years old. All dogs were female; two were spayed. Lesions were unilateral in 3/4 cases. Dogs presented with ulcerated (1) or non-ulcerated (3) mass lesions affecting the periocular skin (3/4), medial canthal area (2/4), or third eyelid (1/4). Results Incisional biopsies revealed pyogranulomatous inflammation in three and granulomatous inflammation in one case. There was no evidence of microbial infection in the specimens. Patients received anti-inflammatory or immunosuppressive dosages of systemic corticosteroids. Three dogs also received systemic cyclosporin (5 mg/kg, sid), and one dog received topical cyclosporin (0.1%, bid). One dog underwent surgical debulking of a circumscribed mass within the left lower eyelid prior to immunosuppressive therapy and developed an additional swelling on the left upper eyelid. Remission of clinical signs was achieved in all patients. Dogs were treated for 5 to 11 months (mean 8.7). No recurrence was reported in 4/4 patients during a mean follow-up period of 17.3 months. In 3/4patients, there was no recurrence within an average of 11 months after discontinuation of therapy. One dog was lost to follow-up. Conclusion Idiopathic granulomatous inflammation is a differential diagnosis for periocular mass lesions. Its diagnosis is based on histopathology and the exclusion of other causes of granulomatous inflammation.

title: Computed Tomographic Findings of Hepatic Rupture Associated With Amyloidosis in a Young Siamese Cat.
abstract: A 3-year-old neutered male Siamese cat with chronic anorexia showed anemia and elevated liver enzyme levels. Ultrasonography disclosed multiple diffusely heterogeneous hepatic lesions and peritoneal effusion, which was identified as hemoabdomen upon fluid analysis. Computed tomography showed finger-like hypoattenuation extending from the left hepatic margin with focal margin loss in the delayed phase, suggesting hepatic rupture. Infiltrative hepatic diseases were considered, and amyloidosis was the top differential diagnosis given the patient's young age, breed predisposition, and suspected hepatic rupture. Blood oozing was confirmed via laparotomy, and Congo red staining established hepatic amyloidosis, though amyloid typing was not pursued.

title: Radiographic Comparison of Pulmonary Lobar Vasculature Dimensions in Medically Managed and Drug-Naive Dogs With Left Heart Failure Secondary to Myxomatous Mitral Valve Disease.
abstract: Myxomatous mitral valve disease (MMVD) is the most common acquired cause of left heart failure (LHF) in dogs, and radiographic identification of pulmonary venous enlargement is traditionally used to support the diagnosis of LHF. However, the absence of venous enlargement has been anecdotally observed after initiation of therapy. Therefore, we aimed to compare radiographic pulmonary vessel size in LHF patients with ongoing medical management ± receiving acute rescue therapy. Dogs with echocardiographically confirmed MMVD and radiographic cardiogenic pulmonary edema were retrospectively selected. Pulmonary lobar artery and vein widths were measured using standardized rib-to-vessel ratios: cranial vessels at the intersection with the fourth rib on lateral projections and caudal vessels at the ninth rib on ventrodorsal/dorsoventral projections. Pulmonary vein-to-artery (PV/PA) and vessel-to-rib ratios were calculated, with enlargement defined as >1.2 and small vessel size as <0.8, and treatment groups were compared using Welch-corrected t-tests. 200 radiographic studies from 163 dogs were reviewed. In all dogs, the veins measured larger than the arteries in all lung lobes. Chronically untreated dogs who received furosemide immediately before radiographs had no venous enlargement. All other groups had vascular asymmetry or venous enlargement in at least two lung lobes. All control dogs with reoccurrence of LHF had absence of venous enlargement after initiation of therapy. Pulmonary venous enlargement was most pronounced in the right caudal lung lobe. These findings indicate that dogs chronically managed for MMVD may decompensate into LHF without radiographic pulmonary venous enlargement and that furosemide administration prior to imaging can normalize vessel size.

title: Computed Tomographic Findings of Ischemic Necrosis of the Accessory Carpal Bone in a Dog.
abstract: A 1-year-and-9-month-old Golden Retriever presented with a 9-month history of right thoracic limb lameness. Radiographs revealed a monostotic, expansile lesion of the right accessory carpal bone (ACB). A computed tomography (CT) confirmed the aggressive nature of the lesion, demonstrating multifocal moth-eaten osteolysis, sclerosis, periosteal reaction, and flexor carpi ulnaris tendinopathy. Differential diagnoses included the ischemic necrosis of the ACB, osteomyelitis, and primary bone neoplasia. Histopathology confirmed osteonecrosis. This case highlights the value of CT in evaluating aggressive carpal lesions and identifies ischemic necrosis as an important differential diagnosis. This case represents the first CT description of this disease in dogs.

title: Evaluation of Intracranial Lesions Using Deep Learning-Based Reconstruction in Canine Brain MRI: Comparison With Conventional Reconstruction on T2-Weighted and FLAIR Sequences.
abstract: Obtaining high-resolution brain MRI in small animals is challenging due to the inherent trade-off between image quality and acquisition time. Deep learning-based reconstruction (DLR) has emerged as a solution to improve image quality without prolonging scan time; however, its clinical utility and potential risks, such as pseudolesions, remain insufficiently evaluated in veterinary patients. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of DLR on lesion assessment and image quality in canine brain MRI and to investigate potential limitations associated with its application. This retrospective study compared DLR with conventional reconstruction in 25 canine brain MRI examinations diagnosed with intracranial diseases. Transverse T2-weighted and fluid-attenuated inversion recovery sequences were reconstructed using both conventional and DLR methods. Quantitative analysis included signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR), and lesion edge sharpness. Two blinded radiologists assessed image quality, lesion conspicuity, artifacts, pseudolesions, and lesion masking. DLR images exhibited significantly higher SNR, CNR, and lesion edge sharpness than conventional images in both sequences (p < 0.05). DLR images also yielded significantly higher qualitative scores for image quality and lesion conspicuity (p < 0.05). Truncation artifact was significantly reduced, whereas motion and pulsation artifacts showed no improvement. No instances of pseudolesions or lesion masking were noted. DLR significantly improves image quality and lesion conspicuity in canine brain MRI and reduces truncation artifacts; however, it does not mitigate motion or pulsation interference. Collectively, these findings suggest that DLR has potential value for improving image quality and lesion visibility in canine brain MRI, whereas further studies are needed to determine its impact on diagnostic performance.

title: Evaluating GPT-5 as a generalist multimodal clinical model.
abstract: Purpose The transition from task-specific artificial intelligence toward general-purpose foundation models raises fundamental questions about their capacity to support the integrated reasoning required in clinical medicine, where diagnosis demands synthesis of ambiguous patient narratives, laboratory data, and multimodal imaging. Approach We provide the first controlled, cross-sectional evaluation of the GPT-5 family (GPT-5, GPT-5 Mini, and GPT-5nano) against its predecessor GPT-4o across a diverse spectrum of clinically grounded tasks, grounded tasks, including the United States Medical Licensing Examination, text-based, text-based reasoning benchmarks (MedQA and MedXpertQA Text), and visual question answering (VQA) in neuroradiology (BraTS), digital pathology (PathVQA and BreakHis), and mammography (EMBED, InBreast, Chinese Mammography Database, and CBIS-DDSM) using a standardized zero-shot chain-of-thought protocol. Results GPT-5 demonstrated substantial performance gains with absolute improvements exceeding 25 percentage points on MedXpertQA. When tasked with multimodal synthesis, GPT-5 effectively leveraged its enhanced training corpora to achieve state-of-the-art or competitive performance across most VQA benchmarks and outperformed GPT-4o by margins of 10% to 40% in mammography tasks requiring fine-grained lesion characterization. However, performance remained moderate in neuroradiology (44% macro-average accuracy) and lagged substantially behind domain-specific models in mammography, where specialized systems exceed 80% accuracy compared with GPT-5's 52% to 64%. Conclusions These findings indicate that although GPT-5 represents a meaningful advance toward general, multimodal clinical inference, generalist models are still not yet substitutes for purpose-built systems in highly specialized, perception-critical tasks. We delineate the current VQA landscape, positioning GPT-5 as a powerful adjunct capable of holistic inference while underscoring that domain adaptation, rigorous validation, and guarantees of reasoning transparency remain essential prerequisites for clinical deployment.

title: Human carotid plaque risk imaging using multiparametric photoacoustic and ultrasound fusion (hCAPRI).
abstract: Assessing the risk of carotid plaque rupture remains limited because current imaging methods cannot provide both plaque composition and structural information in real time. Here, we present human carotid plaque risk imaging (hCAPRI), a multiparametric photoacoustic and ultrasound (PA/US) fusion method for real-time carotid plaque assessment. hCAPRI combines PA imaging for detecting intraplaque hemorrhage (IPH) with US imaging for evaluating the plaque structure. PA imaging measured IPH size and methemoglobin content, while US imaging assessed stenosis severity, calcification, and plaque thickness. Combining these PA/US parameters, we compute an hCAPRI score. In 171 carotid arteries (CAs) from 120 patients, hCAPRI revealed the relationships among the PA/US parameters. In 36 CAs validated with magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), hCAPRI showed high agreement with MRI. The hCAPRI score achieved 89% sensitivity and 84% specificity for high-risk plaque classification. hCAPRI offers a low-cost, real-time, and contrast-free approach for carotid plaque risk imaging.

title: Lighting up necrotic neurons from traumatic brain injury with magnetic quantum dots to decode the cellular origin of MRI.
abstract: The diagnosis of traumatic brain injury (TBI) remains heavily constrained by the limitations of conventional imaging techniques in visualizing the pathological events that determine the disease progression and outcome. To address this clinical challenge, we report a manganese-doped near-infrared quantum dot (QD) to intrinsically integrate the highly sensitive optical imaging with clinical compatible magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Taking the advantages of optical imaging powered by whole-brain clearing and cellular resolution three-dimensional (3D) panoptic imaging, in combination with the systematic in vitro cell studies on different types of cells involved in TBI, we disclosed the interpretable pathology reflected by TBI imaging through the highly sensitive fluorescence of magnetic QDs, i.e., after systemic administration, the nanoprobes were extravasated through the compromised blood-brain barrier and then selectively phagocytosed by activated microglia, which subsequently migrated into the regions rich in dead neurons and neuronal debris. This microglia-mediated tropism decodes the signal origin of MRI enhanced by the nanometer-sized contrast agent, thereby transforming the MRI from an anatomical tool into a pathological reporter. A biocompatible Fe 3 O 4 nanoparticle of similar size was also compared with the magnetic QD mentioned above for validating the translational merits of nanoparticles in MRI diagnosis of TBI.

title: Predictors for Failure of Nonsurgical Treatment in Mild to Moderate Cubital Tunnel Syndrome.
abstract: Background: Activity modification to reduce mechanical stress on the ulnar nerve is an effective treatment for mild to moderate cubital tunnel syndrome (CuTS). However, some patients do not improve with nonsurgical management and ultimately require surgical intervention. This study aimed to identify predictors associated with nonsurgical treatment failure in CuTS. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed data from patients with CuTS classified as McGowan grades 1 and 2. Non-surgical management primarily consisted of activity modification, with adjunctive treatments including vitamin B12, nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, pregabalin or mirogabalin and corticosteroid injections. Treatment failure was defined as the need for subsequent surgical intervention (transition-to-surgery group). The success group included 37 patients, and the transition-to-surgery group included 26 patients. Univariate and multivariate regression analyses were performed to evaluate predictors of nonsurgical treatment failure, including age, sex, body mass index, disease duration, comorbidities (diabetes mellitus, thyroid disease and radiographic cervical spondylosis) and concomitant elbow disorders (osteoarthritis, ganglion cysts and cubitus varus or valgus deformity). Elbow osteoarthritis was assessed radiographically using the Broberg and Morrey classification system. Results: Univariate analysis showed that corticosteroid injections, current smoking, radiographic cervical spondylosis and elbow osteoarthritis were more common in the transition-to-surgery group than in the success group. Multivariate analysis identified corticosteroid injections, radiographic cervical spondylosis and elbow osteoarthritis as independent predictors of nonsurgical treatment failure. title: Phase 2 Trial of <sup>89</sup>Zr-Deferoxamine-Daratumumab for CD38-targeted Immuno-PET/CT Detection of Multiple Myeloma.
abstract: Background Multiple myeloma (MM) imaging is currently suboptimal, which may limit patient care. Zirconium 89 ( 89 Zr) deferoxamine (DFO)-daratumumab is a novel CD38-targeted immuno-PET tracer. Purpose To compare 89 Zr-DFO-daratumumab PET/CT against standard-of-care fluorine 18 ( 18 F) fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) PET/CT for detection of MM. Materials and Methods Participants with MM were accrued to this prospective phase 2 trial between March 2022 and July 2025. Standard-of-care 18 F-FDG PET/CT and bone marrow biopsy were performed, along with research 89 Zr-DFO-daratumumab PET/CT. If there were discrepant lesions between the two scans, image-guided biopsy was considered as the reference standard. The McNemar test was used to compare disease detection between the two imaging modalities. Results This study included 60 participants (median age, 63 years [IQR, 57-71 years]; 32 women). 89 Zr-DFO-daratumumab PET/CT demonstrated at least one positive lesion in 43% (26 of 60; 95% CI: 31, 57) of participants, and 18 F-FDG PET/CT demonstrated at least one positive lesion in 47% (28 of 60; 95% CI: 33, 60) of participants. While there was no overall difference in disease detection between the two imaging modalities ( P = .81), MM was demonstrated only with 89 Zr-DFO-daratumumab PET/CT in 13% (eight of 60) of participants, with subsequent biopsy confirmation of active myeloma. Conclusion In participants with MM, CD38-targeted 89 Zr-DFO-daratumumab immuno-PET helped detect active myeloma in some participants with no signs of disease at 18 F-FDG PET/CT. title: Predicting Lymph Node Metastasis in Part-Solid Lung Adenocarcinomas with a Maximum Solid Portion Diameter of 30.0 mm.
abstract: Background The incidence of lymph node (LN) metastasis in patients with part-solid nodules (PSNs) is known to be low, which makes the intraoperative evaluation of LNs a controversial issue. Purpose To investigate the incidence of LN metastasis and explore clinical-radiologic predicting factors for LN metastasis in PSN lung adenocarcinomas with a solid portion diameter of 30.0 mm or less in a large surgical study sample. Materials and Methods This retrospective study included patients with part-solid lung adenocarcinomas with solid portion diameters of 30.0 mm or less on preoperative CT images from July 2023 to December 2024. For each PSN, overall tumor size, solid portion diameter, consolidation-to-tumor ratio (CTR), location, margin, shape, spiculation, lobulation, pleural retraction, bubble-like lucency, and air bronchogram were independently evaluated by two chest radiologists blinded to clinical information and pathology results. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curve, calibration, and decision curve analysis. Results This study included 1444 patients (median age, 59 years; IQR, 51-67 years; 931 women). The frequency of LN metastasis was 4.7% (68 of 1444 patients). None of the 115 patients with a CTR of 0.25 or less had LN metastasis (N1: 0 of 115; N2: 0 of 115). Rarely (0.2%, one of 552), LN metastasis was found in patients with a solid portion diameter of 6.0 mm or less. Solid portion diameter was the only independent predictor of LN metastasis (odds ratio, 1.25; 95% CI: 1.20, 1.31) in multivariable analysis and showed a superior diagnostic performance compared with CTR (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, 0.86 [95% CI: 0.82, 0.90] vs 0.75 [95% CI: 0.68, 0.80]; P < .001), along with better calibration (Brier score, 0.039 vs 0.044) and greater net benefit. The clinical actionable cutoff for solid portion diameter was 7.3 mm (sensitivity, 95.6%; specificity, 49.6%). Conclusion Solid portion diameter had a superior diagnostic performance compared with CTR in predicting LN metastasis in patients with part-solid lung adenocarcinomas of solid portion diameter of 30.0 mm or less at CT. © RSNA, 2026 Supplemental material is available for this article.

title: Comprehensive Imaging Review of the Ureter.
abstract: The ureter is an important conduit between the kidney and the bladder and is frequently imaged to rule out cancer in the upper genitourinary tract. However, while malignancy can occur, a spectrum of other pathologic ureteral findings can exist, and these can be divided into congenital, intrinsic, and extrinsic abnormalities that range from postoperative and neoplastic conditions to inflammatory disease. This article provides a comprehensive overview of the ureter, including the ureteral anatomy, ureteral imaging strategies, and various ureteral conditions and their associated imaging features. It is important to identify congenital genitourinary variants, as these are frequently linked to further imaging recommendations, such as nuclear medicine renography and fluoroscopic voiding cystourethrography. Intrinsic abnormalities can be iatrogenic, infectious, inflammatory, or neoplastic. Intrinsic ureteral strictures are most commonly iatrogenic, usually resulting from prior surgery or radiation therapy. Ureteral infections include tuberculosis, schistosomiasis, and Escherichia coli infection, which have varying imaging manifestations. Inflammatory conditions include ureteritis cystica and pseudodiverticulosis. Ureteral masses are rarely benign and are most commonly urothelial carcinomas. Processes in the abdomen and pelvis, including mass effect from pregnancy, ureteral compression from advanced pelvic floor prolapse, and rarely, ureteral obstruction from vaginal devices, also can affect the ureter. The ureter can be injured during pelvic surgery or trauma. It also may be involved by deep pelvic endometriosis, mass effect from extrinsic lesions, or reactive change from inflammatory processes. Radiologists need to have a clear understanding of the patient's history and the range of possible ureteral conditions to establish the optimal differential diagnosis.

title: <sup>18</sup>F-FET PET for Detection of Recurrent Disease in Gliomas: Tips and Tricks for Interpretation.
abstract: Gliomas are a heterogeneous group of primary brain tumors that are generally incurable. The current treatment paradigm for these tumors revolves around maximal safe resection and adjuvant chemoradiation; however, posttreatment changes can be difficult to distinguish from residual or recurrent disease. This makes it challenging to know whether treatments are working or the therapy should be escalated. Molecular imaging with amino acid PET has shown promise as a solution to this problem. The authors describe the interpretation considerations for the amino acid radiotracer fluorine 18-fluoroethyltyrosine (FET) in distinguishing posttreatment changes from recurrent glioma. The quantification of FET uptake on PET images and guidelines for interpretation are outlined.

title: Management, Upgrade Rates, and Radiologic Surveillance of Screen-Detected High-Risk Breast Lesions.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate the prevalence, upgrade rate, and radiologic surveillance management of high-risk lesions (HRLs) detected at screening mammography in a Dutch breast cancer screening population. Materials and Methods This retrospective analysis of a prospectively maintained database included patients recalled from the Dutch breast cancer screening program between January 2009 and July 2019. Incidence rates, diagnostic work-up, radiologic surveillance, and upgrades to (pre)malignancy after surgical excision and during radiologic surveillance were evaluated. Results Among 17 809 recalled patients, 514 patients with a mean age of 58 years ± 8.1 (SD) were diagnosed with an HRL. The incidence rate of HRLs was 0.83 per 1000 screens and 2.89 per 100 recalls. The majority of HRLs consisted of papillary lesions (34.4% [177 of 514]) and atypical ductal hyperplasia (ADH) (31.1% [160 of 514]). Surgical excision was performed in 233 cases (45.3%), resulting in 58 HRLs (24.9%) being upgraded to (pre)malignancy. Invasive tumors were mainly found in papillary lesions with atypia and ADH. Of patients diagnosed with an HRL, 324 (63.0%) had an indication for radiologic surveillance. Of these, 257 (79.3%) underwent surveillance, with 109 (42.4%) completing the recommended 5-year surveillance trajectory. During surveillance, 26 patients (10.1%) developed a (pre)malignancy. Invasive tumors were more frequently identified among HRLs upgraded during surveillance than among HRLs upgraded after surgical excision (17 of 26 [65%] vs 16 of 58 [28%]; P = .001). HRLs upgraded to invasive cancer were more likely to be triple-negative compared with screen-detected cancers (9.1% [3 of 33] vs 6.6% [215 of 3277]; P < .001). Conclusion Overall, 16.3% (84 of 514) of screen-detected HRLs were associated with a diagnosis of (pre)malignancy after surgical excision or during radiologic surveillance. Completion of the recommended 5-year surveillance trajectory was achieved in fewer than half of patients undergoing surveillance. Keywords: Breast Mammography, MR-Imaging, Ultrasound, Biopsy/Needle Aspiration, Screening Supplemental material is available for this article. © RSNA, 2026.

title: Comparison of Two Deep Learning Models and Their Combination for 1-year Lung Cancer Detection in Two Screening Cohorts.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate the performance of Sybil, a Medical Open Network for Artificial Intelligence (MONAI)-based nodule model, and their combination for 1-year lung cancer detection in two screening cohorts: the National Lung Screening Trial (NLST) and the Pamplona International Early Lung Cancer Action Program (P-IELCAP). Materials and Methods Baseline low-dose CT (LDCT) examinations from the NLST and the P-IELCAP were analyzed. A prespecified OR-stacked composite model combining Sybil, a MONAI-based nodule model, and a safety-net rule (MONAI-detected nodule > 6 mm with detection confidence > 0.95) was developed and evaluated for 1-year lung cancer detection. Model discrimination was assessed by using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), and operating-point performance metrics were calculated. Results A total of 5110 baseline LDCT examinations were analyzed, including 2343 from NLST and 2767 from P-IELCAP, with 65 lung cancers diagnosed within 1 year. Mean age, mean pack-years, and percentage of female participants were 61.6 years ± 5.1 (SD), 57.3 pack-years ± 24.8, and 39.4% (923 of 2343), respectively, in NLST and 56.0 years ± 9.5, 34.4 pack-years ± 21.5, and 28.6% (791 of 2767), respectively, in P-IELCAP. Lung cancer incidence (per 1000 person-years) was higher in NLST than in P-IELCAP (17.7 vs 8.7; P = .006). Mean Sybil 1-year lung cancer probabilities (scaled by 1000 for presentation) were also higher in NLST than in P-IELCAP (16.4 vs 9.9; P < .01). Sybil achieved an AUC of 0.93 in both cohorts, whereas the MONAI-based model achieved AUCs of 0.90 in NLST and 0.79 in P-IELCAP. The composite model missed two of 65 1-year lung cancers while correctly classifying 2731 of 4965 (55.0%) noncancer examinations as negative, yielding a sensitivity of 63 of 65 (96.9%) and a positive predictive value of 63 of 2297 (2.7%). Conclusion For 1-year lung cancer detection with LDCT, the composite AI model achieved high sensitivity while maintaining acceptable specificity. Keywords: Applications-CT, Thorax, Pulmonary, Sybil, MONAI, NLST, P-IELCAP, Lung Cancer, Low Dose Computed Tomography Supplemental material is available for this article. © RSNA, 2026.

The composite model missed two of 65 1-year lung cancers while correctly classifying 2731 of 4965 (55.0%) noncancer examinations as negative, yielding a sensitivity of 63 of 65 (96.9%) and a positive predictive value of 63 of 2297 (2.7%). Conclusion For 1-year lung cancer detection with LDCT, the composite AI model achieved high sensitivity while maintaining acceptable specificity.
