title: Pancolitis due to Tuberculosis Masquerading as Inflammatory Bowel Disease in a 43-Year-Old Woman: Diagnostic Challenges in a Resource-Limited Setting-A Case Study and Literature Review From Ethiopia.
abstract: Background Gastrointestinal tuberculosis (GI TB) predominantly affects the ileocecal region, making primary colonic involvement exceptionally rare. In TB-endemic, resource-limited settings, differentiating colonic TB from inflammatory bowel disease (IBD)-particularly Crohn's disease (CD)-presents a formidable diagnostic dilemma owing to overlapping clinical, radiological, and ileocolonoscopic features, often leading to diagnostic delays, misdiagnosis, and subsequent complications. Initial clinical presentation treatment and diagnostic re‐evaluation In May 2026, a 43-year-old Ethiopian woman presented to Jimma University Medical Center with a 10-month history of progressive colicky abdominal pain, chronic watery diarrhea, postprandial nonbilious vomiting, and significant weight loss. Prior empirical regimens of antihelminthic agents and broad-spectrum antibiotics administered at peripheral health facilities yielded no clinical improvement. Initial laboratory workup revealed microcytic hypochromic anemia (hemoglobin: 8.5 g/dL), a significantly elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) (92 mm/h), hypoalbuminemia (2.8 g/dL), and a normal carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) level (4 ng/mL). Ileocolonoscopy demonstrated superficial ulceration involving the ascending colon and hepatic flexure in a continuous form with numerous inflammatory polyps, and a small deep ulceration at the terminal ileum. Initial histopathology demonstrated chronic active inflammation without evidence of malignancy or granuloma formation. With a presumed diagnosis of CD, treatment was initiated with prednisolone and azathioprine, which might have contributed to the suspected deterioration of the clinical condition, warranting re-evaluation with contrast-enhanced CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis, which demonstrated diffuse, long-segment circumferential wall thickening involving the terminal ileum, the entire colon, and the rectum, alongside pericolic fat stranding, a mesenteric phlegmon, and multiple necrotic mesenteric lymph nodes, with the largest measuring 2 × 3 cm with peripheral rim enhancement. Fine-needle aspiration cytology (FNAC) of the necrotic lymph nodes revealed epithelioid granulomas and characteristic caseous necrosis. With the above evidence, terminal ileitis and pancolitis due to TB were considered, immunosuppressive medications were discontinued, and standard antituberculosis therapy (2RHZE/4RH) was promptly initiated. The patient started to experience clinical improvement, achieving full resolution of her constitutional and abdominal symptoms and gaining weight at 1 month of follow-up. Conclusion Diagnosing GI TB-especially in atypical sites such as the colon-presents a critical challenge in resource-limited, TB-endemic settings, where differentiating it from IBDs, especially CD, is vital to prevent severe complications from inappropriate therapy. To avoid misdiagnosing GI TB as IBD (which risks disseminated infection from immunosuppression) or IBD as TB (which worsens bowel stricture, fistulae, and perforation), clinicians must perform mandatory pretreatment TB screening using radiologic, immunologic, molecular, and culture modalities before initiating immunosuppressive agents. Furthermore, diagnostic accuracy requires obtaining deep submucosal biopsies during ileocolonoscopy to detect characteristic granulomatous lesions if present. Finally, when an empirical anti-TB trial is necessary, it must be strictly time-limited and followed by objective re-evaluation at 8 weeks-including repeat endoscopy and biopsy-rather than relying solely on clinical symptomatic improvement.

title: Challenges in the Management of Giant Strangulated Hiatal Hernia: A Case Report.
abstract: A giant hiatal hernia (GHH) is generally defined as the herniation of more than half of the stomach into the thoracic cavity, although definitions vary in the literature, with some authors considering herniation of more than one-third of the stomach sufficient for diagnosis. Strangulation is a rare but life-threatening complication that may lead to vascular compromise, gastric ischemia, and ultimately necrosis, requiring urgent diagnosis and individualized surgical management. We report the case of a 54-year-old man with long-standing gastroesophageal reflux disease who presented with chest pain and recurrent vomiting. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) demonstrated a giant type III hiatal hernia with approximately two-thirds of the stomach herniated into the thoracic cavity and associated gastric obstruction. Emergency laparoscopy revealed a severely twisted stomach with extensive necrosis of the fundus and greater curvature. Given the size of the hernia, an adequate exposure of the hiatal area was difficult to achieve, necessitating conversion to a left subcostal laparotomy. After dissection of the two diaphragmatic crus, the sac was reduced and excised, allowing complete reduction of the stomach back into the abdominal cavity. The necrotic areas were managed by longitudinal atypical gastrectomy. Given the large hiatal defect, anterior cruroplasty was performed to prevent an excessive angulation of the esophagus. No antireflux system could be implemented as the fundus was fully removed and Staple-line integrity was confirmed by an intraoperative methylene blue leak test. The postoperative course was uneventful with minimal residual reflux, treated by proton pump inhibitor therapy. We provide this case to demonstrate the treatment of a giant strangulated hernia and challenges stemming from the alternative surgical approach in laparoscopic and robot-assisted practice.

title: Extensive Dural Metastasis as Initial Presentation of Metastatic Prostate Cancer: A Case Report With Durable Disease Control Following Multimodal Treatment.
abstract: Central nervous system involvement in prostate cancer is rare, particularly in the form of dural or pachymeningeal metastases. We report the case of a 72-year-old man presenting with visual disturbances without hemianopsia, and right-sided headache since several weeks caused by an extensive right temporal dural-based lesion with intracranial extension. A minimally invasive frontotemporal burr-hole biopsy was performed for histopathological clarification. Histological and immunohistochemical analyses confirmed metastatic prostatic adenocarcinoma with expression of cytokeratin 8, NKX3.1, PSA, and PSMA. Subsequent systemic staging demonstrated metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer with pulmonary, lymphatic, and extensive osseous metastases. The patient underwent focal radiotherapy (36 Gy in 12 fractions) to the dural lesion and systemic treatment with androgen deprivation therapy and enzalutamide. Due to dizziness and sweating, enzalutamide dosage was reduced from 160 to 80 mg/day with maintained therapeutic response. At approximately 15 months of follow-up, the patient remained neurologically stable with durable local disease control on cranial MRI, marked biochemical response (PSA decline from 177 to 0.6 ng/mL), and no evidence of systemic progression. This case highlights the importance of considering metastatic prostate cancer in the differential diagnosis of dural-based intracranial lesions in elderly men and demonstrates that individualized multimodal treatment can achieve durable disease control even in rare metastatic presentations.

title: Late Presentation of Fetus in Fetu in a 10-Year-Old Boy.
abstract: Fetus in fetu (FIF) is a rare congenital anomaly in which a dysmorphic, parasitic twin is retained within the body of its host twin. It typically presents in infancy, shows a slight male predominance, and is most often located in the retroperitoneum. Differentiating FIF from an abdominal teratoma on imaging is important, as the two entities can closely resemble one another. We report the case of a 10-year-old boy who presented with abdominal pain, low-grade fever, and unintentional weight loss. Antenatal history was unremarkable. Abdominal examination revealed mild distension and left-sided tenderness. Ultrasonography demonstrated an 8.5 × 10.4 × 11.1 cm mass-like lesion in the left hypochondrium, and a provisional diagnosis of teratoma versus FIF was considered. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) of the abdomen showed a large, well-defined, heterogeneous mesenteric mass measuring 10.0 × 11.0 × 14.0 cm containing macroscopic fat, dense tooth-like calcifications, and osseous elements with attenuation of up to 1450 Hounsfield units, together with a well-formed fetal skeleton. Serum tumor markers were within normal limits. A presumptive diagnosis of FIF, supported by imaging and by intraoperative findings that satisfied the Willis criteria, was made at exploratory laparotomy; histopathological confirmation could not be obtained because the specimen was inadequately fixed prior to processing, so a highly differentiated fetiform teratoma cannot be entirely excluded. The child remained well at last follow-up, about 10 weeks after discharge; longer surveillance is required. This case illustrates that FIF, although classically a diagnosis of infancy, should remain in the differential diagnosis of a complex abdominal mass in an older child, and highlights the role of the Willis criteria, radiological correlation, and intraoperative findings when histopathology is unavailable.

title: MRI-Based Analysis of Post-HIFU Efficacy in Uterine Adenomyosis and Personalized Treatment Strategies.
abstract: Objectives To evaluate the clinical outcomes of high-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) ablation in patients with different subtypes of adenomyosis as classified by preoperative magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and to explore the implications for personalized treatment planning. Design A retrospective cohort study. Participants 447 patients with adenomyosis who underwent HIFU treatment were classified according to the Kishi MRI criteria into Type I (intrinsic, n=195), Type II (extrinsic, n=92), Type III (intramural, n=50), and Type IV (full-thickness, n=110). Methods All 447 patients underwent HIFU ablation under standardized procedural protocols.Treatment parameters, non-perfused volume (NPV) ratio, relief of dysmenorrhea (assessed by NRS score), and improvement in menstrual blood volume (assessed by FPS score) were analyzed and compared across subtypes at 3 and 6 months post-treatment. Results Patients with Type IV adenomyosis had significantly larger lesion volumes and required longer treatment durations with higher energy delivery (p<0.001). The NPV ratio was highest in Type I (74.91% ± 28.34%), followed by Type III (70.34% ± 26.12%), both significantly higher than in Type II (60.01% ± 2.9%) and Type IV (65.93% ± 25.41%) (p<0.05). All subtypes demonstrated significant and sustained improvement in both dysmenorrhea and menorrhagia at follow-up (p<0.05). The comprehensive treatment success rate was highest for Type IV at both 3 (21.82%) and 6 months (27.27%). Limitations This study has several limitations. First, the retrospective design inherently introduces selection bias and limits causal inference. Second,long-term follow-up beyond 6 months was not available, precluding assessment of durability of symptom relief and recurrence rates. Conclusions High-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) provides effective symptom relief for all MRI-classified subtypes of adenomyosis. Treatment parameters and efficacy, however, vary by subtype. MRI classification is therefore crucial for guiding treatment and anticipating technical challenges. A personalized approach based on subtype may further optimize therapeutic outcomes.

title: Association Between Hypoperfusion Intensity Ratio and Outcomes After Endovascular Thrombectomy in Posterior Circulation Stroke: A Retrospective Study.
abstract: Background The prognostic utility of the hypoperfusion intensity ratio (HIR) in posterior circulation stroke is undefined. We investigated the association between pretreatment HIR and outcomes after mechanical thrombectomy for acute posterior circulation large vessel occlusion. Methods This post hoc analysis of the ATTENTION (Endovascular Treatment for Acute Basilar Artery Occlusion)/ATTENTION-IA (Intra-Arterial Tenecteplase After Successful Endovascular Recanalisation in Patients With Acute Posterior Circulation Arterial Occlusion) trials included patients with posterior circulation occlusion who underwent mechanical thrombectomy and had baseline computed tomography perfusion. HIR (Tmax>10 s/ Tmax>6 s volume) was analyzed. Functional independence (modified Rankin Scale score, 0-2) at 90 days was the primary outcome. Results Among 139 patients, higher HIR (per 0.1 increment) was independently associated with lower odds of 90-day modified Rankin Scale score of 0 to 2 (adjusted odds ratio, 0.643 [95% CI, 0.422-0.979]; P =0.039). However, its discriminative ability was the modest (area under the curve, 0.617 [95% CI, 0.521-0.712]). The established anterior circulation cutoff (HIR<0.4) did not predict outcomes ( P =0.115). Conclusions Elevated HIR is independently associated with worse 90-day outcomes after posterior circulation mechanical thrombectomy, but its overall prognostic utility is limited, and the anterior circulation threshold (0.4) could not be validated in this underpowered analysis, highlighting circulation-specific pathophysiological differences.

title: SRNR: Deep learning-based MRI super-resolution using noisy high-resolution reference data.
abstract: Deep learning-based super-resolution (SR) techniques offer a powerful tool to enhance the spatial resolution of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) without increasing scan time. However, most supervised SR methods rely on high-resolution, high-signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) reference data for training, which are difficult to acquire in many clinical settings, such as in time-constrained pediatric imaging. Inspired by the Noise2Noise principle, we propose SRNR, a new training paradigm that enables supervised SR using noisy high-resolution images as references. SRNR was systematically evaluated on both pediatric and adult simulated data across different noise levels of the reference data. SRNR generated super-resolved image volumes with high similarity to the high-resolution references (PSNR: 32.5-35.2 dB) and improved downstream image analysis performance, including tissue segmentation (white matter Dice coefficient: 0.951-0.960) and cortical surface reconstruction (cortical thickness absolute difference: 0.200-0.255 mm). Furthermore, SRNR was shown to be effective on clinically acquired pediatric brain MRI data, achieving improvements consistent with those observed in the simulated experiments. These results demonstrate that SRNR substantially reduces reliance on clean, high-SNR training data and enables effective SR under clinically realistic acquisition constraints, thereby improving the feasibility of deploying deep learning-based SR in pediatric MRI and related applications.

title: Static Perimetry-OCT Topographical Overlay Findings in the RUSH2A Study.
abstract: Purpose Ellipsoid zone (EZ) loss on optical coherence tomography (OCT) correlates with diminished sensitivity on static perimetry (SP). We explore a topographical overlay analysis in USH2A-related retinitis pigmentosa (RP) to develop novel endpoints of structural and functional change. Methods Subjects (N = 105) had SP (3× baseline; once annually for 4 years) and annual OCT. B-scans were segmented to outline the EZ. Overlays used visual field modeling and analysis (VFMA) software to superimpose the hill of vision (HOV) onto the en face infrared (IR) fundus image with EZ contours segmented from OCT volume scans. EZ border and three ribbons straddling the EZ border were ray cast onto the HOV. The HOV volume, HOV slope, mean sensitivity (MS), and peak sensitivity were measured. Mixed effect models were used to estimate change rates. Results Significant decrease over 4 years was found in all measures within the EZ, except slope and peak sensitivity. MS decreased for all ribbons, with outer ribbons showing greater progression than inner ribbons. Inner ribbons had larger decreases in volume and slope than outer ribbons. Conclusions SP-OCT overlay analysis showed faster loss of sensitivity outside the EZ margin. The widest ribbon outside the EZ showed greatest progression, suggesting more rapid vision loss occurring distal to the EZ margin. Slope progressed most within the widest inner ribbon, which could mean that slope change is a precursor to EZ loss. Translational relevance This research explores novel endpoints and concepts to characterize the disease progression in USH2A-related RP using imaging and functional overlay techniques.

Subjects (N = 105) had SP (3× baseline; once annually for 4 years) and annual OCT. B-scans were segmented to outline the EZ. Overlays used visual field modeling and analysis (VFMA) software to superimpose the hill of vision (HOV) onto the en face infrared (IR) fundus image with EZ contours segmented from OCT volume scans. EZ border and three ribbons straddling the EZ border were ray cast onto the HOV. The HOV volume, HOV slope, mean sensitivity (MS), and peak sensitivity were measured. Mixed effect models were used to estimate change rates.

Results

Significant decrease over 4 years was found in all measures within the EZ, except slope and peak sensitivity. MS decreased for all ribbons, with outer ribbons showing greater progression than inner ribbons. Inner ribbons had larger decreases in volume and slope than outer ribbons.

Conclusions

SP-OCT overlay analysis showed faster loss of sensitivity outside the EZ margin. The widest ribbon outside the EZ showed greatest progression, suggesting more rapid vision loss occurring distal to the EZ margin. Slope progressed most within the widest inner ribbon, which could mean that slope change is a precursor to EZ loss.

title: Cerebellar and frontal lobe alterations in pulmonary hypertension implicate an inflammatory lung vascular/brain axis.
abstract: Connections between vascular and neurocognitive diseases are emerging but remain poorly defined. Cognitive impairment is increasingly recognized in pulmonary hypertension (PH), a disease traditionally viewed as limited to the heart and lungs. Given that inflammation is shared by PH and neurodegenerative diseases, we investigated its role in driving brain and cognitive deficits in PH. Using structural and functional MRI data from UK Biobank (N = 248 PH) and a prospective validation cohort, we identified reduced cerebellar white matter volume, thinner frontal gyri, and weakened cerebellar-frontal connectivity in patients with PH but not in other heart or lung diseases. These changes were accompanied by worsened executive function and processing speed. Olink proteomics and targeted genomics linked inflammatory plasma proteins and a PH-associated nuclear receptor coactivator 7 (NCOA7) single nucleotide polymorphism, rs11154337, to these deficits. PH cerebellum showed increased microglial activation and white matter derangement. In PH mice, Ncoa7 deficiency worsened cerebellar inflammation and atrophy. Microglial functional assays, cerebellar single-nucleus RNA sequencing, and spatial transcriptomic analyses further implicated Ncoa7-dependent lysosomal, inflammatory, and cell-specific mechanisms of cerebellar pathobiology. These findings identify NCOA7-linked inflammatory dysfunction in the cerebellar-frontal axis in PH, redefining this disease with neurologic consequences and thus offering neural targets for diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic development.

title: The Association of MRI-Derived Tissue Bridge Morphometrics with Baseline Impairment and Recovery in Traumatic Spinal Cord Injury: A Subanalysis of the RISCIS Randomized Controlled Trial.
abstract: Early prognostic biomarkers are essential to optimize treatment and trial design in spinal cord injury (SCI). The Riluzole in SCI Study (RISCIS), a multicenter randomized controlled trial, provided evidence on secondary analyses that riluzole improved functional recovery in acute cervical SCI. The current analysis uses magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to assess lesion and tissue bridge morphometrics against baseline impairment, functional recovery, and treatment response in RISCIS participants. In this preplanned ambispective subanalysis, 24 participants underwent T2-weighted MRI for acute cervical SCI together with neurological and functional assessments to 12 months. A subset also had diffusion tensor imaging (DTI), used to extract fractional anisotropy (FA) values. Segmentation with the Spinal Cord Toolbox (v7.2) gave ventral, dorsal, and total tissue-bridge widths and lesion volume and length. Associations with American Spinal Injury Association Impairment Scale (AIS) grade, upper extremity motor score (UEMS) and total motor score (TMS), lower extremity motor score (LEMS), light touch and pinprick sensory scores, Spinal Cord Independence Measure (SCIM), and Short Form-36 (SF-36) domains at baseline and follow-up were analyzed with regression models adjusted for age and sex. Overall recovery across TMS, SCIM, and SF-36 Physical Component Summary was analyzed with an O'Brien-style global statistical test (GST). Interactions tested whether bridge metrics modified riluzole's effect. At baseline, greater ventral ( β = 9.65, p = 0.017) and total ( β = 6.16, p = 0.021) tissue-bridge widths were associated with higher TMS, and ventral width with higher UEMS ( β = 6.61, p = 0.010). Larger dorsal (odds ratio [OR] = 21.92, p = 0.013), ventral (OR = 4.91, p = 0.049), and total (OR = 3.70, p = 0.019) bridges corresponded to less severe baseline AIS grade. Pinprick scores increased with ventral ( β = 26.56, p = 0.020) and total ( β = 17.50, p = 0.023) bridge width, and light touch scores increased with total bridge width ( β = 16.22, p = 0.045). No imaging metric was associated with LEMS. These individual-metric associations were nominally significant but did not survive correction. In GST analyses, larger ventral ( T = 4.63, p = 0.012, p '= 0.048) and total ( T = 4.30, p = 0.019, p '=0.048) bridges predicted greater overall recovery; both remained significant after correction and were stable across sensitivity analyses. Ventral and total bridge width showed nominally significant interactions with riluzole treatment for upper-limb motor recovery. Exploratory DTI findings were inconclusive and sensitive to individual observations: both the FA-recovery association and the observation of poor outcome despite a preserved tissue bridge rested on a single participant. Overall, we found that midsagittal tissue-bridge width measured ∼72 h after injury from standard-of-care T2-weighted MRI was associated with baseline injury severity and multidomain functional recovery, at a timepoint substantially earlier than the 1 month at which tissue bridges have previously been quantified. Because edema may obscure lesion margins this early, acute bridge widths may underestimate spared tissue resolvable later. The treatment-interaction observation is hypothesis-generating and requires prospective confirmation. These findings support MRI-derived tissue bridges as candidate biomarkers for prognostication and enrichment of neuroprotective trials in SCI.

title: A review of medical image segmentation research based on bibliometrics.
abstract: BackgroundMedical image segmentation is a fundamental step in computer-aided diagnosis and treatment planning, and its research landscape has expanded rapidly with the advancement of artificial intelligence. A systematic bibliometric overview of this field is therefore needed to clarify its intellectual structure and emerging trends.ObjectiveTo provide a comprehensive bibliometric overview of the global research landscape, developmental trends, collaboration networks, and emerging hotspots in the field of medical image segmentation over the past decade.MethodsA bibliometric analysis was performed on 21,437 publications related to medical image segmentation, indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection from 2016 to 2025. The analysis systematically examined publication outputs, country-level contributions, author collaboration networks, journal distributions, and keyword co-occurrence patterns.ResultsThe annual publication count increased remarkably from 25 in 2016 to 5,207 in 2025. China contributed the largest share with 11,556 publications, followed by the United States (3,272) and India (1,924). Core researchers formed stable intra-team collaborations, though inter-team cooperation remained limited. Keyword and citation analyses identified deep learning, convolutional neural networks (CNNs), Transformers, U-Net, and their variants as dominant methodological themes. Case studies on skin and lung segmentation revealed differential research attention and international collaboration patterns across anatomical targets. A historical trajectory analysis showed methodological evolution from traditional image processing to fully convolutional networks and U-Net, and subsequently to hybrid architectures integrating attention mechanisms and Transformers.ConclusionMedical image segmentation has experienced substantial growth, driven by deep learning innovations. Future research may increasingly focus on multimodal foundation models capable of generalizable segmentation across diverse clinical scenarios. This bibliometric review offers researchers a valuable reference for understanding the intellectual structure and frontiers of the field.

title: Tractography-Based Insights into Neuroplasticity and Clinical Heterogeneity in Parkinson's Disease Subtypes.
abstract: Parkinson's disease shows substantial heterogeneity across motor, cognitive, and non-motor domains, reflecting variable patterns of neurodegeneration and compensation across distributed brain circuits. Diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (dMRI) tractography enables pathway-specific characterization of white-matter alterations and provides a framework for linking clinical subtypes to tract-level patterns that may be obscured by skeleton-based or connectomic averaging. Here, we synthesize white-matter evidence across motor, cognitive, genetic, and prodromal dimensions of PD heterogeneity, using tractography as an organizing framework within a broader dMRI and multimodal context. We review diffusion approaches ranging from diffusion tensor imaging to free-water, neurite, and fixel-based models. We distinguish pathway reconstructions from other diffusion and imaging analyses and consider how complementary approaches inform, but do not uniquely determine, interpretations of degeneration and subtype-specific neuroplasticity. Emerging methods, including harmonization pipelines, radiomic tractometry, and machine learning classifiers, may further improve tract-level sensitivity and reproducibility. Cognitive subtypes illustrate how posterior association and limbic tract degeneration, together with cholinergic and noradrenergic dysfunction, shape clinical progression. Integrating tractography with molecular, genetic, functional, and clinical markers may support subtype-specific biomarkers for risk stratification, prognosis, and targeted neuromodulation or rehabilitation strategies, although longitudinal and external validation is required before routine use.

title: Passive Sealing Stent-Grafts for Chimney Endovascular Repair: In Vitro Examination and a Japanese Single-Centre Retrospective Study.
abstract: Purpose Juxtarenal abdominal aortic aneurysms (JAAAs) present with a short infrarenal neck that does not permit standard endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR). The AFX VELA cuff extension with its endoskeletal architecture may reduce type Ia endoleak (TIaEL) through passive sealing. We examined this hypothesis using a double-chimney benchtop model and a clinical cohort treated with VELA-based chimney EVAR (ChEVAR). Materials and methods A benchtop model compared gutter leakage volumes among VELA, Endurant II and Excluder C3 (5 trials per device). A retrospective single-centre cohort (January 2018-April 2024) included consecutive JAAA patients undergoing VELA-based ChEVAR with ≥12-month follow-up. Postoperative computed tomographic (CT) morphometry compared seal-zone geometry across the 3 platforms. Results In the benchtop model, VELA showed a median gutter leakage of 5.0 mL/min (interquartile range [IQR], 4.0-11.0), whereas both comparators exceeded 500 mL/min and were right-censored. In the clinical cohort, 20 patients (55% male; median age 80.0 years) underwent ChEVAR for JAAAs with a median diameter of 53.5 mm and infrarenal neck length of 5.0 mm. Clinically successful sac exclusion was achieved in 19 of 20 patients (95%). Intraoperative TIaEL occurred in 5 patients: 1 major endoleak was sealed with adjunctive gutter coil embolisation, and 4 minor endoleaks resolved spontaneously on the 1-month CT angiogram. Over a median follow-up of 36.5 months, no persistent TIaEL was detected on follow-up imaging, and no chimney stent-graft (SG) occlusion occurred. One patient (5%) required an aortic-related reintervention for a type Ib endoleak. Estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) decreased by ≥20% in 9 patients (45%), and 1 started dialysis at 4 years. On postoperative CT morphometry, relative gutter area was lowest with VELA, intermediate with Endurant II and highest with Excluder C3; circumferential apposition followed the inverse pattern. Conclusion In the benchtop model, VELA produced consistently lower leakage than both comparators, with concordant CT morphometric evidence consistent with a passive sealing mechanism. In this cohort, VELA-based ChEVAR achieved clinically successful sac exclusion in 19 of 20 patients (95%) with no persistent TIaEL and no chimney SG occlusion. title: Bilateral Iliac Branch Endoprosthesis Deployment With IVUS-Guided Contrast-Sparing Technique: A Complex Case Report.
abstract: Background Preserving internal iliac artery (IIA) patency during endovascular aortic repair (EVAR) for aortobiiliac aneurysms typically requires substantial contrast volume, posing risk to patients with renal insufficiency. Case description We present the case of an elderly female with chronic kidney disease (CKD) stage 3b (baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate 35 mL/min/1.73 m², serum creatinine 1.5 mg/dL) and an aortobiiliac aneurysm who underwent complex bilateral iliac side-branch (iliac branch endoprosthesis [IBE]) deployment. The procedure used intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) as the primary guidance to minimize contrast exposure. A notable intraoperative challenge arose on the left side, where retrograde cannulation was unsuccessful due to anatomical tortuosity and sheath dislodgement. We therefore performed a left axillary cut-down, which facilitated successful IIA reconstruction and resolved a type 1b endoleak. The total contrast volume employed was approximately 38 mL. Incidental findings included hyperthyroidism and suspected lymphoproliferative disorder. Conclusion Intravascular ultrasound-guided bilateral IBE is feasible and substantially reduces contrast exposure in patients with renal impairment, though technical flexibility is essential for complex anatomy.Clinical ImpactIVUS-guided bilateral iliac branch endoprosthesis deployment may offer a contrast-sparing option for patients with chronic kidney disease undergoing endovascular repair of complex aortobiiliac aneurysms. Using IVUS for vessel identification, sizing, landing-zone selection, and stent-apposition assessment can reduce reliance on iodinated contrast while preserving internal iliac artery perfusion. This case shows that bilateral reconstruction is feasible with only 38 mL of contrast, even when complex anatomy requires axillary access. Its innovation is using IVUS as the primary guidance modality, with angiography reserved for confirmation and troubleshooting.

title: Successful Management of Infective Native Infrarenal Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Associated With Micrococcus luteus and Streptococcus mitis in a 77-year-Old Man.
abstract: BackgroundInfected native abdominal aortic aneurysm (INAAA) is a rare but life-threatening condition characterized by rapid progression and high mortality.Case SummaryWe report a 77-year-old male with a history of arterial hypertension, ischemic heart disease, and stage IVB hormone-sensitive prostate adenocarcinoma, presenting with lumbar pain and mild inflammatory activation, including leukocytes 8.8 ×10³/µL and C-reactive protein 3.6 mg/dL (normal <0.50 mg/dL). Computed tomography angiography (CTA) demonstrated a 50-mm infrarenal aneurysm, with periaortic inflammatory changes and a periaortic hematoma. A multidisciplinary decision, made 3 hours after admission, favored urgent open surgical repair with resection and in situ reconstruction. Midline laparotomy with debridement and resection of the affected aorta was performed; in situ reconstruction was carried out using a rifampicin soaked bifurcated Dacron graft covered with bovine pericardium with anastomoses to healthy aortic and iliac segments. Intraoperative cultures identified Micrococcus luteus and Streptococcus mitis , rare pathogens in this context. Targeted therapy included intravenous ceftriaxone during hospitalization, followed by oral amoxicillin-clavulanate and doxycycline for seven weeks. Histopathology confirmed chronic granulomatous abscessed inflammation. The postoperative course was uneventful, and the patient was discharged home on postoperative day 17. At six months, follow-up imaging demonstrated a patent reconstruction without signs of persistent infection.ConclusionThese findings highlight the importance of early recognition, aggressive debridement, and coordinated multidisciplinary management in achieving optimal outcomes in INAAA, particularly when atypical microorganisms complicate diagnosis and therapeutic decision-making.

title: Unilateral Biportal Endoscopy Versus Percutaneous Endoscopic Interlaminar Discectomy for Highly Migrated Lumbar Disc Herniation: A Retrospective Comparative Study With Quantitative MRI-Based Decompression Analysis.
abstract: Study designRetrospective comparative cohort study.ObjectiveTo compare the perioperative, clinical, and radiographic outcomes of unilateral biportal endoscopy (UBE) and percutaneous endoscopic interlaminar discectomy (PEID) in the treatment of highly migrated lumbar disc herniation (HMLDH).MethodsA total of 128 patients with single-level HMLDH who underwent UBE (n = 63) or PEID (n = 65) between June 2022 and January 2024 were retrospectively reviewed. All patients completed a minimum follow-up period of 2 years. Perioperative variables, complications, and reoperation events were analyzed. Clinical outcomes were evaluated using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS) and the Oswestry Disability Index (ODI). Radiographic decompression was quantitatively assessed using the postoperative dural sac cross-sectional area (DSCA) expansion rate measured on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).ResultsCompared with PEID, UBE was associated with a significantly shorter operative time, less endoscopic hemostasis time, and lower fluoroscopy time. Intraoperative blood loss was lower in the PEID group. Early postoperative back pain was significantly lower in the PEID group, whereas no significant between-group differences were observed in long-term VAS or ODI outcomes. The overall complication rate was significantly lower in the UBE group. In addition, UBE achieved a significantly greater DSCA expansion rate and a lower rate of residual disc fragments than PEID.ConclusionUBE and PEID achieved comparable long-term clinical outcomes in patients with HMLDH. UBE demonstrated advantages in perioperative efficiency, radiographic decompression, and reduced radiation exposure. Furthermore, UBE was associated with a lower overall complication rate, primarily attributable to a lower incidence of postoperative nerve root irritation.

title: Influence of dominant sequence artifacts on generative AI for virtual contrast-enhancement in breast MRI.
abstract: Background Virtual contrast-enhanced (vCE) breast MRI is a deep learning approach for generating contrast-like images from non-contrast acquisitions. As diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) has emerged as a major contributor to enhancement synthesis, understanding the influence of DWI-related image artifacts is important for the robustness and potential clinical implementation of AI-based contrast-free imaging approaches. We evaluated the robustness of a pix2pix-based vCE synthesis model to artifact-contaminated DWI during training and inference. Materials and methods This IRB-approved, retrospective study included 1,974 multiparametric breast MRI examinations (mean age: 49 years) acquired with two clinical routine 3T MRI scanners (2017-2022). High b-value (b = 1500 s/mm 2 ) DWI images were automatically classified for high-intensity (HI) and low-intensity (LI) artifacts using a pretrained neural network. A pix2pix 2D-GAN was trained either after excluding artifact-affected slices (vCE-clean) or using all available slices (vCE-all). Performance was evaluated using image similarity metrics, lesion-based analysis, reader assessment, and correlation of artifact scores with reconstruction errors. Results Excluding artifact-affected slices during training resulted in a small but statistically significant increase in whole-image structural similarity index (SSIM) with small effect size (vCE-all 0.843 ± 0.034; vCE-clean 0.849 ± 0.031, p < 0.001, d av = 0.20). However, lesion-based metrics and qualitative ratings of lesion enhancement and image quality were comparable between models. During Inference, strong LI DWI artifacts were associated with higher lesion-based errors. Conclusion Controlling for artifacts on diffusion weighted imaging (DWI) during vCE training only minorly influenced technical metrics but not perceived image quality/lesion enhancement. In contrast, severe signal-loss artifacts during inference impaired local performance, highlighting the importance of image quality control during potential deployment.

title: When a glabellar dermoid cyst is not the whole story: the significance of MRI in excluding intracranial segments.
abstract: Background Epidermoid and dermoid cysts are one of the most common benign pediatric tumors of the skull. Ultrasonography is usually the diagnostic tool of choice for their evaluation and diagnosis. Although benign, local growth with cosmetic issues, bone erosion, and occasional intracranial involvement generally warrant surgical resection. Since epidermoid and dermoid cysts may be seen by a wide range of medical disciplines, standardized recommendations for optimal diagnosis and treatment are necessary. Case presentation We report the case of a 14-month-old boy, who underwent neurosurgical removal of a glabellar dermoid cyst classified as an extracranial lesion, and in whom an intracranial lesion was identified on follow-up MRI, represents a rare and unusual clinical course. Ten months after surgery, a surveillance MRI revealed an intracranial lesion in the right frontal parasagittal region, while the child had developed no symptoms. Very careful retrospective review of the initial MRI suggested that an extremely small intracranial part of the lesion might have been faintly visible upon knowledge of the further clinical course. The intracranial lesion was subsequently resected and diagnosed as an epidermoid cyst. In our mini-review, we have compiled evidence that intracranial extension is more common than expected and particularly occurs in craniofacial midline lesions but is definitely not restricted to them. Conclusion Together, this case and literature review highlight the importance of careful preoperative assessment and interdisciplinary discussion to adequately determine the extent of craniofacial dermoid and epidermoid cysts before surgery. This case illustrates that a subtle intracranial lesion may not be recognizable on initial image interpretation despite MRI having been performed. Imaging follow-up is definitely recommended when intraoperative findings raise concern about deeper extension.

title: Clinical accuracy of transferring virtually planned zygomatic implant positions in severely atrophic maxilla: a single-arm study.
abstract: Objectives This study aimed to evaluate the clinical accuracy of transferring virtually planned zygomatic implant positions in severely atrophic maxilla. Materials and methods This clinical accuracy study included 24 participants with severely atrophic edentulous maxilla. All cases were digitally planned using cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) and treated with bilateral zygomatic implants under general anesthesia, with additional anterior conventional implants. Postoperative CBCT was used to superimpose the actual implant positions onto the virtual plan and assess coronal and apical deviations. Results A total of 48 zygomatic implants were placed in 24 participants. Three-dimensional superimposition of the preoperative virtual plans and postoperative CBCT scans demonstrated a mean coronal deviation of 1.917 ± 0.401 mm overall, with values of 1.989 ± 0.540 mm on the right side and 1.846 ± 0.160 mm on the left side. title: The law of surprise: temporal variation and seasonality of acute aortic syndromes: a single-centre epidemiologic cohort analysis spanning 20 years.
abstract: Background and aims Acute aortic syndromes (AAS) represent life-threatening cardiovascular emergencies characterized by high mortality rates despite rapid intervention. Global epidemiological data indicate substantial variance in incidence. Longitudinal single-centre data over extended periods are limited but crucial for understanding diagnostic, demographic, and systemic factors influencing admission trends.(1). This study aimed to analyze annual and seasonal variation trends of AAS over a 20-year period in a single maximal care centre and explore potential chronological and environmental contributors to this variation. Methods This retrospective cohort study evaluated 403 patients admitted with a confirmed diagnosis of AAS between 2005 and 2025 at the University Hospital Erlangen, Germany. All diagnoses were established via computed tomography angiography (CTA) and confirmed intraoperatively. Annual, quarterly, and monthly surgical volumes were calculated, and temporal trends were analyzed using Poisson and negative binomial regression models. Admission rates during public holidays and school vacations were also evaluated. Results Over the 20-year observation period, a steady increasing trend in the annual number of AAS cases was observed, peaking in 2017. Analysis of quarterly distributions revealed a statistically significant dominance of cases in the fourth quarter (Q4: October-December; p < 0.05) compared to the second (Q2) and third (Q3) quarters. Monthly analysis demonstrated a prominent peak in October (incidence rate ratio [IRR] = 1.85 vs. June, p < 0.05). Conversely, fixed public holidays and school vacations were associated with statistically significant reductions in daily admission counts (p < 0.05), with the lowest relative case counts observed during the Christmas vacation period (IRR: 0.40-0.50). Conclusion The case counts of acute aortic syndromes exhibits significant temporal and seasonal variation, characterized by a distinct late-autumn and early-winter peak, alongside significant declines during institutional vacation periods. These findings suggest that acute cardiovascular events are heavily modulated by cyclical environmental and socio-systemic factors.

title: Computed tomography anatomy of the pony thorax and abdomen and an example of a clinical application.
abstract: Background In veterinary medicine, computed tomography (CT) is a valuable diagnostic tool that provides detailed cross-sectional images with higher contrast resolution than conventional radiography. However, owing to the large body-size of horses, CT has been primarily limited in equine veterinary practice to imaging of the head, neck, and extremities, as imaging studies of the thoracic and abdominal cavities are not possible with standard gantry size in medium-to-large horses. In this study, we aimed to characterise the normal thoracic and abdominal anatomy of ponies using CT and to describe an example of the potential clinical applications of abdominal CT. CT examination of two ponies was performed in dorsal recumbency using a helical 16-slice multidetector scanner with a 90 cm-diameter gantry. The normal anatomy of these cavities was described and compared with anatomical cross-sections, and a clinical case involving colic surgery was analysed. Results Most of the thoracic and abdominal organs in the anatomical section were identifiable, and the use of these images as a reference assisted well in the interpretation of the clinical case scans. The advanced imaging technique aided in surgical planning. In the case involving colic surgery, no evidence of thick-walled intestinal segments was found on CT, but contents including gas, fluid, different types of ingests, and sand were identified preoperatively. Nerves or serous membranes (except for the spinal cord) could not be clearly identified on native CT images. Conclusions CT was useful for clinical diagnosis, but the small number of cases included in the study is a limitation that should be acknowledged.

title: Depth-specific characterization of bone microarchitecture in the femoral head: implications for osteoarthritis and osteoporosis research.
abstract: Background Osteoarthritis (OA) and osteoporosis (OP) are highly prevalent musculoskeletal diseases characterized by cartilage loss and increased subchondral bone formation and by systemic bone mass reduction, respectively. The femoral head is commonly examined in both OA and OP research, yet both conditions may coexist in the same patient, making it unclear how local cartilage degeneration and systemic bone mineral density (BMD), as a marker of OP-related skeletal status, contribute to bone microarchitectural changes at different depths. Methods Femoral heads were obtained from 30 patients undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty for hip OA. Ex vivo high-resolution peripheral quantitative computed tomography (HR-pQCT) was performed on the entire femoral head, followed by computational segmentation of the subchondral mineralized plate (SMP) and five concentric trabecular regions. Depth-specific bone microarchitectural parameters were analyzed in relation to histologically assessed cartilage degeneration and systemic BMD measured by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA). Results The cohort had a mean age of 75.4 ± 9.5 years, 53.3% were female, and patients spanned the spectrum of normal BMD (36.7%), osteopenia (46.7%), and osteoporosis (16.7%). Trabecular volumetric tissue mineral density (Tb.vTMD), bone volume to tissue volume (BV/TV), and trabecular thickness (Tb.Th) showed an initial decrease in the superficial trabecular regions, followed by a progressive increase toward deeper regions, whereas cyst-like void volume continuously decreased with depth and almost completely disappeared beyond 9.84 mm in depth. Cartilage degeneration independently predicted subchondral bone microstructure within the SMP and in superficial to intermediate trabecular regions (up to 13.12 mm in depth). Specifically, higher OARSI grades were associated with higher SMP.Th, Tb.vTMD, BV/TV, and Tb.Th. Systemic BMD T-score emerged as an independent predictor of trabecular bone parameters across all depths and represented the sole determinant of BV/TV and Tb.Th in the deepest trabecular region (beyond 13.12 mm depth), while cartilage degeneration was not associated with trabecular bone parameters in the deepest trabecular region. Conclusions Our findings showcase spatially distinct contributions of cartilage degeneration and systemic skeletal status to subchondral bone remodeling, identifying depth as a critical determinant in the analysis of osteochondral alterations in hip OA. Specifically, our findings emphasize that systemic BMD should be considered a covariate in OA research and that deep regions of the femoral head should be used for OP research to minimize potential confounding by local OA-related effects.

title: Quantitative imaging-pathology correlation in nodular fasciitis and diagnostic discrimination from sarcoma.
abstract: Objectives To investigate associations between key magnetic resonance imaging features of nodular fasciitis (NF) and quantitative histopathologic biomarkers, and to evaluate whether their integration provides complementary information for differentiating NF from soft tissue sarcoma (STS) in diagnostically equivocal settings. Materials and methods This retrospective study included 128 patients with NF and 133 with STS who underwent preoperative 3-T MRI between May 2023 and June 2025. Two blinded musculoskeletal radiologists independently evaluated predefined imaging features, including fascial tail sign, T2 heterogeneity score, enhancement pattern, perilesional edema, and mean/minimum apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC). Histopathology quantified cellular density, collagen content, and myxoid degeneration. Imaging-pathology correlations were assessed using Spearman analysis and multivariable regression. Diagnostic performance of MRI-only, pathology-only, and combined models was evaluated using logistic regression, receiver operating characteristic (ROC), area under the curve (AUC) analysis, calibration, decision curve analysis, and bootstrap validation. Results T2 heterogeneity correlated positively with myxoid degeneration (ρ = 0.52) and negatively with collagen content (ρ = -0.28) (p < 0.001). Mean ADC correlated inversely with cellular density (ρ = -0.63, p < 0.001). Mean ADC was significantly higher in NF than STS (p < 0.001). The combined model outperformed MRI alone (AUC, 0.96 vs 0.89) and demonstrated greater net clinical benefit. Bootstrap validation confirmed stable performance (mean AUC, 0.960; 95% confidence interval, 0.938-0.978). Conclusion Imaging features of NF were associated with underlying stromal and cellular substrates. Integrating imaging features with quantitative pathology biomarkers may support radiology-pathology concordance assessment in selected diagnostically equivocal cases. Key points Question How can we improve radiology-pathology concordance and reduce interpretative variability for NF cases presenting with suspicious, diagnostically equivocal magnetic resonance imaging findings? Findings T2 heterogeneity and diffusion measurements are associated with stromal composition and cellularity, while predefined MRI features demonstrated substantial-to-excellent inter-reader agreement. Critical relevance statement Embedding explicit AHA criteria in the prompt let an 8B model approach 671B-model agreement (38.91-81.52%), supporting standardized text-based workflows without fine-tuning.

title: MRI-based deep-learning radiomics nomogram for differentiating FIGO 2023 stage I from stage II-IV endometrial cancer: a multicenter study.
abstract: Objectives Preoperative identification of FIGO 2023 stage I endometrial cancer (EC) is important for treatment planning. We aimed to develop and validate a deep-learning radiomics nomogram (DLRN) based on multiparametric MRI to distinguish stage I EC from stage II-IV disease. Materials and methods This study retrospectively enrolled patients from three centers. Patients from Centers 1 and 2 were randomly split into a training set (n = 616), and an internal test set (n = 158), and Center 3 served as an external test set (n = 232). The DLRN integrated deep-learning features, intratumoral and peritumoral radiomics features, and clinical characteristics. The DLRN was compared with clinical, radiomics, and deep-learning models. Discrimination was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), with AUCs compared using DeLong's test. Results A total of 1006 patients (mean age, 56.5 ± 9.7 years) were analyzed. In the internal test set, the DLRN achieved an AUC of 0.852, higher than the clinical (0.673; p = 0.001), original radiomics (0.765; p = 0.030), and combined radiomics (0.793; p = 0.050) models. In the external test set, the DLRN remained robust (AUC = 0.829) and outperformed the clinical, original radiomics, and combined radiomics models (AUC = 0.680, 0.681, and 0.743; all p < 0.005). With DLRN assistance, radiologists showed improved diagnostic performance. Conclusion The MRI-based DLRN showed robust discrimination between FIGO 2023 stage I and stage II-IV EC across test sets, supporting its potential for preoperative risk stratification and decision support. Key points Question The introduction of the FIGO 2023 staging system has made the differentiation between stages more challenging, highlighting the need for better tools. Findings A new MRI-based deep-learning radiomics nomogram (DLRN) accurately identifies high-risk patients, significantly outperforming traditional and individual clinical prediction methods. Critical relevance statement This tool helps doctors make better preoperative treatment plans, potentially improving patient outcomes in endometrial cancer.

title: Multiphasic CT radiomics-clinical model for predicting acute pancreatitis recurrence: a multicenter survival analysis.
abstract: Objectives To develop and externally validate a predictive model integrating multiphasic CT radiomics and clinical variables to estimate recurrence risk after first-episode acute pancreatitis (AP). Materials and methods This multicenter retrospective study included 548 patients with first-episode AP (training, n = 272; internal validation, n = 117; external validation, n = 159). Clinical and multiphasic CT data were collected, with recurrence as the primary endpoint. After stability-based feature selection, clinical, radiomics, and combined Cox models were constructed. Performance was evaluated using the C-index and time-dependent AUC, with SHAP for interpretability. Results A total of 548 patients were included (median age 42 years; 363 men). Recurrence rates were similar across cohorts (30.1%, 29.9%, and 28.3%; p = 0.702). The combined model achieved C-indices of 0.783 and 0.775 in the internal and external validation cohorts, respectively, numerically higher than those of the clinical model (0.748 and 0.750) and radiomics model (0.647 and 0.619), although the incremental improvement over the clinical model was not statistically significant. In the external validation cohort, time-dependent AUCs remained acceptable through 36 months but declined at 48 months. High-risk patients had lower 3-year recurrence-free survival than low-risk patients (37.4% vs 86.8%; log-rank p < 0.001). SHAP analysis identified the NC-3mm-Radscore as the most influential imaging-derived variable, whereas etiology-targeted prevention was the dominant protective factor. Conclusions The combined model demonstrated acceptable discrimination for predicting recurrence within the first 24 months after first-episode AP and may facilitate individualized follow-up and secondary prevention strategies. Key points Question Can a multiphasic CT radiomics-clinical model improve prediction of AP recurrence over clinical factors alone in a multicenter setting? Findings The combined model demonstrated numerically higher predictive performance than the clinical model, though the incremental improvement was not statistically significant. Critical relevance statement This study critically evaluates the added value of multiphasic radiomics for recurrence prediction in AP, demonstrating that while radiomics captures baseline microenvironmental vulnerability, post-discharge clinical interventions remain the dominant dynamic drivers.

title: AI-accelerated compressed sensing and deep learning reconstruction for colon MRI: prospective validation of image quality and preliminary assessment of staging accuracy versus contrast-enhanced CT.
abstract: Objectives To prospectively validate an AI-accelerated MRI protocol combining L₁-regularized compressed sensing and deep learning reconstruction for colon cancer staging, compared with contrast-enhanced CT (CECT). Materials and methods This single-center study (August 2022-April 2024) enrolled 132 patients with pathologically confirmed colon cancer who underwent both 3.0-T non-contrast MRI and CECT within 1 week. Patients unable to complete an MRI were excluded. MRI sequences included T1- and T2-weighted imaging and diffusion-weighted imaging. Image quality was assessed using a 4-point Likert scale, alongside quantitative analysis of contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) and edge rise distance (ERD). Surgical pathology correlation was available for 33 cases. Five radiologists independently reviewed the images. Results Among 153 matched examination pairs from 132 patients (mean age, 58 ± 11 years), AI-MRI outperformed CECT in both qualitative and quantitative measures. MRI yielded higher image quality scores (4 [IQR 3-4] vs. 3 [IQR 3-3]), improved CNR (5.5 [IQR 4.2-7.0] vs. 1.3 [IQR 0.7-2.2]), and reduced ERD (1.6 mm [IQR 1.2-2.8] vs. 3.7 mm [IQR 2.8-5.0]). MRI provided superior peritoneal sharpness (75.8%) and colonic wall visualization (100%), and superior or equivalent tumor conspicuity (92.2%) and nodal assessment (86.9%), whereas CECT demonstrated better artifact control (45.1%). In preliminary analyses, MRI achieved higher T-staging accuracy (78.8% vs. 30.3%) and N-staging specificity (93.3% vs. 13.3%). Conclusion The AI-accelerated MRI protocol significantly outperformed CECT in image quality and preliminary staging accuracy for colon cancer evaluation while eliminating radiation exposure. Key points Question Can an AI-accelerated MRI protocol provide superior image quality and staging performance compared with contrast-enhanced CT, which has limited diagnostic accuracy for colon cancer staging? Findings AI-accelerated MRI using L₁-regularized compressed sensing and deep learning reconstruction achieved superior image quality and higher preliminary staging accuracy than contrast-enhanced CT. Critical Relevance Statement AI-accelerated MRI improves image quality and staging confidence without radiation exposure, supporting its potential to enhance preoperative assessment and clinical decision-making in colon cancer.

title: Deep learning-based detection and classification of airway nodules on CT for early medical intervention.
abstract: Objectives Airway lesions are common CT findings in interval and post-screen lung cancers; however, airway nodules are frequently overlooked. Robust artificial intelligence (AI) tools for characterizing airway nodules remain limited. This study aimed to develop and evaluate deep learning-based models for the detection and classification of airway nodules on low-dose CT(LDCT) as a second-reading tool. Materials and methods 1813 segmental and more proximal airway nodules were retrospectively identified from 1107 LDCT of 1043 participants. A sphere-based center-points matching network, first used to establish a lung nodule detection model, was transferred to airway nodules and enhanced by incorporating coordinate and multiscale attention. The model was trained on 907 proximal airway nodules and independently tested on 738 proximal nodules across four hospitals. The clinical utility of the AI tool was evaluated through human-AI interaction. For nodule classification, a 3D SEResNeXt101-based model was trained, validated and tested using 286 airway nodules (121 benign, 165 malignant) with a 6:2:2 split and evaluated in an independent testing dataset. Results On the independent testing set, the detection model achieved a high sensitivity of 73.7%. Human-AI interaction demonstrated AI assistance significantly improved radiologists' performance, increasing sensitivity from 39.5% to 72.9% and F1-score from 49.4% to 77.2%, while reducing diagnosis time from 83.8 s to 61.8 s. The classification model showed high sensitivities of 82.1%, 71.4%, 94.3%, 72.7% and specificities of 62.7%, 73.9%, 73.9%, 87.5% across multicenter training, validation, testing and independent testing sets, respectively. Conclusion This AI system significantly enhances the detection and classification of proximal airway nodules, guiding early medical intervention. Key points Question Improved early detection and classification of airway nodules are critical for lung cancer mortality reduction, but AI-based CAD systems targeting airway nodules remain scarce. Findings The DL models for detection and classification of proximal airway nodules on chest CT were developed and assisted radiologists to achieve higher detection accuracy. Critical Relevance Statement The clinical applications of the proposed DL-based system for detecting and classifying proximal airway nodules on chest CT scans help radiologists reduce missed/delayed diagnoses and shorten diagnostic time as a second-reading tool, guiding medical intervention and improving clinical outcomes.

title: Deep learning-based quantification of CT changes after 1 year of pirfenidone treatment as a prognostic marker in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.
abstract: Objectives To evaluate the prognostic value of changes in deep learning-based CT quantification following 1 year of pirfenidone treatment in patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF). Materials and methods This study included patients with IPF who received at least 1 year of pirfenidone between September 2009 and March 2022 at two hospitals. The extent of normal lung and fibrosis (sum of reticular opacity and honeycombing) was quantified on baseline and 1-year follow-up chest CT scans using a deep learning-based tool, and the changes were calculated. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause mortality or lung transplantation; the secondary outcome was a ≥ 10% absolute decline in forced vital capacity (FVC) occurring after the 1-year follow-up. Associations between changes in CT quantification and these outcomes were assessed using Cox proportional hazards regression analyses. Results A total of 436 patients (341 men; mean age, 69.8 years) were included. Greater preservation of normal lung extent over 1 year was associated with a lower risk of the composite outcome (adjusted hazard ratio (HR) per 5% increase: 0.90; 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.85, 0.96; p < 0.001), whereas increases in fibrosis extent were associated with a higher risk (adjusted HR per 5% increase: 1.16, 95% CI: 1.06, 1.27, p = 0.002). Regarding the secondary outcome of ≥ 10% absolute FVC decline, only the change in fibrosis extent remained a significant predictor (adjusted HR per 5% increase: 1.26, 95% CI: 1.09, 1.45, p = 0.001). Conclusions Changes in deep learning-based CT quantification results over 1 year of pirfenidone treatment demonstrated significant prognostic value in patients with IPF. Key points Question Disease progression and mortality in patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) continue to occur unpredictably beyond 1 year of pirfenidone treatment. Findings Changes in deep learning-based quantification of normal lung and fibrosis extent after 1 year of pirfenidone treatment were significant prognostic predictors. Critical relevance statement Incorporating 1-year changes in deep learning-based CT quantification improves prognostication of mortality, lung transplantation, and lung function decline, supporting more individualized risk stratification in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.

title: Prostate: simplified MRI anatomy recognition and training-the P-SMART study: a novel approach to defining prostatic apex, mid-gland and base.
abstract: Objectives Precise lesion localisation on prostate MRI-specifically, identification of whether at the apex, mid-gland, or base-is essential for effective communication and clinical management. This study aimed to assess interobserver agreement of current practice using the Prostate Imaging-Reporting and Data System (PI-RADS) against a novel anatomy-based approach, P-SMART (Prostate Simplified MRI Anatomy Recognition and Training). Materials and methods This multi-reader, two-phase agreement study, used axial and sagittal T2-weighted MRI from a publicly available dataset. Forty MRI cases were annotated with four regions of interest (ROIs). Readers were asked to document ROI location-apex, mid-gland, or base-first using the PI-RADS method, then following a 3-week washout period and short educational intervention, using the P-SMART method. Interobserver agreement was evaluated using Fleiss' kappa (κ) statistics and compared following bootstrap resampling using a paired t-test. Subgroup analyses were performed by reader expertise and prostate size. Results Following quality assurance, 156 ROIs were evaluated by 43 readers in each phase of the study. Overall interobserver agreement improved with P-SMART vs PI-RADS (κ = 0.571 vs 0.399; p < 0.001). originalAbstract:
Objectives

Precise lesion localisation on prostate MRI-specifically, identification of whether at the apex, mid-gland, or base-is essential for effective communication and clinical management. The P-SMART approach, designed to align with the PI-RADS sector map, yielded significantly higher interobserver agreement for prostate lesion-level localisation than the PI-RADS method, across reader experience and gland size, though overall agreement was only moderate. title: Diagnostic performance benchmarks of MRI for prostate cancer: a large-scale cohort study of 33,759 patients.
abstract: Objective To evaluate the real-world diagnostic performance of PI-RADS for detecting clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa) across large-scale worldwide cohorts. Materials and methods This multicenter observational study included 20,429 patients from nine Chinese institutions and a published worldwide meta-analysis dataset comprising 13,330 patients for comparison. All PI-RADS assessments were extracted from original MRI reports produced by clinical radiologists as part of standard diagnostic workflows. Summary receiver operating characteristic curves were constructed using a bivariate random-effects model, and center-level areas under the curve (AUCs) were pooled via random-effects meta-analysis. Subgroup analyses were conducted. Results PI-RADS exhibited overall discriminatory performance for csPCa across nine Chinese cohorts comparable to the META results from 70 studies, though significant inter-center variation was observed. Using a PI-RADS ≥ 3 threshold, pooled sensitivity was 92.6% and specificity was 51.5%. At a PI-RADS ≥ 4 threshold, pooled specificity improved to 78.1%, with a sensitivity of 81.5%. The overall diagnostic performance was consistent across thresholds: The summary ROC (SROC) AUC was 0.903 for PI-RADS ≥ 3 and 0.826 for PI-RADS ≥ 4 in detecting csPCa at the meta-analysis level. Subgroup analyses indicated better performance among older patients (≥ 70 years) and those with higher PSA levels (> 20 ng/mL). PI-RADS v2.1 outperformed v2 or earlier versions in most clinical scenarios. Conclusions This large-scale real-world study provides critical multicenter evidence supporting the use of PI-RADS in clinical practice worldwide, while also revealing substantial variability in scoring and diagnostic performance across institutions. The findings offer an evidence-based overview of PI-RADS implementation in China and worldwide, highlighting both its utility and inconsistencies. Key points Question What are the real-world PI-RADS diagnostic performance benchmarks for clinically significant prostate cancer detection across diverse Chinese multicenter institutions versus global data? Findings PI-RADS demonstrated good overall performance (SROC AUC 0.903 at a threshold of ≥ 3), with superior discriminatory ability in older patients, higher PSA levels, and v2.1 users. Critical relevance statement This article critically assesses substantial inter-institutional heterogeneity in PI-RADS performance, highlighting that pooled estimates should not replace local calibration and that regionally adapted implementation strategies are essential for advancing clinical radiology practice.

title: Feasibility of one-stop multi-energy dynamic photon-counting perfusion CT for resectable HCC evaluation: lesion detection and histopathological correlations.
abstract: Objectives To assess the feasibility of one-stop multi-energy dynamic volume perfusion photon-counting CT (VP-PCCT) for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) evaluation, including lesion detection and correlations with histopathology. Materials and methods From July 2024 to June 2025, 407 participants with suspected malignant liver lesions prospectively underwent VP-PCCT, and 177 patients with pathology-confirmed HCC who received three-phase energy-integrating detector CT (EID-CT) were retrospectively enrolled for comparisons of image quality and lesion detectability. Single-phase images reconstructed from VP-PCCT perfusion datasets were compared with EID-CT. Perfusion parameters were analyzed between groups stratified separately by histological grade and microvascular invasion (MVI), and logistic regression was employed to identify independent indicators. Results Ninety-two participants [median age, 62 years (IQR, 53-69); 76 males] with pathology-confirmed HCC were included in the VP-PCCT group and matched with 92 in the EID-CT group. Compared with EID-CT, 40-keV VP-PCCT provided comparable image quality for HCC and vessels with a similar tumor detection rate but a lower radiation dose. Poorly-differentiated HCCs showed higher tumor hepatic perfusion index (HPI tumor ) and peritumoral blood flow (BF peritumor ); MVI-positive HCCs exhibited lower tumor arterial liver perfusion (ALP tumor ) and normalized blood flow of peritumoral region (BF norm_peritumor ) (all p < 0.05). HPI tumor [odds ratio (OR): 1.06] and BF peritumor (OR: 1.04) were independent risk factors for poorly differentiated HCC, whereas decreased ALP tumor (OR: 0.97) and BF norm_peritumor (OR: 0.25) were associated with MVI positivity (all p < 0.05). Conclusions One-stop VP-PCCT delivers high-quality morphologic and perfusion evaluation in a single low-dose scan, with hemodynamic profiles that may be associated with histological grade and MVI status. Key points Question Clinical use of dynamic volume perfusion CT for comprehensively evaluating HCC without additional multiphase contrast-enhanced imaging remains limited. Findings Multi-energy dynamic photon-counting perfusion CT provided high-quality morphologic imaging of HCC at a low dose, with perfusion parameters independently indicating poorly differentiated HCC and MVI. Critical relevance statement One-stop multi-energy dynamic photon-counting perfusion CT enables high-quality morphologic and functional assessment in a single low-dose scan, providing comprehensive HCC evaluation with hemodynamic profiling that may support the assessment of histological grade and MVI.

title: Radiomics analysis of brain-tumor interface on multiparametric MRI for prediction of brain metastasis primary site.
abstract: Objectives Brain metastasis (BM) frequently occurs in advanced cancer patients, and accurate identification of the primary origin is essential for personalized treatment. Conventional imaging often lacks sensitivity and specificity for BM source prediction. This study aimed to develop and validate a multiparametric MRI-based radiomics model emphasizing brain-tumor interface (BTI) features to improve noninvasive BM origin identification. Materials and methods The primary cohort included 429 patients (740 BMs) from two centers, non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), small cell lung cancer (SCLC), breast cancer (BC), and gastrointestinal cancer (GIC), and an independent validation cohort of 33 patients (84 BMs) from a third center. All underwent pre-treatment 3.0 T MRI with T1-weighted contrast-enhanced (T1CE) and T2-weighted (T2W) sequences. Radiomic features were extracted from tumor core and BTI regions (2, 4, 6, 8 mm). Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression was used for feature selection, and radiomics signatures (RS) were evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. Results The constructed RS-BTI4 based on the 4-mm BTI region generated the best overall performance, with area under the ROC curve (AUCs) in the training cohort were 0.855 (LC/NLC), 0.910 (SCLC/NSCLC), and 0.890 (BC/GIC); in validation cohort, 0.726, 0.856, and 0.809; and in external validation cohort, 0.739, 0.750, and 0.792, respectively. RS-BTI4 consistently outperformed models based on other BTI radial widths and the whole tumor region in identifying the primary origin of BM. Conclusion BTI-derived radiomic features demonstrate strong potential for noninvasive identification of BM origin, with the 4-mm BTI region showing optimal predictive performance. Key points Question Conventional MRI cannot reliably identify the primary origin of brain metastases, particularly when the primary tumor remains unknown at diagnosis. Findings The 4-mm brain-tumor interface model showed the most favorable overall performance, measured by area under the curve, across three binary classification tasks and validation cohorts. Critical relevance statement Integrating brain-tumor interface radiomics with multiparametric MRI may improve noninvasive estimation of BM origin and support more targeted diagnostic evaluation in clinical radiology.

title: Peripheral and soft-tissue vascular malformations in the 2025 ISSVA classification: a practical MRI approach.
abstract: The 2025 update of the International Society for the Study of Vascular Anomalies (ISSVA) classification introduced several imaging-relevant changes, including the recognition of potentially unique vascular anomalies. Although the main framework for vascular tumors remains unchanged, with continued subdivision into benign, borderline, and malignant tumors, the most radiologically relevant structural changes concern vascular malformations, which were reorganized into fast-flow lesions, slow-flow lesions, and developmental anomalies of named vessels. These updates are important for radiologists because imaging plays a central role in assessing hemodynamic characteristics, defining lesion extent, and identifying findings relevant to procedural planning and multidisciplinary management. This educational review presents an author-derived four-step framework that organizes established MRI observations for peripheral and soft-tissue vascular malformations according to the structure and terminology of the 2025 ISSVA classification, including hemodynamic assessment, vascular components, tissue composition, lesion extent, and treatment-relevant anatomy. KEY POINTS: Question Imaging-relevant organizational and terminology changes in the 2025 ISSVA classification require practical guidance for consistent MRI assessment and reporting of peripheral and soft-tissue vascular malformations. Findings An author-derived four-step, flow-based framework organizes hemodynamics, dominant vascular components, tissue composition, lesion extent, and treatment-relevant anatomy into structured MRI assessment. Critical relevance statement The MRI-focused framework provides a practical way to apply the 2025 ISSVA classification consistently in image interpretation, terminology, and reporting of peripheral and soft-tissue vascular malformations.

title: Time-dependent diffusion MRI in determining mismatch repair status of endometrial cancer.
abstract: Objectives Mismatch repair (MMR) proteins are important in determining therapeutic strategy in endometrial cancer (EC). We investigated the role of microstructural parameters derived from time-dependent diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (td-dMRI) in differentiating MMR status of EC. Materials and methods This prospective single-center study enrolled patients with suspected EC who underwent preoperative td-dMRI. Tumors were classified as MMR-deficient (dMMR) and MMR-proficient (pMMR) by immunohistochemistry. The microstructural parameters, including intracellular volume fraction ( vin ), cell diameter ( d ), cellularity ( ρ ), extracellular diffusivity ( Dex ), and water exchange rate constant ( kin ), were derived by fitting td-dMRI data with three methods (IMPULSED, JOINT, and EXCHANGE), together with the apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC). Differences in these microstructural parameters between dMMR and pMMR EC were compared. The diagnostic performances were evaluated by the areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Results Eighty-two patients (17 dMMR, 61.8 ± 10.1 years and 65 pMMR, 58.6 ± 11.8 years) were recruited. dMMR EC exhibited higher vin , ρ and lower Dex , ADC values than pMMR EC (p ≤ 0.003). IMPULSED and JOINT demonstrated higher AUCs than conventional ADC (p = 0.025 and 0.046, respectively). The combined selected microstructural parameters ( vin and Dex ) derived from JOINT achieved an AUC of 0.903; JOINT demonstrated superior parametric stability and marginally better calibration than IMPULSED. Conclusion In this exploratory study, td-dMRI discriminated between dMMR and pMMR ECs, providing information on the intricate microscopic organizational structures in tumors. The microstructural parameters may serve as a promising method to improve the diagnostic efficacy of diffusion-weighted MRI in differentiating MMR status of EC. Objectives

Mismatch repair (MMR) proteins are important in determining therapeutic strategy in endometrial cancer (EC). We investigated the role of microstructural parameters derived from time-dependent diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (td-dMRI) in differentiating MMR status of EC.

This prospective single-center study enrolled patients with suspected EC who underwent preoperative td-dMRI. The combined selected microstructural parameters ( vin and Dex ) derived from JOINT achieved an AUC of 0.903; JOINT demonstrated superior parametric stability and marginally better calibration than IMPULSED.

In this exploratory study, td-dMRI discriminated between dMMR and pMMR ECs, providing information on the intricate microscopic organizational structures in tumors. The microstructural parameters may serve as a promising method to improve the diagnostic efficacy of diffusion-weighted MRI in differentiating MMR status of EC.
